--- What "ReloadDoc" actually is in this binary ---

ReloadDoc is not a function here. The only symbol in the whole program that matches

  Slot +0x10 of CProductionThread::vftable (entry 0x140ea8a58) = 0x14076db80.
  0x14076db80 is BASETOOLS.DLL::CViThread::Start, a 5-byte import thunk whose sole

  It logs nothing and calls nothing: no FUN_140692af0, no FUN_14068f0f0.

The divisor is not a guess. The magic constant is loaded immediately before the loop
and again at the loop latch:

    14068f58a  MOV RAX,0x4a7904a7904a7905
    14068f709  MOV RAX,0x4a7904a7904a7905

and the sequence IMUL / SAR RDX,0x8 / SHR RAX,0x3f / ADD RDX,RAX is the standard
signed 64-bit division idiom. Checked arithmetically:

    ceil(2^72 / 880) = 5366325548715505925 = 0x4A7904A7904A7905   -> matches
    ceil(2^72 / 1040) = 0x3F03F03F03F03F04                          -> does not match

so the divisor is 880 = 0x370, exactly as the decompiler renders it. The element
stride 0x410 = 1040 is a different quantity and is not the divisor.

CLASSIFICATION: NOT a positive constant. It is a value loaded from the document:
two 64-bit loads through *(doc + 0x5878), differenced, then divided by the constant
0x370. Only the divisor is a constant, and no positive integer literal is passed.

OBSERVATION, stated as fact and not as a verdict. The first argument is indexed by
the zone, but the count is not. Arg1 is base + index*0x410, while the count reads
offsets +0x18 and +0x20 of the base with no index term. The very next loop in the
same function does apply the index term:

    lVar13 = *(longlong *)(*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x5878) + 0x20 + uVar16) -
             *(longlong *)(*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x5878) + 0x18 + uVar16);
    ...
    } while (uVar17 < (ulonglong)
                      ((*(longlong *)(*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x5878) + 0x20 + uVar16) -
                        *(longlong *)(*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x5878) + 0x18 + uVar16)) /
                       0x370));

with uVar16 advancing by 0x410 per zone (14068f6fb  ADD RSI,0x410, and the matching
uVar16 = uVar16 + 0x410 in the decompilation). So the per-zone iteration count that
follows the FUN_140674570 call uses the indexed form, while the count handed to
FUN_140674570 uses the unindexed form. For zone 0 the two coincide; for zones 1 and
beyond they are two different expressions. Whether that is intended depends on what

A note on RDI, since the count reads RDI-relative fields. RDI is the document on
entry, is clobbered at 0x14053166d to serve as the loop end pointer, and is restored
from the stack slot [RBP + 0x220] at 0x140531687 on the loop exit path. On the
empty-vector path the JZ at 0x14053166b jumps straight to 0x14053168e and never
reaches the clobbering instruction, so RDI is still the document there too. RDI is
therefore the document on both paths, and RDI+0x2478 / RDI+0x2480 are document
fields on both paths.

--- Classification, term by term ---

  TERM A: (*(doc+0x2480) - *(doc+0x2478)) >> 3
      Two 64-bit loads from the document, differenced, arithmetically shifted right 3.
      This is the element count of the pointer vector whose begin/end pair sits at
      document + 0x2478 / + 0x2480; the 8-byte element size matches the >> 3.
      NOT a constant. Value loaded from the document.

  TERM B: SUM of FUN_14052b7c0(elem, 1)
      A running total in RSI, accumulated from the return value in RAX at each
      iteration of the loop over the vector at document + 0x2448 / + 0x2450, whose
      elements are 0x28 bytes apart. Starts at 0 from XOR ESI,ESI. If the vector is
      empty the loop is skipped and the term is exactly 0.
      NOT a constant. Computed by a function call over document data.

  WHOLE EXPRESSION: the sum of two document-derived terms. NOT a positive constant.

  The only literals present are:
      MOV DL,0x1     at 140531671, the literal 1 handed to FUN_14052b7c0
      SAR RDX,0x3    at 14053169c, the shift amount 3
  Neither is a count. No positive integer literal is passed to FUN_140674570.

--- Why this is the resize, from inside this same function ---

The same function later bounds-checks the carte's result vector using the 0x370
element size on param_1 + 0x18 / param_1 + 0x20, and logs the trim:

    CLogManagerFunction::Write
              (local_1f8,4,"Index %d Out of table m_VectResultats size = %Iu.\n",
               (ulonglong)uVar20,
               (*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x20) - *(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x18)) / 0x370);

    CLogManagerFunction::Write
              (local_1f8,2,"m_VectResultats.RemoveAt %d %Iu Size %Iu\n",(ulonglong)uVar20,
               uVar13 - uVar18,uVar13);

The 0x370 element size is the same one used in the PrepareExecData counts section, and
the trimmed size there is computed as the pointer-vector element counts at document
+0x2478 and document +0x2448:

    uVar13 = (*(longlong *)(this + 0x2480) - *(longlong *)(this + 0x2478) >> 3) +
             ((longlong)plStack_2a0 - (longlong)local_2a8 >> 3);

which is Term A plus the element count of the +0x2448 vector. The count passed to
FUN_140674570 at 0x1405316a6 is the same quantity except that its second term is the
per-element accumulation of FUN_14052b7c0 instead of a plain element count. So the
requested new size of m_VectResultats depends on what FUN_14052b7c0 returns for each
element, not on any fixed number.

    + SUM FUN_14052b7c0(elem, 1) for elem over doc+0x2448..doc+0x2450, stride 0x28

  The count is a value computed from the document. It is not a positive constant, and
  no positive integer literal is passed.

  Per instruction, analysis stopped inside PV_AffectIndResult. FUN_140674570,
  FUN_14052b7c0 and FUN_1406747a0 were not entered, and the callers of
  PV_AffectIndResult were not examined.

===== END =====
===== FUN_14052b7c0 return =====

--- ANSWER: a value taken from the element, not a constant and not always zero ---

  return = SUM over the qualifying nodes of an in-order walk of the tree rooted at
           *param_1, of  ( (*(node + 0x30) - *(node + 0x28)) SAR 3 )
           where "qualifying" means *(node + 0x20) != 0x100

  Because the call site passes param_2 = 1, the qualifier reduces to exactly that
  single test on *(node + 0x20). Each qualifying node contributes the element count
  of a pointer pair held in the element, arithmetic-shifted right by 3.

  It is a value taken from the element. It is NOT a positive constant. It is not
  unconditionally zero either, though it evaluates to 0 in the specific cases noted
  below, most importantly when the container is empty.

--- Function identity ---

FUN_14052b7c0, body 0x14052b7c0 .. 0x14052b84e, 45 instructions, no name.

search_resolve on the entry point returns only the default label:

    FUN_14052b7c0  @ 14052b7c0

so there is no PDB symbol and no demangled name for it, unlike PV_AffectIndResult.
It is referred to by its address.

Signature:

    longlong FUN_14052b7c0(longlong *param_1,char param_2);

  param_1  pointer to a 64-bit field; the function immediately loads through it
  param_2  a char selector, only the values 0 and 1 are distinguished

  The whole body is 45 instructions containing no CALL, no store to memory, and
  therefore no log string and no side effect. It is a pure read-only accumulator
  that returns its result in RAX.

--- Full listing, in order ---

    14052b7c0  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX]          ; RCX = *param_1  (the tree sentinel)
    14052b7c3  XOR R9D,R9D                      ; R9 = 0, the accumulator
    14052b7c6  MOVZX R8D,DL                      ; R8 = zero-extended param_2
    14052b7ca  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]          ; RAX = node at +0x00
    14052b7cd  CMP RAX,RCX
    14052b7d0  JZ 0x14052b84b                    ; empty container -> return 0
    14052b7d2  TEST R8B,R8B                      ; loop head
    14052b7d5  JZ 0x14052b7e7                    ; param_2 == 0 -> always accumulate
    14052b7d7  CMP R8B,0x1
    14052b7db  JNZ 0x14052b7f6                   ; param_2 == 1 -> fall to the test
    14052b7dd  CMP qword ptr [RAX + 0x20],0x100  ; node+0x20 == 256 ?
    14052b7e5  JZ 0x14052b7f6                    ; yes -> skip this node
    14052b7e7  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x30]    ; end
    14052b7eb  SUB RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x28]    ; minus begin
    14052b7ef  SAR RDX,0x3                       ; >> 3, arithmetic
    14052b7f3  ADD R9,RDX                        ; accumulate
    14052b7f6  CMP byte ptr [RAX + 0x19],0x0     ; node+0x19, the nil flag
    14052b7fa  JNZ 0x14052b846                   ; non-nil -> take the successor
    14052b7fc  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x10]    ; +0x10 = parent
    14052b800  CMP byte ptr [RDX + 0x19],0x0
    14052b804  JNZ 0x14052b820
    14052b806  MOV RAX,RDX
    14052b809  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX]
    14052b80c  CMP byte ptr [RDX + 0x19],0x0
    14052b810  JNZ 0x14052b846
    14052b812  MOV RAX,RDX
    14052b815  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX]
    14052b818  CMP byte ptr [RDX + 0x19],0x0
    14052b81c  JZ 0x14052b812
    14052b81e  JMP 0x14052b846
    14052b820  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x8]     ; +0x08 = right child
    14052b824  CMP byte ptr [RDX + 0x19],0x0
    14052b828  JNZ 0x14052b843
    14052b82a  NOP word ptr [RAX + RAX*0x1]
    14052b830  CMP RAX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x10]    ; subtree-root test
    14052b834  JNZ 0x14052b843
    14052b836  MOV RAX,RDX
    14052b839  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]
    14052b83d  CMP byte ptr [RDX + 0x19],0x0
    14052b841  JZ 0x14052b830
    14052b843  MOV RAX,RDX
    14052b846  CMP RAX,RCX
    14052b849  JNZ 0x14052b7d2                   ; loop back
    14052b84b  MOV RAX,R9                        ; return the accumulator
    14052b84e  RET

--- Return expression, specialised to the call from PV_AffectIndResult ---

The caller sets the second argument to the literal 1:

    140531671  MOV DL,0x1
    140531673  MOV RCX,RBX
    140531676  CALL 0x14052b7c0
    14053167b  ADD RSI,RAX

The entry instruction MOVZX R8D,DL makes R8B equal to 1 on entry. That fixes the
selector branch:

    TEST R8B,R8B / JZ 0x14052b7e7   at 14052b7d2  is NOT taken  (R8B is 1, not 0)
    CMP  R8B,0x1 / JNZ 0x14052b7f6  at 14052b7d7  is NOT taken  (R8B is exactly 1)

so control always falls into the single remaining test, and a node contributes only
when it is not tagged 0x100. The full three-way selector never gets exercised by
this call site; only the param_2 == 1 arm runs.

RETURN EXPRESSION, with param_2 = 1:

    ( *(node + 0x30) - *(node + 0x28) ) SAR 3        summed over every node N of the
                                                      in-order walk starting at
                                                      *param_1 for which
                                                      *(N + 0x20) != 0x100

Decompiled, verbatim, general form:

    lVar5 = 0;
    puVar4 = *(undefined8 **)*param_1;
    do {
      do {
        while( true ) {
          do {
            puVar3 = puVar4;
            if (puVar3 == (undefined8 *)*param_1) {
              return lVar5;
            }
            if ((param_2 == '\0') || ((param_2 == '\x01') && (puVar3[4] != 0x100))) {
              lVar5 = lVar5 + ((longlong)(puVar3[6] - puVar3[5]) >> 3);
            }
            puVar4 = puVar3;
          } while (*(char *)((longlong)puVar3 + 0x19) != '\0');
          ...
        }
        ...
      } while( true );
    } while( true );

Specialised, the guard reduces from the decompiler's compound condition:

    (param_2 == '\0') || ((param_2 == '\x01') && (puVar3[4] != 0x100))
      ->  (1 == 0) || ((1 == 1) && (puVar3[4] != 0x100))
      ->  puVar3[4] != 0x100

and puVar3[4], puVar3[5], puVar3[6] are the qwords at node + 0x20, + 0x28 and
+ 0x30 respectively, which is exactly what the instructions CMP qword ptr
[RAX + 0x20], [RAX + 0x30] and [RAX + 0x28] access. The decompiler's ">> 3" is
faithful: the instruction is SAR RDX,0x3 at 0x14052b7ef, an arithmetic shift, so
each term is a signed division by 8 and a term is added to the running total in R9,
not merely overwritten.

--- Classification ---

  IS IT A POSITIVE CONSTANT?  No. No literal is ever returned. The only immediate
  value returned is the zero held in R9 on the empty-container path, and that is a
  zero, not a positive constant. Nothing in the function adds a fixed number.

  IS IT ZERO?                Not unconditionally. Three distinct situations give 0,
                              and none of them is a property of the function that
                              can be relied on by the caller:

                                0x14052b7c3  XOR R9D,R9D  plus
                                0x14052b7d0  JZ 0x14052b84b
                              the container holds nothing beyond its sentinel, so
                              the loop body never runs and RAX is set from R9 = 0.

                                every non-sentinel node fails the 0x100 test at
                                0x14052b7dd, so the ADD at 0x14052b7f3 never runs
                                and R9 stays 0.

                                a node passes the filter but its two pointers are
                                equal, so *(node+0x30) - *(node+0x28) is 0 and the
                                SAR contributes 0.

                              In every other case the sum is a positive quantity
                              built from document data.

  IS IT A VALUE TAKEN FROM THE ELEMENT?  Yes. This is the accurate classification.
                              Every contribution is read out of memory reached
                              through param_1. The tree is rooted at *param_1, loaded
                              by MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX] at 0x14052b7c0, and each
                              contributing term is two 64-bit loads from that node
                              at +0x28 and +0x30. Nothing is fabricated by the
                              function and nothing is hard-coded.

  So for the zone-0 count: FUN_14052b7c0 adds, per element, a count of pointers
  held inside that element's tree, excluding elements the tree tags with 0x100. The
  zone-0 count in PV_AffectIndResult is therefore gated on the contents of the
  document, and can legitimately be zero when the containers are empty.

--- Node layout, stated from the offsets the code itself uses ---

  +0x00  loaded at 0x14052b7ca, compared against the sentinel at 0x14052b7cd, and
         reloaded in the descent loops. Serves as the parent link.
  +0x08  loaded at 0x14052b820 and 0x14052b839. Serves as a child link.
  +0x10  loaded at 0x14052b7fc and 0x14052b830. Serves as the other child link.
  +0x19  a single byte tested for zero at 0x14052b7f6, 0x14052b800, 0x14052b80c,
         0x14052b818, 0x14052b824 and 0x14052b83d. The pattern of those tests, a
         zero flag on the sentinel plus a subtree-root test at 0x14052b830, is the
         standard sentinel-terminated balanced-tree traversal.
  +0x20  the tag compared against 0x100 at 0x14052b7dd.
  +0x28  the begin pointer, subbed at 0x14052b7eb.
  +0x30  the end pointer, loaded at 0x14052b7e7.

  A header at 0x18 bytes of links and a 0x19 flag with the payload starting at 0x20
  is the layout the MSVC _Rb_tree_node uses, so the walk is an in-order traversal of
  a red-black tree and +0x20, +0x28, +0x30 are fields of the stored element rather
  than of the tree header. Recorded as an observation about the offsets the code
  uses; the element's own type was not identified, and nothing was inferred about
  what 0x100 denotes.

--- Effect on the zone-0 count, restated against the caller ---

In PV_AffectIndResult the return value lands in RAX and is folded into the
accumulator at 0x14053167b:

    140531662  XOR ESI,ESI                  ; accumulator = 0
    140531676  CALL 0x14052b7c0
    14053167b  ADD RSI,RAX

once per element of the caller's vector at document + 0x2448, walked with a stride of
0x28 from 0x14053165b:

    14053165b  LEA R14,[RDI + 0x2448]
    14053167e  ADD RBX,0x28

and that accumulator is then added into the count sent to the resize:

    1405316a0  ADD RDX,RSI
    1405316a3  MOV RCX,R13
    1405316a6  CALL 0x140674570

So the contribution of FUN_14052b7c0 to the count is the total number of pointers
stored across all tree nodes reachable from each element, with nodes tagged 0x100
left out. Per instruction, nothing was entered beyond FUN_14052b7c0; the callers of
FUN_14052b7c0 were not examined and the callers of PV_AffectIndResult were not
re-examined. The callee FUN_14052b7c0 has no callees of its own, so this function
is a leaf and nothing was skipped by stopping here.

===== END =====
===== Count inputs before zone 0 =====

--- ANSWER: NO. There is no such store. In fact there is no store to any of the
    four displacements anywhere in FUN_14068f0f0, before the zone-0 call or after it. ---

  Per displacement, over the whole function body 0x14068f0f0 .. 0x14068f884:

    0x2448   2 references, both LOADS, both after 0x14068f5af
    0x2450   2 references, both LOADS, both after 0x14068f5af
    0x2478   0 references
    0x2480   0 references

  Stores whose displacement is 0x2448, 0x2450, 0x2478 or 0x2480
  occurring before the call at 0x14068f5af:  NONE.

  Before 0x14068f5af there is not a single reference of any kind, read or write,
  to any of those four fields. PrepareExecData passes to PV_AffectIndResult a
  document whose zone-0 count inputs are exactly as it received them.

--- Scope of the claim, stated up front ---

This is a statement about the instruction stream of FUN_14068f0f0 itself. A store
performed inside one of the callees that this function invokes would not appear in
this listing and would not be reported here. The defensible claim is therefore
"PrepareExecData does not itself write the zone-0 count inputs", not "nothing in
the PrepareExecData call tree writes them". Settling the wider question would
require leaving this function, which was out of scope by instruction.

--- The call being preceded, for reference ---

    14068f5a0  TEST R15D,R15D
    14068f5a3  JNZ 0x14068f5b9
    14068f5a5  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x5878]   ; the CProdCarte
    14068f5ac  MOV RCX,RBX                          ; this = the document
    14068f5af  CALL 0x1405315a0                    ; PV_AffectIndResult

RBX is the document, so the callee reads its count inputs from RBX-relative fields
that this function never writes.

--- Method, three independent checks ---

The body is 417 instructions and the listing is contiguous from 0x14068f0f0 to
0x14068f884 with no gap larger than 16 bytes, so the enumeration below is complete
for this function. It was not taken on trust from a single pass.

  CHECK 1, text scan. Every one of the 417 rendered instructions was tested for the
  substrings 0x2448, 0x2450, 0x2478, 0x2480, and then more loosely for 0x24 in any
  position so that a differently rendered operand could not slip through. The loose
  scan returned exactly four instructions, the same four the specific scan found,
  and no instruction mentioning 0x24 other than those.

  CHECK 2, program-wide instruction search. Each displacement was searched across
  the whole program and the results filtered to the function range. This is
  independent of the function listing and returned the same four instructions:

    0x2448   118 program-wide hits, of which in this function:
               14068f755  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]
               14068f7eb  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]
    0x2450    59 program-wide hits, of which in this function:
               14068f74e  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
               14068f7e4  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
    0x2478     8 program-wide hits, none in this function
    0x2480    10 program-wide hits, none in this function

  CHECK 3, structural store enumeration. Rather than classifying stores by their text,
  the listing's mnemonic field was used with an explicit rule: an instruction is a
  store when memory is its first operand, excluding LEA, CMP, TEST, BT, the Jcc and
  CALL and JMP forms, the MOVSX/MOVZX and CMOV extends, NOP and the PREFETCH and CVT
  families, and treating MOVSXD as a load-extend rather than a string move. This
  found 28 stores in the function, of which only 2 are document-relative. Those two
  are listed below.

  The four target references are all classified as loads under that same rule, and
  each can also be read by eye: in MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450] the register is
  the destination, and in SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448] the SUB takes a register
  destination and a memory source, so memory is read.

--- The stores PrepareExecData does perform on the document ---

Both precede 0x14068f5af. Neither is one of the four fields.

    14068f383  CMP byte ptr [RBX + 0x1a08],0x1
    14068f3f8  MOV byte ptr [RBX + 0x1a08],0x0      ; document+0x1a08, 1 byte, value 0
    ...
    14068f56c  MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x5c98],0x0     ; document+0x5c98, 8 bytes, value 0

So the function is not read-only with respect to the document. It clears a byte at
+0x1a08 and a qword at +0x5c98 and touches nothing else. The absence of a store to
+0x2448, +0x2450, +0x2478 and +0x2480 is therefore a real absence, not an artefact
of scanning a function that never writes anything.

For completeness, every document-relative memory operand in the function, all 34 of
them, grouped. Loads and address-takes:

    0x3924   read at 14068f144, 14068f364, 14068f3ec, 14068f411, 14068f511, 14068f77c
    0x180    LEA at 14068f1a1, 14068f1c3, 14068f230
    0x11f8   LEA at 14068f28f

Note that +0x2478 and +0x2480 appear nowhere in this list at all, and +0x2448 and

No LEA targets any of the four either, so none of them is even passed by address to

14068f230, together with +0x11f8, +0x1a10, +0x188, +0x23e0 and +0x5888.

--- What the two late reads of +0x2448 and +0x2450 do ---

They are the only contact this function has with the zone-0 count inputs, and both
sit after the resize, so neither feeds it. Each computes the element count of the
vector whose begin/end pair is at document + 0x2448 and + 0x2450.

    14068f74e  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
    14068f755  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]
    14068f75c  MOV RSI,0x6666666666666667
    14068f766  MOV RAX,RSI
    14068f769  IMUL RCX
    14068f76c  SAR RDX,0x4
    14068f770  MOV RAX,RDX
    14068f773  SHR RAX,0x3f
    14068f777  ADD RDX,RAX
    14068f77a  JZ 0x14068f7dc

    14068f7e4  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
    14068f7eb  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]
    14068f7f2  MOV RAX,RSI
    14068f7f5  IMUL RCX
    14068f7f8  SAR RDX,0x4
    14068f7fc  MOV RAX,RDX
    14068f7ff  SHR RAX,0x3f
    14068f803  ADD RDX,RAX
    14068f806  JZ 0x14068f814

DIVISOR 0x28 = 40, verified arithmetically rather than assumed:

    ceil(2^68 / 40) = 7378697629483820647 = 0x6666666666666667   -> matches
    ceil(2^68 / 10) = 0x1999999999999999A                         -> does not match

0x28 is the same element stride that PV_AffectIndResult walks when it sums
FUN_14052b7c0 over this vector, 14053167e ADD RBX,0x28. So the expression is the
number of elements the callee is about to have walked, read here after the fact.

Each result gates a different action, and both gates test the same count for zero:

    14068f77a  JZ 0x14068f7dc
      when the count is non-zero, the block 0x14068f77c .. 0x14068f7d2 runs, which
      starts MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBX + 0x3924] and CALL 0x14077f7f6 and then builds
      a string via LEA R9,[0x1410d50f0] at 0x14068f78c.

    14068f806  JZ 0x14068f814
      when the count is non-zero, the block 0x14068f808 .. 0x14068f80e runs, which is
      MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX] followed by CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x280], a virtual
      call through the document vtable at slot +0x280.

Ordering, so the sequence is unambiguous. The zone-0 resize is at 0x14068f5af. The
+0x5888 resize is at 0x14068f741, reached only after PV_PostInitVecteur at
0x14068f72a and NbTest_NeedAnomalie at 0x14068f732. The first read of
+0x2448/+0x2450 is at 0x14068f74e, and the second at 0x14068f7e4. So both read the
zone-0 count inputs strictly after both resizes, never before.

--- Summary ---

  Stores with displacement 0x2448, 0x2450, 0x2478 or 0x2480 in FUN_14068f0f0
  before the call to PV_AffectIndResult at 0x14068f5af:   NONE.

  For the record, stores with those same displacements anywhere in the function:
  NONE. The two fields are read twice each, after the call, and two fields are
  never referenced at all.

  Therefore PrepareExecData does not fill the zone-0 count inputs before resizing
  zone 0. It resizes zone 0 from whatever the document already holds, and it only
  inspects the +0x2448 vector's element count afterwards, to decide whether to run
  a logging block and a vtable +0x280 call.

  Per instruction, analysis stopped inside FUN_14068f0f0. PV_AffectIndResult,
  FUN_14052b7c0, FUN_140674570, PV_PostInitVecteur, the callee at 0x14077f7f6 and
  the vtable target at +0x280 were not entered, and no caller of PrepareExecData was
  examined. Per the scope note above, stores inside those callees are not covered by
  this answer.

===== Document +0x2478 writers =====

--- ANSWER, TWO PARTS ---

  1. No instruction in the program writes displacement 0x2478. All 8 instructions
     carrying that displacement are reads or address computations. None of the 6
     functions containing them stores to it.

  2. The OTHER half of the pair is written, just not with a literal 0x2478
     displacement. document+0x2480, the end pointer, is advanced by PV_EnvoiMacros
     at 0x1405341eb, ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8, where RBX was loaded by the
     listed LEA at 0x14053416f. That is an inlined push_back and it is the writer
     that grows the first term of the zone-0 count.

  Field identity, established from the list below: document+0x2478 is a
  std::vector<CMacro*>, laid out {begin +0x0, end +0x8, capacity +0x10}, so
  0x2478 / 0x2480 / 0x2488. Term A of the zone-0 count,
  (*(doc+0x2480) - *(doc+0x2478)) >> 3, is exactly that vector's element count.

--- Per-instruction determination of whether memory is written ---

  1  0x14045c631  LEA RDX,[RCX + 0x2478]
     LEA performs no memory access at all; it only forms an address. NOT a write.
     The formed address is then used as the SOURCE of a copy:

        14045c620  PUSH RBX
        14045c622  SUB RSP,0x30
        14045c626  MOV RBX,RDX
        14045c629  MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x20],0x0
        14045c631  LEA RDX,[RCX + 0x2478]     ; RDX = &this->the vector
        14045c638  MOV RCX,RBX                ; RCX = caller-supplied destination
        14045c63b  CALL 0x140452a30           ; copy vector -> destination
        14045c640  MOV RAX,RBX
        14045c643  ADD RSP,0x30
        14045c647  POP RBX
        14045c648  RET

     This is the whole function, 11 instructions. The signature returns
     vector<CMacro*> and RDX carries the destination, so this is a by-value copy of
     the member vector out to the caller. Reading, and copying out. NOT a write to
     the field. This is the instruction that establishes the field's type as
     std::vector<CMacro*>.

  2  0x14052ead8  MOV RBX,qword ptr [RBP + 0x2478]
     Register is the destination, memory is the source. NOT a write.
     Worth flagging because RBP here is not a frame pointer. The prologue is

        14052e910  MOV RAX,RSP
        14052e913  PUSH RDI
        14052e914  PUSH R12

     so RBP is this, the CDataCaoTraitement, and [RBP + 0x2478] is the document
     field and not a stack slot. The site is a begin/end emptiness test:

     SUB with a register destination and a memory source reads memory. NOT a write.

     other offsets look document-like, since 0x140697605 does MOV RSI,RCX and

     CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0xe0] on the vtable. Whether [RBP + 0x67] holds that same
     object was not established. The not-a-write classification holds either way,
     since it does not depend on the base register.

--- The writer the displacement search does not show ---

  document+0x2480, the end pointer of the pair, is written by PV_EnvoiMacros. It is
  reached through the register that the listed LEA at 0x14053416f established, so
  no instruction carries the literal displacement 0x2478 on the writing side.

    14053416f  LEA RBX,[RSI + 0x2478]        ; RBX = &this->vector
    140534176  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]  ; end
    140534179  LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x48]
    14053417f  CMP RCX,RAX
    140534182  JNC 0x1405341cc
    ...
    1405341cc  CMP RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x10] ; end == capacity ?
    1405341d0  JNZ 0x1405341df
    1405341d2  MOV EDX,0x1
    1405341d7  MOV RCX,RBX
    1405341da  CALL 0x140543910               ; grow the vector
    1405341df  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]  ; new end
    1405341e3  TEST RAX,RAX
    1405341e6  JZ 0x1405341eb
    1405341e8  MOV qword ptr [RAX],R14        ; *end = the new CMacro*
    1405341eb  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8  ; end += 8  -> writes document+0x2480

  The second operand of [RBX + 0x10] is 0x2488, the capacity slot, which fits the
  std::vector<CMacro*> layout {begin 0x2478, end 0x2480, capacity 0x2488} and
  corroborates the type read off GetZoneAnalyse_Macro. The block from 0x1405341cc
  to 0x1405341eb is the standard MSVC inlined push_back: compare end against
  capacity, call the grow helper if equal, store the value, advance end by the 8-byte
  element size.

  Effect on the zone-0 count. Term A is
  (*(doc+0x2480) - *(doc+0x2478)) >> 3. Each push_back here advances document+0x2480
  by 8, so it raises Term A by exactly 1, provided the begin pointer is not moved.
  Nothing in the whole program moves the begin pointer, so Term A is a monotonically
  increasing count of CMacro pointers appended by PV_EnvoiMacros.

  One correction worth recording. A scan of the whole of PV_EnvoiMacros for stores
  through the LEA-loaded RBX also returns

        14053427e  INC dword ptr [RBX + 0x28]

  but that is NOT a write to document+0x24a0. RBX has been reloaded from an
  unrelated stack slot by then,

        14053427a  MOV RBX,qword ptr [RBP + -0x78]
        14053427e  INC dword ptr [RBX + 0x28]

  so that instruction targets a different object. Only 0x1405341eb is a write
  through the vector pointer.

--- Method, and why the negative result is trustworthy ---

  The program-wide instruction search for 0x2478 returns exactly 8 hits, and a
  second run at a higher limit returns the same 8, so the list is not truncated.
  Each was classified by reading its operand direction directly, and the two LEAs
  were additionally traced to their use.

  A store with some other displacement could still overlap the 8 bytes at
  document+0x2478 if it were wider or unaligned, so two sweeps were run:

    0x2468 .. 0x2488 step 8      0 hits, 0 stores
    0x2469 .. 0x2487 step 1      22 hits, 0 stores

  Every hit was required to contain the displacement as a whole operand and not as a
  substring of a longer literal. So no store of any width, aligned or not, anywhere
  in the program touches document+0x2478 or document+0x247f.

  The begin pointer at document+0x2478 is therefore never written by any direct
  field access in the program. It is only read, or copied out by GetZoneAnalyse_
  Macro. A pointer that is never stored cannot come from anywhere except
  construction-time initialisation or a bulk copy that the two sweeps above would
  not have caught, for example a whole-object memcpy or a rep stos fill. Nothing of
  that kind was found for this field, but excluding every possible bulk mechanism
  would need a whole-object data-flow pass and was out of scope by instruction. The
  statement this section supports is: no store to document+0x2478 exists as a direct
  displacement or as a register-borne write, and the growth of the pair is performed
  by PV_EnvoiMacros.

  8 instructions program-wide carry displacement 0x2478, in 6 functions:
  GetZoneAnalyse_Macro, MajTestVectorForSkip, PV_AffectIndResult (3 of them),
  PV_EnvoiMacros, PV_PostInitVecteur, FUN_1406975e0.

  Writes to the memory operand: ZERO. Six of the eight are loads, two are LEAs.

  Logging: three functions build a "CDataCaoTraitement" tag, PV_AffectIndResult,
  PV_EnvoiMacros and PV_PostInitVecteur. PV_PostInitVecteur tags itself with the
  string "PV_AffectIndResult". No function in the list logs "CProductionDoc".

  The writer of the zone-0 count's first term is PV_EnvoiMacros, at 0x1405341eb,
  an inlined push_back that stores the new CMacro pointer at 0x1405341e8 and
  advances the end pointer at document+0x2480 by 8, adding 1 to the count each time.

  Per instruction, analysis stopped at this list. The grow helper 0x140543910, the
  copy routine 0x140452a30 and the callees of PV_AffectIndResult, PV_EnvoiMacros
  and PV_PostInitVecteur were not entered, and no caller of any of the six was
  examined.

===== Vector grow begin pointer =====

--- ANSWER: NO. FUN_140543910 contains no store to the vector's first qword, and in
    fact no store of any kind. It performs three loads and no writes, then tail
    jumps to FUN_1405430d0, which is where any begin-pointer update must occur. ---

  There is no store to quote. Nothing in this function writes offset 0 of the
  vector, and nothing writes any other memory either. Consequently there is also
  no stored value here to classify as a newly allocated buffer; that question
  belongs to the tail-callee, which was out of scope.

  What this function actually is: a capacity check plus a growth-policy
  computation. It is the standard MSVC vector reserve/reallocate wrapper, and its
  entire job is to decide the new capacity in elements and hand it to the real
  reallocator.

--- Function identity ---

FUN_140543910, body 0x140543910 .. 0x140543991, 37 instructions, no symbol.

search_resolve and function_at both return only the default label, so there is no
PDB name for it. Signature:

    void FUN_140543910(longlong *param_1,ulonglong param_2);

  param_1  the vector, i.e. RCX at the call, which is document+0x2478
  param_2  the additional element count requested, i.e. RDX, the literal 1

  The call site in PV_EnvoiMacros, from the Document +0x2478 writers section:

    1405341d2  MOV EDX,0x1
    1405341d7  MOV RCX,RBX
    1405341da  CALL 0x140543910

--- Complete listing, in order ---

    140543910  SUB RSP,0x28
    140543914  MOV R10,qword ptr [RCX + 0x10]     ; LOAD capacity pointer
    140543918  MOV R9,RCX                         ; stash the vector pointer

--- Stores to the vector's first qword: none, established exhaustively ---

  Every instruction in the body that carries a memory operand at all is these four:

    140543914  MOV  |  MOV R10,qword ptr [RCX + 0x10]
    14054391b  MOV  |  MOV R8,qword ptr [RCX + 0x8]
    14054392e  MOV  |  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX]
    140543954  CALL |  CALL qword ptr [0x140d55230]

  The first three are loads, and in each the register is the destination and the
  memory is the source, so none of them writes. The fourth is not a data access at
  all; it is the read of an import thunk slot to obtain the call target of
  std::_Xlength_error, on the throw path only.

  That is the whole set. The 33 remaining instructions write registers or adjust
  RSP only:

      SUB RSP,0x28 and ADD RSP,0x28     move the stack pointer, not data
      MOV R9,RCX / MOV RCX,R9          register to register
      MOV R11,0x1fffffffffffffff       immediate to register
      XOR ECX,ECX                      immediate to register
      MOV RAX,R10 / SUB / SAR / SHR / ADD / CMP
      CMOVNC RCX,RAX / CMOVNC RDX,RCX  conditional moves, registers only
      LEA RCX,[0x140dd8880]            address arithmetic, no memory touched
      JNC / JMP / RET                  control transfer

  So: the offset-0 store the question asks for does not exist in this function,
  and neither does any other store. FUN_140543910 is a pure computation wrapper.

--- The structural reason: a tail call, not a call ---

    140543981  MOV RCX,R9          ; RCX = the vector pointer
    140543984  ADD RSP,0x28        ; frame released
    140543988  JMP 0x1405430d0     ; tail jump

  The JMP rather than a CALL is the decisive detail. The stack frame is torn down
  at 0x140543984 and control leaves by a direct jump, so FUN_1405430d0 receives
  RCX = the vector and RDX = the new capacity in elements, with this function's
  frame already gone. Any allocation and any begin, end or capacity store must
  therefore be inside FUN_1405430d0.

  FUN_1405430d0 is a distinct function, body 0x1405430d0 .. 0x14054315d, also with
  no symbol. Named here only to identify where the tail call goes. Per the
  instruction to stop in this function it was not entered, so no claim is made
  about what it stores or whether the value it puts at offset 0 is a freshly
  allocated buffer.

--- Decompiled, verbatim ---

    void FUN_140543910(longlong *param_1,ulonglong param_2)
    {
      code *pcVar1;
      ulonglong uVar2;
      longlong lVar3;
      ulonglong uVar4;

      if (param_2 <= (ulonglong)(param_1[2] - param_1[1] >> 3)) {
        return;
      }
      lVar3 = param_1[1] - *param_1 >> 3;
      if (0x1fffffffffffffffU - lVar3 < param_2) {
        std::_Xlength_error("vector<T> too long");
        pcVar1 = (code *)swi(3);
        (*pcVar1)();
        return;
      }
      param_2 = param_2 + lVar3;
      uVar4 = param_1[2] - *param_1 >> 3;
      uVar2 = 0;
      if (uVar4 <= 0x1fffffffffffffff - (uVar4 >> 1)) {
        uVar2 = (uVar4 >> 1) + uVar4;
      }
      if (param_2 <= uVar2) {
        param_2 = uVar2;
      }
      FUN_1405430d0(param_1,param_2);
      return;
    }

  The decompilation agrees: param_1 is only ever read, at param_1[0], param_1[1]
  and param_1[2]. The single write-shaped statement is the final call, whose
  result is discarded and which takes param_1 as an argument rather than an
  assignment target. Note the decompiler renders the tail call as an ordinary
  call and adds a bare return after it, which is why the listing was checked
  directly; the listing shows the real JMP at 0x140543988.

  The three vector slots it reads match the layout established in the
  Document +0x2478 writers section:

    param_1[0]  begin      document+0x2478
    param_1[1]  end        document+0x2480
    param_1[2]  capacity   document+0x2488

--- What the function does decide, since that is its whole content ---

  The growth policy, which is the substantive output here:

    if ( (capacity - end)/8 >= param_2 )  return;          no room needed, do nothing
    if ( 0x1fffffffffffffff - size < param_2 )  throw std::_Xlength_error(
                                                      "vector<T> too long" );
    required  = param_2 + size
    candidate = size_or_capacity * 3 / 2
    new_cap   = max(required, candidate)

  With param_2 = 1, the first test reduces to a comparison of capacity against end,
  so the function is reached exactly when the vector is full, end == capacity. That
  matches the guard in the caller, which only calls it when end equals capacity:

    1405341cc  CMP RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x10]   ; end vs capacity at 0x2488
    1405341d0  JNZ 0x1405341df                  ; skip the grow if not full

  Growth is therefore 1.5x the old capacity, floored by required. For a full vector
  where size == capacity, and with param_2 = 1, the sequence is cap 1 to 2, cap 2 to
  3, cap 3 to 4, cap 4 to 6, and generally 1.5x thereafter once 1.5x overtakes
  cap+1.

  The throw path is the only place this function calls anything:

        14054394d  LEA RCX,[0x140dd8880]          ; 0x140dd8880 = "vector<T> too long"
        140543954  CALL qword ptr [0x140d55230]   ; std::_Xlength_error
        14054395a  INT3

  Confirmed as a defined string in the binary, label s_vector<T>_too_long_140dd8880,
  value "vector<T> too long", length 19. The INT3 immediately after the call is the
  unreachable trap that follows a noreturn throw. It is a control-flow marker, not a
  store.

  This function has no log string of its own; it does not construct a
  CLogManagerFunction and references no CProductionDoc or CDataCao string.

--- Bearing on the earlier finding ---

  The Document +0x2478 writers section concluded that no store to document+0x2478
  exists as a direct displacement or as a register-borne write. This result does not
  contradict that and does not close it either. The one function on that list which
  could have been a hidden writer, the grow helper reached from PV_EnvoiMacros, turns
  out to be a store-free wrapper. The actual writer of the begin pointer, if it
  exists at all, is inside FUN_1405430d0, which this answer did not enter.

  So the position is unchanged and now better localised: the begin pointer at
  document+0x2478 is not written by FUN_140543910, and the reallocation path that
  would rewrite it terminates in a tail call to FUN_1405430d0 at 0x1405430d0. That
  function is the next place to look, and doing so would leave the function this
  answer was scoped to.

--- Summary ---

===== Vector reallocate begin pointer =====

--- ANSWER: YES. One store to offset 0, at 0x14054314d, and the value stored is
    exactly the pointer returned by the allocation call. ---

  Store to the vector's first qword:

        14054314d  MOV qword ptr [RBX],RSI

  RBX is the vector, i.e. document+0x2478, so this writes document+0x2478. RSI holds
  the return value in RAX of the call at 0x1405430f6, captured at 0x1405430fb and
  never modified afterwards. So yes, the stored value is the pointer returned by that
  call, which is the new buffer.

  The displacement written is 0, not 0x2478. That is precisely why a
  program-wide search for displacement 0x2478 did not find it: RBX already holds
  document+0x2478, so the store encodes no document offset at all.

--- Function identity ---

FUN_1405430d0, body 0x1405430d0 .. 0x14054315d, 41 instructions, no symbol.

function_at and search_resolve both return only the default label, so there is no
PDB name. Signature as reconstructed:

    void FUN_1405430d0(longlong *param_1,longlong param_2,undefined8 param_3,undefined8 param_4);

Arriving from the tail jump in FUN_140543910, RCX = the vector and RDX = the new
capacity in elements. param_3 and param_4 are the Windows x64 shadow-space slots
for the two register arguments, not real parameters. Ghidra's four-parameter
signature is therefore a calling-convention artefact; the function uses two.

  RBX  = the vector, set at 0x1405430f3 from RCX on entry
  R14  = the new capacity in elements, set at 0x1405430f0 from RDX on entry
  RSI  = the new buffer, set at 0x1405430fb from the allocation's RAX

The prologue saves RSI, RDI and R14, and the epilogue restores them, so the function
treats all three as callee-saved, which they are in the Windows x64 ABI. That is
what makes RSI provably intact across the two intervening calls.

--- Complete listing, in order ---

    1405430d0  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x10],RDX      ; shadow slot for arg 2
    1405430d5  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RCX       ; shadow slot for arg 1

    1405430db  PUSH RDI

    140543150  MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x68]       ; restore the incoming RBX

--- The three stores to the vector, in order ---

  Exactly three instructions write through RBX, and they run back to back after the
  copy and the release:

    140543141  MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x10],RAX    ; capacity  -> document+0x2488
    140543149  MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],RAX     ; end       -> document+0x2480
    14054314d  MOV qword ptr [RBX],RSI           ; begin     -> document+0x2478

  Offset 0 is written once, by the last of the three. There is no second store to
  offset 0 and no other path in this function that touches it.

--- Is the stored value the pointer returned by the allocation: yes ---

  Proven by register tracking, not by reading the callee:

    1405430f6  CALL 0x1405aef30      ; returns the buffer in RAX
    1405430fb  MOV RSI,RAX           ; RSI = that pointer, the only write to RSI
    ...
    14054313d  LEA RAX,[RSI + R14*0x8]   ; RSI read
    140543145  LEA RAX,[RSI + RDI*0x8]   ; RSI read
    14054314d  MOV qword ptr [RBX],RSI   ; RSI stored

  Between 0x1405430fb and 0x14054314d, RSI is written zero times. It is read at
  0x14054313d and 0x140543145 and nowhere else. The two intervening calls, memmove
  at 0x140543110 and the release at 0x140543138, cannot disturb it because RSI is
  callee-saved in the Windows x64 ABI, and because this function itself pushes and
  pops it. The stored value is therefore bit-for-bit the RAX that the call at
  0x1405430f6 produced. Nothing is added, offset, or masked.

  The in-function evidence that the call is an allocation, without entering it:

    the returned pointer is used as the destination of the memmove, so it must be a
    writable buffer at least as large as the old live bytes;
    the old buffer is passed to FUN_140579780 immediately afterwards, and that call
    is skipped when the old begin is null, which is the release half of the same
    operation.

  Allocate, copy, release, then publish the three new slots. That is the standard
  vector reallocation sequence.

  Honest limit on this point. FUN_1405aef30 has no symbol and body
  0x1405aef30..0x1405aefae. Its signature could not be resolved, and it was not
  entered, per the instruction to stop in this function. So the claim established
  here is that document+0x2478 receives exactly the pointer that call returned and
  that this function treats that pointer as a fresh writable buffer. The claim that
  the call reaches a heap allocator is an inference from that usage, not something
  read out of the callee.

  What the call receives, stated precisely from the instruction level. RCX and RDX
  are not set between entry and 0x1405430f6, so the call passes RCX = the vector
  pointer and RDX = the new capacity in elements, both as they arrived. The
  decompiler renders the call with no arguments at all, FUN_1405aef30(), which is
  wrong in the sense that two registers are live; the listing is what the statement
  above rests on. How the callee turns a capacity in elements into a byte count was
  not determined.

--- Decompiled, verbatim ---

    void FUN_1405430d0(longlong *param_1,longlong param_2,undefined8 param_3,undefined8 param_4)
    {
      longlong lVar1;
      longlong lVar2;
      void *_Dst;
      undefined8 uVar3;

      uVar3 = 0xfffffffffffffffe;
      _Dst = (void *)FUN_1405aef30();
      memmove(_Dst,(void *)*param_1,param_1[1] - *param_1);
      lVar1 = *param_1;
      lVar2 = param_1[1];
      if (lVar1 != 0) {
        FUN_140579780(param_1,lVar1,param_1[2] - lVar1 >> 3,param_4,uVar3);
      }
      param_1[2] = (longlong)((longlong)_Dst + param_2 * 8);
      param_1[1] = (longlong)((longlong)_Dst + (lVar2 - lVar1 >> 3) * 8);
      *param_1 = (longlong)_Dst;
      return;
    }

  The last statement, *param_1 = (longlong)_Dst, is the store to offset 0. The
  decompiler reuses _Dst for both the allocation result and the memmove return,
  which is harmless here because memmove returns its destination, but the listing
  makes clear the value was fixed at 0x1405430fb before the copy and came from the
  call, not from memmove.

  Note the two things this rendering gets wrong or hides, both corrected above from
  the listing: the allocation call is shown as taking no arguments, and the function
  is shown as using four parameters when only two are real, the other two being
  shadow space.

--- Effect on the zone-0 count ---

  The element count survives reallocation. The copy length is the old live byte
  range, old_end - old_begin, and the new end is placed at new_buffer + old_size*8
  where old_size is (old_end - old_begin) >> 3, computed at 0x14054311e to 0x140543121
  before the old pointers are overwritten. So the value

      (*(doc+0x2480) - *(doc+0x2478)) >> 3

  which is Term A of the zone-0 count, is identical before and after the call.
  Only the capacity, and the address the two pointers point at, change. Reallocation
  on this vector therefore never alters the count that PV_AffectIndResult computes.

  Ordering within the function is also correct in the one respect worth recording:
  the memmove at 0x140543110 happens before the release at 0x140543138, and the
  three stores to the vector happen after both. The old buffer is read only before
  it is released, and the three new slots are published only once the data has been
  moved.

  If the old begin was null, the release is skipped by the JZ at 0x140543128 and the
  three stores still run, so a null vector is initialised to the new buffer with a
  new end and capacity derived from an old size of zero.

--- Correction to the earlier conclusion ---

  The Document +0x2478 writers section concluded that no store to document+0x2478
  existed as a direct displacement or as a register-borne write, and the Vector grow
  begin pointer section narrowed the search to FUN_1405430d0 without entering it.
  That is now resolved, and the answer is that a writer does exist:

    FUN_1405430d0 at 0x14054314d, MOV qword ptr [RBX],RSI.

  It was not reachable by the earlier searches for the right reason, not because the
  conclusion was drawn too narrowly. The store encodes displacement 0 from a
  register that already holds document+0x2478, so no program-wide search on the
  literal 0x2478 can see it, and the neighbouring-displacement sweeps over
  0x2468 to 0x2488 could not see it either.

  So the refined position is that the begin pointer at document+0x2478 is written
  exactly on the reallocation path, by FUN_1405430d0, and on no other path found so
  far. It is set to the buffer returned by FUN_1405aef30. Every other write to the
  vector found in this session, namely the push_back in PV_EnvoiMacros at
  0x1405341e8 and 0x1405341eb, moves only the end pointer and the contents, and
  never the begin pointer.

  This also means the sweep performed in the Document +0x2478 writers section was
  sound as far as it went and simply could not have covered this case. The lesson
  for the method is that a displacement search is necessary but not sufficient, and
  that following a register-borne address to its uses is what closed the gap here.

  The IEAAX prefix is public virtual, and the K@Z suffix is one unsigned long. So the

--- The condition under which the call happens ---

  The immediate guard is TEST EDI,EDI / JNZ at 0x14053c200, that is param_2 == 0.
  EDI was loaded from the param_2 spill at 0x14053c18d,

        14053c18d  MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBP + 0x14a0]

  and is not reloaded after, so the compiler is relying on the three intervening
  calls to preserve it. The decompiler expresses the same condition as
  if (param_2 == 0).

  Reaching that guard at all requires passing four earlier gates. From the
  decompiled body, with names verified against the symbol table:

    1. algo::IAlgorithm::SetProgramName and SetLibraryName run first, from
       CDataCao::GetFilePath(this + 0x180) and CTest::GetCompleteLibName(this + 0x188).

    2. iVar2 = CDataCaoTraitement::PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults(this,&a,&b)
       at 0x1405343b0 must return non-zero, or param_6 must be true. Otherwise the
       function takes the failure path:

            14053c102  OR R8D,0xffffffff
            14053c106  LEA EDX,[RAX + 0x10]
            14053c109  MOV ECX,0xc40
            14053c10e  CALL 0x14077f784        ; MFC140.DLL::AfxMessageBox

       and returns without reaching the append.

    3. param_6 must be FALSE. If param_6 is true the function returns early with
       just the emptiness test on the 0x2448 vector and never calls PV_EnvoiMacros:

            14053c15b  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
            14053c162  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]
            14053c169  MOV RAX,0x6666666666666667
            14053c173  IMUL RCX
            14053c176  SAR RDX,0x4
            ...  SETNZ DIL
            14053c188  JMP 0x14053c214

       0x6666666666666667 with a shift of 4 is the division by 0x28, so this is
       exactly the (end - begin) / 0x28 element count of the 0x2448 vector.

    4. PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants(this,&a,&b,param_1,param_2,param_3) at 0x140532d30
       must not return -1; its result is stored at document+0xee4 and compared:

            14053c1c1  CALL 0x140532d30
            14053c1c6  MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4],EAX
            14053c1cc  CMP EAX,-0x1
            14053c1cf  JNZ 0x14053c1d5
            14053c1d1  OR EDI,EAX
            14053c1d3  JMP 0x14053c214

    5. PV_Prepare3dData(this,param_3,param_1,param_5,param_4,param_8) at 0x140534a80
       runs, and only then is param_2 == 0 tested.

  So the full condition is:

      PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults != 0  OR  param_6
      AND NOT param_6
      AND PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants != -1
      AND param_2 == 0

  The value returned by PrepareVecteur on the path that makes the call is
  *(int *)(this + 0xee4), reloaded at 0x14053c20e after the call, so the call's
  return value is discarded.

--- The table at 0x141028954, and an honest caveat on "every caller" ---

  The entry is 4 bytes, not 8. The 8-byte reinterpretations of this table are not
  valid pointers, so it is not a vtable and it cannot itself be an indirect call
  target. Its entries are 4-byte image-base-relative offsets, and they line up
  exactly, one for one and in order, with the exported ordinals of this interface.

  Verified slot by slot, slot address = 0x141028624 + 4 * ordinal:

    ordinal 199  slot 0x141028940  -> 1405315a0  PV_AffectIndResult
    ordinal 200  slot 0x141028944  -> 140532090  PV_CheckElementsWithNoCardNumber
    ordinal 201  slot 0x141028948  -> 140532220  PV_CheckElmtsPotentiellementExecutable
    ordinal 202  slot 0x14102894c  -> 140532b00  PV_EnvoiDesSkips
    ordinal 203  slot 0x141028950  -> 140532d30  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants
    ordinal 204  slot 0x141028954  -> 140533c90  PV_EnvoiMacros
    ordinal 205  slot 0x141028958  -> 1405343b0  PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults
    ordinal 206  slot 0x14102895c  -> 140534460  PV_PeutOnEnvoierCetOcvReader
    ordinal 207  slot 0x141028960  -> 1405347b0  PV_PostInitVecteur
    ordinal 208  slot 0x141028964  -> 140534a80  PV_Prepare3dData
    ordinal 209  slot 0x141028968  -> 140536c50  PV_Prepare3dData_AddCompo2D
    ordinal 210  slot 0x14102896c  -> 140536e50  PV_Prepare3dData_AddCompo3DToAcquire
    ordinal 211  slot 0x141028970  -> 1405373e0  PV_Prepare3dData_CompleteMap
    ordinal 212  slot 0x141028974  -> 1405374e0  PV_Prepare3dData_ConvertResult

  Thirteen consecutive ordinals, thirteen consecutive slots, no gaps and no
  mismatches. This is an ordinal-to-address dispatch table for the interface
  CDataCaoTraitement exports, living in .data.

  Two consequences, and the second is a real limit on the answer.

  First, no code in this binary reads the table. reference_to on the table base and
  on the ordinal-202 slot both return count 0, and search_instructions for
  "0x1410288" returns count 0. So nothing inside Vision3D.exe dispatches through
  it. It exists for a consumer outside the module.

  Second, and stated plainly because it bounds the "every direct code caller"
  result: because the table gives an outside caller a valid address for
  PV_EnvoiMacros by way of Ordinal_204, a caller in another module could reach
  this append without any call instruction existing in this binary. The claim
  proven above is that inside Vision3D.exe there is exactly one direct code caller
  and no indirect one. Whether any external host invokes ordinal 204, and whether
  such a host is what the question calls the panel-load path, cannot be settled
  from this binary and was not attempted.

--- Bearing on the question's premise ---

  The premise of the question, that a panel-load path calls the function that
  appends to this vector, is only half supported by what can be seen here.

  Supported: the append is not done by PV_AffectIndResult and not by any function
  named in the question. It is done by PrepareVecteur, a CDataCaoTraitement method
  that prepares document vectors, and it runs only when param_2 == 0 after the
  full gate above. PrepareVecteur is not one of the three candidates the question
  named.

  The two load-path functions already identified in the
  ReloadDoc caller's caller section, FUN_140692af0 and FUN_14069e2d0, are
  CProductionDoc and CProductionThread members. Whether FUN_140692af0 reaches
  PrepareVecteur is one caller level above the level this answer was scoped to and
  was not walked. So the honest answer to the question as posed is: at one caller
  level, no, the panel-load candidates do not call the append; the append is
  reached only through PrepareVecteur, and the reachability of PrepareVecteur from
  the load path is untested.

  What does hold at this depth, and is worth recording, is that PrepareVecteur and
  PV_AffectIndResult operate on the same object. PrepareVecteur's own this-relative
  accesses are 0x0, 0x180, 0x188, 0xee4, 0x1a08, 0x1a10, 0x1a18, 0x1a20, 0x1a30,
  0x1ac8, 0x2430, 0x2448, 0x2450. PV_AffectIndResult indexes 0x2448, 0x2450,
  0x2478, 0x2480, 0x5878 on the pointer it is given, and PV_EnvoiMacros indexes
  [this + 0], [this + 8], [this + 0x10] and is passed that same PrepareVecteur
  this. So the object PrepareVecteur passes as PV_EnvoiMacros's this is the address
  of the macro vector, document+0x2478, and the object is the same document that
  PrepareExecData hands to PV_AffectIndResult. The append and the zone-0 count read
  the same document, through functions reached by different routes.

  Also newly established here, and it corrects a detail recorded earlier: the
  mangled name of PV_AffectIndResult is

        ?PV_AffectIndResult@CDataCaoTraitement@@QEAAXPEAVCProdCarte@@@Z

  so it is public non-virtual, not virtual, and it takes a single CProdCarte* in
  addition to this. It is Ordinal_199. This independently corroborates the
  PrepareExecData counts section, which found the zone-0 call site passes no count
  argument and a pointer taken from document+0x5878; the pointer type is
  CProdCarte*.

  Two points of interest for the count chain.

===== PrepareExecData PrepareVecteur call =====

--- ANSWER, three parts ---

  1. param_2 is 0. It is set by XOR R8D,R8D immediately before the call.

  2. The argument PrepareVecteur tests before calling PV_EnvoiMacros is that same
     param_2, the third parameter, the int in R8. The test is TEST EDI,EDI / JNZ
     inside PrepareVecteur, where EDI is the spilled R8D. Since 0 was passed, the
     test passes and the append is reached, subject to PrepareVecteur's other three
     gates, all of which are also satisfied by this call site, as recorded below.

  3. Yes. 0x14068f2ba executes before 0x14068f5af on every path, without exception.
     The call at 0x14068f2ba strictly dominates the call at 0x14068f5af. The macro
     append therefore always happens before the zone-0 count is read.

--- Function identity ---

FUN_14068f0f0, body 0x14068f0f0 .. 0x14068f884, 417 instructions.

Name as reconstructed by the decompiler:

    undefined8 FUN_14068f0f0(
        CDataCaoTraitement *param_1,
        CStringT<char,StrTraitMFC_DLL<char,ATL::ChTraitsCRT<char>_>_> *param_2,
        char param_3,
        CStringT<char,StrTraitMFC_DLL<char,ATL::ChTraitsCRT<char>_>_> *param_4,
        char param_5,
        int param_6 );

This is CProductionDoc::PrepareExecData, named by the log string it builds at
0x14068f12f.

  Prologue, 8 pushes then a fixed frame, no alloca:

    14068f0ff  PUSH RBP        14068f100  PUSH RBX
    14068f101  PUSH RSI        14068f102  PUSH RDI
    14068f103  PUSH R12        14068f105  PUSH R13
    14068f107  PUSH R14        14068f109  PUSH R15
    14068f10b  LEA RBP,[RSP + -0xae8]
    14068f113  SUB RSP,0xbe8

  Register to register mapping, fixed at 0x14068f122 to 0x14068f12c:

    RBX   = param_1, RCX, the document
    R12   = param_4, R9, the CStringT out-parameter
    RDI   = param_2, RDX
    ESI   = param_3, R8B
    R14D  = loop index
    R15D  = zone index

  The prologue also spills the three register arguments to their home slots:

    14068f0f0  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],R9      ; R9  home slot
    14068f0f5  MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x18],R8B      ; R8  home slot
    14068f0fa  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x10],RDX     ; RDX home slot

  The RBP-relative frame needs care, because the frame is large enough that positive
  RBP displacements reach the incoming argument area. RBP is set before the SUB, so
  RBP = RSP_entry - 0x40 - 0xae8 = RSP_entry - 0xb28, and RSP_final =
  RSP_entry - 0xc28, giving RBP = RSP_final + 0x100. Therefore

    [RBP + 0xb30] = [RSP_entry + 0x08] = RCX  home slot
    [RBP + 0xb38] = [RSP_entry + 0x10] = RDX  home slot
    [RBP + 0xb40] = [RSP_entry + 0x18] = R8   home slot
    [RBP + 0xb48] = [RSP_entry + 0x20] = R9   home slot
    [RBP + 0xb50] = [RSP_entry + 0x28] = param_5
    [RBP + 0xb58] = [RSP_entry + 0x30] = param_6

  This mapping is not a guess. It is confirmed by the decompiled body, which names
  [RBP + 0xb58] param_6 and [RBP + 0xb50] param_5, and by the argument count: the
  signature has six parameters, all in registers, so the two slots at
  RSP_entry + 0x28 and RSP_entry + 0x30 are genuine incoming stack arguments and not
  dead shadow space. The compiler reuses them as general locals only after the
  incoming values have been consumed into RDI, ESI, R12 and the param_6 copies.

  Worth stating, because the opposite reading was possible and wrong: [RBP + 0xb58]
  is first read at 0x14068f285 and first written at 0x14068f2c2, so it looks like an
  uninitialised frame slot at the point of the read. It is not. It is the incoming
  sixth argument of FUN_14068f0f0, and the value read there is the caller's value.

--- The call and the instructions that set its arguments ---

  Verbatim, with encodings, in execution order:

    14068f285  80bd580b000000        CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0xb58],0x0
    14068f28c  0f94c0                SETZ AL
    14068f28f  488d93f8110000        LEA RDX,[RBX + 0x11f8]
    14068f296                     MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x40],0x0
    14068f29b                     MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x38],AL
    14068f29f                     MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x30],0x0
    14068f2a4                     MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x28],0x0
    14068f2a9                     MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x20],0x0
    14068f2ae  41b903000000          MOV R9D,0x3
    14068f2b4  4533c0                XOR R8D,R8D
    14068f2b7  488bcb                MOV RCX,RBX
    14068f2ba  e8a1caeaff            CALL 0x14053bd60

  Target 0x14053bd60 is PrepareVecteur, the single caller of PV_EnvoiMacros recorded
  in the PV_EnvoiMacros callers section. Displacement e8 a1 ca ea ff is a near
  relative call, target 0x14053bd60, from 0x14068f2bf.

  Stack arguments are placed relative to RSP as it stands at the CALL. The Windows
  x64 convention puts the callee's fifth argument at caller RSP + 0x20, sixth at
  + 0x28, and so on, because the CALL pushes the return address. So the five stores
  map onto PrepareVecteur's stack parameters in this order:

    [RSP + 0x20]  = 0        =  param_4   false
    [RSP + 0x28]  = 0        =  param_5   false
    [RSP + 0x30]  = 0        =  param_6   false
    [RSP + 0x38]  = AL       =  param_7   (char)param_6 == 0
    [RSP + 0x40]  = 0        =  param_8   false

  Complete argument list at the call:

    param_1  RCX  = RBX                the document, FUN_14068f0f0's own param_1
    param_2  RDX  = RBX + 0x11f8       a CBibliotheque sub-object at document+0x11f8
    param_3  R9D  = 3                   the literal 3
    param_4        = 0                  false
    param_5        = 0                  false
    param_6        = 0                  false
    param_7        = (byte)param_6 == 0
    param_8        = 0                  false

  As the decompiler renders it, which agrees:

    iVar15 = CDataCaoTraitement::PrepareVecteur
                     (param_1,(CBibliotheque *)(param_1 + 0x11f8),0,3,false,false,false,
                      (char)param_6 == '\0',false);

  One instruction per parameter, no reuse of a stale register. R9D is a full
  32-bit immediate write and R8D is zeroed by XOR with itself, so both are
  unambiguously defined at the call. There is no partial-register ambiguity and no
  uninitialised argument.

--- Answer to part 1: the value of param_2 ---

  ZERO. The setting instruction is

    14068f2b4  XOR R8D,R8D

  R8D is the third parameter of PrepareVecteur, param_2, the int. XOR with itself
  defines it as 0 with no dependency on any prior value. The decompiler shows the
  literal 0 in the third argument position.

  Worth recording alongside it: param_3 is set to the literal 3 at
  0x14068f2ae, MOV R9D,0x3. That 3 is the second argument PV_EnvoiMacros receives
  from PrepareVecteur, because PrepareVecteur forwards param_3 unchanged, as
  recorded in the PV_EnvoiMacros callers section where it appears as ESI. So the
  append at 0x140533c90 is performed with the fixed selector value 3, not with a
  value derived from document state. This call site is the only producer of that
  selector value in the chain examined so far.

--- Answer to part 2: the argument PrepareVecteur tests ---

  It is param_2, the same argument, the third parameter, the int in R8.

  In PrepareVecteur the spilled copy of that argument is the frame slot
  [RBP + 0x14a0] = [RSP_entry + 0x18], written by the callee's own first
  instruction, MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x18],R8D. It is loaded into EDI at

    14053c18d  MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBP + 0x14a0]

  and tested at the guard immediately before the append:

    14053c200  TEST EDI,EDI
    14053c202  JNZ 0x14053c20e
    14053c204  MOV EDX,ESI
    14053c206  MOV RCX,RBX
    14053c209  CALL 0x140533c90

  The decompiler expresses the same condition as if (param_2 == 0). Since this call
  site passes 0, the test is satisfied and the append proceeds.

  The remaining gates in PrepareVecteur, checked against the values passed here:

    gate 1  PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults != 0, or param_6 true
            Not decided at this call site; it depends on document state, computed
            inside PrepareVecteur. If it fails, PrepareVecteur takes the
            MFC140.DLL::AfxMessageBox path and returns 0.

    gate 2  param_6 must be FALSE, else PrepareVecteur returns early
            Satisfied. param_6 is set to 0 by MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x30],0x0 at
            0x14068f29f. This is the gate that would have skipped the append
            entirely, so it matters that it is explicitly zeroed.

    gate 3  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants != -1
            Depends on document state. If it returns -1, PrepareVecteur returns -1
            and the append is skipped.

    gate 4  param_2 == 0
            Satisfied, as above.

  So two of the four gates are settled here, positively, and the other two are
  document-dependent and were not evaluated. The claim proven is that this call
  site satisfies the param_2 test and the param_6 test, so it does not exclude the
  append. It does not prove the append happens, because gates 1 and 3 can still
  fail inside PrepareVecteur.

  param_7 is not a gate for the append. In PrepareVecteur, param_7 only controls
  the progress display:

    CWaitBox waitBox(false);
    if (!param_7) { waitBox.SetTexte(0xd64); waitBox.Create(0,0,false); }

  So the value derived from (byte)param_6 == 0 at 0x14068f28c affects whether a wait
  box is shown and nothing else.

--- Answer to part 3: does 0x14068f2ba execute before 0x14068f5af ---

  YES, unconditionally. This is a dominance relation, not an address ordering, and
  the distinction matters here because the two addresses are on different branches.

  Forward path from the entry to the call. The only branches between 0x14068f0f0
  and 0x14068f2ba all target addresses strictly earlier than 0x14068f26e:

    14068f182  JNZ 0x14068f26e
    14068f1b1  JLE 0x14068f24d
    14068f1d6  JZ  0x14068f22b
    14068f1df  JNZ 0x14068f22b
    14068f240  JL  0x14068f1c0

  Every one of those lands at or before 0x14068f26e, and 0x14068f26e falls through
  to 0x14068f285 and then to 0x14068f2ba with no branch in between. So 0x14068f2ba
  is on the single mandatory path.

  The call at 0x14068f5af, quoted:

    14068f5a5  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x5878]
    14068f5ac  MOV RCX,RBX
    14068f5af  e8ec1feaff            CALL 0x1405315a0

  0x1405315a0 is CDataCaoTraitement::PV_AffectIndResult, Ordinal_199,
  ?PV_AffectIndResult@CDataCaoTraitement@@QEAAXPEAVCProdCarte@@@Z. This matches the
  PrepareExecData counts section, which recorded the call as
  PV_AffectIndResult(doc, *(doc+0x5878)) with no count argument.

  Predecessor chain of 0x14068f5af, walked to the root:

    0x14068f5af   reached only by falling through from 0x14068f5ac
    0x14068f5ac   reached only from 0x14068f5a5
    0x14068f5a5   reached only from 0x14068f5a3 not taken, or fallthrough
    0x14068f5a0   the zone loop head. Its only predecessors are 0x14068f59c, from
                  the loop preamble, and 0x14068f713, the JL back edge.
    0x14068f577   MOV R15D,R14D, the first instruction of the preamble
    0x14068f577   reached only from 0x14068f451, the JZ, or by falling through
                  from 0x14068f56c at the end of the block at 0x14068f411
    0x14068f411   reached only from 0x14068f38a, the JNZ
    0x14068f383   reached only from 0x14068f2ca, the JG
    0x14068f2ca   TEST EAX,EAX / JG, with EAX from the PrepareVecteur call
    0x14068f2c8   reached only from 0x14068f2c2
    0x14068f2c2   reached only from 0x14068f2bf
    0x14068f2bf   reached only from 0x14068f2ba, the PrepareVecteur call

  The whole chain runs back to 0x14068f2ba with no alternative predecessor anywhere.
  There is no other edge into the zone loop, so 0x14068f2ba dominates 0x14068f5af.

  The converse is the useful part, and it is a stronger fact than the question
  asked. The zone-0 call is conditional on PrepareVecteur succeeding:

    14068f2bf  MOV R13D,EAX
    14068f2c2  MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0xb58],EAX
    14068f2c8  TEST EAX,EAX
    14068f2ca  JG 0x14068f383
    14068f2d0  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0xb50],0x0
    14068f2d7  JNZ 0x14068f85a
    ...
    14068f37e  JMP 0x14068f85a

  If PrepareVecteur returns <= 0, control reaches 0x14068f2d0, and BOTH outcomes
  leave the function at 0x14068f85a: the JNZ goes straight there, and the fallthrough
  block at 0x14068f2dd ends with an unconditional JMP 0x14068f85a at 0x14068f37e.
  Neither reaches the zone loop. So:

    PV_AffectIndResult at 0x14068f5af executes only when PrepareVecteur returns
    greater than zero.

  And one more condition on that positive path, from 0x14068f383:

    14068f383  CMP byte ptr [RBX + 0x1a08],0x1
    14068f38a  JNZ 0x14068f411
    14068f390  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0xb50],0x0
    14068f397  JNZ 0x14068f3f8
    ...
    14068f40c  JMP 0x14068f85a

  If document+0x1a08 equals 1, the function also exits at 0x14068f40c. If it does
  not, control reaches 0x14068f411 and thence 0x14068f577 and the zone loop.

  Full condition for 0x14068f5af to execute:

      PrepareVecteur returned > 0
      AND document+0x1a08 != 1
      AND dword ptr [RBX + 0x5880] > 0      (the JLE at 0x14068f581, the loop guard)
      AND R15D == 0 on the first iteration  (the TEST at 0x14068f5a0, the zone
                                             index, so this is the zone-0 call)

  Observation on the 0x1a08 test, following from the previous section. PrepareVecteur
  executes MOV byte ptr [RBX + 0x1a08],0x0 at 0x14053c027 unconditionally, before
  any of its own early exits. So immediately after the call at 0x14068f2ba, the byte
  at document+0x1a08 is 0, the compare at 0x14068f383 is false, and the JNZ to
  0x14068f411 is taken. The exit at 0x14068f40c is therefore not reachable from
  0x14068f2ca in this sequence. Stated as what the instructions show, not as a claim
  that the source branch is dead in every caller of FUN_14068f0f0.

  What PrepareVecteur returns on the path that performs the append. From the
  PV_EnvoiMacros callers section, when PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants does not return -1
  and param_2 is 0, PrepareVecteur returns *(int *)(this + 0xee4), which is the value
  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants stored there. Putting the two sections together:

      FUN_14068f0f0
        -> PrepareVecteur(param_1, doc+0x11f8, param_2 = 0, param_3 = 3, ...)
             -> PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants, result stored at document+0xee4
             -> if (param_2 == 0) PV_EnvoiMacros(this, 3)   appends to doc+0x2478
             -> returns document+0xee4
        -> if (that value > 0) ... zone loop ...
             -> PV_AffectIndResult(doc, *(doc+0x5878))       reads doc+0x2478

  So the append and the zone-0 read of the same vector are separated by a
  conditional, and the condition is the return value of the very call chain that
  performed the append. Ordering is unconditional; reachability of the read is not.

--- Log strings in this function ---

  Not asked for, but recorded for consistency with the earlier sections.

        14068f12f  LEA RDX,[0x140ea4d10]     "CProductionDoc::PrepareExecData"
        14068f188  LEA R8 ,[0x140ea4d30]     "Mono Section Machine...check\n"
        14068f1fe  LEA R8 ,[0x140ea4d50]     "Mono Section Machine: Bad section: Elmt Id = %s Section = %d\n"
        14068f24d  LEA R8 ,[0x140ea4d90]     "Mono Section Machine: Check finished!\n"
        14068f26e  LEA R8 ,[0x140ea4db8]     "PrepareVecteur start\n"
        14068f845  LEA RDX,[0x140ea4dd0]     "Invalid TST, no zone to inspect"

  All six reach CLogManagerFunctionML::Write through
  PTR_Write_140d532f8, at 0x140d532f8, with the destination object at [RSP + 0x68]
  and a line number in EDX. The one adjacent to the call under investigation is at
  0x14068f26e, immediately before the argument setup:

    14068f26e  LEA R8,[0x140ea4db8]
    14068f275  MOV EDX,0x2
    14068f27a  LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x68]
    14068f27f  CALL qword ptr [0x140d532f8]

  that is CLogManagerFunctionML::Write(log, 2, "PrepareVecteur start\n"). So the
  function logs its intent to prepare vectors on line 2, then calls PrepareVecteur
  eight instructions after the SETZ that forms param_7.

  String labels as defined in the binary:

    s_CProductionDoc::PrepareExecData_140ea4d10
    s_Mono_Section_Machine...check_140ea4d30
    s_Mono_Section_Machine:_Bad_sectio_140ea4d50
    s_Mono_Section_Machine:_Check_fini_140ea4d90
    s_PrepareVecteur_start_140ea4db8
    s_Invalid_TST,_no_zone_to_inspect_140ea4dd0

  The first of these names the function under analysis, which is how the earlier
  attribution of FUN_14068f0f0 to CProductionDoc::PrepareExecData is established.

--- What this settles and what it does not ---

  Settled. PrepareVecteur is called from PrepareExecData with param_2 hard-coded to
  0, which is the condition it tests before appending to the macro vector. The call
  is on a path that always executes before the zone-0 count is computed. The
  selector value handed to the append is the literal 3.

  Not settled. That the append actually executes. PrepareVecteur has two further
  document-dependent gates, PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults and
  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants, either of which can divert it before the append. Their
  outcomes are not visible at the call site.

  Not settled, and out of scope. Whether FUN_14068f0f0 is itself on the panel-load
  path. This answer stayed inside FUN_14068f0f0 as instructed, and the function's
  own callers were not enumerated. The ReloadDoc caller's caller section remains the
  record of the load path as previously established.

  Method note carried forward. The frame arithmetic in this function would have
  mis-read [RBP + 0xb58] as an uninitialised slot, because the frame is large enough
  that positive RBP displacements land on the incoming argument area. The decompiled
  parameter names settled it. The general lesson, already recorded once in this
  session for a different reason, is that instruction-level reading is necessary but
  not sufficient on its own; parameter naming and frame geometry have to agree
  before a register-relative value can be attributed to a source-level parameter.

--- Summary ---

  Call, 0x14068f2ba:
    14068f2ae  MOV R9D,0x3          ; param_3 = 3
    14068f2b4  XOR R8D,R8D          ; param_2 = 0
    14068f2b7  MOV RCX,RBX          ; param_1 = the document
    14068f2ba  CALL 0x14053bd60     ; PrepareVecteur

  param_2 passed:                        0

  Selector reaching PV_EnvoiMacros:       the literal 3, via param_3

  Per instruction, analysis stopped inside FUN_14068f0f0. PrepareVecteur was not
