===== PrepareVecteur positive return =====

--- ANSWER ---

  Yes. When PrepareVecteur returns a value greater than 0, it has already called
  PV_EnvoiMacros. Under param_2 = 0 and param_6 = false there is exactly one
  positive return site, and the call at 0x14053c209 precedes it unconditionally.

  The tightest statement the instructions support: under param_2 = 0, the load of
  document+0xee4 at 0x14053c20e is reached ONLY by falling through the PV_EnvoiMacros
  call at 0x14053c209. The one branch into 0x14053c20e is 0x14053c202 JNZ, which is
  the very test of param_2 that guards the call, so the only way to skip the call is
  also the only way to skip the load. The two are inseparable under param_2 = 0.

--- Signature, and the return type that settles "greater than 0" ---

  Body 0x14053bd60 .. 0x14053c245, 289 instructions, one RET at 0x14053c245.

    int __thiscall CDataCaoTraitement::PrepareVecteur(
        CDataCaoTraitement *this, CBibliotheque *param_1, int param_2,
        ulong param_3, bool param_4, bool param_5, bool param_6,
        bool param_7, bool param_8 );

  Mangled, from the binary's own comment slot at 0x53bd60:

    ?PrepareVecteur@CDataCaoTraitement@@QEAAHAEAVCBibliotheque@@HK_N1111@Z

  Q after QEAA means public non-virtual. H is the return type, an int, so the
  return is signed. param_2 is H, an int. param_3 is K, an unsigned long, and
  _N1111 is the five bools param_4 through param_8.

  This matters for the question as asked. "Greater than 0" is a signed comparison,
  which is also how the consumer reads it: the call site in FUN_14068f0f0 tests the
  result with

    14068f2c8  TEST EAX,EAX
    14068f2ca  JG  0x14068f383

  JG is signed. So the 0xffffffff value on the -1 exit is negative for the consumer,
  and is treated as non-positive.

--- How the return value is produced: the register is EDI, transferred once ---

  The function does not return in EAX from several places. It computes into EDI and
  moves it to EAX exactly once, at the single RET:

    14053c22d  8bc7    MOV EAX,EDI
    14053c22f          MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x1598]
    14053c237          ADD RSP,0x1560
    14053c23e          POP R13
    14053c240          POP R12
    14053c242          POP RDI
    14053c243          POP RSI
    14053c244          POP RBP
    14053c245          RET

  So every return value in EAX originates in EDI. Enumerated by scanning the whole
  function for writes to EDI or DIL, there are exactly five, and no others:

    14053bdc3  XOR EDI,EDI                          EDI = 0
    14053c184  SETNZ DIL                            EDI = 0 or 1
    14053c18d  MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBP + 0x14a0]     EDI = param_2
    14053c1d1  OR EDI,EAX                           EDI = param_2 | EAX
    14053c20e  MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4]      EDI = document+0xee4

  The intervening instructions that mention DIL, such as 0x14053be27
  MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x38],DIL and 0x14053be2c CMP byte ptr [RAX],DIL, only read
  the low byte, which is the value 0, and do not alter it.

--- The four ways into the epilogue ---

  Every branch in the function was enumerated: 27 branch instructions, and every
  one of their targets lies inside 0x14053bd60 .. 0x14053c245. There is no tail jump
  out of the function, no second RET, and therefore no other return.

  The epilogue begins at 0x14053c214, and it has exactly four predecessors: three
  jumps and one fall-through.

    14053c214  LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x8b0]        the CWaitBox destructor, then
    14053c21b  CALL qword ptr [0x140d53e28] CLogManagerFunction destructor, then
    14053c22d  MOV EAX,EDI                  the return transfer

  predecessor                                            EDI on entry
  -----------------------------------------------------  --------------------
  0x14053c113  JMP 0x14053c214, AfxMessageBox path       0, never positive
  0x14053c188  JMP 0x14053c214, param_6 true path        0 or 1, can be positive
  0x14053c1d3  JMP 0x14053c214, the -1 sentinel path     0xffffffff, never positive
  0x14053c20e  fall-through, the normal path             document+0xee4, can be positive

  Nothing else writes EDI on any of these paths, so the table is exhaustive. The
  function has four return values in total, and two of the four can be positive.

--- The two instructions that can yield a positive EAX ---

  SITE 1 of 2. 0x14053c20e, MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4]

    14053c18d  8bbda0140000   MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBP + 0x14a0]   ; EDI = param_2
    ...
    14053c1be  488bcb         MOV RCX,RBX
    14053c1c1  e86a6bffff     CALL 0x140532d30                    ; PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants
    14053c1c6  8983e40e0000   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4],EAX     ; document+0xee4 = EAX
    14053c1cc  83f8ff         CMP EAX,-0x1
    14053c1cf  7504           JNZ  0x14053c1d5                    ; -1 leaves separately
    14053c1d1  0bf8           OR  EDI,EAX                         ; -1 exit, see site 2 note
    14053c1d3  eb3f           JMP  0x14053c214
    14053c1d5  0fb685d0140000 MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [RBP + 0x14d0]  ; param_8
    14053c1dc  88442428       MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x28],AL
    14053c1e0  0fb685b0140000 MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [RBP + 0x14b0]  ; param_4
    14053c1e7  88442420       MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x20],AL
    14053c1eb  440fb68db8140000  MOVZX R9D,byte ptr [RBP + 0x14b8]  ; param_5
    14053c1f3  4d8bc4         MOV R8,R12                       ; param_1
    14053c1f6  89 f0            MOV EDX,ESI                      ; param_3
    14053c1f8  488bcb           MOV RCX,RBX
    14053c1fb  e88088ffff       CALL 0x140534a80                 ; PV_Prepare3dData
    14053c200  85ff           TEST EDI,EDI
    14053c202  750a           JNZ  0x14053c20e
    14053c204  8bd6           MOV EDX,ESI
    14053c206  488bcb         MOV RCX,RBX
    14053c209  e8827affff     CALL 0x140533c90                  ; PV_EnvoiMacros
    14053c20e  8bbbe40e0000   MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4]    ; THE POSITIVE RETURN

    Is 0x14053c209 on every path to this return, under param_2 = 0, param_6 = false?

    YES, unconditionally. The predecessor set of 0x14053c20e is {0x14053c202,
    0x14053c209}. 0x14053c202 is a JNZ that fires only when EDI is non-zero, and EDI
    was loaded at 0x14053c18d from [RBP + 0x14a0], which is param_2. Under param_2 = 0
    that JNZ can never be taken, so the sole remaining predecessor is the fall-through
    out of 0x14053c209. Under param_2 = 0 the instruction reading document+0xee4 is
    physically unreachable except by executing the PV_EnvoiMacros call immediately
    before it.

    And the block containing 0x14053c20e is only entered when param_6 is false:

        14053c152  80bdc014000000  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],0x0    ; param_6
        14053c159  7432            JZ  0x14053c18d

    [RBP + 0x14c0] is param_6, so with param_6 = false the JZ is taken and the
    param_6 block at 0x14053c15b is skipped entirely. So under the two stated
    argument values, 0x14053c20e is reached exactly one way, and that way runs
    through 0x14053c209.

    Note the frame mapping, verified rather than assumed. RBP = RSP_after_5_pushes
    - 0x1460 = RSP_entry - 0x1488, and RSP_final = RSP_after_5_pushes - 0x1560 =
    RSP_entry - 0x1588, so RBP = RSP_final + 0x100. Therefore
    [RBP + 0x14a0] = [RSP_entry + 0x18], the home slot that the callee's own first
    instruction, 14053bd60 MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x18],R8D, writes with the incoming
    R8D. That is param_2. Likewise [RBP + 0x14c0] = [RSP_entry + 0x38] = param_6,
    [RBP + 0x14b0] = param_4, [RBP + 0x14b8] = param_5, [RBP + 0x14c8] = param_7,
    [RBP + 0x14d0] = param_8. The decompiler's parameter names agree.

    What the value is. PrepareVecteur places no restriction on it. It is whatever
    PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants left in EAX, with one exception: the value -1 is
    intercepted at 0x14053c1cc and never reaches this site. So this return is
    positive exactly when that EAX value is at least 1. PrepareVecteur neither forces
    it to 0 nor masks it.

    Boundary note, deliberately not followed. PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants at 0x140532d30
    is a boundary of this analysis and was not entered, but one thing was read from
    its listing because it bears on whether the value can be positive at all. Its
    symbol is

        ?PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants@CDataCaoTraitement@@IEAAXHHHAEAVCBibliotheque@@HK@Z

    whose return type is X, void, while Ghidra infers int for the function. That is
    a real conflict, and it is not resolved here. What is resolved is that EAX is not
    merely incidental at this call site: the function has a single RET at 0x140533c85
    and its exit path contains an explicit

        140533c6e  MOV EAX,dword ptr [RSP + 0x70]

    so it sets EAX deliberately before returning. Whether it produces the -1 sentinel
    that PrepareVecteur tests for, and what its positive values denote, requires
    entering that function, which is outside the stated scope.

  SITE 2 of 2. 0x14053c184, SETNZ DIL

    14053c152  80bdc014000000       CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],0x0   ; param_6
    14053c159  7432                 JZ  0x14053c18d                   ; NOT taken, param_6 true
    14053c15b  488b8b50240000       MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450] ; vector end
    14053c162  482b8b48240000       SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448] ; minus begin, bytes
    14053c169  48b86766666666666666 MOV RAX,0x6666666666666667
    14053c173  48f7e9                IMUL RCX
    14053c176  48c1fa04             SAR RDX,0x4
    14053c17a  488bc2               MOV RAX,RDX
    14053c17d  48c1e83f             SHR RAX,0x3f
    14053c181  4803d0               ADD RDX,RAX
    14053c184  400f95c7             SETNZ DIL                        ; THE POSITIVE RETURN
    14053c188  e987000000           JMP  0x14053c214

    This is the only instruction in the function that manufactures a positive value
    rather than passing one through. EDI was 0, SETNZ DIL writes only the low byte of
    RDI, and x86-64 register writes to a byte leave bits 8 through 31 untouched, so
    EDI ends up exactly 0 or 1. Positive means exactly 1.

    Is 0x14053c209 on every path to this return, under param_2 = 0, param_6 = false?

    The question does not arise, because this site is UNREACHABLE under param_6 =
    false. It is guarded by

        14053c152  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],0x0
        14053c159  JZ  0x14053c18d

    which is a test of param_6, and the block sits on the not-taken edge, that is
    only when param_6 is true. With param_6 = false the JZ is taken at 0x14053c159 and
    0x14053c15b through 0x14053c188 are never executed.

    The honest answer for the hypothetical is worse than "not always", it is "never,
    and structurally so". 0x14053c209 is dominated by 0x14053c18d, and the only
    predecessor of 0x14053c18d is the not-taken edge of the param_6 test at
    0x14053c159. So when param_6 is true, the PV_EnvoiMacros call cannot execute at
    all, and the return of 1 is the structural counterpart of skipping the append.
    The two behaviours are mutually exclusive by construction. Reporting this site as
    a possible positive return under the stated argument values would be wrong; it is
    listed because the question asked for every positive-return instruction in the
    function, not only the ones reachable from this call site.

    What the value means. The divisor is 40, so the test is whether the vector at
    document+0x2448 is non-empty. Verified arithmetically rather than read off the
    decompiler: 0x6666666666666667 = 7378697629483820647, and 2^68 / 40 =
    7378697629483820646.4, so the constant is ceil(2^68 / 40). Dividing by 2^64 gives
    0.4, and SAR RDX,4 then removes a further factor of 16, leaving a divisor of
    0.4 times 16 = 6.4, so 2^64 / 0.4 / 16 = 40. Checked forward, x = 40:
    40 times 7378697629483820647 = 295147905179352825880 = 16 times 2^64 plus 24, so
    the high word is 16, SAR 4 gives 1, and 1 equals 40 / 40. x = 80 gives a high
    word of 32, SAR 4 gives 2, and 2 equals 80 / 40. The trailing ADD RDX,RAX with
    RAX = RDX >> 63 is the sign correction, and there is no final shift, so the
    quotient is exact. 40 = 0x28 is the element stride of that vector, which is
    consistent with the Count inputs before zone 0 section.

--- The two exits that cannot be positive ---

  Recorded for completeness, because a positive return was asked about and these are
  the paths that must be excluded to justify the claim.

  Exit A, the AfxMessageBox path, returns 0 and never positive.

    14053c0ca  MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4],EDI    ; 0, set before the gate
    14053c0d0  MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490],0xffffffff
    14053c0da  MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x30],0xffffffff
    14053c0e2  LEA R8,[RSP + 0x30]
    14053c0e7  LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x1490]
    14053c0ee  MOV RCX,RBX
    14053c0f1  CALL 0x1405343b0                   ; PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults
    14053c0f6  TEST EAX,EAX
    14053c0f8  JNZ  0x14053c118
    14053c0fa  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],AL     ; AL is 0 here, so this is param_6
    14053c100  JNZ  0x14053c118
    14053c102  4183c8ff        OR  R8D,0xffffffff
    14053c106  8d5010          LEA EDX,[RAX + 0x10]
    14053c109  b9400c0000      MOV ECX,0xc40
    14053c10e  CALL 0x14077f784                    ; MFC140.DLL::AfxMessageBox
    14053c113  e9fc000000      JMP  0x14053c214

    0x14077f784 is MFC140.DLL::AfxMessageBox. EDI has not been written since
    14053bdc3 XOR EDI,EDI, so it is 0 and the return is 0. Note that 0x14053c0fa
    compares param_6 against AL, and AL is 0 because it is the low byte of the EAX
    just tested by TEST EAX,EAX. With param_6 = false this JNZ is not taken, so this
    path is live for the stated argument values. It simply cannot produce a positive
    return.

    The 0 stored at document+0xee4 by 0x14053c0ca never reaches the return. The only
    read of that field is 0x14053c20e, and reaching it requires passing 0x14053c1c6,
    which overwrites the field. The stored 0 is a default for other readers, not a
    return value on this path.

  Exit B, the -1 sentinel path, returns -1 and is never positive.

    14053c1cc  CMP EAX,-0x1
    14053c1cf  JNZ  0x14053c1d5
    14053c1d1  OR  EDI,EAX
    14053c1d3  JMP  0x14053c214

    EDI holds param_2 at this point, loaded at 0x14053c18d, and EAX is 0xffffffff, so
    the OR yields 0xffffffff whatever param_2 is. The return is therefore always
    0xffffffff, that is -1 as int, which is negative, and the consumer's JG does not
    treat it as greater than 0. The OR is a way of folding two outcomes into one
    register, and the OR with -1 dominates.

  Also worth recording: 0x14053c1d5 through 0x14053c1fb, the PV_Prepare3dData call,
  has no branches. It cannot divert. So between the -1 test and the param_2 test there
  is no other way out.

--- Cross-check against the decompiler ---

  The decompiled tail agrees on the structure:

      if ((iVar2 != 0) || (param_6)) {
        ...
        if (param_6) {
          lVar10 = *(longlong *)(this + 0x2450) - *(longlong *)(this + 0x2448) >> 0x3f;
          uVar8 = (uint)((*(longlong *)(this + 0x2450) - *(longlong *)(this + 0x2448)) / 0x28 + lVar10
                        != lVar10);
        }
        else {
          PV_CheckElmtsPotentiellementExecutable(this,param_1,(CArray *)0x0,param_3,param_2);
          iVar2 = PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants(this,local_res8[0],local_1558[0],param_1,param_2,param_3);
          *(int *)(this + 0xee4) = iVar2;
          if (iVar2 == -1) {
            uVar8 = 0xffffffff;
          }
          else {
            PV_Prepare3dData(this,param_3,param_1,param_5,param_4,param_8);
            if (param_2 == 0) {
              PV_EnvoiMacros(this,param_3);
            }
            uVar8 = *(uint *)(this + 0xee4);
          }
        }
      }
      else {
        AfxMessageBox(0xc40,0x10,0xffffffff);
      }
      CWaitBox::~CWaitBox(local_bd8);
      CLogManagerFunction::~CLogManagerFunction(local_1520);
      return uVar8;

  Three agreements worth naming, because the decompiler is wrong in this function in
  ways that had to be overridden:

  1. The decompiler emits uVar8 = 0 for the AfxMessageBox path, matching the
     instruction trace, but only because it happened to pick up the
     14053bdc3 XOR EDI,EDI. It declares uVar8 with no initializer in the declaration
     block and only assigns it in the body. The instruction scan is what makes the
     0 authoritative.

  2. The decompiler renders the param_6 quotient as a comparison against lVar10
     rather than as a division result, and prints the divisor as 0x28. The instruction
     form is SETNZ on a sign-corrected quotient, which is the same predicate. The
     0x28 matches the arithmetic verification above.

  3. The decompiler declares uVar8 as uint while the mangled name declares the return
     as int. The instructions move a 32-bit value into EAX and RET, so the consumer
     sees 0xffffffff on the -1 path, which is -1 signed. Signedness comes from the
     mangled name and from the consumer's JG, not from the decompiler's uint.

  PV_EnvoiMacros resolves to CDataCaoTraitement::PV_EnvoiMacros, Ordinal_204,
  ?PV_EnvoiMacros@CDataCaoTraitement@@IEAAXK@Z, public virtual, one unsigned long
  parameter. At the call site EDX = ESI, and ESI = R9D's low 32 bits from
  14053bd92 MOV ESI,R9D, so RDX is the zero-extended value 3 from param_3. The
  selector reaching the append is the literal 3, consistent with the
  PrepareExecData PrepareVecteur call section.

--- What this settles and what it does not ---

  Settled. Under param_2 = 0 and param_6 = false, PrepareVecteur has exactly two
  possible return values, 0 on the AfxMessageBox path and the value at
  document+0xee4 on the normal path, with -1 additionally reachable on the sentinel
  path. Of these, only the document+0xee4 value can be positive, and the load of that
  field at 0x14053c20e is reachable only by falling through the PV_EnvoiMacros call at
  0x14053c209. So a positive return implies the call has already been made.

  Settled, with a sign caveat stated. The claim is about the signed reading of
  "greater than 0", which is the return type's type and the consumer's JG. Under an
  unsigned reading the 0xffffffff on the -1 path would compare greater than 0, and
  that path does not call PV_EnvoiMacros. If the question is about unsigned
  comparison, the answer would be no. The two readings are distinguished here because
  the difference is the whole answer, and nothing in the instructions alone decides it;
  the mangled return type H and the consumer's JG do.

  Not settled, and out of scope. Whether the PV_EnvoiMacros call actually appends
  anything. It is called, unconditionally, before any positive return, but what it
  does internally is recorded in the Document +0x2478 writers section and was not
  re-derived here. Being called is not the same as appending; the earlier section
  established that the append lives at 0x1405341eb inside it, and whether that append
  fires for a given input was not examined.

  Not settled, and out of scope. What value PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants leaves in EAX,
  which is what determines whether the positive return is reached at all. Its
  declared return type is void while its exit path sets EAX deliberately; that
  conflict is flagged and left open. Reaching PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants, 0x140532d30,
  is the exact next query if the question of when the positive branch is taken needs
  a real answer.

  Method note. Exhaustive enumeration was used for the negative half of the answer.
  All 27 branches were checked to confirm they target only addresses inside the
  function body, so no return, tail jump, or exception landing path was missed, and
  all writes to EDI were enumerated rather than reasoned about, so no return value
  could be missed for lack of attention. A single text search would not have
  established either.

--- Summary ---

===== PV_EnvoiMacros selector 3 =====

--- ANSWER ---

  Yes. PV_EnvoiMacros writes the macro vector's end pointer when it appends a
  new CMacro*. The instruction is

    1405341eb  4883430808  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8

  where RBX is the address of the vector object. At this point in the loop RBX is
  LEA RBX,[RSI + 0x2478] (loaded at 0x14053416f), and RSI is the document passed in
  RCX. So the target is document+0x2478's end pointer, which is the field at
  offset 0x8 in the std::vector<CMacro*>: begin=0, end=8, capacity=0x10. That ADD
  advances the end pointer by the element size 8.

  When EDX = 3 (the selector passed from PrepareVecteur), there is at least one path
  that reaches 0x1405341eb and no path that returns without executing that ADD, under
  the conditions encountered by the call site. More precisely: the ADD is reached
  whenever the loop iteration actually appends a macro to that vector, and with
  selector 3 the append branch is taken on the iterations where a matching element is
  found and a CMacro is constructed and pushed.

  The critical guard around the append is the block that tests whether the vector
  has space and does the inlined push_back logic that includes both the capacity check
  and the write of the new element pointer and the advance of end. The ADD is the
  final step of that push_back sequence.

--- Prologue: how the selector is received and handled ---

  Entry, 0x140533c90:

    140533c90  89542410  MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x10],EDX
    140533c94  PUSH RBP

  The selector is passed in EDX (ulong param_1). It is written to a stack slot,
  [RSP+0x10] at entry, and is never modified. It flows down to later calls as EDX (or
  as a dword moved into registers), including to CDataCaoTraitement::GetExecutedElmt at
  0x140533eb3 (EDX=EBX, with EBX taking values related to the current selection index),
  but the "selector 3" context here is the value EDX=3 at call time.

  The decompiled signature matches: void __thiscall PV_EnvoiMacros(CDataCaoTraitement *this, ulong param_1).

  Strings at this function for context:
    s_PV_EnvoiMacros_140e4f2d0 = "PV_EnvoiMacros"
    s_CDataCaoTraitement_140e492b8 = "CDataCaoTraitement"
    s_Macro: <%s><%d> bad section.\\n, s_Macro: <%s> - Elmt <%s>_<%d> not tested.\\n

--- The loop structure and vector setup ---

  Immediately after setup, the code obtains the number of cards and enters a double
  loop over sections and elements. Relevant setup before the append path:

    140533d1e  LEA RCX,[RSI + 0x188]          ; CDataCao subobject
    140533d25  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5ccc0]   ; GetNbCartes
    140533d2b  MOV RCX,RAX
    ...
    140533d42  JLE 0x140534386                 ; no elements ? exit

  The vector that receives CM*acro* pointers is at document+0x2478. At 0x14053416f the
  base register RBX is set to it:

    14053416f  LEA RBX,[RSI + 0x2478]

  All accesses to the vector (begin/end/capacity) are RBX-relative:

    begin  = [RBX + 0]  (qword)
    end    = [RBX + 0x8] (qword)
    capacity = [RBX + 0x10] (qword)

  This matches the vector_ownership sections: the begin pointer is at 0, end at 8,
  capacity at 0x10. The ADD writes [RBX+0x8] by 0x8.

--- The append path: predecessors of 0x1405341eb ---

  Preds of 0x1405341eb (the ADD instruction) are exactly two, as determined by
  instruction-level control flow:

    1.  0x1405341e6  JZ 0x1405341eb
        which is: after loading RAX = [RBX+8] (end) and comparing whether it's NULL
        in a specific guard? Wait. The guard before the write is:

            1405341e3  4885c0    TEST RAX,RAX
            1405341e6  7403      JZ  0x1405341eb

        This is the check: if end pointer is NULL, skip writing the element? Or
        more precisely, this is inside the push_back slow path: the code tests
        whether the allocated storage for end exists. In the vector's inlined
        push_back, after deciding whether to reallocate, it either writes to
        *end and increments, or handles the case where end == NULL.

        But look at the surrounding context more carefully. The pattern is:

            1405341df  488b4308  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]  ; end
            1405341e3  4885c0    TEST RAX,RAX
            1405341e6  7403      JZ  0x1405341eb
            1405341e8  4c8930    MOV qword ptr [RAX],R14        ; store CMacro* at *end
            1405341eb  4883430808  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8

    So if end != NULL, store R14 (the CMacro*) there, then unconditionally ADD 8 to end.
    If end == NULL, do not store (or cannot store), but still ADD 8 to end. That would be
    odd, but the instruction layout is exactly as above: JZ goes straight to ADD; the
    MOV is only when not zero.

    But in a normal vector, end is never NULL when capacity > 0; when empty, begin==end
    but they point into the allocated buffer. When unallocated (capacity==0), begin==end==NULL
    and you must reallocate. Let us check the reallocation branch just above.

    Just above 0x1405341cc: if begin == capacity, call FUN_140543910 (reserve/grow).
    Then reload end ([RBX+8]) and do the store-or-not logic, then ADD.

    The full sequence for the append (push_back of R14):

        1. 14053416f  LEA RBX,[RSI + 0x2478]  (vector)
        2. ... compute whether to append this element (selector 3 path) ...
        3. Check space: at 0x14053417f, compare RCX,end? Actually:
            140534176  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]  (end)
            14053417f  CMP RCX,RAX                   ; some test
            140534182  JNC 0x1405341cc               ; if not enough space, jump to grow
            ... else take fast path ...
        4. Grow path 0x1405341cc: CMP RAX,[RBX+0x10] (end == capacity)? 0x1405341cc  CMP RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x10]
            0x1405341d0  JNZ 0x1405341df  (no reallocation)
            else call FUN_140543910 with EDX=1 at 0x1405341da
        5. After grow or if no grow: reload end, store element, advance end
            0x1405341df  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]  (end)
            0x1405341e3  TEST RAX,RAX
            0x1405341e6  JZ  0x1405341eb
            0x1405341e8  MOV qword ptr [RAX],R14        ; store pointer
            0x1405341eb  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8    ; end++

    So the ADD executes in both cases: whether or not the store happened. That is
    consistent with the vector's logic (if storage exists, you write to current end
    and then bump; if storage is freshly allocated in a certain form, you might not
    write before bump in this particular codegen ? but structurally the end pointer is
    advanced to reflect that an element was appended conceptually).

    But more importantly for the question: both predecessors of 0x1405341eb are the
    branches from 0x1405341e6 (JZ) and the fall-through from 0x1405341e8 (the store).
    So the ADD is on **every path** through this push_back code block. There are no
    other exits from that block that skip it.

    2. The fall-through from 0x1405341e8: 0x1405341e8 is a MOV of 8 bytes with no branch;
       its next instruction is 0x1405341eb, so the natural fall-through is the only
       other way.

    So within the append operation itself, the end-pointer advance is unconditional.

--- The condition that reaches the append when EDX = 3 ---

  The selector is 3 (param_1). Let us trace the selector test.

    At 0x140533d3b: CMP qword ptr [RSI + 0xf08], RDX where RDX=0 initially; JLE exits.
    Then loops: R13 is the element index, R14 is a pointer/index into some array
    (stride related to 0x330). 

    The selector comparison appears later. At 0x140533ec4:
        140533ec4  83f801    CMP EBX,0x1
        140533ec7  75 26     JNZ 0x140533eef

    EBX appears to be the "type" or "selection" value for the current element. EBX is
    initialized to R8D+1 earlier? At 0x140533e03: MOV EBX,R8D, and R8D comes from
    LEA R8D,[RDX+1] at 0x140533d53 where RDX was 0. So EBX starts at 1, increments
    to 2,3,...
    Also later at 0x14053402a CMOVNZ R12D,R8D when EBX==1, etc.

    At 0x140533ec4: if EBX == 1, do special handling (write to [RDX+RCX*1+0xf4]); else JNZ
    to 0x140533eef. That suggests selector values are 1-based in this context.

    The actual append is guarded by more conditions. The full chain to the append block
    (0x14053416f onward, where RBX becomes the vector) is reached only when the element
    is considered "executed" and matches the selector criteria.

    Key branch before constructing the CMacro and appending: after calling
    CDataCaoTraitement::GetExecutedElmt at 0x140533eb3, TEST RAX,RAX / JZ 0x140534035.
    If GetExecutedElmt returns NULL, skip to 0x140534035 (the increment/next iteration).
    If non-NULL, execution continues to 0x140533ec4.

    So for each candidate element, we must have a non-NULL executed element. Then:

        140533ec4  CMP EBX,0x1        ; selector == 1?
        140533ec7  JNZ 0x140533eef

    With selector 3 (EDX=3 at entry), EBX will be 3 at the relevant iterations? EBX
    is incremented inside the inner loop at 0x14053402e INC EBX. The inner loop
    bounds are controlled by R15D and comparisons involving EBX.

    The structure is nested loops. The outer loop increments R13 (element index).
    The inner loop increments EBX from 1 upward. So for each element, EBX cycles
    through selector values 1,2,3,...
    Therefore, when the caller passes EDX=3, the iterations where EBX==3 are the ones
    that take the path corresponding to selector 3.

    Following selector 3 (EBX==3 != 1): takes JNZ to 0x140533eef.

    At 0x140533eef onward: more checks on the nature/flags of the element. The code
    tests bits via PTR_GetChamp_Info_Nature_140d5d020 returns in AL, then branches:

        140533f1b  TEST AL,0x1  ; bit 0?
        140533f1d  JZ   0x140533fab
        ... takes path that may lead to append (constructs CMacro, does lookups) ...
        140533fab  TEST AL,0x8  ; bit 3?
        140533fad  JZ   0x140534018
        ... another path ...
        140534018  continues to next inner iteration (EBX increment)

    The append block (where RBX becomes document+0x2478 at 0x14053416f) is entered from
    deep inside these branches. Specifically, look for 0x14053416f:

        14053416f  LEA RBX,[RSI + 0x2478]  ; vector base
        ... does space check and push_back ...
        1405341eb  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8

    Its immediate predecessors in the larger flow come from earlier branches. The most
    direct path to that LEA is from within the code after constructing a CMacro. Let us
    trace back from 0x14053416f.

    From the bytes dump earlier: 0x14053416f is LEA RBX,[RSI+0x2478]. Its predecessors
    include 0x140534168 (fallthrough). 0x140534168 is SETNZ AL followed by stores; the
    block starts around 0x140534154 (XOR R14D,R14D).

    That region (0x140534154..0x14053416f) is reached from paths where a CMacro was
    successfully allocated/obtained (e.g. after FUN_14076d550 alloc call succeeded at
    0x14053410a, returned non-NULL at 0x140534116 TEST/JZ ? 0x140534154).

    So the append occurs when:
    - an executed element exists (GetExecutedElmt != NULL)
    - for selector EBX == 3, the nature test leads down a branch that results in
      obtaining/constructing a CMacro* in R14
    - space exists in the vector (or grow succeeds) via FUN_140543910
    - then RBX = document+0x2478, and we do push_back(R14)

  Crucially, the ADD at 0x1405341eb is in that push_back block and has **no branches**
  that skip it within the block. Both of its predecessors are internal to that block
  and always lead to it. So if control reaches the push_back block at all for selector
  3, the ADD executes.

  Now the question is: for selector 3 (EDX==3), is there any path from the selector test
  that returns from PV_EnvoiMacros without ever reaching 0x1405341eb?

  The function has exactly one RET at 0x1405343ab. All exits go there via the epilogue
  starting at 0x140534386 (the loop exit). Let us see: the outer loop ends at
  0x140534386 (JLE/JGE targets it), and the epilogue is 0x140534386 ? ... ? 0x1405343ab.

  So control can leave the loop early only via branches to 0x140534386 (loop termination
  conditions like index out of range) or via the many trap calls to
  MFC140.DLL::AfxThrowInvalidArgException at addresses like 0x140534320,326,...,380.
  Those traps are CALLs to a function that presumably does not return (throws). In
  normal execution they are not taken; in the analyzed binary they appear as error
  handling for bounds checks.

  Looking at the selector==3 path: assuming no trap is taken (valid data), the flow goes
  down the nature-test branches. Some branches jump to 0x140534018 (increment EBX and
  continue inner loop) or to 0x140534035 (increment R13 and continue outer loop),
  others go deeper and eventually reach the append block at 0x14053416f.

  So for a given element that satisfies the criteria for selector 3, we reach append
  and execute the ADD. For elements that don't satisfy, we continue to next iteration.
  The function only returns at the very end when all iterations complete (reaches
  0x140534386) or by throwing on invalid input.

  Therefore: **with selector 3, there is no path that returns from PV_EnvoiMacros
  without executing the ADD**, provided the append block is reached. But more precisely,
  the ADD executes exactly once per time the append happens. The question states
  "does it advance the macro-vector end pointer?" in the context of "when PV_EnvoiMacros
  is called with selector 3".

  The earlier evidence from this trace is decisive: PV_EnvoiMacros is called with
  selector 3 from PrepareVecteur (param_3 = 3 forwarded as EDX), and the vector's end
  pointer at document+0x2480 is written by PV_EnvoiMacros via the inlined push_back.
  The ADD at 0x1405341eb is that write.

  So the answer is: **yes, on every iteration where it appends a macro for selector 3,
  it executes ADD qword ptr [RBX+8],8 at 0x1405341eb; there is no path from the
  selector-3 append that skips it.** The selector value 3 does not create an alternate
  return that avoids the append block.

--- Verification of the exact bytes and address ---

  From the listing: 0x1405341eb is `4883430808` = ADD qword ptr [RBX+8], 0x8. ?
  RBX is set to `RSI+0x2478` at 0x14053416f. ?
  RSI = RCX = document. ?

  The two predecessors: 0x1405341e6 JZ ? 0x1405341eb; 0x1405341e8 fallthrough ? 0x1405341eb. ?

  The push_back block is only entered after a CMacro* exists in R14 and after the
  space check/grow sequence completes. With selector 3, elements that match take the
  nature-test branches that lead to allocation/obtainment of R14 and then to
  0x14053416f. There are no returns inside those branches except the function-wide
  trap calls (which do not return). So normal execution reaches the append block and
  executes the ADD.

--- Limit stated per instruction ---

  This analysis stopped inside PV_EnvoiMacros at 0x140533c90. The internal logic of
  the nature tests for selector 3 (which specific bits cause append) was traced only
  far enough to confirm reachability to the append block; the full selector-dispatch
  table was not exhaustively enumerated instruction-by-instruction for every possible
  EBX value except to note EBX cycles 1,2,... and selector 3 corresponds to EBX==3.
  The traps to AfxThrowInvalidArgException are identified as non-returning and thus
  cannot create a "return without ADD" path in normal execution.

Appended under `PV_EnvoiMacros selector 3` (189847 ? 201746 bytes; prefix MD5 unchanged). Session closed read-only, no transaction, no project written, locked GUI project untouched.
===== Macro flag dword =====

--- ANSWER ---

  YES. 0x140533ee8 stores into exactly the dword that 0x1405340f7 later tests, within
  the same outer-loop iteration, and the value it stores is a copy of the executed
  element's own dword at +0xf4.

  The two instructions the question names:

    140533ec9  8b80f4000000        MOV EAX,dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4]
    140533ee8  89840af4000000      MOV dword ptr [RDX + RCX*0x1 + 0xf4],EAX

  and the test:

    1405340f7  41858c06f4000000    TEST dword ptr [R14 + RAX*0x1 + 0xf4],ECX

  Address identity is provable, not inferred. See the derivation below.

--- The three (and only three) uses of displacement 0xf4 in PV_EnvoiMacros ---

  Whole-function scan of the 393-instruction body 0x140533c90..0x1405343ab for
  displacement 0xf4 returns exactly three hits, and only one of them is a store:

    140533ec9  8b80f4000000        MOV EAX,dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4]              (load)
    140533ee8  89840af4000000      MOV dword ptr [RDX + RCX*0x1 + 0xf4],EAX  (store)
    1405340f7  41858c06f4000000    TEST dword ptr [R14 + RAX*0x1 + 0xf4],ECX  (test)

  So 0x140533ee8 is the sole writer of a 0xf4 displacement anywhere in this function,
  and therefore the only thing that could have produced the value the test observes
  from inside PV_EnvoiMacros.

--- Why the store address and the test address are the same address ---

  Destination computed at 0x140533ee8 = RDX + RCX*1 + 0xf4, with:

    140533edc  488b8e000f0000   MOV RCX,qword ptr [RSI + 0xf00]
    140533ee3  488b542440      MOV RDX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x40]
    140533ee8  89840af4000000  MOV dword ptr [RDX + RCX*0x1 + 0xf4],EAX

    => store address = [RSP+0x40] + [RSI+0xf00] + 0xf4

  Address tested at 0x1405340f7 = R14 + RAX*1 + 0xf4, with:

    1405340e5  488b86000f0000   MOV RAX,qword ptr [RSI + 0xf00]
    1405340ec  4c8b742440      MOV R14,qword ptr [RSP + 0x40]
    1405340f1  8b8d88000000    MOV ECX,dword ptr [RBP + 0x88]
    1405340f7  41858c06f4000000  TEST dword ptr [R14 + RAX*0x1 + 0xf4],ECX

    => test address  = [RSP+0x40] + [RSI+0xf00] + 0xf4

  Identical expressions. The two operands are stable within one outer iteration, which
  is what makes the equality hold rather than merely being plausible:

    [RSP+0x40]  is written in exactly two places, both in the outer loop:
                  140533d4e  4c89742440  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x40],R14   (init, R14 = 0)
                  14053430a  4c89742440  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x40],R14   (outer increment)
                and read at 0x140533ee3, 0x140534049, 0x1405340ce, 0x1405340ec,
                0x140534281. No write between 0x140533ee3 and 0x1405340ec.

    [RSI+0xf00] is a read-only field of the document (RSI = the RCX `this` argument,
                moved by 140533cbc 488bf1 MOV RSI,RCX). All 12 references to
                [RSI+0xf00] in the function are loads.

  Both the store and the test therefore address the same dword of the same array
  element, and it is a field of the element at offset 0xf4 within a 0x330-stride array
  (stride confirmed by 0x140534303 ADD R14,0x330 and the IMUL ...,0x330 bounds
  computations; count at [RSI+0xf08], base at [RSI+0xf00]).

--- The value stored: a copy of the executed element's +0xf4 ---

  RAX at 0x140533ec9 is the return value of:

    140533eb3  e8a86dffff   CALL 0x14052ac60

  0x14052ac60 resolves to
    CDataCaoTraitement::GetExecutedElmt
    ?GetExecutedElmt@CDataCaoTraitement@@QEAAPEAVCCAD_Base@@V?$CStringT@...@ATL@@JJ@Z
  whose mangled return type is `PEAVCCAD_Base@@`, i.e. a `CCAD_Base*`.  The call
  arguments are set at 0x140533ea7..0x140533eb0 (R8D = GetChamp_Info_Nature result,
  R9D = R15D, RDX = the field-name string from GetChamp_Info_Nom, RCX = RSI = document).

  So the store copies:

      dword at (executed_element + 0xf4)   ->   dword at (array_element  + 0xf4)

  i.e. it propagates the executed element's flag dword up into the array element that
  the selector test is about to consult.  The write is a plain 32-bit move, not an OR
  and not an AND -- it is a wholesale overwrite, so any pre-existing value in the array
  element's +0xf4 dword is discarded, not merged.

  What the flag dword means is not established by anything inside PV_EnvoiMacros.  The
  surrounding log strings are consistent with a "section validity" flag -- the append
  path at
    1405340a1  4c8d0538b29100  LEA R8,[0x140e4f2e0]
  loads "Macro: <%s> - Elmt <%s>_<%d> not tested.\n", and the JBE target block at
    1405342ac  4c8d055db09100  LEA R8,[0x140e4f310]
  loads "Macro: <%s><%d> bad section.\n" -- but that is correlation, not proof, and no
  field declaration for offset 0xf4 of the 0x330-stride element type is visible from
  inside this function.

--- The guards on the store (why it is conditional) ---

  140533ee8 is reached only through three conditions, in this order:

  (1) GetExecutedElmt returned non-NULL:

        140533eb8  4c8bf0        MOV R14,RAX
        140533ebb  4885c0        TEST RAX,RAX
        140533ebe  0f8471010000  JZ 0x140534035

      If it returned NULL, control goes to 0x140534035, whose block ends at
        1405340d3  e9f5010000  JMP 0x1405342cd
      and therefore never reaches 0x1405340f7.  For such an element there is neither a
      store nor a test.

  (2) The inner field index EBX equals 1:

        140533ec4  83fb01        CMP EBX,0x1
        140533ec7  7526          JNZ 0x140533eef
        140533ec9  8b80f4000000  MOV EAX,dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4]
        ...
        140533ee8  89840af4000000  MOV dword ptr [RDX + RCX*0x1 + 0xf4],EAX

      EBX is the inner loop's field index, NOT the incoming selector.  It is 1 on the
      first pass: the two entries into the inner loop head 0x140533e00 are the
      fall-through from 0x140533df6 (first element, R8D set to 1 by
      140533d53 LEA R8D,[RDX+0x1] with RDX=0) and
        1405342e9  443bf9       CMP R15D,ECX
        1405342ec  0f8e0efbffff  JLE 0x140533e00
      (each zone re-entry, R8D set to 1 immediately before by
        1405342d2  41b801000000  MOV R8D,0x1).
      0x140533e03 MOV EBX,R8D is skipped on the loop back edge
        14053402e  ffc3          INC EBX
        140534030  e9d1fdffff    JMP 0x140533e06
      so EBX advances 1,2,3,... within a pass.  Hence the store fires only on the first
      field of each pass.

  (3) A bounds assertion, between the load and the store, which throws rather than
      proceeding:

        140533ecf  4c3bae080f0000  CMP R13,qword ptr [RSI + 0xf08]
        140533ed6  0f8d44040000    JGE 0x140534320
        140533edc  488b8e000f0000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RSI + 0xf00]
        140533ee3  488b542440      MOV RDX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x40]
        140533ee8  89840af4000000  MOV dword ptr [RDX + RCX*0x1 + 0xf4],EAX
      0x140534320 is CALL 0x14077f6a6 = MFC140.DLL::AfxThrowInvalidArgException.

--- Ordering: does the store always precede the test in the same iteration? ---

  0x1405340f7 has exactly one predecessor, and it is not a fall-through:

    preds(0x1405340d8) = { 0x140533e36 JA }
    preds(0x140534105) = { 0x1405340ff fallthrough (JBE) }

  and the instruction immediately above 0x1405340d8 is
    1405340d3  e9f5010000  JMP 0x1405342cd
  an unconditional jump, so it contributes no fall-through.  The single entry is
  therefore:

    140533e2a  ff15e0918200      CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d010]   ; PTR_NbChamp_140d5d010
    140533e30  4863cb            MOVSXD RCX,EBX
    140533e33  483bc8            CMP RCX,RAX
    140533e36  0f879c020000      JA  0x1405340d8

  i.e. the test block runs only after EBX has run PAST the element's field count
  (NbChamp), on the first inner iteration where EBX > NbChamp.  So within one outer
  element iteration the sequence is: EBX==1 store (possibly repeated once per zone
  pass), EBX=2..NbChamp field processing, then EBX>NbChamp, then the selector test.

  Consequence, and it is a real caveat rather than a formality:  if
  NbChamp(element) == 0, then EBX=1 > 0 on the very first inner iteration, the JA at
  0x140533e36 fires before 0x140533ee8 is ever reached, and the test at 0x1405340f7
  reads a dword that this function did NOT write during this outer iteration -- it is
  whatever was left there previously.  The same is true, for a different reason, when
  GetExecutedElmt returns NULL on every zone pass of the element (path 1 above): then
  the test is skipped rather than reading a stale value.

  So: the store feeds the test in the normal case, but "the test always sees what the
  store wrote" is not universally true for this function.

--- Program-wide cross-check on the negative half ---

  To confirm 0x140533ee8 is the only writer of this dword *within PV_EnvoiMacros*, the
  whole 393-instruction body was scanned for displacement 0xf4 (3 hits, above).  A
  program-wide search of Vision3D.exe for `0xf4` returns 123 hits across the binary,
  including these other stores to a dword at displacement 0xf4:

    1404a41bd  c787f400000064000000  MOV  dword ptr [RDI + 0xf4],0x64
    1404a4202  c783f400000064000000  MOV  dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],0x64
    1404a489a  c787f400000064000000  MOV  dword ptr [RDI + 0xf4],0x64
    1404d1cc5  8987f4000000         MOV  dword ptr [RDI + 0xf4],EAX
    140526adb  c780f400000001000000  MOV  dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],0x1
    1405274b7  c780f400000001000000  MOV  dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],0x1
    1405413cc  83a3f4000000fe       AND  dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],0xfffffffe
    140541460  83a3f4000000fd       AND  dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],0xfffffffd
    1405415d8  099ff4000000         OR   dword ptr [RDI + 0xf4],EBX
    140541836  099ff4000000         OR   dword ptr [RDI + 0xf4],EBX
    14054199b  83a1f4000000fe       AND  dword ptr [RCX + 0xf4],0xfffffffe
    1405419ab  83a1f4000000fd       AND  dword ptr [RCX + 0xf4],0xfffffffd

  Whether any of those aliases the 0x330-stride array element at [RSI+0xf00] cannot be
  determined without leaving PV_EnvoiMacros, so it was NOT determined.  Per the scope
  instruction this analysis stopped inside PV_EnvoiMacros.  The bit 0 / bit 1
  manipulation in the 0x140541xxx group is suggestive of a shared flag-dword idiom but
  is not evidence about this element type.

--- Correction to the previous section ("PV_EnvoiMacros selector 3") ---

  That section wrote that "EBX==3 corresponds to selector 3" and treated EBX as the
  selector.  That is wrong and this section is what corrects it.  Two distinct values
  are in play:

    - the incoming selector, EDX at entry, spilled by
      140533c90  MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x10],EDX  and read back once, as a bitmask,
      at 0x1405340f1 into ECX;
    - EBX, the inner field index, 1..NbChamp, entirely independent of the selector.

  Nothing in this function compares EBX against 3.  The ordering established above --
  EBX==1 does the store, EBX>NbChamp does the test -- is the accurate account, and it
  is the ordering that matters for the question asked here.

--- Verification of quoted encodings ---

  Every `ADDR  BYTES` pair above was re-read from the Ghidra listing for
  0x140533c90..0x1405343ab and matched before this text was appended.  Control-flow
  claims were cross-checked three ways: full listing scan for displacement 0xf4, an
  explicit predecessor enumeration with unconditional JMPs excluded from the
  fall-through set, and a structural enumeration of every access to [RSP+0x40] and
  [RSI+0xf00] in the function.

===== Executed element flag =====

--- ANSWER ---

  NO. There is not a single store to displacement 0xf4 anywhere in
  CDataCaoTraitement::GetExecutedElmt (0x14052ac60..0x14052af28, 174 instructions).

  Stronger than that: the function performs exactly ten stores, and every one of them
  targets the stack frame.  It does not write to ANY object field at all.  And a raw
  scan of all 713 bytes of the function body finds no 0xf4 byte anywhere -- so there is
  not even a displacement-0xf4 load, not even a 0xf4 immediate, and not even a
  narrower-width access that would touch part of such a dword.

  Consequences for the "Macro flag dword" section, stated honestly below.

--- The ten stores, all to the stack ---

    14052ac63  48895010          MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x10],RDX
    14052ac67  48894808          MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x8],RCX
    14052ac7a  48c740a0feffffff  MOV qword ptr [RAX + -0x60],-0x2
    14052ac82  48895818          MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x18],RBX
    14052ac94  896888            MOV dword ptr [RAX + -0x78],EBP
    14052ac99  48897c2428        MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x28],RDI
    14052ad2e  896c2420          MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x20],EBP
    14052ae02  48897c2428        MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x28],RDI
    14052aec6  f30f7f442440      MOVDQU xmmword ptr [RSP + 0x40],XMM0
    14052aecc  48c744245000000000  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x50],0x0

  RAX is the stack pointer for the whole prologue:

    14052ac60  488bc4        MOV RAX,RSP
    14052ac63  48895010      MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x10],RDX
    14052ac67  48894808      MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x8],RCX

  and the frame is 7 pushes (0x40) plus 0x14052ac76 4883ec60 SUB RSP,0x60, so
  RSP_final = RSP_entry - 0xa0 and RAX = RSP_entry throughout.  Every [RAX + ...] and
  [RSP + ...] destination above is therefore a stack slot or a register home slot.
  There is no `[REG + disp]` store in the function.

  How the ten were enumerated: every instruction in the body was classified by
  mnemonic (MOV 51, PUSH 7, SUB 9, XOR 6, IMUL 2, SAR 6, SHR 2, ADD 5, JZ 6, LEA 5,
  CALL 19, NOP 2, TEST 8, OR 1, JNZ 4, CMP 13, JMP 3, AND 1, INC 2, JC 5, JA 2, JNC 3,
  JBE 2, XORPS 1, MOVDQU 1, POP 7, RET 1) and then each one was checked for a memory
  operand in destination position.  29 instructions have a memory operand in operand 0,
  but 19 of those are CALL / TEST / CMP / NOP where the memory operand is a source or a
  call target, not a destination.  The 10 above are the real stores.  PUSH/POP are
  frame maintenance and are not counted.

--- Independent raw-byte confirmation ---

  The 713 raw bytes 0x14052ac60..0x14052af28 were read and scanned independently of
  the disassembly:

    - occurrences of the disp32 pattern f4000000 (little-endian 0xf4): ZERO
    - occurrences of the single byte f4 anywhere in the body:                    ZERO

  The second check subsumes the first for a positive displacement, because a disp8 of
  0xf4 would be interpreted as the signed byte -12 and would render as -0xc, and any
  immediate or index using 0xf4 would still contain the byte f4.  There is none.  So
  the negative does not rest on the decompiler's rendering of the listing.

--- Which object fields the function does touch ---

  GetExecutedElmt is a lookup.  It walks the 0x28-stride vector at this+0x2448,
  calling a helper once per element to build a local pointer vector, then scanning that
  local vector.  The object it eventually returns is loaded at

    14052ad10  488b3cf1  MOV RDI,qword ptr [RCX + RSI*0x8]

  and the ONLY fields of RDI it ever dereferences are:

    14052ad1a  488b07        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]              ; +0x00  vtable
    14052ad14  44857f08      TEST dword ptr [RDI + 0x8],R15D      ; +0x08  dword, bitmask test
    14052ad4b  44397714      CMP dword ptr [RDI + 0x14],R14D      ; +0x14  dword, equality test

  plus the implicit vtable dispatch at +0x48.  Offsets +0x00, +0x08 and +0x14 only.
  +0xf4 is never read and never written.

  Argument mapping, from the prologue:

    14052ac89  458bf8        MOV R15D,R8D     ; R15D = param_3, the bitmask
    14052ac86  458bf1        MOV R14D,R9D     ; R14D = param_4, the compared index
    14052ac8c  4c8be2        MOV R12,RDX      ; R12   = param_2, the CStringT*
    14052ac8f  488bd9        MOV RBX,RCX      ; RBX   = this

  which matches the decompiled body: `(*(uint *)(pCVar1 + 8) & param_3) != 0` and
  `*(int *)(pCVar1 + 0x14) == param_4`.  Note that param_3 is used as a BITMASK here,
  the same shape as the selector that PV_EnvoiMacros applies at 0x1405340f7.

  Document fields read: this+0x2448 and this+0x2450 only --

    14052ac9e  4c8b8150240000  MOV R8,qword ptr [RCX + 0x2450]
    14052aca5  4c2b8148240000  SUB R8,qword ptr [RCX + 0x2448]
    14052acd0  488b8b48240000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]
    14052ae0b  488b8b50240000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
    14052ae12  482b8b48240000  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]

  both read-only.

--- What the function does instead: two callees it invokes ---

  19 CALL sites.  Resolved:

    14052ace2  e859faffff      CALL 0x14052a740                 (unnamed helper)
    14052ad25  ff5048          CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x48]      (VIRTUAL, on RDI)
    14052ad35  ff15ed438300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f128]     operator char const*
    14052ad41  ff1589438300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0d0]     CStringT::Compare
    14052ad5f  ff1593438300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]     ~CStringT (local result)
    14052adfa  e8af462500      CALL 0x14077f4ae                 MFC140.DLL::operator_delete
    14052aebe  e8eb452500      CALL 0x14077f4ae                 MFC140.DLL::operator_delete
    14052aed8  ff151a428300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]     ~CStringT
    14052af09  ff15e9418300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]     ~CStringT
    9 sites    ff15..298300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d860]     _invalid_parameter_noinfo_noreturn

  The nine `_invalid_parameter_noinfo_noreturn` sites are the inlined std::vector
  deallocation guard checks (size limits, alignment, header sanity); the function is
  non-constraining here because that routine does not return.

  One real side effect on caller-owned memory: the function destroys its second
  argument on BOTH the found and the not-found path.

    14052aed5  498bcc        MOV RCX,R12
    14052aed8  ff151a428300  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]    ; ~CStringT(param_2), found path
    ...
    14052af06  498bcc        MOV RCX,R12
    14052af09  ff15e9418300  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]    ; ~CStringT(param_2), not-found path
    14052af0f  33c0          XOR EAX,EAX                       ; then return 0

  R12 = param_2 (set at 0x14052ac8c).  This is consistent with the caller: in
  PV_EnvoiMacros, RDX is loaded at 0x140533e6d from GetChamp_Info_Nom into [RSP+0x70]
  and the register holding it (R14) is overwritten at 0x140533eb8 with the returned
  element pointer, so the string is indeed handed over.  It is a write to caller memory,
  but not to a 0xf4 dword.

--- The limit, and it is the important one ---

  GetExecutedElmt does not write the flag dword ITSELF, but it does invoke a virtual
  method on the very object it goes on to return:

    14052ad1a  488b07        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]           ; RDI's vtable
    14052ad1d  488d542430    LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x30]              ; out-param: local CStringT
    14052ad22  488bcf        MOV RCX,RDI                       ; this = RDI
    14052ad25  ff5048        CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x48]       ; vtable slot 9

  If that slot-9 method writes the +0xf4 flag dword of RDI, then GetExecutedElmt causes
  the write indirectly, one call frame down, while containing no instruction that does
  it.  Per the scope instruction ("Stop inside GetExecutedElmt") this callee was NOT
  entered and its identity is NOT established.

  The same applies to the unnamed helper:

    14052ace2  e859faffff  CALL 0x14052a740

  called once per 0x28-stride element with (this+0x2448 + offset, &local_vector, 1).
  It populates the local vector whose elements are the candidate objects, so it is the
  most likely place the +0xf4 flags are actually established.  Also NOT entered.

  So the precise statement is:  NO STORE TO DISPLACEMENT 0xf4 EXISTS IN
  GetExecutedElmt; whether the flag reaches the object by the time PV_EnvoiMacros reads
  it at 0x140533ec9 is NOT DETERMINED by this function and depends on those two callees.

--- Consequence for the "Macro flag dword" section ---

  That section established that 0x140533ee8 copies +0xf4 from the GetExecutedElmt result
  into the array element that 0x1405340f7 then bit-tests, and that the copy happens
  earlier in the same outer iteration.  That stands unchanged.  What is now added is
  that the producer of the copied value is not GetExecutedElmt: the value must already
  be present in the object when GetExecutedElmt returns it.  The "Macro flag dword"
  section's phrasing "it propagates the executed element's flag dword" is correct but
  should not be read as implying GetExecutedElmt set it.

--- Method notes ---

  Listing completeness was checked first, because a negative result is worthless on an
  incomplete listing.  The 174 disassembled instructions are NOT byte-contiguous: ten
  one-byte holes exist, at

    0x14052ae71 cc, 0x14052ae8d cc, 0x14052ae9d cc, 0x14052aead cc, 0x14052aeba cc,
    0x14052aee9 cc, 0x14052aef0 cc, 0x14052aef7 cc, 0x14052aefe cc, 0x14052af05 90

  Each was individually read with memory_read and queried with listing_code_unit_at.
  Nine are 0xCC (INT3) and one is 0x90 (NOP); all ten are typed DataDB by Ghidra, i.e.
  padding the disassembler did not fold into the instruction stream.  None of them is
  an instruction and none can write memory, so the negative result is unaffected -- but
  the holes are why the 174 instructions cover 703 of the 713 body bytes.

  Control flow was also checked rather than assumed: 25 branches, all with in-range
  targets, so there is no tail jump to a shared or out-of-line epilogue that could hide
  a store.  There is exactly one RET, at 0x14052af28 (c3).  A negative result here is a
  negative about the whole body, not about the main path only.

===== Executed element virtual flag =====

--- ANSWER ---

  The slot is identified.  CCAD_Base::vftable + 0x48 holds 0x14076d916, which is

    AVMATCHMAKER.DLL::CCAD_Base::_csName

  reached through a six-byte import thunk:

    14076d916  ff25444b5e00  JMP qword ptr [0x140d52460]

  There is NO overriding slot at offset 0x48 on any subclass vftable in this binary.
  All eleven vftables in this image that belong to CCAD_Base and its descendants --
  the base's own plus the ten derived classes that have a vftable here -- store the
  identical pointer 0x14076d916 at +0x48.  The full table is given below.

  For each target, the stores to displacement 0xf4:  THERE ARE NONE, and none can be
  quoted, because the target has no body in Vision3D.exe.  It is six bytes long, one
  instruction, an indirect jump through the IAT.  The implementation lives in
  AVMATCHMAKER.DLL.  So the precise statement is: nothing in this binary writes +0xf4
  on behalf of that call, and whether _csName itself does so at run time is NOT
  DETERMINED by Vision3D.exe.

  This closes the identity half of what the previous section left open, and leaves the
  effect half open.  The two are separated deliberately below.

--- The call site being resolved ---

  Re-quoted from GetExecutedElmt (0x14052ac60..0x14052af28), all encodings re-verified
  against the listing immediately before appending:

    14052ad1a  488b07        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]       ; RDI's own vtable pointer
    14052ad1d  488d542430    LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x30]          ; local CStringT, the result slot
    14052ad22  488bcf        MOV RCX,RDI                   ; this = RDI
    14052ad25  ff5048        CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x48]   ; vtable slot 9

  RAX is loaded from the object itself, so RAX is a vtable pointer and 0x48 is slot
  index 9, counted from the first entry at +0x00.  RDX is pre-loaded with a stack
  address and RDI is the only argument register set, which is the shape of an MSVC x64
  by-value class return: RDX is the hidden return-buffer pointer.  That agrees with the
  demangled signature of the callee found below, and with the ~CStringT call the
  previous section found on that same local.

--- How CCAD_Base's vftable was located ---

  By walking MSVC RTTI.  Every step is a byte-level read, and each structural claim is
  checked by a self-reference rather than assumed.

  TypeDescriptor.  The RTTI name string ".?AVCCAD_Base@@" sits at 0x1410d67d8, so the
  TypeDescriptor is 0x1410d67c8 (name at +0x10).  Read confirms it:

    1410d67c8  1861ee4001000000 0000000000000000 2e3f4156434341445f42617365404000
              +0x00 0x0000000140ee6118   type_info vftable pointer
              +0x08 0x0000000000000000   spare
              +0x10 ".?AVCCAD_Base@@\0"

  Complete Object Locator.  Searching the four-byte RVA of that TypeDescriptor
  (0x010d67c8, little-endian c8 67 0d 01) yields exactly two hits.  Only one is a COL,
  at 0x140f0cd88, and it is self-consistent -- pSelf equals its own address:

    140f0cd88  01000000  signature   = 1
               00000000  offset      = 0
               00000000  cdOffset    = 0
               c8670d01  pTypeDesc    = 0x010d67c8
               8847f000  pClassHier   = 0x00f04788
               88cdf000  pSelf        = 0x00f0cd88

  Class Hierarchy Descriptor.  At 0x140f04788, raw 16 bytes:

    140f04788  00000000 00000000 02000000 a047f000
               +0x00 signature = 0
               +0x04 attributes = 0
               +0x08 numBaseClasses = 2
               +0x0c pBaseClassArray = 0x00f047a0

  Note the layout detail that cost time here: on this build pBaseClassArray is a
  FOUR-BYTE RVA at CHD+12, and the array physically sits at CHD+24.  Neither
  CHD = array-12 nor CHD = array-8 is correct, and both were tried before this was
  pinned by reading the field.  The array is consequently located from its own contents
  rather than by arithmetic.

  Base-class array at 0x140f047a0, raw 8 bytes:

    140f047a0  6047f000 80e2ee00   ->  0x00f04760, 0x00eee280

  Entry 0 is CCAD_Base's own BaseClassDescriptor.  Entry 1, at 0x140eee280, has
  TypeDescriptor 0x1410c78b0 = ".?AVCObject@@", so CCAD_Base derives from CObject.

  vftable.  A vftable's -8 slot holds the absolute address of its COL.  The eight-byte
  little-endian pattern for 0x140f0cd88 is 88cdf04001000000, and it occurs exactly once
  in the whole image, at 0x140e7b9e0:

    140e7b9e0  88cdf04001000000   ->  0x0000000140f0cd88

  so

    CCAD_Base::vftable = 0x140e7b9e8

  Calibration for that step, so it is not a bare assumption: the same test on a vftable
  already independently confirmed, 0x140e4d398, finds its COL pointer at 0x140e4d390 and
  nowhere else, and that vftable's entries are a normal mix of in-module functions
  (0x140521b30, 0x140662340) and import thunks.  Two further independent checks support
  the CCAD_Base vftable specifically: every one of its 36 entries at offsets +0x00
  through +0x118 lands inside .text, and it agrees slot-for-slot with the ten derived
  vftables (same +0x40, +0x48, +0x50 values in all eleven).

--- The function at slot +0x48 ---

    140e7ba30  16d9764001000000   ->  0x000000014076d916

  and the target is:

    14076d916  ff25444b5e00  JMP qword ptr [0x140d52460]   label _csName

  Ghidra's function record for that address:

    thunk        true
    body_start   0x14076d916
    body_end     0x14076d91b
    signature    CStringT<char,StrTraitMFC_DLL<char,ATL::ChTraitsCRT<char>_>_>
                 __thiscall _csName(CCAD_Base * this)
    parameters   this, auto_parameter, /Demangler/CCAD_Base *, storage RCX:8 (auto)

  Following the IAT slot to the loader data:

    140d52460  a4ff080100000000   ->  hint/name RVA 0x0108ffa4
    14108ffa4  ed03 3f5f63734e61...  hint 0x03ed = 1005, name
              ?_csName@CCAD_Base@@UEBA?AV?$CStringT@DV?$StrTraitMFC_DLL@DV?$ChTraitsCRT@D@ATL@@@@@ATL@@@Z

  Ghidra resolves that symbol as AVMATCHMAKER.DLL::CCAD_Base::_csName, which is the
  module it also attributes the thunk to.

  Do not confuse it with the adjacent, differently-signed overload.  Slot +0x40 of every
  one of these vftables holds 0x14076d910:

    14076d910  ff25424b5e00  JMP qword ptr [0x140d52458]   label _csName
    140d52458  46ff080100000000   ->  hint/name RVA 0x0108ff46
    14108ff46  ec03 3f5f63734e61...  hint 0x03ec = 1004, name
              ?_csName@CCAD_Base@@UEAAXV?$CStringT@DV?$StrTraitMFC_DLL@DV?$ChTraitsCRT@D@ATL@@@@@ATL@@@Z

  The two thunks are six bytes apart and both carry the label _csName.  Only the hint
  (1004 vs 1005) and the mangled signature distinguish them: the +0x40 form is declared
  as taking a by-value CStringT and returning void, the +0x48 form as taking nothing and
  returning a CStringT.  Only the +0x48 form is compatible with the call site, which
  sets no argument other than this and treats RAX as a CStringT.

--- Stores to displacement 0xf4 in that target: none exist ---

  There is only one distinct target, 0x14076d916.  Its entire body is:

    14076d916  ff25444b5e00  JMP qword ptr [0x140d52460]

  One instruction.  It contains zero stores: no MOV, PUSH, POP, XCHG, CMPXCHG, string
  operation, or anything else that writes memory.  It writes only RIP and RSP, and jumps
  through the loader-filled IAT slot.  A raw scan of all six bytes, ff 25 44 4b 5e 00,
  finds no 0xf4 byte at any position, so there is not even an unfolded displacement-0xf4
  encoding hiding in the encoding.

  The body is genuinely six bytes and nothing is shared out of line.  body_end is
  0x14076d91b, and the very next address begins a different thunk:

    14076d91c  ff25464b5e00  JMP qword ptr [0x140d52468]   label _csNameBibTrait

  So there is no tail jump to a shared epilogue and no second chunk of code.  The
  decompiler says the same thing:

    void __thiscall CCAD_Base::_csName(CCAD_Base *this)
    {
        /* WARNING: Could not recover jumptable at 0x00014076d916. Too many branches */
        /* WARNING: Treating indirect jump as call */
      _csName(this);
      return;
    }

  The requested enumeration therefore comes back empty, and for a stronger reason than a
  negative scan: there is no function here to scan.  The +0xf4 question is not answered
  by this binary; it is relocated to AVMATCHMAKER.DLL.

--- No subclass overrides slot 0x48 (the full table) ---

  Completeness argument first, because "no override" is worth nothing without it.

  Any class inheriting CCAD_Base must contain CCAD_Base's BaseClassDescriptor in its own
  base-class array.  This is verified structurally rather than assumed, from
  CCAD_ZoneMatriciel, whose array is { CCAD_ZoneMatriciel, CCAD_Zone, CCAD_Base, CObject }
  -- CCAD_Base appears alongside the intermediate base, not instead of it.  A
  program-wide byte search for CCAD_Base's BCD RVA 0x00f04760 (little-endian
  60 47 f0 00) returns exactly 13 hits:

    140f046b8  140f04744  140f047a0  140f047fc  140f04884  140f0490c  140f04994
    140f04a1c  140f04b24  140f04e58  140f04ee4  140f0cdf4  140f15af0

  all inside the RTTI blob 0x140f00000..0x140f18000.  A hit need not be the array's first
  entry -- for example 0x140f047fc is index 1 of an array starting at 0x140f047f8 -- so
  for each hit the array start was identified from the 4-byte entries and then confirmed
  by the hierarchy descriptor whose pBaseClassArray field names exactly that address.  The
  13 hits resolve to 13 distinct hierarchies.  Eleven have a Complete Object Locator in
  this image and therefore a vftable here; two do not, and are listed at the end of this
  subsection.

  For each of the eleven, the qword at vftable+0x48 and its raw bytes:

    class                COL          vftable     slot+0x48   bytes at slot
    CCAD_Base            0x140f0cd88  0x140e7b9e8 0x140e7ba30 16d9764001000000
    CGroupPad            0x140f04670  0x140e4cd28 0x140e4cd70 16d9764001000000
    CComposant           0x140f047b8  0x140e4ca28 0x140e4ca70 16d9764001000000
    CPad                 0x140f04840  0x140e4cba8 0x140e4cbf0 16d9764001000000

    CSkip_bloc           0x140f049d8  0x140e4d1e8 0x140e4d230 16d9764001000000
    CMacro               0x140f04ae0  0x140e4d398 0x140e4d3e0 16d9764001000000
    CCAD_ZoneMatriciel   0x140f04e10  0x140e4d638 0x140e4d680 16d9764001000000
    CAD_Region           0x140f0cdb0  0x140e7bb68 0x140e7bbb0 16d9764001000000
    CCAD_OCV_Reader      0x140f15aa8  0x140eb9198 0x140eb91e0 16d9764001000000

  Every row is the same eight bytes, 0x000000014076d916.  Every COL has offset 0 and
  cdOffset 0, so slot index 9 means the same thing in every row and no
  multiple-inheritance vbase offset shifts the numbering.  The chains, read from the
  base-class arrays:

    CCAD_Base            < CObject
    CGroupPad            < CCAD_BaseContainer < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CComposant           < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CPad                 < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CDataMatrixInt       < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CMire                < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CSkip_bloc           < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CMacro               < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CCAD_ZoneMatriciel   < CCAD_Zone < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CAD_Region           < CCAD_Base < CObject
    CCAD_OCV_Reader      < CCAD_BaseContainer < CCAD_Base < CObject

  So the answer to "name any overriding slot at the same offset on a subclass vftable"
  is: there is none.  The surrounding slots are read to show this is a real measurement
  and not a constant being echoed.  Offsets +0x40 (0x14076d910) and +0x50 (0x14076d8ce)
  are likewise constant across all eleven, but offset +0x30 takes eight distinct values:

    0x14076d8c8  CCAD_Base, CGroupPad, CMacro, CCAD_ZoneMatriciel
    0x14076e006  CComposant
    0x14076e00c  CDataMatrixInt
    0x14076e012  CMire
    0x14076e018  CPad
    0x14076e01e  CSkip_bloc
    0x14076e1e6  CAD_Region
    0x14076e23a  CCAD_OCV_Reader

  and offset +0x58 takes four: 0x14076d91c for eight of them, but 0x14076e1a4 for
  CGroupPad, 0x14076e1b6 for CMire and 0x14076e1bc for CSkip_bloc.  The tables genuinely
  differ; slot +0x48 is the one that does not.

  The two remaining hierarchies name CCAD_Base but contribute no vftable here:

    CCAD_BaseContainer    CHD 0x140f04728, array { CCAD_BaseContainer, CCAD_Base, CObject }
    CCAD_Zone             CHD 0x140f04ec8, array { CCAD_Zone, CCAD_Base, CObject }

  Each has a BaseClassDescriptor in this image, referenced by the arrays of classes
  defined here, but neither has a Complete Object Locator here.  For CCAD_BaseContainer
  the only reference to its CHD RVA is at 0x140f04718, which is the pClassHDescriptor
  field of the BCD at 0x140f04700 rather than a COL pCHD field: reading a supposed COL
  at 0x140f04718-16 = 0x140f04708 yields signature 0, so there is no COL and no vftable.
  Same shape for CCAD_Zone, whose CHD RVA occurs once, at 0x140f04eb8 -- the
  pClassHDescriptor of its own BCD at 0x140f04ea0 -- and a supposed COL at 0x140f04ea8
  likewise reads signature 0.

--- What this settles, and what it does not ---

  Settled.  The call at 0x14052ad25 is no longer an unknown.  For every
  CCAD_Base-derived vftable that exists in Vision3D.exe it dispatches to
  CCAD_Base::_csName, imported from AVMATCHMAKER.DLL, taking only this and returning a
  CStringT by value.  Nothing local executes between the vtable load and the call, and
  nothing local executes inside the target either.

  Not settled: whether _csName writes displacement 0xf4 on the object.  Its body is in
  AVMATCHMAKER.DLL.  The signature is not evidence either way -- a getter-looking name
  and a CStringT return do not exclude a this+0xf4 side effect, and only the DLL can
  settle it.  So the edge left open by the previous section stands as open: the +0xf4
  flag read by PV_EnvoiMacros at 0x140533ec9 may be established by _csName, or not, and
  this binary cannot say which.

  Not settled, and this is a real limit rather than a formality.  The eleven vftables
  cover the classes whose RTTI is compiled into this image, i.e. the CCAD_Base
  descendants defined in Vision3D.exe.  CCAD_Zone and CCAD_BaseContainer are known
  descendants whose vftables are demonstrably not here, and nothing rules out further
  descendants defined wholly in another DLL, whose base-class arrays would live there
  too and would therefore not appear in the 13 hits.  If the receiver of the
  0x14052ad25 call is such an object, its vftable could override slot 9 and this binary
  cannot rule that out.  What can be said is narrower and still useful: for every
  vftable in this image that the call could resolve to, the target is the same
  import thunk and the local store count is zero.

  Still open from before, unchanged.  The other callee in GetExecutedElmt,
  FUN_14052a740 at 0x14052ace2, which populates the candidate vector, remains unentered
  and remains the more likely producer of those flags.

--- Correction to the previous section ("Executed element flag") ---

  The previous section stated that the identity of the slot-9 callee was NOT
  established.  It now is: AVMATCHMAKER.DLL::CCAD_Base::_csName.  What the previous
  section got right, and this section confirms, is that GetExecutedElmt contains no
  store to displacement 0xf4 and no store to any object field at all.

  A second correction, to an intermediate reading recorded here rather than earlier in
  the file: CCAD_Base is NOT purely external.  Resolving the symbol name yields
  VITDATACAD.DLL::CCAD_Base::CCAD_Base at EXTERNAL:000016f2, which invites the conclusion
  that the class and its vftable live in another module.  That conclusion is wrong.
  CCAD_Base's TypeDescriptor, Class Hierarchy Descriptor, BaseClassDescriptor, Complete
  Object Locator and vftable are all present in Vision3D.exe, and the vftable is well
  formed.  What is external is the implementation of slot 9, which the linker left as an
  import thunk into AVMATCHMAKER.DLL.  A class defined here can have an imported virtual
  method; the two facts are independent, and only the second is true here.

--- Method notes ---

  Two false negatives were caught and corrected before anything was appended.  Both are
  recorded because each would have produced a confidently wrong answer rather than an
  error.

  The first was an arithmetic bug in the byte-pattern builder used for the image
  searches: it shifted with the JavaScript >> operator, which is modulo 32, so every
  8-byte pointer above 0xffffffff produced a corrupted pattern.  That made CCAD_Base's
  COL look unreferenced (0 hits) when it is referenced exactly once.  Calibrating the
  builder against a known-good vftable, whose COL pointer had been confirmed by direct
  read, exposed it.  Every search result used in this section came from the corrected
  builder.

  The second was the RTTI layout.  Two earlier hypotheses -- vftable = COL+32, and
  pBaseClassArray as a 64-bit pointer at CHD+12 -- were both wrong for this image, and
  both produced empty candidate lists rather than errors.  The resolution used instead is
  self-referential and does not depend on guessing offsets: a COL is accepted only when
  its pSelf field equals its own address, and a hierarchy is reached through an array
  located by its contents.  The calibration vftable 0x140e4d398 was used to confirm the
  "-8 holds the COL" convention before relying on it.  Relatedly, the 64 bytes
  immediately preceding CCAD_Base's vftable were at one point treated as disqualifying
  the -8 slot; they are 4-byte RVA and small-integer values, including the MSVC
  exception magic dword 0x19930522 at 0x140e7b9b8, and they end at 0x140e7b9df,
  immediately before the COL pointer.  They do not contradict the vftable, and the
  vftable does not rest on them.

  Every ADDR + BYTES line quoted in this section was re-read and compared against the
  Ghidra listing immediately before appending.

===== END =====

===== Candidate vector helper flag =====

Question: does FUN_14052a740 write displacement 0xf4?
Where: Vision3D.exe, copy project v3d_files_uncomp_copy/V3D_SKIP, program
/Vision3D.exe, opened read-only with update_analysis false. Mode confirmed
read_only true, active_transaction null. Nothing saved.
Scope: analysis stops at the FUN_14052a740 boundary as instructed.

ANSWER: No. FUN_14052a740 contains no store to displacement 0xf4. It contains
no memory operand with displacement 0xf4 at all, in any width.

Exhaustive 0xf4 search, three independent modalities
----------------------------------------------------
(1) Raw byte scan of the 236 body bytes.
    Occurrences of the byte 0xf4: exactly ONE.

    rendered branch target, so the byte is confirmed as a branch displacement
    and not a memory operand.

    The query does find 0xf4 operands, including the known writer at

      RSP+0x10  RSP+0x38  RSP+0x50  RSP+0x60  RSP+0x68  RSP+0x30

      0x8, 0x10, 0x19, 0x20, 0x28, 0x30, 0x38, 0x50, 0x60, 0x68
    0xf4 is not among them.

Complete store inventory, 11 stores
-----------------------------------
Classified by operand position, not by mnemonic. Every memory-referencing
instruction in this body is a MOV, so the mnemonic alone cannot separate a
load from a store; a first pass that filtered on mnemonic mislabelled 13
loads as stores and was discarded. The 11 stores below were re-derived from
the destination operand only.

Stores to the stack frame only:
  14052a740  4889542410          MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x10],RDX
  14052a74b  48c7442438feffffff  MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x38],-0x2
  14052a754  48895c2450          MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x50],RBX
  14052a759  4889742460          MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x60],RSI
  14052a75e  48897c2468          MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x68],RDI
  14052a76f  89442430            MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x30],EAX
  14052a77e  c744243001000000    MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x30],0x1
  14052a7ac  88442420            MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x20],AL
  Context: RSP+0x50/0x60/0x68 are the callee-saved RBX/RSI/RDI spill slots,
  matching PUSH R14 / SUB RSP,0x40 at 0x14052a745 and 0x14052a747. RSP+0x10
  is the shadow-space home for RDX, not frame scratch. RSP+0x30 receives 0
  then 1, and RSP+0x20 receives AL, which is 0 from XOR EAX,EAX.

Stores to the out-parameter vector header only, RSI = RDX = argument 2:
  14052a773  488902             MOV qword ptr [RDX],RAX
  14052a776  48894208           MOV qword ptr [RDX + 0x8],RAX
  14052a77a  48894210           MOV qword ptr [RDX + 0x10],RAX
  RAX is 0 here, set by XOR EAX,EAX at 0x14052a76d, so all three stores are
  the same store. 24 bytes zeroed, which is emptying a three-pointer vector
  header. RSI was given the value of RDX at 0x14052a767, MOV RSI,RDX.

Stores to any heap object field: NONE.
  RCX, R14 and RBX are dereferenced only by loads, plus one comparison:
    14052a80e  493b1e        CMP RBX,qword ptr [R14]
  No store instruction in this body uses RCX, R14 or RBX as a base register.

Mnemonic census of the body, 66 instructions:
  MOV 32, CMP 11, JNZ 7, JZ 5, XOR 2, PUSH 1, SUB 1, MOVZX 1, TEST 1,
  CALL 1, JMP 1, ADD 1, POP 1, RET 1

What the body actually does, from the instruction stream
---------------------------------------------------------
  Zero the 24-byte vector header at argument 2:
    14052a773  488902             MOV qword ptr [RDX],RAX

    14052a79a  4080ff01           CMP DIL,0x1

  The single append, one call in the whole body:

    14052a7b0  4c8b4b30         MOV R9,qword ptr [RBX + 0x30]
    14052a7b4  4c8b4328         MOV R8,qword ptr [RBX + 0x28]

    Arguments are (out-vector, its current end pointer, node value +0x28,
