===== Element base copy =====

Question: which call copies bytes over offset 0xf00 of the object PV_EnvoiMacros reads?
Find the function that stores the CDataCaoTraitement vftable, and the constructors of
CDocCompose and CProductionDoc. In each, quote every memcpy, memmove, memset, or REP MOVS
whose destination is that object and whose length is greater than 0xf00. Quote the length.
If a constant length is not greater than 0xf00, skip it. Stop at the first call that covers
offset 0xf00. If none of the three functions has one, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  NONE OF THE THREE HAS SUCH A CALL. There is no call to quote, so there is no length to
  quote and no call that covers offset 0xf00.

    function                                   copy primitives found
    -----------------------------------------  ----------------------
    CDataCaoTraitement ctor (0x14051df90)      NONE - zero calls, zero REP MOVS
    CDocCompose ctor (FUN_1405cb880)           ONE, and it is skipped - see below
    CProductionDoc ctor (FUN_14067dea0)        NONE - zero calls, zero REP MOVS

  The single copy primitive in the three is a memset in the CDocCompose constructor, and it
  fails BOTH halves of your test: its destination is not the object, and its length is not
  greater than 0xf00. Section 2.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Locating the three functions
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Each was found by walking RTTI rather than by guessing from a name, because two of the
  three have no symbol.

  The type descriptors were located by exact-match search for the mangled name, then the
  complete-object-locator was found by scanning .rdata for the 4-byte RVA of the type
  descriptor, and the vftable is the 8 bytes immediately after the slot that holds the COL
  pointer. Every COL was validated with `sig == 1` and `COL == imagebase + pSelfRVA`, and
  every vftable[-1] was read back and confirmed to hold that COL address:

    class              TypeDescriptor   COL          vftable
    -----------------  ---------------  -----------  -----------
    CDataCaoTraitement  0x1410d79f8      0x140f04cd8  0x140e4d8a0
    CDocCompose         0x1410da268      0x140f0a268  0x140e76078
    CProductionDoc      0x1410df988      0x140f12e78  0x140ea3868

  The functions that store those vftables, found by searching the rendered instruction text
  for each vftable address and re-deriving the target from the disp32:

      14051dfcc  488d05cdf89200  LEA RAX,[0x140e4d8a0]   -> 0x140e4d8a0  in  CDataCaoTraitement  0x14051df90..0x14051e54b
      1405cb8af  488d05c2a78a00  LEA RAX,[0x140e76078]   -> 0x140e76078  in  FUN_1405cb880       0x1405cb880..0x1405cbf15
      14067decc  488d0595598200  LEA RAX,[0x140ea3868]   -> 0x140ea3868  in  FUN_14067dea0       0x14067dea0..0x14067f879

  So the function that stores the CDataCaoTraitement vftable is the CDataCaoTraitement
  constructor at 0x14051df90, and the CDocCompose and CProductionDoc constructors are
  FUN_1405cb880 and FUN_14067dea0. Each also has a matching destructor that stores the same
  vftable (~CDataCaoTraitement at 0x14051fbf0, FUN_1405cc710, FUN_14067fc20); the question
  asked for constructors, so the destructors were not searched for copy primitives.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. The one copy primitive, and why it is skipped
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The CDocCompose constructor contains exactly one call to a copy primitive:

      1405cbbf4  b950010000        MOV ECX,0x150
      1405cbbf9  e852191a00        CALL 0x14076d550
      1405cbbfe  488bd8            MOV RBX,RAX
      1405cbc01  4889456f          MOV qword ptr [RBP + 0x6f],RAX
      1405cbc05  4885c0            TEST RAX,RAX
      1405cbc08  7425              JZ 0x1405cbc2f
      1405cbc0a  33d2              XOR EDX,EDX
      1405cbc0c  41b850010000      MOV R8D,0x150
      1405cbc12  488bc8            MOV RCX,RAX
      1405cbc15  e830a61d00        CALL 0x1407a624a
        0x1407a624a  void * __cdecl memset(void * _Dst, int _Val, size_t _Size)

  Reading the three arguments in MSVC x64 order:

      RCX = RAX   = the return of `operator new(0x150)` at 0x1405cbbf9
      EDX = 0     = the fill value
      R8D = 0x150 = the length

  So this is `memset(new_object, 0, 0x150)`. It fails your test on both counts:

    - DESTINATION. RCX is RAX, the freshly allocated block, not `this`. The allocation is
      0x150 bytes and the pointer is kept in RBX and in a local at [RBP + 0x6f]; the CDocCompose
      object itself is never the destination. This is a sub-object being zero-filled, not a
      copy over the document.
    - LENGTH. 0x150 = 336, which is NOT greater than 0xf00 = 3840. Per your rule, skipped.

  For completeness, the other two constructors were searched the same way and contain no call
  to any of memcpy, memmove, memset or memcmp, and no REP-prefixed string move at all:

      CDataCaoTraitement ctor  0x14051df90..0x14051e54b   354 instructions   0 copy primitives
      CProductionDoc ctor       0x14067dea0..0x14067f879  1291 instructions   0 copy primitives

  The CDataCaoTraitement constructor's calls are all sub-object constructions - CDocument,
  CStringArray, CMap, SAcquisitionCapabilities, CUIntArray, CMapStringToString - and the
  CProductionDoc constructor's are likewise container and member initialisations. Neither
  performs a bulk copy over the object.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. What this means for the chain
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The previous section established that nothing in Vision3D.exe writes the qword at
  [this + 0xf00] by any store, ADD, or LEA. This section closes the last obvious
  alternative: a bulk copy that would cover it without ever naming the offset.

  It does not. So the value PV_EnvoiMacros reads at [this + 0xf00] is not written by any
  code in this binary by any mechanism I have now checked - not a direct store, not an
  address computation, and not a bulk copy. The remaining possibilities are outside what I
  can see from here: a write from another module (this program imports 67 DLLs), a write to
  a different object than the one PV_EnvoiMacros is called on, or runtime-generated code.

  I am recording that as the state of the question rather than picking one of those, because
  each of them is a different investigation and none is supported by evidence in hand.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Every instruction encoding quoted was extracted from this payload by regex, not
    hand-listed, and each re-read with a fresh memory_read and compared byte for byte.
  * The three vftable addresses were re-derived from the disp32 of their LEA instructions,
    and each vftable[-1] was read back and confirmed to hold the COL address found by the
    RTTI walk. The LEA helper self-tests on the instruction lengths in use and takes the
    length from the bytes rather than assuming it.
  * The three COLs were validated with `sig == 1` and `COL == imagebase + pSelfRVA`, and the
    type descriptor RVA was checked against the address the byte scan found.
  * The copy-primitive search covered all four CRT names (memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp) by
    resolved signature, plus a separate scan for REP-prefixed string moves, in all three
    constructors. The detector is proven live: it found the memset above, which is a real call
    to a real named function, so a zero elsewhere is a measurement and not a dead detector.
  * FOUR ERRORS I MADE AND DISCARDED this session, all in the RTTI walk, and all of which
    produced plausible-looking output rather than a failure:
      - I assumed the COL sits immediately before the vftable and computed vftable = COL + 8.
        Reading the candidate showed its first entries were the COL's own fields repeated back,
        which is not a vftable. The correct relation is that the 8 bytes at vftable[-1] HOLD A
        POINTER TO the COL; the two are separate allocations. I then searched .rdata for the
        4-byte RVA of the type descriptor to locate the COL, which is the standard approach.
      - My little-endian byte encoder used `>>>`, which truncates to 32 bits, so for addresses
        above 2^31 it produced the wrong pattern and the scan returned zero hits. Fixed by
        using division and modulo instead of shifts. This is the same truncation that produced
        a spurious 0x100000000 in an earlier section of this file.
      - I searched for the RVA's hex STRING instead of its little-endian BYTES, so the pattern
        was the reverse of what was needed. That is the fourth separate encoding mistake in
        this file, and the reason the rule I now apply is that byte patterns are always built
        from the value in code, never typed.
      - Twice I hand-computed the expected LE bytes of an address and got it wrong, so my own
        self-test failed while the encoder was correct. I replaced the hand-computed
        expectations with one grounded in bytes already verified in an earlier section - the
        disp32 `24 c3 8f 00` at 0x14055a965, which is LE of 0x008fc324 and sums with its
        next-instruction address to the already-verified 0x140e56c90.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The three destructors were not searched. The question asked for constructors, and a
    destructor performing a bulk copy over the object would be unusual, but I did not check
    and am not claiming anything about them.
  * "No copy primitive in the constructor" is a statement about calls to the four CRT names
    and REP string moves. A copy performed by an inlined loop of ordinary MOVs would not be
    caught by either scan. Given that the previous section already showed the address
    `this + 0xf00` is never computed into a register, an inlined loop would still have to form
    that address somehow, so this is a weakened possibility rather than an open one - but I
    did not prove it closed.
  * I did not verify that the three vftable-storing functions are the ONLY constructors of
    their classes. A second constructor, or a constructor in another translation unit, could
    exist. What I verified is that these are the functions that store the vftable, and that
    they contain no qualifying copy.
  * The memset's destination being a fresh allocation is read from the register flow
    (RCX = RAX = return of operator new). I did not check what that 0x150-byte object is or
    where it is kept, only that it is not the CDocCompose object.

===== Large object copies =====

Question: which other function copies a range longer than 0xf00 onto one of these objects?
The three constructors and their destructors are already checked: 0x14051df90, 0x14051fbf0,

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer

  THERE ARE THREE, AND NONE OF THEM IS ONTO ONE OF THE THREE CLASSES.

  Every copy in the binary whose length is a constant greater than 0xf00:

    #  length   primitive  function      destination

  has either. That is stated as a limit in section 5, not papered over.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Coverage - what was searched and how completely
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Three families of copy, located by their resolved call target, not by name pattern:

    memcpy    thunk 0x1407a6244, `JMP qword ptr [0x140d5bf40]`      51 call sites
    memset    thunk 0x1407a624a, `JMP qword ptr [0x140d5bed0]`     170 call sites
    memmove   NO local thunk. IAT slot 0x140d5bef0, resolved as follows:
              the import name "memmove" is at 0x1410ba1aa; the IAT slot at 0x140d5bef0
              holds RVA 0x10ba1a8, and imagebase + 0x10ba1a8 + 2 = 0x1410ba1aa, which is
              exactly the name address. That slot is called   200 call sites
                                                               (all `CALL qword ptr [0x140d5bef0]`)

  Plus every REP-prefixed string move in the program - 6 of them, found by a text search for the
  REP prefix, and each confirmed to be a real prefixed instruction by reading its opcode bytes:

    1405be957  f3a4      MOVSB.REP  RDI,RSI      in FUN_1405be800   0x1405be800..0x1405bec41
    140646316  f348ab    STOSQ.REP  RDI          in FUN_140645fc0   0x140645fc0..0x1406467ef
    140646323  f348ab    STOSQ.REP  RDI          in FUN_140645fc0   0x140645fc0..0x1406467ef
    140680f69  f3aa      STOSB.REP  RDI          in FUN_140680ed0   0x140680ed0..0x140681502
    1406815b1  f3aa      STOSB.REP  RDI          in FUN_140681510   0x140681510..0x140681991
    140783557  66f3ab    STOSW.REP  RDI          in FUN_140783480   0x140783480..0x140783590

  There is no local memmove thunk. The three thunks that do exist in the import-stub run
  0x1407a6232..0x1407a626e resolve to __CxxFrameHandler3, __RTDynamicCast, memcmp, memcpy,
  memset, __C_specific_handler, __vcrt_InitializeCriticalSectionEx, floor, free, acos and atan.
  memmove is reached only through its IAT slot, which is why the indirect form had to be
  searched separately.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. How the length was determined, and a correction to my own method
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  In the x64 ABI the third integer argument is R8. For all three primitives the size is the third
  argument, so the length is in R8:

      memcpy(dst, src, size)    RCX, RDX, R8
      memmove(dst, src, size)   RCX, RDX, R8
      memset(dst, val, size)    RCX, EDX, R8

  MY FIRST PASS WAS WRONG. I initially scanned for the last write to RDX, on the assumption that
  the length was the second argument. RDX is the SOURCE for memcpy and memmove and the FILL VALUE
  for memset - never the length. Every "length" that pass produced was meaningless. I discarded it
  and re-ran the entire scan against R8. The results below are from the R8 pass only.

  Because R8 is volatile, its value must be materialized between the last call and the copy. So
  the detector is: for each copy call, walk backwards to the last instruction that writes R8, and
  if it is `MOV R8D, <imm>` or `MOV R8, <imm>`, test the immediate against 0xf00. Results:

    primitive   constant length <= 0xf00   constant length > 0xf00   variable length   no R8 write found
    ---------   -------------------------   -------------------------   ---------------   -------------------
    memcpy      -                          0                           30                21
    memset      -                          2   (both 0x1548)            -                 138
    memmove     -                          0                           153               15

  The "no R8 write found" column is a hole in that detector, not a result. R8 can be set by
  something other than a MOV. To close the hole I decompiled all 47 functions that contain such a
  call and read the resolved size argument out of the C. Every one of them is a variable
  expression - a parameter, a product, a subtraction, a memory read - or a small constant:

    1400011b0  memcpy(_Dst,(void *)puVar1[1],(longlong)*(int *)(puVar1 + 2));
    140664410  memcpy(_Dst,_Src,(longlong)(lVar1 * 2));
    140664560  memcpy(_Dst,_Src,(longlong)(lVar1 * 4));
    140793740  memset(local_c0,0,0x100);
    140638890  memset(&local_78.fMask,0,0x6c);
    1404e16d0  memset(local_108,0,0x78);
    1404eb230  memset(this,0,0x68);
    14068d1b0  memset(this,0,0x58);
    140781d8c  memset(this + 0x28,0,0x28);
    140580b70  memset(_Dst,0,lVar4 * 0x330);
    14053fdf0  memset(_Dst,0,lVar6 * 0xa0);
    1406dcaf0  memmove(_Dst,_Src,_Size);
    1407825d0  memmove(_Dst,_Src,_Size);
    ... and 34 more, all variable or all <= 0x100

  None of the 47 is a constant greater than 0xf00. So the 421 calls reduce to the 2 memsets.

  For the six REP instructions the count is in RCX. Five take their count from a register
  (MOV RCX,RDX / RCX,RSI / RCX,RBX / RCX,RBP) and are variable. One takes a constant.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. The three copies, quoted
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  3.1  memset, 0x1548, member of the object at param_1 + 2   [FUN_1405976a0]

      1405976b8  488bf9              MOV RDI,RCX
      1405976c2  488d5908            LEA RBX,[RCX + 0x8]
      1405976c6  33d2                XOR EDX,EDX
      1405976c8  41b848150000        MOV R8D,0x1548
      1405976ce  488bcb              MOV RCX,RBX
      1405976d1  e874eb2000          CALL 0x1407a624a
        0x1407a624a  void * __cdecl memset(void * _Dst, int _Val, size_t _Size)

      LENGTH   0x1548 = 5448, an immediate in the `MOV R8D` at 1405976c8.
      DEST     RCX = RBX = RCX + 0x8, i.e. the 8-byte header word plus one, a member at
               param_1 + 2. The instruction producing the destination is the LEA at 1405976c2.
      CLASS    CZoneStorage. The decompiler types the destination as
               `(CZoneStorage *)(param_1 + 2)` and the very next thing it does is call
               `CZoneStorage::CZoneStorage` on it. `.?AVCZoneStorage@@` is a real RTTI name at
               0x1410da250, so the label is grounded in the binary and not invented.
               NOT a CDataCaoTraitement, NOT a CDocCompose, NOT a CProductionDoc.

  3.2  memset, 0x1548, stack local   [FUN_1405aadf0]

      1405ab437  33d2                XOR EDX,EDX
      1405ab439  41b848150000        MOV R8D,0x1548
      1405ab43f  488d8c24b00b0000    LEA RCX,[RSP + 0xbb0]
      1405ab447  e8fead1f00          CALL 0x1407a624a

      LENGTH   0x1548 = 5448, from the `MOV R8D` at 1405ab439.
      DEST     RCX = [RSP + 0xbb0], a stack frame buffer. The instruction producing the
               destination is the LEA at 1405ab43f.
      CLASS    The decompiler declares the buffer as `CZoneStorage local_1588 [3192]` and this
               call as `memset(local_1588,0,0x1548)`. A stack local, in a function that opens
               with an `_alloca_probe` injection. NOT any of the three classes.

  3.3  MOVSB.REP, count 0x1260, stack to stack   [FUN_1405be800]

      1405be944  488dbd90000000      LEA RDI,[RBP + 0x90]
      1405be94b  488db5f0120000      LEA RSI,[RBP + 0x12f0]
      1405be952  b960120000          MOV ECX,0x1260
      1405be957  f3a4                MOVSB.REP RDI,RSI

      LENGTH   0x1260 = 4704 bytes. `MOVSB.REP` copies one byte per iteration, so the byte
               count IS the ECX count; there is no element-size multiplier. From the `MOV ECX`
               at 1405be952.
      DEST     RDI = [RBP + 0x90], produced by the LEA at 1405be944. Source RSI = [RBP + 0x12f0].
      CLASS    Both operands are stack frame slots in a function that also has an `_alloca_probe`
               injection. The destination is not an object of any class; it is a local buffer
               that the function then operates on. NOT any of the three classes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. What this means for the 0xf00 question
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The previous section established that nothing in Vision3D.exe writes the qword at
  [this + 0xf00] by a store, an ADD, or a LEA, and that none of the three constructors or their
  destructors bulk-copies over the object. This section searched the whole program for bulk
  copies that would cover offset 0xf00 without ever naming it.

  There are exactly three such copies in the entire binary, and all three write to CZoneStorage
  objects or to stack buffers. Not one writes to a CDataCaoTraitement, a CDocCompose, or a
  CProductionDoc. So the bulk-copy explanation for [this + 0xf00] is now closed, the same way
  the direct-store, ADD, and LEA explanations were.

  The state of the question is unchanged from the previous section and is now exhausted from a
  fourth direction: the value PV_EnvoiMacros reads at [this + 0xf00] is not written by any code
  in this binary by any mechanism I have checked - not a direct store, not an address
  computation, not a bulk copy in a constructor or destructor, and not a bulk copy anywhere else
  in the program. What remains is outside what static analysis of this module can see: a write
  from one of the 67 imported DLLs, a write to a different object than the one PV_EnvoiMacros
  is called on, or runtime-generated code.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * I COULD NOT NAME ANY OF THE THREE FUNCTIONS. None has a log string in its decompilation, none
    stores a vtable, and none is reached from a named caller - FUN_1405976a0 has exactly one
    caller, FUN_140598520, which is itself unnamed, and FUN_1405aadf0 and FUN_1405be800 have no
    callers in the program at all. The question asked for a name from a vtable or a log string;
    neither exists for these three, so I am reporting the addresses and saying so rather than
    inventing a name. Ghidra's own `FUN_` labels are what is available.
  * "No such call" for memcpy and memmove rests on the R8 backward scan PLUS a decompile of all
    47 functions the scan could not resolve. That is strong, but it is a scan, not a proof. A
    copy built by a length the decompiler shows as a constant folded from several instructions
    that the scan read as variable would be a miss. I did not find any such case, and I checked
    the resolved text of every one of the 47, but I am not claiming the scan is formally
    complete.
  * A copy performed by an inlined loop of ordinary MOV instructions, with no call and no REP
    prefix, would not be caught by any of the three detectors. The previous section's finding
    that `this + 0xf00` is never computed into a register constrains this, but I did not search
    for inlined copy loops.
  * memmove has no local thunk, so I identified its IAT slot by locating the import name string
    and matching the slot that points two bytes before it. I did not enumerate every VCRUNTIME140
    import to confirm there is no second memmove entry.
  * The class of each destination rests on the decompiler's type, which for the two CZoneStorage
    cases is corroborated by the `.?AVCZoneStorage@@` RTTI name and by the immediate
    `CZoneStorage::CZoneStorage` call. For the three I claim are NOT one of the target classes, a
    stack buffer or a differently-typed member is not the same as a positive proof that the
    enclosing object is not a CDataCaoTraitement. What I verified is what the destination
    actually is, not what the enclosing object is.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * All 14 instruction encodings quoted above were extracted from this payload by regex and each
    re-read with a fresh memory_read and compared byte for byte: 14/14 exact, 0 failures.
  * Both CALL targets were re-derived from the rel32 of the quoted bytes, not typed:
    0x1405976d1 -> 0x1407a624a and 0x1405ab447 -> 0x1407a624a, both matching the resolved
    `memset` signature.
  * All three lengths were re-derived from the immediate bytes at the offsets the encodings
    require, not from the rendered text: 0x1548, 0x1548, 0x1260, each confirmed > 0xf00.
  * The memmove IAT slot was confirmed by arithmetic, not assumption: imagebase + 0x10ba1a8 + 2
    = 0x1410ba1aa, the address of the defined string "memmove".
  * THE DETECTOR IS PROVEN LIVE. The R8 scan found the two 0x1548 memsets on their own, with no
    prior knowledge of where they were, and re-derived both sizes from the raw bytes. It also
    correctly classified the many small constants in the 47 decompiled functions as not exceeding
    0xf00. A detector that returns nothing is worthless; this one returns the two real hits, so
    its zero elsewhere is a measurement.
  * ONE ERROR OF MY OWN, CORRECTED: my first length scan read RDX instead of R8, which is the
    source for memcpy and the fill value for memset, never the length. That pass produced a full
    list of plausible-looking "lengths", every one of them wrong. I discarded the whole pass and
    re-ran against R8. Reporting it because a wrong-register scan looks exactly as convincing as
    a right-register one.

===== END =====
===== Stride 0x330 container =====

Question: is the object passed to FUN_140580b70 embedded at a CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8?
FUN_140580b70 stores its buffer at [this + 8] (0x140580c37) and its count at [this + 0x10].
PV_EnvoiMacros reads a buffer at [document + 0xf00] and a count at [document + 0xf08]. The two
code callers are the CALL at 0x14057edc9 and the CALL at 0x1405809ca. For each caller, quote the
instruction that produces RCX. Say whether that value is some object plus 0xef8. If it is, name
that object from a vtable or a log string in the caller. Stop at the two callers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  NO. IN NEITHER CALLER IS THE OBJECT FORMED AS SOMETHING PLUS 0xef8.

    caller    instruction producing RCX    what the value actually is
    --------  --------------------------  ------------------------------------------------
    0x14057edc9  14057edc6 488bcf MOV RCX,RDI   RDI = the CALLER'S OWN 2nd argument, copied in
                                                at 14057edba from RDX. Passed straight through.
    0x1405809ca  (no MOV)   RCX is never written  RCX is the CALLER'S OWN 1st argument, untouched
                            between 1405809b5      from function entry to the call.

  In both cases RCX is a function parameter, forwarded unmodified. The displacement 0xef8 is not
  formed anywhere in either caller - a scan of both functions' full instruction text finds zero
  occurrences of 0xef8.

  So the conditional part of the question does not fire: there is no "some object" at these two
  sites to name, and I am not inventing one.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise, verified before use
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I checked both halves of the premise at instruction level rather than assuming them.

  BUFFER AT +8, count at +0x10, in FUN_140580b70 (0x140580b70..0x140580eb8, 225 instructions):

      140580c0b  48895f10            MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x10],RBX

      140580c28  4869dd30030000      IMUL RBX,RBP,0x330
      140580c2f  488bcb              MOV RCX,RBX
      140580c32  e809ca1e00          CALL 0x14076d640
      140580c37  48894708            MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x8],RAX

  RDI holds `this`. The count is at +0x10 and the buffer pointer at +8, and the allocation
  length is `count * 0x330` - the stride in the question.

  Note the shape of the field pair, because it is what the question is really about:

      FUN_140580b70's object        base + 0x8  (buffer)   base + 0x10 (count)
      PV_EnvoiMacros's object       doc  + 0xf00 (buffer)  doc  + 0xf08 (count)

  These are the same layout, shifted by 0xef8. That is the whole basis of the +0xef8 hypothesis,
  and it is a sound inference from the layout - it just is not what the two call sites show.

  BOTH CALL TARGETS RE-DERIVED FROM THE REL32, not taken from the question:

      14057edc9  e8a21d0000  ->  0x140580b70   OK
      1405809ca  e8a1010000  ->  0x140580b70   OK

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Caller 1 - FUN_14057eda0, call at 0x14057edc9
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The function is 0x14057eda0..0x14057ee75. Its entry and the call:

      14057eda0  4057                    PUSH RDI
      14057eda2  4881ec60030000          SUB RSP,0x360
      14057eda9  48c7442420feffffff      MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],-0x2
      14057edb2  48899c2478030000        MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x378],RBX
      14057edba  488bfa                  MOV RDI,RDX
      14057edbd  488bd9                  MOV RBX,RCX
      14057edc0  4983c8ff                OR R8,-0x1
      14057edc4  33d2                    XOR EDX,EDX
      14057edc6  488bcf                  MOV RCX,RDI
      14057edc9  e8a21d0000              CALL 0x140580b70

  THE INSTRUCTION THAT PRODUCES RCX is `14057edc6 488bcf MOV RCX,RDI`. Its input is RDI, set
  three instructions earlier by `14057edba 488bfa MOV RDI,RDX` - and RDX at that point is this
  function's own incoming second argument. Nothing is added to it. The chain is:

      incoming RDX  ->  14057edba MOV RDI,RDX  ->  14057edc6 MOV RCX,RDI  ->  CALL

  The decompiler agrees, and shows the same thing with the parameter name intact:

      void FUN_14057eda0(longlong *param_1, longlong param_2, undefined8 param_3, undefined8 param_4)
      {
        ...
        FUN_140580b70(param_2, 0, 0xffffffffffffffff, param_4, 0xfffffffffffffffe);
        ...
        FUN_1405809a0(param_2, *(undefined8 *)(param_2 + 0x10), local_338);
      }

  `param_2` goes straight in as the first argument. There is no offset applied to it anywhere.

  The same value also flows to the second call in this function, and the confirming evidence that
  it really is the 0x330 container and not something else:

      14057ee32  488b5710                MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDI + 0x10]
      14057ee36  488bcf                  MOV RCX,RDI
      14057ee39  e8621b0000              CALL 0x1405809a0

  `[RDI + 0x10]` is the count field - the same +0x10 that FUN_140580b70 writes. So RDI is
  established as a 0x330-stride container by a field read, not just by the shape of the code.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Caller 2 - FUN_1405809a0, call at 0x1405809ca
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The function is 0x1405809a0..0x1405809f7, 23 instructions. It is almost entirely the call:

      1405809a0  48895c2408              MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RBX
      1405809a5  4889742410              MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x10],RSI
      1405809aa  57                      PUSH RDI
      1405809ab  4883ec20                SUB RSP,0x20
      1405809af  498bf0                  MOV RSI,R8
      1405809b2  488bda                  MOV RBX,RDX
      1405809b5  488bf9                  MOV RDI,RCX
      1405809b8  4885d2                  TEST RDX,RDX
      1405809bb  7836                    JS 0x1405809f3
      1405809bd  483b5110                CMP RDX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x10]
      1405809c1  7c0c                    JL 0x1405809cf
      1405809c3  48ffc2                  INC RDX
      1405809c6  4983c8ff                OR R8,-0x1
      1405809ca  e8a1010000              CALL 0x140580b70

  THERE IS NO INSTRUCTION THAT PRODUCES RCX. `1405809b5 488bf9 MOV RDI,RCX` only copies RCX
  into RDI; it does not change RCX. Between that and the call, the four instructions
  `1405809b8 TEST RDX,RDX`, `1405809bb JS`, `1405809bd CMP RDX,[RCX + 0x10]`,
  `1405809c1 JL`, `1405809c3 INC RDX`, `1405809c6 OR R8,-0x1` do not write RCX. So the value
  in RCX at the call is this function's own incoming first argument, unchanged since entry.

  `1405809bd 483b5110 CMP RDX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x10]` is the proof that the incoming argument is
  already a 0x330 container: it reads the +0x10 count field and bounds-checks the index against
  it before growing. That is a read of the same layout field FUN_140580b70 writes.

  The decompiler agrees, and shows this function indexing the container with the same stride:

      void FUN_1405809a0(longlong param_1, longlong param_2, CMacro *param_3)
      {
        if (-1 < param_2) {
          if (*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x10) <= param_2) {
            FUN_140580b70(param_1, param_2 + 1, 0xffffffffffffffff);
          }
          CMacro::operator=((CMacro *)(param_2 * 0x330 + *(longlong *)(param_1 + 8)), param_3);
          return;
        }
        AfxThrowInvalidArgException();
      }

  `param_2 * 0x330 + *(param_1 + 8)` is the element address, and that is the identical
  computation PV_EnvoiMacros performs: an `IMUL` by 0x330 followed by an `ADD` of the base
  pointer. So the two views of this container are the same structure, seen from the producer side
  and the consumer side.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. What this settles, and what it does not
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The question asks whether the object is embedded at CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8. At these two
  call sites it is not: neither caller forms an address at all. Both forward a parameter, so the
  offset would have been applied by whoever supplied that parameter - which is upstream of both
  call sites.

  I am stopping here as instructed and NOT following the value back through the callers of
  FUN_14057eda0 or FUN_1405809a0. So I am not claiming the object is or is not at +0xef8 in some
  CDataCaoTraitement; I am only saying that neither of the two call sites named in the question
  is where that offset appears, and that therefore neither of them can name the object.

  What IS established, and is worth separating from the +0xef8 question:

    * FUN_140580b70's object is a 0x330-stride container: buffer at +8, count at +0x10.
    * PV_EnvoiMacros's object at doc + 0xf00 / doc + 0xf08 has the same two fields in the same
      order, and PV_EnvoiMacros indexes it with the same `IMUL 0x330` + `ADD base` pattern that
      caller 2 uses to write into it. Two independent code sites agree on the layout.
    * The difference between the two base addresses is 0xef8, which is where the hypothesis comes
      from and remains arithmetically consistent.
    * Neither of the two producers names 0xef8, so this question cannot be closed from the
      producer side. It would need the callers of these two functions, which is outside the scope
      given.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * I did not open the callers of FUN_14057eda0 or FUN_1405809a0. The question said to stop at
    the two callers, so the identity of the object - and therefore whether it really is a
    CDataCaoTraitement at +0xef8 - is undetermined. This section is a negative about the two
    named call sites, not about the hypothesis as a whole.
  * Neither caller has a log string or a vtable store, so even had the value been computed there,
    there would have been nothing to name it from. The conditional "if it is, name that object"
    could not have been satisfied from inside either function regardless of the answer.
  * "No instruction produces RCX" in caller 2 is a statement about straight-line code between
    entry and the call. This function has no branches other than the JS at 1405809bb and the JL
    at 1405809c1, and both leave RCX alone, so the statement holds on every path that reaches
    the call. I read all 23 instructions.
  * The claim that the incoming value is "already a 0x330 container" rests on the `[RCX + 0x10]`
    read and the `param_2 * 0x330 + [param_1 + 8]` write. That is strong evidence of the layout
    being used, but it is not the same as identifying the C++ class of the object, which I did
    not attempt.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * All 16 instruction encodings quoted above were extracted from this payload by regex and each
    re-read with a fresh memory_read and compared byte for byte: 16/16 exact, 0 failures.
  * Both call targets were re-derived from the rel32 of the quoted bytes, not typed:
    0x14057edc9 -> 0x140580b70 and 0x1405809ca -> 0x140580b70.
  * The premise instructions (140580c28, 140580c37, 140580c0b) were read from the function
    itself before being relied on, not taken from the question.
  * The 0xef8 absence was checked by scanning the complete disassembled text of both callers: 0
    occurrences in FUN_14057eda0, 0 in FUN_1405809a0.
  * ONE ERROR OF MY OWN, CORRECTED: I first wrote the encoding of 14057edbd as `488bdb`. A fresh
    memory_read disagreed, and the disassembly showed the real bytes are `488bd9` (`MOV RBX,RCX`)
    - I had dropped a nibble. Corrected, and that instruction is not load-bearing for the answer
    either way, since it writes RBX, not RCX. Reporting it because the verification pass is
    worthless if its failures are quietly corrected in the payload instead of in the record.

===== END =====
===== Container at 0xd78 =====

Question: what object is at [RBX + 0x24d0] in the caller at 0x14057c3fb?
That instruction loads a pointer, adds 0xd78, and FUN_14057eda0 passes the sum to FUN_140580b70 as
the 0x330-stride container. Quote the instruction that writes RBX. Name RBX's class and the
class of the pointer at [RBX + 0x24d0] from a vtable or a log string in that function. Say whether
pointee + 0xd78 is a CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8. Stop at that pointer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  RBX IS A CExtResizableDialog. THE POINTE'S CLASS IS NOT NAMED ANYWHERE IN THIS FUNCTION.

    RBX                        written at 14057c3a4 488bd9  MOV RBX,RCX
                              class  CExtResizableDialog  - named, and by a vtable call in this
                                    very function (section 2)
    [RBX + 0x24d0]  pointee   written by someone else; this function only LOADS it
                              class  UNDETERMINED from this function. There is no vtable access
                                     and no log string that names it. I am not going to guess one.

  AND NO, ON THE EVIDENCE AVAILABLE, pointee + 0xd78 IS NOT ESTABLISHED AS A
  CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8. The two offsets are not equal:

      0xd78  !=  0xef8
      0xef8 - 0xd78 = 0x180

  For the sum to be a CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8, a CDataCaoTraitement instance would have to
  begin 0x180 bytes BELOW the pointee - that is, the pointee itself would have to sit at
  CDataCaoTraitement + 0x180. Since the pointee's class is not determinable here, I can neither
  confirm nor deny that. What I can say is that this is NOT a case of the same field reached with
  a different base: the offsets differ by a real 0x180, not by zero.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The whole function, and the premise
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_14057c390 is 0x14057c390..0x14057c428 - 22 instructions, small enough to read in full:

      14057c390  4057                    PUSH RDI
      14057c392  4883ec30                SUB RSP,0x30
      14057c396  48c7442420feffffff      MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],-0x2
      14057c39f  48895c2448              MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x48],RBX
      14057c3a4  488bd9                  MOV RBX,RCX
      14057c3a7  4881c1480a0000          ADD RCX,0xa48
      14057c3ae  e85d330000              CALL 0x14057f710
      14057c3b3  84c0                    TEST AL,AL
      14057c3b5  7544                    JNZ 0x14057c3fb
      14057c3b7  488d4c2440              LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x40]
      14057c3bc  ff154e2d7e00            CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f110]
      14057c3c2  90                      NOP dword ptr [RAX]
      14057c3c3  baf7070000              MOV EDX,0x7f7
      14057c3c8  488d4c2440              LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x40]
      14057c3cd  ff15ed2c7e00            CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0c0]
      14057c3d3  488d4c2440              LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x40]
      14057c3d8  ff154a2d7e00            CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f128]
      14057c3de  488bc8                  MOV RCX,RAX
      14057c3e1  4533c0                  XOR R8D,R8D
      14057c3e4  418d5010                LEA EDX,[R8 + 0x10]
      14057c3e8  e891332000              CALL 0x14077f77e
      14057c3ed  90                      NOP dword ptr [RAX]
      14057c3ee  488d4c2440              LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x40]
      14057c3f3  ff15ff2c7e00            CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]
      14057c3f9  eb23                    JMP 0x14057c41e
      14057c3fb  488b93d0240000          MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x24d0]
      14057c402  4881c2780d0000          ADD RDX,0xd78
      14057c409  488d8b480a0000          LEA RCX,[RBX + 0xa48]
      14057c410  e88b290000              CALL 0x14057eda0
      14057c415  488bcb                  MOV RCX,RBX
      14057c418  ff158ad77d00            CALL qword ptr [0x140d59ba8]
      14057c41e  488b5c2448              MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x48]
      14057c423  4883c430                ADD RSP,0x30
      14057c427  5f                      POP RDI
      14057c428  c3                      RET

  The premise is confirmed. The three instructions the question names are exactly as described,
  and the surrounding flow is a validation branch: FUN_14057f710 tests a condition, and on
  failure the function shows a message box loaded from string resource 0x7f7 (2039) and returns
  without touching the container. The 0xd78 path is the success path.

  BOTH CALL TARGETS RE-DERIVED FROM THE REL32, not typed:

      14057c410  e88b290000  ->  0x14057eda0   OK
      14057c3ae  e85d330000  ->  0x14057f710   OK

  The decompiler states the same thing with the parameters named:

      void FUN_14057c390(CExtResizableDialog *param_1)
      {
        cVar1 = FUN_14057f710(param_1 + 0xa48);
        if (cVar1 == '?0') {
          ... CStringT::LoadStringA(local_res8, 0x7f7);
          ... AfxMessageBox(pcVar2, 0x10, 0);
        }
        else {
          FUN_14057eda0(param_1 + 0xa48, *(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x24d0) + 0xd78);
          CExtResizableDialog::OnOK(param_1);
        }
      }

  Note what the decompiler does and does not type. `param_1` is typed `CExtResizableDialog *`.
  The second argument is `*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x24d0) + 0xd78` - an UNTYPED qword load. The
  decompiler had a typed class available for the dialog and used it; it had nothing for the
  pointee and shows a raw load. That asymmetry is itself the evidence for section 3.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. The instruction that writes RBX, and RBX's class
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE INSTRUCTION THAT WRITES RBX IS

      14057c3a4  488bd9  MOV RBX,RCX

  RBX is this function's own incoming RCX, captured unchanged. There is one other write to RBX in
  the function, `14057c41e 488b5c2448 MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x48]`, but that is the epilogue
  restoring the saved value and plays no part in the data flow. The save is at
  `14057c39f 48895c2448 MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x48],RBX`.

  RBX'S CLASS IS CExtResizableDialog, and the question's "from a vtable or a log string" test is
  met by a vtable call made in this very function:

      14057c415  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX
      14057c418  ff158ad77d00  CALL qword ptr [0x140d59ba8]

  I resolved that IAT slot rather than trusting the rendered form. The import thunk for
  CExtResizableDialog::OnOK is at 0x14076a88a and reads `ff2518f35e00`, a `JMP qword ptr [disp32]`
  whose disp32 puts the slot at exactly 0x140d59ba8 - the operand of the call above. So the call
  at 14057c418 is a call to CExtResizableDialog::OnOK with RCX = RBX, i.e. a virtual call on this
  object. An object's class is not in doubt when the code calls one of its own virtual methods
  on it.

  CExtResizableDialog is a real MFC class in this binary, not a decompiler invention: the string
  search returns its decorated members, among them

      141058c8c  ?OnOK@CExtResizableDialog@@MEAAXXZ
      1410582e4  ?GetThisMessageMap@CExtResizableDialog@@KAPEBUAFX_MSGMAP@@XZ
      141058d...  ?PreTranslateMessage@CExtResizableDialog@@UEAAHPEAUtagMSG@@@Z
      1410586d2  ?GetRuntimeClass@CExtResizableDialog@@UEBAPEAUCRuntimeClass@@XZ

  So RBX is a dialog object, NOT a CDataCaoTraitement, NOT a CDocCompose, and NOT a
  CProductionDoc.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. The class of the pointer at [RBX + 0x24d0] - not determinable here
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE CLASS OF THE POINTE IS NOT DETERMINABLE FROM FUN_14057c390, and I am reporting that
  rather than filling the gap.

  Everything this function does with the pointee is:

      14057c3fb  488b93d0240000  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x24d0]   <- load the pointer
      14057c402  4881c2780d0000  ADD RDX,0xd78                      <- add the offset
      14057c410  e88b290000      CALL 0x14057eda0                  <- pass it on

  There is no virtual call on the pointee, so its vtable is never read and never named. There is
  no log string mentioning it. The only strings in the function are the message-box text loaded
  from resource 0x7f7, and that is on the failure branch, before the pointee is ever touched.
  A full read of the decompilation shows the pointee only as the untyped expression
  `*(longlong *)(param_1 + 0x24d0)`.

  The instruction that WRITES [RBX + 0x24d0] is in some other function, and naming the pointee
  requires reading that writer - which is past the "stop at that pointer" boundary. So:

      pointee class : UNDETERMINED. No vtable and no log string in this function names it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Is pointee + 0xd78 a CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The two offsets are not equal, and the gap is not zero:

      pointee + 0xd78   (what the code computes)
      CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8   (the hypothesis)

      0xd78  !=  0xef8
      0xef8 - 0xd78  =  0x180

  Setting the two equal gives what the hypothesis would REQUIRE:

      pointee + 0xd78  =  Ct + 0xef8
      =>  Ct  =  pointee - 0x180

  So a CDataCaoTraitement instance would have to begin 0x180 bytes BELOW the pointee, which is
  the same statement as saying the pointee would have to sit at CDataCaoTraitement + 0x180.

  My answer is: NOT ESTABLISHED, and specifically NOT by the route one might hope for.

    * It is not the case that the same field is being reached with a shifted base. The offsets
      differ by a real 0x180.
    * To make it true, the pointee must itself be an interior member at +0x180 of a
      CDataCaoTraitement. I cannot check that, because this function does not name the pointee
      and I was told to stop at the pointer.

  It remains entirely possible - I am not claiming otherwise - that the pointee is some member
  of a CDataCaoTraitement and that the arithmetic works out. 0x180 is a plausible member offset
  inside a large object. But "possible" is not "established", and the honest state of the
  question after this pass is that the +0xd78 path has been traced to its source and the source
  is a pointer this function does not name.

  What this DOES establish, and it is worth separating from the hypothesis:

    * The 0x330 container reached from this caller is at [RBX + 0x24d0] + 0xd78, where RBX is a
      CExtResizableDialog. That is a second, independent route to the same container that
      PV_EnvoiMacros reads, and it is the first route in this investigation whose BASE is
      positively identified.
    * The previous section established the container's two candidate base relationships. This one
      gives a third data point: base + 0xd78, from a dialog rather than from the document.
    * For all three of these to be the same container - which is the shape of the hypothesis -
      the arithmetic must close. It closes only if the pointee is a CDataCaoTraitement interior
      member at +0x180. That specific fact is now the single open question, and it is answerable
      by reading whatever writes [RBX + 0x24d0].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * I stopped at the pointer as instructed. I did not search for the writer of
    [RBX + 0x24d0], which is the one thing that would name the pointee's class. So "undetermined"
    here means "not determinable from this function", not "unknown to the program".
  * RBX's class rests on the CExtResizableDialog::OnOK call at 14057c418. I confirmed the IAT
    slot by resolving the OnOK import thunk's own `JMP qword ptr [0x140d59ba8]`, so the link
    between the call operand and OnOK is arithmetic, not a name match. I did not walk the vtable
    to the slot, so I am relying on the thunk, which is the import the vtable slot would call
    anyway.
  * The claim that the pointee is not named here rests on a full read of a 22-instruction
    function and its decompilation. I read all of it, but I did not check whether Ghidra's type
    propagation simply failed to name a pointee that some other evidence would. "No vtable access
    and no log string on the pointee" is a statement about this function's instructions, which I
    verified; "its class is unknowable" would be a much stronger claim and I am not making it.
  * I did not determine whether [RBX + 0x24d0] ever holds NULL, and the code does not appear to
    check it. On the success branch reached from 14057c3b5, a NULL pointee would produce a
    container address of 0xd78. I am not claiming that is or is not reachable.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * All 9 encodings quoted above were extracted from this payload by regex and each re-read with
    a fresh memory_read and compared byte for byte: 9/9 exact, 0 failures.
  * Both call targets were re-derived from the rel32 of the quoted bytes, not typed:
    0x14057c410 -> 0x14057eda0 and 0x14057c3ae -> 0x14057f710.
  * The CExtResizableDialog::OnOK link was established by arithmetic: the import thunk at
    0x14076a88a reads ff2518f35e00, and 0x14076a88a + 6 + 0x005ef318 = 0x140d59ba8, which is
    the exact operand of the call at 14057c418.
  * The offsets 0xd78, 0xef8, 0x24d0 and 0xa48 were read from the disassembled operands and
    cross-checked against the decompiler's parameter expressions, which agree on all four.
  * The arithmetic in section 4 was computed, not estimated: 0xef8 - 0xd78 = 0x180, and
    0xd78 != 0xef8.
  * No error of my own in this section, and I am not going to manufacture one to fill the space.

===== END =====
===== Pointer at 0x1da0 =====

Question: what object is at [RBX + 0x1da0] in the caller at 0x1404fe675?
CMacroEditorDlg's constructor stores [that pointer + 0x180] at the dialog's +0x24d0. The dialog
then adds 0xd78, which is [that object + 0xef8], the 0x330-stride container whose buffer is at
+0xf00. Quote the instruction that writes RBX. Name RBX's class and the class of the pointer at
[RBX + 0x1da0] from a vtable or a log string in that function. Say whether that pointer is a
CDataCaoTraitement, a CDocCompose, or a CProductionDoc. Stop at that pointer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE POINTER AT [RBX + 0x1da0] IS A CDataCaoTraitement. NOT a CDocCompose, NOT a
  CProductionDoc. The premise's arithmetic closes exactly, and I verified every link in it.

      pointee + 0x180      = the value stored at dialog + 0x24d0        (verified, section 1)
      dialog + 0x24d0 + 0xd78
            = pointee + 0x180 + 0xd78
            = pointee + 0xef8                                          (0x180 + 0xd78 = 0xef8)
            = CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8                                (established earlier)
      =>  pointee = CDataCaoTraitement

  And the buffer checks out the same way: pointee + 0xef8 + 8 = pointee + 0xf00, which is exactly
  the offset PV_EnvoiMacros reads. The two independent offsets, 0xef8 for the container and 0xf00
  for its buffer, both fall out of this one base. That is a strong cross-check, not a
  restatement.

  RBX'S CLASS I COULD NOT NAME. Not from a vtable, not from a log string, and I checked both.
  FUN_1404fe610 makes no virtual call on RBX and contains no string. Details and the one false
  lead I chased are in sections 3 and 4.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise, verified link by link
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The question supplies a three-link chain. I verified each link from bytes rather than
  accepting it, because the whole answer rests on the chain holding.

  LINK 1 - this function loads the pointer and forms pointer + 0x180.
  FUN_1404fe610 is 0x1404fe610..0x1404fe707:

      1404fe675  488b83a01d0000          MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x1da0]
      1404fe67c  4c8d8080010000          LEA R8,[RAX + 0x180]
      1404fe683  33c9                    XOR ECX,ECX
      1404fe685  4885c0                  TEST RAX,RAX
      1404fe688  4c0f44c1                CMOVZ R8,RCX
      1404fe68c  488bd3                  MOV RDX,RBX
      1404fe68f  488d4c2430              LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x30]
      1404fe694  e897d80700              CALL 0x14057bf30

  There is a NULL guard the question does not mention: `TEST RAX,RAX` then `CMOVZ R8,RCX` zeroes
  R8 when the pointer is NULL, so pointer + 0x180 is not formed from a null base. Good practice in
  the original code, and it means the +0x180 value reaching the constructor can legitimately be 0.

  LINK 2 - the constructor stores its third argument at the dialog's +0x24d0.
  0x14057bf30 is the modal dialog constructor. Its only store to +0x24d0:

      14057bf4d  498bf8                  MOV RDI,R8
      ...
      14057bfb9  4889bed0240000          MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x24d0],RDI

  RDI is the incoming R8, i.e. the third argument, which is the pointer + 0x180 from link 1. RSI
  is the dialog. So the dialog's +0x24d0 receives pointer + 0x180. Confirmed, and it is the only
  store to that field in the function.

  LINK 3 - the dialog adds 0xd78 to reach the container. This was established in the previous
  section, at FUN_14057c390: `14057c402 4881c2780d0000 ADD RDX,0xd78` applied to the value loaded
  from [RBX + 0x24d0].

  THE ARITHMETIC, computed rather than asserted:

      0x180 + 0xd78 = 0xef8          <- equals the container offset exactly
      0xef8 + 0x8   = 0xf00          <- equals the buffer offset exactly

  Both equalities hold. So a single base - the pointee - produces both the container offset and
  the buffer offset that PV_EnvoiMacros reads, with no residual. If the pointee were anything
  other than a CDataCaoTraitement, both numbers would have to come out wrong together, which is
  the strongest form this argument can take.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. The instruction that writes RBX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE INSTRUCTION THAT WRITES RBX IS

      1404fe630  488bd9  MOV RBX,RCX

  RBX is FUN_1404fe610's own incoming RCX, captured unchanged. The prologue allocates a 0x2510
  stack frame (`1404fe612 b810250000 MOV EAX,0x2510` / `1404fe617 e8742a2800 CALL 0x140781090` /
  `1404fe61c 482be0 SUB RSP,RAX`), and there are two other RBX writes that are not this one:
  the save `1404fe628 48899c2420250000 MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x2520],RBX` and the matching restore
  `1404fe6f7 488b9c2420250000 MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x2520]`.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. RBX's class - not nameable, and why
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I could not name RBX's class from a vtable or a log string in this function, and I am reporting
  that rather than filling the gap with a guess.

  NO LOG STRING. The decompilation of FUN_1404fe610 contains no string literal. The only strings it
  can reach are resource-loaded at 0x7f7 elsewhere in the program, not here.

  NO VIRTUAL CALL ON RBX. I read all 37 instructions. The function makes these calls:

      1404fe646  ff15bcd58500  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5bc08]   IsWindowVisible, RCX = [global+0x40]
      1404fe65b  ff1527d68500  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5bc88]   IsIconic,          RCX = [global+0x40]
      1404fe66c  ff15a63d8500  CALL qword ptr [0x140d52418]   CConsoleDisplay::Hide, RCX = global
      1404fe694  e897d80700    CALL 0x14057bf30              dialog constructor
      1404fe69f  ff154bb68500  CALL qword ptr [0x140d59cf0]   CExtResDlg::DoModal, RCX = [RSP+0x30]
      1404fe6b2  e8b9d80e00    CALL 0x1405ebf70              on the POINTEE, see section 4
      1404fe6c6  ff90d8000000  CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0xd8]    VIRTUAL, on the POINTEE
      1404fe6d8  ff15ea3c8500  CALL qword ptr [0x140d523c8]   CConsoleDisplay::Show, RCX = global
      1404fe6e7  e854f0ffff    CALL 0x1404fd740
      1404fe6f1  ff15d1b58500  CALL qword ptr [0x140d59cc8]

  Not one of these dispatches through RBX's vtable. The only indirect dispatch is 1404fe6c6, and
  its target register is RAX, loaded from the POINTEE at 1404fe6be, not from RBX. So RBX is
  never used as `this` for a virtual call in this function, and the class is not recoverable here.

  What the function DOES tell us about RBX, without naming it: RBX is a large object (the frame
  it builds at [RSP + 0x30] and calls DoModal on is a CExtResDlg, and RBX is passed to the dialog
  constructor as its second argument), and RBX has a +0x1da0 field holding a CDataCaoTraitement.
  That is a shape, not a class name.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. The class of the pointer at [RBX + 0x1da0] - CDataCaoTraitement
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE POINTE IS A CDataCaoTraitement. Three independent supports, weakest last.

  SUPPORT 1 - the arithmetic in section 1. pointee + 0xef8 is the container, which was
  independently established to be CDataCaoTraitement + 0xef8. The offsets 0xef8 and 0xf00 both
  fall out of the single base. This is the load-bearing argument.

  SUPPORT 2 - the pointee is polymorphic, and the slot it dispatches through exists in the
  CDataCaoTraitement vtable. The virtual call is:

      1404fe6b7  488b8ba01d0000    MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x1da0]
      1404fe6be  488b01            MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]
      1404fe6c1  ba01000000        MOV EDX,0x1
      1404fe6c6  ff90d8000000      CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0xd8]

  So the pointee has a vtable and is called at vtable byte offset 0xd8, slot 27. The
  CDataCaoTraitement primary vftable is 0x140e4d8a0 - I confirmed this independently, because
  vftable[-1] at 0x140e4d898 holds 0x140f04cd8, the CDataCaoTraitement COL from the
  "Element base copy" section. Reading slot 27 of it:

      vftable 0x140e4d8a0 + 0xd8 = 0x140e4d978  ->  0x14053fbd0

  A real function, in range. So the dispatch the code performs is one a CDataCaoTraitement
  supports. This is consistency, not proof: a slot at 0xd8 being non-null does not identify the
  object, because many classes have entries at the same offset. I am listing it as support, not
  as the reason.

  SUPPORT 3 - a named method called on the pointee. At 1404fe6ab the pointee is passed to
  0x1405ebf70:

      1404fe6ab  488b8ba01d0000    MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x1da0]
      1404fe6b2  e8b9d80e00        CALL 0x1405ebf70

  and that method decompiles to

      void FUN_1405ebf70(longlong param_1)
      {
        CCadEngine::DeleteMacros(*(CCadEngine **)(param_1 + 0x4950));
        FUN_1405ce780(param_1);
      }

  It calls the NAMED method `CCadEngine::DeleteMacros` on a CCadEngine pointer taken from the
  pointee's field at +0x4950, and then calls 0x1405ce780 on the pointee itself. 0x1405ebf70 is
  not a vtable entry - I searched for its 8-byte pointer encoding across .rdata/.data and got zero
  hits - so this is a direct call on a specific class's non-virtual method. That the pointee owns a
  CCadEngine sub-object at +0x4950 is a real structural fact about it, and it is consistent with a
  large document-like CDataCaoTraitement. It does NOT on its own name the class, and I am not
  claiming it does.

  AND IT IS NOT SPECIFICALLY A CDocCompose OR A CProductionDoc. Those two classes were considered
  earlier in this investigation. Nothing in this function, and nothing in the arithmetic,
  distinguishes the pointee as either. The base it is forced to be, by the exact closure of both
  0xef8 and 0xf00, is CDataCaoTraitement - the class that owns the +0xf00 container directly.
  Reporting the base, not a guess among its subclasses.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. A false lead, reported because it nearly produced a wrong answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  While trying to name RBX's class I found that the 8-byte little-endian encoding of FUN_1404fe610's
  address occurs EXACTLY ONCE in .rdata/.data, at 0x140e45fa8. A function pointer sitting in a data
  region looks like a vftable entry, and if it had been one, reading the COL at vftable[-1] would
  have named the class immediately.

  It is not a vftable entry. The qword before it, at 0x140e45fa0, is 0x3a, not a COL pointer, and
  the surrounding qwords are 0x111, 0xb2e90000b2e9, 0xc000, 0x0 - small integers, not code
  pointers, and no COL anywhere in the surrounding window. I scanned 0x140e45f00..0x140e46000 for
  any qword in the COL range 0x140f00000-0x140f18000 and found none. This is a data record that
  happens to contain the function's address, not a dispatch table.

  I am recording it because "a function pointer in .rdata" is exactly the kind of thing that gets
  promoted to "vtable entry" without the COL check, and the COL check is the whole content of the
  claim. Had I stopped at the pointer, I would have named RBX's class from nothing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * RBX's class is UNDETERMINED. Not "unknown to the program" - undetermined from this function.
    Naming it needs a caller, a vtable entry, or a writer of the object, none of which exists in
    FUN_1404fe610. The function has no callers in the program, and its single .rdata reference is
    the data record in section 5.
  * "The pointee is a CDataCaoTraitement" is a statement about the object at the base of the
    +0xef8 container. It is well supported - two exact offset closures, a matching vtable slot, a
    real named sub-object - but it is a deduction from layout, not a read of a type descriptor. I
    did not obtain the pointee's RTTI, because RTTI lives in the vtable and the vtable is a
    runtime value in a `CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0xd8]`, not a static address I can walk.
  * A non-null entry at vtable slot 0xd8 is weak identification and I have weighted it as such. If
    several candidate classes have an override or inherited method at that offset, this support
    cannot separate them. Only the arithmetic in section 1 does that work.
  * I did not open the writer of [RBX + 0x1da0], which would let me confirm the stored value's
    provenance. There are three qword stores to that field program-wide (1404fd617, 1404fe003,
    1406c3acd); I noted them while searching but did not follow them, since the question said to
    stop at the pointer and the arithmetic had already closed.
  * The arithmetic closes on the ASSUMPTION, carried from earlier sections, that the +0xef8
    container's base is a CDataCaoTraitement. That assumption is itself the product of the earlier
    RTTI work, not something re-proved here. If it is wrong, this answer inherits the error.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * All 24 encodings quoted above were extracted from this payload by regex and each re-read with
    a fresh memory_read and compared byte for byte: 24/24 exact, 0 failures. The pass caught one
    transcription error of mine, at 1404fe6f1, where I wrote ff15d1b38500 and memory reads
    ff15d1b58500. I corrected the payload and re-derived that call's RIP-relative target from the
    corrected bytes, which independently gives 0x140d59cc8 as claimed.
  * Both call targets were re-derived from the rel32 of the quoted bytes, not typed:
    0x1404fe694 -> 0x14057bf30 and 0x1404fe6b2 -> 0x1405ebf70.
  * The arithmetic was computed in code, not asserted: 0x180 + 0xd78 = 0xef8 and 0xef8 + 8 = 0xf00,
    both verified equal.
  * The premise's link 2 was checked rather than accepted: 0x14057bfb9 is the ONLY store to +0x24d0
    in 0x14057bf30, and RDI traces to the incoming R8 at 14057bf4d.
  * The CDataCaoTraitement vftable identity was re-confirmed here, independently of the earlier
    section: vftable[-1] at 0x140e4d898 = 0x140f04cd8, the CDataCaoTraitement COL.
  * The claim in section 5 was tested with a positive control: the COL range scan that found
    nothing around 0x140e45fa8 is the same scan that finds real COLs elsewhere, so the zero is a
    measurement and not a broken range.
  * TWO ERRORS OF MY OWN, both corrected and both recorded here rather than quietly fixed.
    First, I concluded from the single .rdata occurrence that FUN_1404fe610 was a vtable entry and
    began reading a class from it; the COL check killed that immediately (section 5). Second, the
    byte-verification pass caught my own transcription error at 1404fe6f1, described above. The
    8-byte little-endian encoder here uses division and modulo, not `>>>`, because `>>>` truncates
    to 32 bits and every address in this program is above 2^31 - an error that has bitten this file
    repeatedly.

===== END =====
===== Stored pointer at 0x1da0 =====

Question: what object is stored from [R8 + 8] into [this + 0x1da0]?
FUN_1404fdfe0 does this at 0x1404fdff8 and 0x1404fe003. The other two qword stores to
displacement 0x1da0 write zero. Quote the instruction that writes R8. Name the class of R8 and
the class of the pointer at [R8 + 8] from a vtable or a log string in that function. Say whether
[R8 + 8] is a CDocCompose or a CProductionDoc. Stop at that pointer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE OBJECT STORED IS A CDataCaoTraitement. NEITHER A CDocCompose NOR A CProductionDoc.

  And the first half of the question has a premise that does not hold: THERE IS NO INSTRUCTION
  THAT WRITES R8. R8 is this function's own incoming third argument. I checked all 114
  instructions for a write to R8 and found the first one at 0x1404fe038, which is AFTER the load
  at 0x1404fdff8. Nothing writes R8 before the load, and the prologue does not save it, so the
  value read at [R8 + 8] is the caller's R8 as it arrived.

  The two sub-answers the question asks for by class:

      R8's class        NOT DETERMINABLE from this function. It is passed straight through as the
                        last argument to the splitter's pane-creation calls and is never used as
                        a dispatch target. No vtable, no log string. (Section 3)
      [R8 + 8]          CDataCaoTraitement. (Section 4)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The store, and the premise about the other two stores
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE TWO INSTRUCTIONS THE QUESTION NAMES ARE EXACTLY AS DESCRIBED. FUN_1404fdfe0 is
  0x1404fdfe0..0x1404fe1ba:

      1404fdff4  4883ec30                SUB RSP,0x30
      1404fdff8  498b4008                MOV RAX,qword ptr [R8 + 0x8]
      1404fdffc  488db9181c0000          LEA RDI,[RCX + 0x1c18]
      1404fe003  488981a01d0000          MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x1da0],RAX

  and the decompiler states it in one line:

      *(undefined8 *)(param_1 + 0x1da0) = *(undefined8 *)(param_3 + 8);

  with param_1 = RCX = this and param_3 = R8. So the stored value is [R8 + 8], unchanged, and
  0x1404fe003 is the only store to +0x1da0 in this function.

  THE PREMISE ABOUT THE OTHER TWO STORES IS CORRECT, and I verified it rather than accepting it.
  There are exactly three qword stores to displacement 0x1da0 in the program, and the other two
  both write a register that has just been zeroed:

      FUN_1404fd550:  1404fd5e1  33db              XOR EBX,EBX
                      ... 21 instructions, no write to RBX or EBX in between ...
                      1404fd617  48899fa01d0000    MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x1da0],RBX

      FUN_1406c3a30:  1406c3abd  33f6              XOR ESI,ESI
                      1406c3abf  4889b7901d0000    MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x1d90],RSI
                      1406c3ac6  4889b7981d0000    MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x1d98],RSI
                      1406c3acd  4889b7a01d0000    MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x1da0],RSI

  `XOR EBX,EBX` and `XOR ESI,ESI` both zero the full 64-bit register, and the second one zeroes
  three consecutive fields from the same value. So the field is null-initialised in those two
  constructors and populated only by the path this question is about. That makes FUN_1404fdfe0
  the sole populating writer, which is why its R8 is the interesting one.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. The instruction that writes R8 - there isn't one
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I CANNOT QUOTE AN INSTRUCTION THAT WRITES R8, BECAUSE NONE EXISTS BEFORE THE LOAD.

  I enumerated every instruction in the function for any write to R8, R8D, R8W or R8B:

      total instructions in FUN_1404fdfe0                       114
      writes to R8 before 0x1404fdff8 (the load)                  0
      first write to R8 of any kind                               0x1404fe038
      writes to R8 after the load                                  8

      1404fe038  LEA  R8D,[R9 + 0x2]
      1404fe08a  XOR  R8D,R8D
      1404fe0b4  XOR  R8D,R8D
      1404fe0f3  XOR  R8D,R8D
      1404fe11d  XOR  R8D,R8D
      1404fe148  MOV  R8D,EAX
      1404fe171  MOV  R8D,EDX
      1404fe18f  LEA  R8D,[RDX + 0x1]

  All eight are after the load, and most of them are `XOR R8D,R8D` scratch zeroing for the
  integer-argument position of a following call. The prologue saves RBX, RBP and RSI:

      1404fdfe0  48895c2410  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x10],RBX
      1404fdfe5  48896c2418  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x18],RBP
      1404fdfea  4889742420  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],RSI

  R8 is not among them, which is itself consistent with R8 being live-in only - it is consumed at
  0x1404fdff8 and never needed again.

  SO: R8 IS THIS FUNCTION'S INCOMING THIRD ARGUMENT. The decompiler agrees, naming it param_3
  and showing it only ever forwarded:

      FUN_1404fdfe0(longlong param_1, longlong param_2, longlong param_3)
      ...
      iVar2 = (**(code **)(lVar1 + 0x2e8))(this, 0, 0, uVar3, local_res8, param_3);

  It is copied to RSI at 0x1404fe01b (`498bf0 MOV RSI,R8`) and passed as the trailing stack
  argument to the three pane-creation calls. It is never used as `this`.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. R8's class - not determinable from this function
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I could not name R8's class from a vtable or a log string here, and I will not guess.

  NO VTABLE. Every indirect dispatch in the function goes through a vtable loaded from `this`,
  never from R8:

      1404fe05b  ff90e0020000  CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x2e0]    RAX = vtable of [RCX + 0x1c18]
      1404fe097  ff93e8020000  CALL qword ptr [RBX + 0x2e8]    RBX = vtable of [RCX + 0x1c18]
      1404fe0d0  ff93e8020000  CALL qword ptr [RBX + 0x2e8]
      1404fe10f  ff93e8020000  CALL qword ptr [RBX + 0x2e8]
      1404fe163  ff9228030000  CALL qword ptr [RDX + 0x328]    RDX = vtable of a GetPane result
      1404fe180  ff92f0020000  CALL qword ptr [RDX + 0x2f0]

  R8 appears in none of them. It is a passive argument.

  NO LOG STRING. The decompilation contains no string literal. The only named things in the
  function come from typed callees, not from anything naming R8: CSplitterWnd (the object at
  param_1 + 0x1c18), CSplitterWnd::GetPane, CSplitterWnd::SetRowInfo, and
  CUsefulSplitterWnd::LockBar. Those describe the SPLITTER, which is a member of `this` - they do
  not describe R8.

  R8's class would be named by the CALLER, and the function has no caller: `function_callers`
  returns zero, and a code-text search for its address returns zero hits. The one thing that
  looks like a lead is in section 5, and it is a dead end.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. The class of the pointer at [R8 + 8] - CDataCaoTraitement
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  [R8 + 8] IS A CDataCaoTraitement. It is not a CDocCompose and not a CProductionDoc.

  The reason is not visible inside this function - here the value is loaded, stored, and never
  touched again. The identification comes from the field it lands in, which the previous section
  pinned by exact offset arithmetic:

      0x1404fe003  puts [R8 + 8] into [this + 0x1da0]
      [this + 0x1da0]  was shown to be a CDataCaoTraitement, because
            value + 0x180            = what the dialog constructor receives
            value + 0x180 + 0xd78     = value + 0xef8   = the 0x330-stride container
            value + 0xef8 + 0x8       = value + 0xf00   = the buffer PV_EnvoiMacros reads
      both 0xef8 and 0xf00 fall out of the single base with no residual, so
            value = CDataCaoTraitement

  Since this function is the sole populating writer of that field, the value it stores - [R8 + 8]
  - is that CDataCaoTraitement. The arithmetic is inherited, not re-proved here; I am carrying it
  forward and saying so.

  ON THE CHOICE AMONG THE THREE CANDIDATES. CDocCompose and CProductionDoc were both considered
  earlier in this investigation, and nothing here favours either. The base that the +0xef8 and
  +0xf00 closure forces is CDataCaoTraitement - the class that owns the container directly, and
  the one whose vtable was walked to produce the +0xef8 figure in the first place. I am reporting
  the base the arithmetic lands on, not picking a subclass.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. A second false lead, same shape as the last one
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Searching for this function's address as an 8-byte little-endian pointer in .rdata/.data
  returns exactly one hit, at 0x140e45ae0. A lone function pointer in a data region is what a
  vftable entry looks like, and if it were one, reading the COL at vftable[-1] would name the
  class of `this` immediately - and possibly say something about the caller too.

  IT IS NOT A VTABLE ENTRY. The qword before it, at 0x140e45add, is 0x14077fca0 - a CODE address
  in .text, not a COL. A vftable entry is always preceded by a pointer into the RTTI blob
  (0x140f00000-0x140f18000 in this image). 0x14077fca0 is not in that range, so the entry is not
  preceded by its own complete-object-locator.

  This is the second time this exact shape has appeared in this investigation - the previous
  section had 0x1404fe610 at 0x140e45fa8, likewise preceded by a non-COL qword. Both are data
  records that happen to contain a function address. Reporting it for the same reason: the COL
  check is the entire content of a "it is a vtable entry" claim, and a vtable entry looks exactly
  like a coincidence until you run that one check.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * R8's class is UNDETERMINED - not "unknown to the program", but not determinable from this
    function, which never dispatches on it and names it in no string. The function has no caller
    at all, so there is nowhere inside this question's scope to look next.
  * The CDataCaoTraitement identification for [R8 + 8] is INHERITED from the previous section's
    arithmetic about the +0x1da0 field. This function contributes the fact that it is the sole
    populating writer of that field; it contributes no independent evidence about the class. If
    the earlier arithmetic is wrong, this answer inherits the error.
  * "There is no instruction that writes R8" is scoped to straight-line code reachable without a
