  * ONE ERROR OF MY OWN, CORRECTED: my first two passes for this question filtered on the
    displacement appearing anywhere in the text, which returned 19 and 59 "writers" that were in
    fact all LOADS into registers. A store has the memory operand on the left of the comma. I
    rewrote the filter to require that, which is the filter reported above.

===== END =====
===== Tree insert under PrepareVecteur =====

Question: which PrepareVecteur callee adds a node to the tree at document+0x2448?
PrepareVecteur (FUN_14053bd60) runs before PV_AffectIndResult. PrepareExecData calls it at
0x14068f2ba and calls PV_AffectIndResult at 0x14068f5af. PrepareVecteur itself does LEA of
document+0x2448 at 0x14053c062 and calls FUN_14045f700 at 0x14053c069. It also calls these four
functions, which pass &document+0x2448 on:
  0x14053c125 FUN_14053bb80 -> 0x140547ff0
  0x14053c13b FUN_140532b00 -> 0x140547ff0
  0x14053c1c1 PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants (0x140532d30) -> 0x140548110
  0x14053c1fb FUN_140534a80 -> 0x14052b260, 0x14052aff0, 0x14051d480, 0x140544560
Node links are +0x00 left, +0x08 parent, +0x10 right, the nil flag is the byte at +0x19, the key
is at +0x20, and the begin and end of the node's vector are at +0x28 and +0x30.
For FUN_14045f700, 0x140547ff0, 0x140548110, 0x14051d480 and 0x140544560, say whether each one
allocates a node and links it into the tree, clears the tree, or only reads it. For each one that
inserts, give the operator new call and its size, and say whether PrepareVecteur reaches it under
PrepareExecData's arguments: param_2 == 0, selector 3, and param_6 == false. If none of them
inserts, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  NONE OF THE FIVE INSERTS A NODE. SAYING SO AND STOPPING, AS THE QUESTION INSTRUCTS.

    function          classification                          evidence
    ---------------  --------------------------------------  --------------------------------------
    FUN_14045f700     CLEARS the tree and empties a vector   relinks the header to itself twice,
                                                             then sets vector end = vector begin
    0x140547ff0       APPENDS a 0x28-byte record to an array  not a tree node; advances a cursor
                                                             by 0x28
    0x140548110       APPENDS a 0x28-byte record to an array  a near-clone of 0x140547ff0
    0x14051d480       REMOVES/DELETES a node                 calls operator_delete twice
    0x140544560       CLEARS the tree, freeing every node    calls operator_delete per node, then
                                                             relinks the header to itself

  NOT ONE OF THEM CALLS operator new. That is the direct answer to the allocation half of the
  question: there is no operator new call and no size to quote, because no allocation happens.

  So the conditional part of the question does not fire. I did not proceed to the reachability
  analysis under PrepareExecData's arguments, because there is no insert to be reached.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise, verified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  All six instruction sites named in the question are exactly as described. From PrepareVecteur
  0x14053bd60:

      14053c062  488d8b48240000  LEA RCX,[RBX + 0x2448]
      14053c069  e89236f2ff      CALL 0x14045f700
      14053c125  e856faffff      CALL 0x14053bb80
      14053c13b  e8c069ffff      CALL 0x140532b00
      14053c1c1  e86a6bffff      CALL 0x140532d30
      14053c1fb  e88088ffff      CALL 0x140534a80

  The first two are the direct case the question describes. The other four are the wrappers whose
  callees the question lists. So the five functions to classify are reached as stated.

  For the record, the 0x28 stride in the two append functions is decisive on its own: a node of
  this tree needs at least 0x38 bytes, because its vector end is at +0x30 and the record is
  addressed past it. A 0x28-byte record cannot be a node. That is the same 0x28 sub-tree array
  whose members are summed in FUN_14052b8a0 and FUN_14045bd70, from the section "Tree at 0x2448".

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. FUN_14045f700 - CLEARS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  It tears down two sub-trees and empties a vector. It never allocates and never links a new node.

      14045f72a  488b5108        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x8]
      14045f72e  488b09          MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX]
      14045f731  e8fa87feff      CALL 0x140447f30
      14045f736  498b06          MOV RAX,qword ptr [R14]
      14045f739  49894608        MOV qword ptr [R14 + 0x8],RAX      <- sub-tree 1 relinked to itself
      ...
      14045f74f  e8dc87feff      CALL 0x140447f30
      14045f754  498b4618        MOV RAX,qword ptr [R14 + 0x18]
      14045f758  49894620        MOV qword ptr [R14 + 0x20],RAX     <- sub-tree 2 relinked to itself
      ...
      14045f79f  498b4630        MOV RAX,qword ptr [R14 + 0x30]
      14045f7a3  49894638        MOV qword ptr [R14 + 0x38],RAX     <- vector end = vector begin

  The two relinks are the C idiom for "make this the sole remaining node": the sub-tree's
  begin, parent and right fields are all pointed back at itself. The third store collapses the
  vector at +0x30..+0x38 by setting its end equal to its begin. Between them the function walks
  the vector calling a virtual at +0x8 with argument 1, which is a per-element notification, not
  an insertion.

  CLASSIFICATION: clears the tree. No operator new.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. 0x140547ff0 and 0x140548110 - ARRAY APPEND, NOT A NODE INSERT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  These two are near-clones. Both bounds-check an array, grow it if the cursor has reached the
  end, copy a 0x28-byte record into the slot, and advance:

      if (uVar2 == param_1[2]) { FUN_140543ce0(param_1,1,param_3,param_4,-2); }   grow
      ...
      FUN_140447060(uVar2, lVar1, &local_res8);                                     copy
      *(undefined1 *)(uVar2 + 0x10) = *(undefined1 *)(lVar1 + 0x10);
      FUN_140447000(local_res8, lVar1 + 0x18, &local_res8);
      ...
      param_1[1] = param_1[1] + 0x28;                                             advance

  The triple param_1[0], param_1[1], param_1[2] is begin, cursor, end - a contiguous buffer, not
  a left/parent/right triple. And the 0x28 stride is too small for a node. The single
  byte-copy to slot +0x10 is a flag inside that 0x28-byte record, not the node's parent link at
  +0x08.

  CLASSIFICATION: neither inserts a tree node. Each appends one 0x28-byte record to an array of
  sub-trees. No operator new in either - the growth is delegated to FUN_140543ce0.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. 0x14051d480 - REMOVES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  It takes a node, relinks it against a replacement, and frees it:

      FUN_140447060(local_30, param_1, local_res8, param_4, -2);
      local_20 = *(undefined1 *)(param_1 + 0x10);
      FUN_140447000(local_18, param_1 + 0x18, local_res8);
      FUN_140520c60(param_1, param_2);
      FUN_140520c60(param_2, local_30);
      FUN_1404605c0(local_18, local_res8, *local_18[0], local_18[0]);
      operator_delete(local_18[0]);
      FUN_140461230(local_30, local_res8, *local_30[0], local_30[0]);
      operator_delete(local_30[0]);

  Two operator_delete calls and no operator new. This is the opposite of an insert: it unlinks a
  node and frees its storage.

  CLASSIFICATION: removes a node. Not an insert.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. 0x140544560 - CLEARS, FREEING EVERY NODE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  It walks the node list from the leftmost node, frees each node's vector, frees the node, and
  then relinks the header to itself:

      1405445a4  e867b5fdff      CALL 0x14051fb10        free the node's vector
      1405445ad  e8fcae2300      CALL 0x14077f4ae        operator delete, via a thunk
      1405445b6  807b1900        CMP byte ptr [RBX + 0x19],0x0    the nil flag, loop test
      1405445bc  488b07          MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]
      1405445bf  48894008        MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x8],RAX     node parent = node
      1405445c3  488b07          MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]
      1405445c6  488900          MOV qword ptr [RAX],RAX           node left   = node
      1405445c9  488b07          MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]
      1405445cc  48894010        MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x10],RAX    node right  = node
      1405445d0  48c7470800000000  MOV qword ptr [RDI + 0x8],0x0

  The three relinks at 0x1405445bf, 0x1405445c6 and 0x1405445cc are the giveaway: an insert would
  set a new node's links to DIFFERENT nodes. Here every link is set to the node itself, which is
  the sentinel configuration for an empty tree. The loop test at 0x1405445b6 is the nil flag at
  +0x19 described in the question, confirming this loop really is walking the node chain.

  CLASSIFICATION: clears the tree, freeing each node. Not an insert.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. On the allocation question, stated directly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The question asks for the operator new call and its size for each inserter. There is no such
  call to give, because no inserter exists among the five. I verified this two ways rather than by
  reading the decompilation once:

    * The decompiled text of each of the five functions was searched for operator new and operator
      delete. operator new: 0 occurrences in all five. operator delete: present in 0x14051d480 and
      0x140544560, absent from the other three.
    * The call target of every CALL in each of the five was enumerated. None is an allocator.
      0x140544560 calls only 0x140542a50, 0x14051fb10 and 0x14077f4ae; 0x140547ff0 and 0x140548110
      call only 0x140543ce0, 0x140447060 and 0x140447000; 0x14045f700 calls only 0x140447f30 (twice)
      and one indirect call, which is the per-element virtual at node+0x8.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. What this means, and what I did not do

  Of the five functions PrepareVecteur reaches with the document's tree header, two clear the
  tree, one removes a node, and two append 0x28-byte records to an array of sub-trees. None
  creates a node. The array that the two append functions extend is precisely the array that
  FUN_14052b8a0 and FUN_14045bd70 later walk at stride 0x28 - so a record added there becomes a
  sub-tree that the summing function can descend into, which is how the zone-0 sum acquires its
  terms. That is a plausible route to populating the sum WITHOUT any single call looking like a
  tree insert, and it is worth stating as an observation rather than a conclusion, because I did
  not follow it.

  Per the question's instruction I stopped here and did not perform the reachability analysis
  under PrepareExecData's arguments of param_2 == 0, selector 3 and param_6 == false. That
  analysis is about whether PrepareVecteur REACHES an insert; since none of the five is an
  insert, the question of reachability does not arise for any of them. I make no claim about
  whether the other callees PrepareVecteur reaches - 0x14052b260, 0x14052aff0 and the wrappers
  themselves - contain an insert that lies deeper. 0x14052b260 was classified in the section
  "Tree at 0x2448" as a lower_bound search rather than an insert, but that is outside the five
  the question asked about and I did not re-examine it here.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The classification is of the five functions the question named, at the granularity of their
    own bodies. A function among them that delegates insertion to a callee would be misfiled. I
    enumerated every direct call in all five and none is an allocator, which bounds this risk but
    does not eliminate it for a deeper chain reached through 0x140543ce0, 0x140447060 or
    0x140447000. I did not open those.
  * "Allocates a node" was taken to mean an operator new call in the function. An allocation done
    by a hand-rolled allocator, or a new returning from a different name, would not be caught by
    that test. The decompiler renders both operator new and operator delete by name, and it
    rendered operator delete in two of the five, so the naming is working.
  * I did not verify the "0x38 bytes minimum" claim for a node by measuring an allocated node; I
    inferred it from the vector end at +0x30 that the question states. The 0x28 stride argument
    rests on that inference plus the observation that the two append functions treat their
    storage as a begin/cursor/end buffer.
  * I did not re-verify that PrepareExecData calls PrepareVecteur at 0x14068f2ba and
    PV_AffectIndResult at 0x14068f5af, nor the values of its arguments. That part of the premise
    was not needed, because the conditional it gates does not fire.
  * The observation in section 7 about the 0x28 array feeding the sum is an observation. I did not
    trace a record from insertion through to a term in FUN_14052b7c0's total.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * All 26 encodings quoted above were extracted from this payload by regex and each re-read with
    a fresh memory_read: 26/26 byte-exact, 0 failures.
  * The operator-new / operator-delete classification was made twice by independent means - from
    the decompiled text and from an enumeration of every call target - and the two agree.
  * The "clears" classification for 0x140544560 rests on the three relink instructions at
    0x1405445bf, 0x1405445c6 and 0x1405445cc all storing the node's own address, which is a
    property of the instructions and not of the decompiler's prose. I read the instructions.
  * The premise call sites were read from PrepareVecteur's own listing rather than taken from the
    question.
  * No error of my own in this section.

===== END =====
===== Node allocated by FUN_140447060 =====

Question: where does the node allocated by FUN_140447060 get linked, and what is stored at its
+0x28?
FUN_140547ff0 and FUN_140548110 each call FUN_140447060 and FUN_140447000. FUN_140447060 calls
operator new (0x14076d550) with ECX = 0x40 at 0x14045cdc7, and FUN_140447000 calls it with
ECX = 0x28 at 0x14045cca7. Both set the new block's +0x00, +0x08 and +0x10 to point at itself
and write the word 0x101 at +0x18. In FUN_140547ff0, follow the pointer returned by
FUN_140447060. Say which register receives it, and quote the instruction that stores it into the
0x28-byte record or into a tree node. Then quote every instruction in FUN_140447060 and in
FUN_140547ff0 that writes offset +0x28 or +0x30 of that block. If neither function writes those
two offsets, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE NODE IS LINKED AT OFFSET +0x00 OF THE 0x28-BYTE RECORD, BY ONE INSTRUCTION:

      140447091  488903  MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX

  inside FUN_140447060, where RBX is the caller's first argument - the array cursor - and RAX is
  the freshly allocated 0x40 block. That is the only place the node pointer is stored.

  AND NEITHER FUN_140447060 NOR FUN_140547ff0 WRITES OFFSET +0x28 OR +0x30 OF THAT BLOCK. Saying
  so and stopping, as the question instructs.

      function          instructions   memory-operand instructions   writes +0x28   writes +0x30
      ---------------  -------------  ---------------------------  ------------  ------------
      FUN_140447060            23                     9                 0             0
      FUN_140547ff0            77                    17                 0             0

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Two corrections to the premise, made before using it
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Both concern attribution rather than substance; the sizes and the offsets are right.

  CORRECTION 1 - FUN_140447060 DOES NOT CALL operator new ITSELF, AND 0x14045cdc7 IS NOT IN IT.
  The address 0x14045cdc7 belongs to FUN_14045cdb0 (0x14045cdb0..0x14045ce02). FUN_140447060
  calls that helper at 0x14044708c. The 0x40 size and the self-linking are real, but they are
  FUN_14045cdb0's, one level down.

      14044708c  e81f5d0100  CALL 0x14045cdb0

  The same correction applies to the 0x45cca7 / 0x28 side: that address is in the corresponding
  helper for FUN_140447000, not in FUN_140447000 itself. I did not open that helper, because the
  question's question is about the two named functions, and the answers below do not depend on it.

  CORRECTION 2 - "BOTH SET THE NEW BLOCK'S +0x00, +0x08 AND +0x10" IS TRUE OF THE HELPER, NOT OF
  FUN_140447060. Verified in FUN_14045cdb0:

      14045cddd  488900          MOV qword ptr [RAX],RAX            +0x00 = itself
      14045cde0  488d4808        LEA RCX,[RAX + 0x8]
      14045cde9  488901          MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX            +0x08 = itself
      14045cdec  488d4810        LEA RCX,[RAX + 0x10]
      14045cdf5  488901          MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX            +0x10 = itself
      14045cdf8  66c740180101    MOV word ptr [RAX + 0x18],0x101    the 0x101 word

  with the allocation immediately above them:

      14045cdc2  b940000000  MOV ECX,0x40
      14045cdc7  e884073100  CALL 0x14076d550    -> RAX

  So the new block arrives already self-pointed at +0x00, +0x08 and +0x10 with 0x101 at +0x18, and
  the offsets +0x20 through +0x3F are left as operator new returned them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Following the pointer returned by FUN_140447060
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_140447060 is 23 instructions. Here is its whole body, with the flow:

      140447060  4c89442418  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x18],R8        save the 3rd argument
      140447065  48894c2408  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RCX        save the 1st argument
      ...
      14044707d  488bfa      MOV RDI,RDX                         RDI = 2nd argument
      140447080  488bd9      MOV RBX,RCX                         RBX = 1st argument
      140447083  33c0        XOR EAX,EAX                         RAX = 0
      140447085  488901      MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX              clear the record's +0x00
      140447088  48894108    MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RAX        clear the record's +0x08
      14044708c  e81f5d0100  CALL 0x14045cdb0                     the allocator
      140447091  488903      MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX              THE STORE
      140447094  440fb6442440  MOVZX R8D,byte ptr [RSP + 0x40]
      14044709a  488bd7      MOV RDX,RDI
      14044709d  488bcb      MOV RCX,RBX
      1404470a0  e8eb080000  CALL 0x140447990
      1404470a6  488bc3      MOV RAX,RBX                         return value = RBX
      ...
      1404470b3  c3          RET

  THE POINTER RETURNED BY FUN_140447060 IS NOT THE NODE. Its return value is RAX = RBX, which is
  the caller's first argument - the record - not the allocated block. The node is one indirection
  below the return value, at [return value + 0x00].

  WHICH REGISTER RECEIVES THE NODE: RAX, from the allocator call. The allocator returns the block
  in RAX, and 0x140447091 stores that RAX. RBX holds the destination throughout, unchanged since
  0x140447080.

  WHERE IT IS STORED: at offset +0x00 of the 0x28-byte record, by

      140447091  488903  MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX

  and into a TREE NODE nowhere. The preceding two stores at 0x140447085 and 0x140447088 zero the
  record's +0x00 and +0x08; the third overwrites the +0x00 that was just cleared with the node
  pointer, leaving the record as { node, 0, ... }.

  IN FUN_140547ff0, the call is made twice on two paths, and the return value is DISCARDED both
  times - RAX is overwritten by the next instruction on each path:

      14054805f  488b7b08      MOV RDI,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]   RDI = the array cursor
      140548077  488bd6        MOV RDX,RSI
      14054807a  488bcf        MOV RCX,RDI                     RCX = cursor = the record
      14054807d  e8deefefff    CALL 0x140447060
      140548083  0fb64610      MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [RSI + 0x10]   <- RAX overwritten at once

  and the mirrored path at 0x1405480d5 followed by 0x1405480db. So the caller does not use the
  return value at all; the node pointer is reached only through the record it was stored into.

  It follows that the node is not linked into a TREE by this code path. It is placed in a record
  of an array whose cursor is the array's +0x08 field, and that array is advanced at the end:

      1405480fa  4883430828  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x28

  This is consistent with the section "Tree insert under PrepareVecteur", where these two
  functions were classified as appending 0x28-byte records to a begin/cursor/end buffer rather
  than inserting nodes.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. The +0x28 and +0x30 question - every store, in both functions
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I enumerated every instruction in both functions with a memory operand, so the negative rests on
  a complete list rather than on a scan for a pattern.

  FUN_140447060 - nine instructions touch memory, and only three of them write to the record:

      140447060  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x18],R8          stack, the 3rd argument
      140447065  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RCX          stack, the 1st argument
      14044706f  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],-0x2        stack, the -2 marker
      140447078  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x48],RBX         stack, save RBX
      140447085  MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX                record +0x00
      140447088  MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RAX          record +0x08
      140447091  MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX                record +0x00, the node pointer
      140447094  MOVZX R8D,byte ptr [RSP + 0x40]       a READ
      1404470a9  MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x48]         a READ

      writes to +0x28 : NONE
      writes to +0x30 : NONE

  FUN_140547ff0 - seventeen instructions touch memory. The writes are:

      140548063  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x58],RDI         stack
      140548068  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x60],RDI         stack
      140548087  MOV byte ptr [RDI + 0x10],AL          record +0x10, one byte
      140548092  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x50],RCX        stack
      1405480bb  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x58],RDI        stack
      1405480c0  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x60],RDI        stack
      1405480df  MOV byte ptr [RDI + 0x10],AL          record +0x10, the mirrored path
      1405480ea  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x50],RCX        stack
      1405480fa  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x28        the array cursor, +0x28 as an AMOUNT

      writes to +0x28 of the block : NONE
      writes to +0x30 of the block : NONE

  Two things in that list are worth disambiguating, because they contain the digits 0x28 and could
  be mistaken for hits on a textual search:

    * 1405480fa uses 0x28, but as the amount ADDED to the array's cursor at [RBX + 0x8]. It is not
      a write to offset 0x28 of the block, and it does not touch the block at all.
    * 140548087 and 1405480df write a single BYTE at [RDI + 0x10]. RDI is the record, and +0x10 is
      a flag byte inside the 0x28-byte record - not the node's parent link at +0x08, and not
      anything at +0x28.

  So: NEITHER FUNCTION WRITES OFFSET +0x28 OR +0x30 OF THE 0x40 BLOCK. Stating that and stopping.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. What this means, and where the +0x28 must therefore come from
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The block allocated by FUN_14045cdb0 is 0x40 bytes, self-pointed at +0x00, +0x08 and +0x10, with
  0x101 written at +0x18. Its +0x28 and +0x30 - the vector begin and end that the summing function
  FUN_14052b7c0 reads as node+0x28 and node+0x30 - are never written by the allocating function or
  by the function that stores the pointer.

  That does not mean they are never written. It means the write happens in a function further
  down, and the two candidates reachable from this code are FUN_140447990 - called by
  FUN_140447060 at 0x1404470a0 with RCX = RBX, the record, not the block - and FUN_140447000, which
  the two append functions call with RCX = RDI + 0x18. I did not open either, and I am not
  claiming which one supplies the vector fields. Stating the boundary of what I checked is the
  honest end of this question.

  One consequence is worth flagging for the rest of the investigation. If FUN_14052b7c0 sums
  (node+0x30 - node+0x28) >> 3 over these nodes, and the node is linked into a record rather than
  into the tree at document+0x2448, then this path is not the one that feeds the zone-0 sum at
  all - it builds the 0x28-stride sub-tree array instead, which the summing function reaches
  through FUN_14052b8a0 and FUN_14045bd70. That is consistent with the previous section, and I
  record it as an observation rather than a conclusion.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The negative covers the two functions the question named, at the level of their own
    instructions. Neither calls operator new directly - the allocation is in FUN_14045cdb0 - so if
    the question intended the allocating helper to be included, that is a third function I did
    enumerate separately and which also writes nothing at +0x28 or +0x30. Its full body is quoted
    in section 1, and its last write is the 0x101 word at +0x18.
  * I did not open FUN_140447990 or FUN_140447000, so I make no claim about whether either writes
    the vector fields. Both are named in the question as being called by the two append functions,
    and either could be where the +0x28 and +0x30 are set.
  * "The return value is discarded" is a statement about straight-line code on the two paths
    shown. Both are short and the overwriting instruction immediately follows the call in each;
    I read both paths in full.
  * I did not verify the 0x28 / 0x45cca7 side of the premise at all, since the question's two
    subject functions are FUN_140447060 and FUN_140547ff0 and FUN_140447000 is neither. I note
    the attribution correction in section 1 without having confirmed it, and I flag that as such -
    it is an inference from the symmetry of the helper at 0x14045cdb0, not a measurement.
  * I did not determine the class of the record or of the node. The question did not ask, and the
    RTTI for a node allocated by operator new with no vtable store is not something I looked for.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * All 29 encodings quoted above were extracted from this payload by regex and each re-read with
    a fresh memory_read: 29/29 byte-exact, 0 failures.
  * The premise attribution was checked before use, and both corrections in section 1 are
    measurements - function_at placed 0x14045cdc7 in FUN_14045cdb0, and FUN_140447060's call graph
    shows it calling that helper at 0x14044708c rather than calling operator new itself.
  * The +0x28 / +0x30 negative rests on a COMPLETE enumeration of every memory-operand
    instruction in both functions - 9 in FUN_140447060 and 17 in FUN_140547ff0, all listed in
    section 3 - not on a pattern search that might have missed a form. I also disambiguated the two
    instructions that contain the digits 0x28 but are not writes to the block.
  * The return-value claim is supported by the instruction pair at 0x140447091 and 0x1404470a6,
    read from the listing: RAX is set to the record on the way out, and in both callers it is
    overwritten by the very next instruction.
  * Two errors of my own in this section, both found and corrected before the result was written.
    First, I searched for 0x14045cdc7 as if it were inside FUN_140447060 and got an empty
    instruction list, which was the clue that it belonged to a different function. Second, my
    first pass at the store enumeration used a mnemonic filter that also admitted MOVZX reads, so
    the list initially mixed loads with stores; I separated them in the reported version and the
    counts of writes in section 3 reflect only the storing instructions.

===== END =====
===== Vector copy at node +0x28 =====

Question: does FUN_140452960 copy the elements, or only the three pointers?
FUN_140447640 calls it at 0x14044768b with RCX = new node + 0x28 and RDX = source node + 0x28.
Quote the instructions that read the source's begin, end and capacity, and the instructions that
write the destination's. If it allocates a new buffer, give the call and the size register. If it
only copies the three pointer fields and shares the source buffer, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  IT COPIES THE ELEMENTS. IT ALLOCATES A NEW BUFFER AND MEMmOVES THE CONTENTS. IT DOES NOT SHARE
  THE SOURCE BUFFER.

      allocation call   1404529d1  e85ac51500  CALL 0x1405aef30
      size register     RDX, set at 1404529ce from the ELEMENT COUNT
      allocation size   count * 8, computed inside the allocator at 1405aef56
      element copy      1404529fb  ff15ef949000  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5bef0]   <- memmove

  The source's begin and end are read and the byte count derived from them. The source's CAPACITY
  is never read. The destination's three pointer fields are all written to point into the NEW
  buffer. So the "only copies three pointers and shares" branch does not apply.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise, verified - and one detail worth stating
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The call site is exactly as described:

      14044767d  488b07          MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]
      140447680  488901          MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX        <- the caller copies the key
      140447683  488d5708        LEA RDX,[RDI + 0x8]
      140447687  4883c108        ADD RCX,0x8
      14044768b  e8d0b20000      CALL 0x140452960

  One clarification on the argument values. The question describes RCX and RDX as "new node +
  0x28" and "source node + 0x28". At the call instruction they are the addresses DEST + 0x28 and
  SOURCE + 0x28 - the two instructions above turn whatever base the caller held into those by
  adding 0x8 to RCX and forming RDI + 0x8 in RDX. Either way, inside FUN_140452960 the two
  arguments point at the vector's FIRST field, so:

      RCX = &dest.begin    RDX = &source.begin
      and therefore  [RCX + 0x8] = dest.end, [RCX + 0x10] = dest.capacity
                       [RDX + 0x8] = source.end, [RDX + 0x10] = source.capacity

  Also note that the caller has ALREADY copied the field at +0x20 of the node - the key - with the
  instruction at 0x140447680, before making this call. FUN_140452960 is concerned only with the
  vector at +0x28.

  FUN_140452960 is 0x140452960..0x140452a21, 50 instructions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. The instructions that READ the source
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  It saves the source base in R14 at the first instruction, then reads it twice - once to compute
  the element count, once to set up the copy:

      140452983  4c8bf2  MOV R14,RDX          <- source base preserved
      140452986  488bf1  MOV RSI,RCX          <- dest base preserved

      140452996  488b5a08  MOV RBX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]    <- READ source.end
      14045299a  482b1a    SUB RBX,qword ptr [RDX]          <- READ source.begin, subtract
      14045299d  48c1fb03  SAR RBX,0x3                      <- / 8  => ELEMENT COUNT

      1404529e8  498b7e08  MOV RDI,qword ptr [R14 + 0x8]    <- READ source.end again
      1404529ec  498b16    MOV RDX,qword ptr [R14]          <- READ source.begin again
      1404529f2  482bfa    SUB RDI,RDX                      <- byte count = end - begin

  SOURCE BEGIN   read at 14045299a and 1404529ec
  SOURCE END     read at 140452996 and 1404529e8
  SOURCE CAPACITY  NEVER READ. There is no instruction in the function that touches
                    [RDX + 0x10] or [R14 + 0x10].

  That is not an oversight in my reading - the complete 50-instruction body is enumerated in
  section 5 and contains no such access. A vector copy legitimately does not need the source's
  capacity: the destination's capacity is computed fresh for the count it is given.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. The instructions that WRITE the destination
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The destination's three fields are zeroed, then all three are set to point into the new buffer:

      ZEROED FIRST, twice over - the second pass is after the count is known:
      14045298b  488901    MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX           dest.begin    = 0
      14045298e  48894108  MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RAX     dest.end      = 0
      140452992  48894110  MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x10],RAX    dest.capacity = 0
      1404529a1  488901    MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX           dest.begin    = 0
      1404529a4  48894108  MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RAX     dest.end      = 0
      1404529a8  48894110  MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x10],RAX    dest.capacity = 0

      THEN SET INTO THE NEW BUFFER:
      1404529d6  488906    MOV qword ptr [RSI],RAX           dest.begin    = new buffer
      1404529d9  48894608  MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x8],RAX     dest.end      = new buffer
      1404529e0  488d0cd8  LEA RCX,[RAX + RBX * 0x8]        new buffer + count*8
      1404529e4  48894e10  MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x10],RCX    dest.capacity = begin + count*8
      140452a01  488d041f  LEA RAX,[RDI + RBX * 0x1]        new buffer + byte count
      140452a05  48894608  MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x8],RAX     dest.end      = new buffer + bytes

  RSI holds the destination base throughout, saved at 0x140452986. All three destination fields
  end up pointing into the newly allocated block, and none of them retains the source's pointer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. The allocation and the element copy
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ALLOCATION. The count computed at 0x14045299d is passed in RDX:

      1404529ac  4885db          TEST RBX,RBX         <- if count is zero, skip to the end
      1404529af  7458            JZ 0x140452a09
      1404529b1  48b8ffffffffffffff1f  MOV RAX,0x1fffffffffffffff
      1404529bb  483bd8          CMP RBX,RAX          <- length_error if count too large
      1404529ce  488bd3          MOV RDX,RBX          <- SIZE REGISTER = element count
      1404529d1  e85ac51500      CALL 0x1405aef30     <- the allocator

  0x1405aef30 is a vector element allocator, not operator new directly. It takes the COUNT and
  scales it:

      1405aef34  4885d2                    TEST RDX,RDX          <- 0 count returns null
      1405aef40  48b8ffffffffffffff1f      MOV RAX,0x1fffffffffffffff
      1405aef4a  483bd0                    CMP RDX,RAX           <- bad_alloc guard
      1405aef56  488d0cd500000000          LEA RCX,[RDX * 0x8]    <- COUNT * 8 = byte size
      1405aef5e  4881f900100000            CMP RCX,0x1000
      1405aef67  488d4127                  LEA RAX,[RCX + 0x27]   <- round up
      1405aef7a  e8d1e51b00                CALL 0x14076d550       <- operator new
      1405aef8e  4883c027                  ADD RAX,0x27
      1405aef92  4883e0e0                  AND RAX,-0x20         <- 32-byte alignment
      1405aef96  488948f8                  MOV qword ptr [RAX + -0x8],RCX   <- store byte size

  So the size handed to operator new is the element count multiplied by eight and rounded up to a
  32-byte boundary, and the byte size is stashed immediately below the returned pointer, as
  operator new[] does.

  ELEMENT COPY. The three arguments are set up and the copy made:

      1404529e8  498b7e08  MOV RDI,qword ptr [R14 + 0x8]   <- arg3, source.end
      1404529ec  498b16    MOV RDX,qword ptr [R14]         <- arg2, source.begin
      1404529f2  482bfa    SUB RDI,RDX                    <- arg3 = byte count
      1404529f5  4c8bc7    MOV R8,RDI                     <- R8 = byte count
      1404529f8  488bc8    MOV RCX,RAX                    <- RCX = new buffer
      1404529fb  ff15ef949000  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5bef0]

  The call goes through the IAT slot at 0x140d5bef0. I re-confirmed that slot's identity rather
  than assuming it from an earlier section: the slot holds RVA 0x10ba1a8, and
  imagebase + 0x10ba1a8 + 2 = 0x1410ba1aa, which is a defined string reading "memmove". So this is
  memmove(new_buffer, source_begin, byte_count) - the standard argument order, and a real
  element-by-element copy, not a pointer copy.

  The result is then finalised:

      1404529dd  488b06    MOV RAX,qword ptr [RSI]         <- reload dest.begin
      140452a09  488bc6    MOV RAX,RSI                    <- return the destination

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Completeness - the whole function, so the negative rests on a full read
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Every instruction in FUN_140452960, for the record:

      140452960  48894c2408  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RCX
      140452965  4156        PUSH R14
      140452967  4883ec30    SUB RSP,0x30
      14045296b  48c7442420feffffff  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],-0x2

      140452989  33c0        XOR EAX,EAX
      14045298b  488901      MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX

      140452992  48894110    MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x10],RAX
      140452996  488b5a08    MOV RBX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]

      1404529a4  48894108    MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RAX

      1404529e8  498b7e08    MOV RDI,qword ptr [R14 + 0x8]
      1404529ec  498b16      MOV RDX,qword ptr [R14]
      1404529ef  488bd8      MOV RBX,RAX
      1404529f2  482bfa      SUB RDI,RDX
      1404529f5  4c8bc7      MOV R8,RDI
      1404529f8  488bc8      MOV RCX,RAX
      1404529fb  ff15ef949000  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5bef0]
      140452a01  488d041f    LEA RAX,[RDI + RBX * 0x1]

  There is no access to [RDX + 0x10] or [R14 + 0x10] anywhere in the list, which is the basis for
  the "source capacity never read" statement. The two calls that write memory other than the

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. What this means for the node at +0x28

  This resolves a loose end from the section "Node allocated by FUN_140447060". That section found
  that the 0x40 block's +0x28 and +0x30 - the vector begin and end that the summing function
  FUN_14052b7c0 reads - are not written by FUN_140447060 or by FUN_140547ff0, and named
  FUN_140447990 and FUN_140447000 as the two candidates further down.

  FUN_140452960 is neither of them, and it is not reached from FUN_140447060 at all - FUN_140447060
  calls 0x140447990, not 0x140452960. So this section does not close that loose end, and I am not
  claiming it does. What it does establish is the answer to the question asked: when a node's
  vector is copied by this routine, the copy is deep - a fresh allocation sized from the element
  count, and a memmove of the byte range - so the destination does not alias the source.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * "The source capacity is never read" is a statement about FUN_140452960's 50 instructions,
    which are listed in full above. If some caller pre-set the destination's capacity and expected
    it to be reused, that behaviour is not in this function.
  * I established the IAT slot 0x140d5bef0 is memmove from the import name at
    imagebase + 0x10ba1a8 + 2. I did not follow the call into the CRT to confirm it behaves as
    memmove, and I make no claim beyond its identity and its three arguments.
  * I did not open FUN_140447990, which is what FUN_140447060 actually calls. It remains a
    candidate for where the node's +0x28 and +0x30 are established, and this section leaves that
    exactly where it was.
  * The question's phrase "RCX = new node + 0x28" is the value at the call instruction. I have
    described it as it is at entry to FUN_140452960, which is what the function's own instructions
    operate on. If the caller held node + 0x20 at 0x140447680 and the question's +0x28 refers to
    the node base rather than the register, the two descriptions agree on the field being copied -
    the vector at node + 0x28.
  * I did not check whether any OTHER caller of FUN_140452960 passes different arguments or relies
    on the source capacity. This section is about the one call site named.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * All 65 encodings quoted above were extracted from this payload by regex and each re-read with
    a fresh memory_read: 65/65 byte-exact, 0 failures.
  * The memmove identification is arithmetic, not a name match on the call operand: the IAT slot
    holds RVA 0x10ba1a8 and imagebase + 0x10ba1a8 + 2 = 0x1410ba1aa reads "memmove". I re-derived
    this rather than relying on the earlier section that established the same slot.
  * The allocator's behaviour - count times eight, rounded to 32 bytes - is read from
    FUN_1405aef30's own instructions at 0x1405aef56, 0x1405aef67, 0x1405aef8e and 0x1405aef92, and
    agrees with its decompilation.
  * The "never reads source capacity" claim rests on a complete listing of all 50 instructions,
    not on a search for a displacement. That is why the full body is reproduced in section 5.
  * The size register is identified from the instruction that sets it, 0x1404529ce MOV RDX,RBX,
    immediately before the allocator call - not from the decompiler's parameter naming.
  * No error of my own in this section.

===== END =====
===== Writers of node vector +0x28 =====

Question: what writes the element count of the vector at node+0x28 before FUN_140452960 copies it?

The copy at 0x140452996 reads [source+8] and [source], subtracts, and shifts right by 3. That is
the count. The source is the node passed to FUN_140447640 in RDX. Find the instructions that
store a pointer into a field at node offset +0x28, +0x30 or +0x38, and name the function for
each. Keep only the stores that are not inside FUN_140452960 itself. If the only writer is the
copy, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE COPY IS NOT THE ONLY WRITER. There are three other functions that store into a field at
  node +0x28, +0x30 or +0x38, and one of them is what actually produces a non-zero count:

      FUN_140547800    the node-vector APPENDER. Advances node+0x30 by 8. THIS IS THE WRITER OF
                      THE COUNT for a growing vector.
      FUN_14045d8f0    the vector REALLOCATE, reached by tail-jump from FUN_140543880 which
                      FUN_140547800 calls. Rewrites all three of node+0x28, node+0x30,
                      node+0x38 onto a fresh buffer.
      FUN_1405162f0    the node CONSTRUCTOR for this family. Zeroes all three fields.
      FUN_140472aa0    the tree DESTROY. Frees the buffer, then zeroes all three fields.

  FUN_140547800 is called with RCX = node + 0x28, so its [RBX + 0x8] is node + 0x30 - the very
  field FUN_140452960 subtracts to form the count. That closes the loose end left open by the
  sections "Node allocated by FUN_140447060" and "Vector copy at node +0x28".

      count writer (append)     14054784e  4883430808  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8
      count writer (append)     140547880  4883430808  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8
      with                     RBX = RCX = node + 0x28,  so [RBX + 0x8] = node + 0x30

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise, verified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The question states the source node arrives in RDX. Confirmed at the entry of FUN_140447640:

      140447654  488bfa        MOV RDI,RDX
      140447657  e8545a0100    CALL 0x14045d0b0

  And the copy call in that same function, with the base already advanced to node + 0x28:

      14044766a  488d4820      LEA RCX,[RAX + 0x20]
      140447687  4883c108      ADD RCX,0x8
      14044768b  e8d0b20000    CALL 0x140452960

  The count itself is formed at instruction level, as the question describes:

      140452996  488b5a08      MOV RBX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]    <- source end   = node+0x30
      14045299a  482b1a        SUB RBX,qword ptr [RDX]          <- source begin = node+0x28
      14045299d  48c1fb03      SAR RBX,0x3                      <- the count

  The layout is confirmed independently by the SECOND caller of FUN_140452960, which forms the
  same address by arithmetic rather than inheriting it:

      14052b2ac  4883c228      ADD RDX,0x28
      14052b2b0  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX
      14052b2b3  e8a876f2ff    CALL 0x140452960

  That is FUN_14052b260, a tree lower-bound on the key at node+0x20 that copies out the matching
  node's vector. node + 0x28 is the vector base, reached by adding 0x28 to a node pointer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Why the obvious search method does not work, and what I did instead
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I first tried the literal method the question implies: search every instruction whose
  destination operand is a qword store at displacement 0x28, 0x30 or 0x38. That fails as an
  identification method, and I report the numbers so the failure is on the record:

    * Program-wide over .text, the search for "0x28" returns 20000 mentions and is SATURATED at
      the tool's limit. I do not have a complete program-wide count and I do not claim one.
    * Restricted to the 0x140440000-0x140560000 window that contains every node function in this
      trace, the search IS complete (4785 mentions for 0x28, 6810 for 0x30, 3215 for 0x38) and
      yields 845 / 814 / 437 qword stores, of which 163 / 102 / 84 are non-stack. Those 163 land
      in roughly 120 unrelated functions.
    * Intersecting to the 11 functions that write all three of +0x28, +0x30 and +0x38 is not
      decisive either. I checked the two that write two different bases, FUN_14046de20 and
      FUN_14046df00, and they are a DIFFERENT structure: a 0x50-byte record with the magic
      constant 0x42ff0000 written at offset 0, which decompiles as class "Mat" and calls
      0x14076d76c. Not a node. Displacement alone cannot separate a node from a graphics record
      that happens to have fields at the same offsets.

  So I identified the writers by following the node's lifecycle instead - who allocates it, who
  initialises it, who appends to it, who destroys it - and then confirming each by instruction
  level. That is what sections 3 to 6 give. The displacement search is reported above as a dead
  end, not as the method.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. FUN_140547800 - the appender, and the writer of the count
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_140547800 takes RCX = the vector base and RDX = the element to insert or append. It is a
  std::vector insert-or-append over 8-byte elements: it locates the insertion point, grows if
  the end has reached the capacity, stores one qword, and advances the end by 8.

  The three vector fields it reads and the one it advances:

      14054780a  488b4108      MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x8]    <- end      (node+0x30)
      14054780e  488bfa        MOV RDI,RDX
      140547811  488bd9        MOV RBX,RCX                       <- RBX = node + 0x28
      140547814  483bd0        CMP RDX,RAX                       <- element <= end?
      140547817  7345          JNC 0x14054785e                   <- else append path
      140547819  488b09        MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX]           <- begin    (node+0x28)
      14054781c  483bca        CMP RCX,RDX
      14054781f  773d          JA 0x14054785e

  Grow test, capacity is node+0x38:

      140547828  483b4310      CMP RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x10]    <- end == capacity?
      14054782e  ba01000000    MOV EDX,0x1
      140547833  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX                       <- RBX = node + 0x28
      140547836  e845c0ffff    CALL 0x140543880                  <- the grow

  THE COUNT IS WRITTEN HERE, on the in-range path - the store of the element, then the bump of
  the end pointer that changes the count:

      14054783b  488b5308      MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]     <- end = node+0x30
      14054783f  4885d2        TEST RDX,RDX
      140547842  743c          JZ 0x140547880
      140547844  488b03        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX]           <- begin = node+0x28
      140547847  488b0cf8      MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + RDI*0x8] <- element to copy in
      14054784b  48890a        MOV qword ptr [RDX],RCX           <- store it
      14054784e  4883430808    ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8     <- END += 8  => COUNT INCREASES

  And on the plain append path, which is the one that builds a node's vector from empty:

      14054785e  483b4310      CMP RAX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x10]
      140547862  750d          JNZ 0x140547871
      140547864  ba01000000    MOV EDX,0x1
      140547869  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX
      14054786c  e80fc0ffff    CALL 0x140543880
      140547871  488b4b08      MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]
      140547875  4885c9        TEST RCX,RCX
      140547878  7406          JZ 0x140547880
      14054787a  488b07        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]
      14054787d  488901        MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX           <- store the element
      140547880  4883430808    ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x8     <- END += 8  => COUNT INCREASES

  RBX holds the vector base, set once near the top of the function:

      14054780e  488bfa        MOV RDI,RDX                        <- RDI = the element
      140547811  488bd9        MOV RBX,RCX                        <- RBX = node + 0x28

  Note for the record, and it is a tooling fault rather than only mine: the FIRST listing render
  I took these from returned the byte string "488bf9" at 0x140547811, which is MOV RDI,RDX and
  contradicts the mnemonic the same render gave ("MOV RBX,RCX"). I transcribed that byte string
  into this file before checking it. A fresh listing and an independent memory_read both return
  488bd9, which is the encoding that actually matches the mnemonic, and 488bfa at 0x14054780e.
  The same first render returned "488b4310" at 0x140547828 and 0x14054785e where the real bytes
  are 483b4310. Both are corrected below from memory_read, not from the listing.

  So with RBX = node + 0x28, the two instructions the question is really about are:

      [RBX + 0x0]  = node + 0x28   begin
      [RBX + 0x8]  = node + 0x30   end      <- the field FUN_140452960 subtracts
      [RBX + 0x10] = node + 0x38   capacity

  and 14054784e / 140547880 are the two instructions that change the count.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Who calls it with node + 0x28 - the base is node + 0x28, not the node
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Two call sites, both unambiguous at instruction level.

  (a) FUN_140523880, at 0x14052394c. The node was just created by FUN_1405162f0 and linked into
      the tree by FUN_140519f50; RBX then holds the node:

      140523923  e8c829ffff    CALL 0x1405162f0
      140523937  4c8d4820      LEA R9,[RAX + 0x20]
      14052393b  e81066ffff    CALL 0x140519f50
      140523940  488b5de8      MOV RBX,qword ptr [RBP + -0x18]   <- RBX = the node
      140523944  488d4b28      LEA RCX,[RBX + 0x28]              <- RCX = node + 0x28
      140523948  488d5530      LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x30]              <- RDX = &element
      14052394c  e8af3e0200    CALL 0x140547800

  (b) PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants, at 0x1405331ca. This is a live PV_ function from the panel-load
      set, and it forms the base with an explicit add:

      1405331ba  488b8db0000000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBP + 0xb0]   <- RCX = a node pointer
      1405331c1  4883c128        ADD RCX,0x28                     <- RCX = node + 0x28
      1405331c5  488d542450      LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x50]             <- RDX = &element
      1405331ca  e831460100      CALL 0x140547800

  FUN_140547800 has 11 direct call sites program-wide. I opened two of them, the two above,
  because those are the ones in the node-building path. I did NOT open the other nine, so I do
  not claim that node+0x28 is the base at all eleven; I claim it at these two.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. The other two writers, named
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5a. FUN_14045d8f0 - the reallocate, reached from FUN_140547800 via FUN_140543880
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_140543880 is a capacity calculator. It computes the new capacity in RDX, restores RCX to
  the vector base in R9, and TAIL-JUMPS, so the field writes happen in the target:

      140543884  4c8b5110      MOV R10,qword ptr [RCX + 0x10]    <- capacity (node+0x38)
      14054388b  4c8b4108      MOV R8,qword ptr [RCX + 0x8]     <- end      (node+0x30)
      140543899  483bc2        CMP RAX,RDX
      14054389c  735f          JNC 0x1405438fd                   <- enough room, return
      1405438f1  498bc9        MOV RCX,R9                       <- restore the base
      1405438f8  e9f39ff1ff    JMP 0x14045d8f0                   <- TAIL JUMP, no return

  FUN_14045d8f0 then allocates a new buffer, memmoves the old contents across and rewrites all
  three fields onto it:

      14045d910  4c8bf2        MOV R14,RDX                      <- new capacity
      14045d913  488bd9        MOV RBX,RCX                      <- RBX = node + 0x28
      14045d916  e815161500    CALL 0x1405aef30                  <- allocate, count in RDX
      14045d91b  488bf0        MOV RSI,RAX                      <- new buffer
      14045d923  4c8b4308      MOV R8,qword ptr [RBX + 0x8]     <- old end
      14045d927  488b13        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX]           <- old begin
      14045d95d  4a8d04f6      LEA RAX,[RSI + R14*0x8]
      14045d961  48894310      MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x10],RAX    <- node+0x38 = capacity
      14045d965  488d04fe      LEA RAX,[RSI + RDI*0x8]
      14045d969  48894308      MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],RAX     <- node+0x30 = end
      14045d96d  488933        MOV qword ptr [RBX],RSI           <- node+0x28 = begin

  Note that 0x14045d969 recomputes the end from the OLD element count RDI, not from the new
  capacity, so the count survives the reallocation unchanged. It rewrites the pointer, not the
  value.

5b. FUN_1405162f0 - the constructor, which zeroes all three
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  This is the node constructor for the family that FUN_140523880 builds. R9 is set to node + 0x20
  and the three vector fields are the next three qwords after it:

      140516306  e8a56df4ff    CALL 0x14045d0b0                  <- allocate the 0x40 node
      140516310  66c740180000  MOV word ptr [RAX + 0x18],0x0
      140516316  4c8d4820      LEA R9,[RAX + 0x20]              <- R9 = node + 0x20
      14051631a  4d85c9        TEST R9,R9
      14051631d  7417          JZ 0x140516336
      14051631f  488b0b        MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX]
      140516322  488b11        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RCX]
      140516325  498911        MOV qword ptr [R9],RDX            <- node+0x20 = key
      140516328  33c9          XOR ECX,ECX                       <- zero
      14051632a  49894908      MOV qword ptr [R9 + 0x8],RCX     <- node+0x28 = 0  (begin)
      14051632e  49894910      MOV qword ptr [R9 + 0x10],RCX    <- node+0x30 = 0  (end)
      140516332  49894918      MOV qword ptr [R9 + 0x18],RCX    <- node+0x38 = 0  (cap)

  0x14051632a, 0x14051632e and 0x140516332 are stores of zero, so they establish a count of
  zero. They are writers of the fields but they are not what makes a count non-zero.

5c. FUN_140472aa0 - the destroy, which frees the buffer then zeroes all three
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_140472aa0 recurses over the tree, frees each node's buffer with operator delete and then
  clears the three fields before freeing the node itself:

      140472b36  e873c93000    CALL 0x14077f4ae                  <- operator_delete(buffer)
      140472b3b  48896b28      MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x28],RBP    <- node+0x28 = 0
      140472b3f  48896b30      MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x30],RBP    <- node+0x30 = 0
      140472b43  48896b38      MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x38],RBP    <- node+0x38 = 0
      140472b47  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX
      140472b4a  e85fc93000    CALL 0x14077f4ae                  <- operator_delete(node)

  RBP is zero on that path: 140472ac7 XOR EBP,EBP and 140472ac2 saves it. So again these are
  count-zeroing stores, reached only during teardown.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Summary table
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUNCTION             node+0x28 (begin)      node+0x30 (end/count)   node+0x38 (cap)
  ------------------  ---------------------  ---------------------  -----------------
  FUN_140547800       reads only             14054784e ADD +8        reads only
                       (grows via 140543880)  140547880 ADD +8        (grows via 140543880)
  FUN_14045d8f0       14045d96d MOV          14045d969 MOV           14045d961 MOV
                       new buffer             new+count*8             new+cap*8
  FUN_1405162f0       14051632a = 0          14051632e = 0           140516332 = 0
  FUN_140472aa0       140472b3b = 0          140472b3f = 0           140472b43 = 0
  ------------------  ---------------------  ---------------------  -----------------
  FUN_140452960       1404529d6              140452a05               1404529e4
  (EXCLUDED BY THE QUESTION - the copy)

  So: the answer to "what writes the element count" is FUN_140547800, at 0x14054784e or
  0x140547880 depending on whether the element lands in range or is appended, with the value
  coming from node+0x38 growing through FUN_140543880 into FUN_14045d8f0. FUN_1405162f0 and
  FUN_140472aa0 also store into those three offsets but only ever store zero, at construction and
  at teardown respectively.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. What this closes, and what it does not
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  This closes the loose end recorded in the section "Node allocated by FUN_140447060", which
  noted that the +0x28 and +0x30 fields were not written by FUN_140447060 or FUN_140547ff0 and
  named FUN_140447990 and FUN_140447000 as the candidates further down. I opened
  FUN_140447990 and it writes the node's tree self-links (+0x00 and +0x10), not its vector. I
  then found the writer by working backwards from the node allocators rather than forwards from
  the reader, and it is neither of those two candidates.

  It also adds a writer that earlier sections in this file did not have. The section "Tree insert
  under PrepareVecteur" examined FUN_14045f700, FUN_140547ff0, FUN_140548110, FUN_14051d480 and
  FUN_140544560. FUN_140547800 sits in the same address range as FUN_140547ff0 and was not in
  that set.

  What it does not do: I have not shown that the vector is non-empty at the moment FUN_140452960
  runs. The chain FUN_140523880 builds a node, inserts it, and appends one element to it, which
  is consistent with a count of 1 at copy time, but I have not executed anything and I am not
  asserting a runtime value.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The displacement search I report in section 2 is COMPLETE only for the 0x140440000-0x140560000
    window. Program-wide it saturates at the tool's 20000-mention limit, so I have no
    program-wide count of stores to 0x28/0x30/0x38 and I make no claim about one. I identified
    the writers by lifecycle, not by exhausting the displacement space, and a writer I did not
    reach by that route would not appear above.
  * FUN_140547800 has 11 call sites. I opened 2. The other 9 may pass bases other than node+0x28.
  * FUN_140543880 is reached by a tail JMP, so it is not a normal callee. I treated
    FUN_14045d8f0 as part of the grow path on the strength of that JMP; I did not check for other
    entries into FUN_14045d8f0.
  * "node" throughout means the 0x40 block that FUN_14045cdb0 and FUN_14045d0b0 allocate. I have
    not proven that the node FUN_140523880 appends to is byte-identical in layout to the node
    FUN_140447640 later copies. Both are 0x40, both self-link at +0x00/+0x08/+0x10, both carry a
    flag at +0x19, and both are read with +0x20 as a key by FUN_14052a740 and FUN_14052b7c0 -
    but the identification is by convergent layout evidence, not by a single instruction.
  * 0x14077f4ae is treated as operator delete on the strength of its position between the buffer
    free and the three zeroing stores. I did not verify the import.
  * My own error in this section, stated rather than dropped: three byte strings I quoted were
    wrong. One originated in a corrupted listing render (0x140547811, 0x140547828, 0x14054785e
    - see the note in section 3) and I transcribed them without checking. All three are now
    taken from memory_read and the count below is 87/87.

9. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Every ADDR/BYTES pair quoted in this section was extracted from this file by regex and
    re-read with a fresh memory_read. The count and result are recorded with the append.
  * Call targets were re-derived from the rel32 with SIGNED arithmetic, not taken from the
    rendered operand. Self-test on a known call: 14057c410 e8 8b 29 00 00 -> 0x14057eda0.
    Applied to 14045be39 e8 f2 c5 fe ff -> 0x140448430, and to every CALL quoted above.
  * The claim that node+0x28 is the vector base is established three independent ways: the
    arithmetic ADD RDX,0x28 at 0x14052b2ac, the LEA RCX,[RBX + 0x28] at 0x140523944, and the
    ADD RCX,0x28 at 0x1405331c1. It is not inherited from an earlier section.
  * Every negative in this section rests on a complete listing of the function in question, not
    on a search for a displacement. The 44-instruction body of FUN_140547800, the 37 of
    FUN_140543880, the 41 of FUN_14045d8f0, the 15 of FUN_1405162f0 and the 59 of
    FUN_140472aa0 were each read in full.
  * No program was saved. The project was opened read-only with update_analysis off, and
    program_mode_get reported read_only true with no active transaction before closing.
