===== Zone node at 0xb0 =====

Question: in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants, where does the node at [RBP+0xb0] come from, and does the
append at 0x1405331ca run under PrepareExecData's arguments?

At 0x1405331ba the function loads RCX from [RBP+0xb0], adds 0x28, and calls FUN_140547800 at
0x1405331ca. Quote the instruction that writes [RBP+0xb0], and say whether the value is a node
allocated in this function or a node loaded from the tree at document+0x2448. Then give the
condition that guards 0x1405331ca. PrepareExecData calls PrepareVecteur with param_2 = 0,
selector 3 and param_6 = false, and PrepareVecteur calls this function at 0x14053c1c1. Say
whether that condition is true under those arguments. If the append is skipped under those
arguments, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer, and two things the question gets wrong
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  WHERE [RBP+0xb0] COMES FROM: it is not written by any instruction in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants.
  It is an OUT-PARAMETER. The address is formed and handed to FUN_14051bc60 at 0x1405331b5, and
  that function writes it in one of two places:

      14051bcb6  48891f        MOV qword ptr [RDI],RBX      <- the node FOUND by key lookup
      14051bcbc  c6470800      MOV byte ptr [RDI + 0x8],0x0 <- found flag = 0
      ...
      14051bd13  488907        MOV qword ptr [RDI],RAX      <- a node NEWLY INSERTED
      14051bd19  c6470801      MOV byte ptr [RDI + 0x8],0x1 <- inserted flag = 1

      address handed over:   1405331aa  488d95b0000000  LEA RDX,[RBP + 0xb0]

  IT IS NEITHER OF THE TWO THINGS THE QUESTION OFFERS. It is not a node allocated directly in
  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants - the allocation is two calls deeper, inside FUN_14051bc60. And it is
  NOT loaded from the tree at document+0x2448. It comes from a LOCAL tree that
  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants default-constructs in its own stack frame on every call:

      140532df9  48897598      MOV qword ptr [RBP + -0x68],RSI
      140532e01  488d4d98      LEA RCX,[RBP + -0x68]
      140532e05  e8d6ef0000    CALL 0x140541de0               <- builds the 0x40 sentinel
      140532e0a  48894598      MOV qword ptr [RBP + -0x68],RAX

  THE GUARD on 0x1405331ca is:

      140533163  81fb00008000  CMP EBX,0x800000
      140533169  752f          JNZ 0x14053319a                <- append runs when EBX != 0x800000

  where EBX was loaded at 0x140532e69 as dword [RAX+0x8] - a per-ZONE DATA FIELD, not a
  parameter of any of these functions.

  SO THE ANSWER TO "IS IT TRUE UNDER THOSE ARGUMENTS" IS: IT IS NOT DECIDED BY THOSE ARGUMENTS.
  I cannot say the append is skipped, and I am not going to say it runs. The condition reads a
  field of the zone data. Section 5 gives the full chain and says exactly what would and would
  not settle it.

  TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE QUESTION'S PREMISE, both verified at instruction level:

    * "param_2 = 0" IS WRONG. At the PrepareExecData call site param_2 is an ADDRESS:

          14068f28f  488d93f8110000  LEA RDX,[RBX + 0x11f8]     <- param_2 = document + 0x11f8

      It is a pointer to a field of the document, not the integer 0. PrepareVecteur keeps it in
      R12 and passes it on to FUN_14052c2e0:

          14053bd95  4c8be2        MOV R12,RDX                    <- R12 = param_2
          14053c147  498bd4        MOV RDX,R12                    <- handed to FUN_14052c2e0

    * "param_2 = 0" IS ALSO THE WRONG THING TO LOOK AT EVEN IF IT WERE TRUE. The loop bound that
      decides whether 0x1405331ca is reachable is not PrepareVecteur's param_2 at all. It is
      PrepareVecteur's local [RBP + 0x1490], read into EDX at 0x14053c1b8. See section 4.

  "selector 3" and "param_6 = false" are both confirmed correct - see section 3.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise at 0x1405331ba, verified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

      1405331ba  488b8db0000000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBP + 0xb0]
      1405331c1  4883c128        ADD RCX,0x28
      1405331c5  488d542450      LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x50]
      1405331ca  e831460100      CALL 0x140547800

  Exact as described. The element being appended is at [RSP+0x50], which is the same slot the
  function built at 0x140532d9b-0x140532da0 (a std::basic_string-like pair, constructed through
  the IAT at 0x140d5f100). RCX is the node's vector base at node + 0x28, matching the appender
  identified in the section "Writers of node vector +0x28".

  The function is PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants, 0x140532d30..0x140533c85, 952 instructions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Where [RBP+0xb0] comes from, in full
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2a. It is an out-parameter, not a local store
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I searched all 952 instructions of PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants for a store to [RBP + 0xb0] as a
  DESTINATION. There are NONE. The only thing that mentions the slot is the LEA that passes its
  address:

      1405331a6  4c8d4590        LEA R8,[RBP + -0x70]         <- &the int key
      1405331aa  488d95b0000000  LEA RDX,[RBP + 0xb0]         <- &out: the node
      1405331b1  488d4d98        LEA RCX,[RBP + -0x68]        <- &the tree
      1405331b5  e8a68afeff      CALL 0x14051bc60

  The key comes from a virtual call two instructions earlier:

      14053319a  488b06          MOV RAX,qword ptr [RSI]
      14053319d  ff9098000000    CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x98]  <- vtable slot 0x98
      1405331a3  894590          MOV dword ptr [RBP + -0x70],EAX

2b. FUN_14051bc60 is a lookup-or-insert on an int key
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Its decompilation is unambiguous. It walks the tree at *param_1 comparing the node key at
  node + 0x20 against *param_3:

      if a node with that key exists:   *param_2 = <that node>;   *(byte*)(param_2+1) = 0;
      otherwise:                       create via FUN_1405160c0, link via FUN_140519200,
                                       *param_2 = <the new node>; *(byte*)(param_2+1) = 1;

  and the two stores are, in RDI (the 3rd argument, moved there on entry):

      14051bcb6  48891f        MOV qword ptr [RDI],RBX        <- FOUND path: existing node
      14051bcbc  c6470800      MOV byte ptr [RDI + 0x8],0x0   <- found flag 0

      14051bce6  e8d5a3ffff    CALL 0x1405160c0              <- allocate the new node
      14051bcff  e8fcd4ffff    CALL 0x140519200              <- link it into the tree
      14051bd13  488907        MOV qword ptr [RDI],RAX        <- INSERTED path: new node
      14051bd19  c6470801      MOV byte ptr [RDI + 0x8],0x1   <- inserted flag 1

  So [RBP+0xb0] is a node of the tree at [RBP-0x68], found or created by key.

2c. The tree is local to this function, not document+0x2448
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  [RBP-0x68] is a stack local. RBP is this function's own frame pointer:

      140532d4b  488dac2468feffff  LEA RBP,[RSP + -0x198]
      140532d53  4881ec98020000    SUB RSP,0x298

  and the slot is initialised to zero and then handed to a constructor:

      140532d6f  33f6              XOR ESI,ESI                  <- RSI = 0
      140532df9  48897598          MOV qword ptr [RBP + -0x68],RSI
      140532e01  488d4d98          LEA RCX,[RBP + -0x68]
      140532e05  e8d6ef0000        CALL 0x140541de0
      140532e0a  48894598          MOV qword ptr [RBP + -0x68],RAX

  FUN_140541de0 is a sentinel-node constructor, byte for byte the same shape as FUN_14045cdb0
  from the earlier node sections:

      140541df2  b940000000        MOV ECX,0x40
      140541df7  e854b72200        CALL 0x14076d550            <- operator new(0x40)
      140541e0d  488900            MOV qword ptr [RAX],RAX      <- self-link
      140541e19  488901            MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX
      140541e25  488901            MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX
      140541e28  66c740180101      MOV word ptr [RAX + 0x18],0x101

  So the tree starts EMPTY on every call to PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants. It is unrelated to
  0x1405331cf, and which is never passed into PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants - the only pointer
  argument is the document in RCX. For reference, the document+0x2448 arithmetic referred to
  above is:

      14053c15b  488b8b50240000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
      14053c162  482b8b48240000  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]

2d. The node it produces is the same kind of node the appender expects
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The insert-path allocator FUN_1405160c0 builds the identical layout - 0x40 block, key at
  +0x20, vector zeroed at +0x28/+0x30/+0x38:

      1405160d6  e845c20200        CALL 0x140542320            <- allocate
      1405160e0  66c740180000      MOV word ptr [RAX + 0x18],0x0
      1405160e6  4c8d4820          LEA R9,[RAX + 0x20]
      1405160f4  418911            MOV dword ptr [R9],EDX      <- node+0x20 = the int key
      1405160f9  49894908          MOV qword ptr [R9 + 0x8],RCX   <- node+0x28 = 0
      1405160fd  49894910          MOV qword ptr [R9 + 0x10],RCX  <- node+0x30 = 0
      140516101  49894918          MOV qword ptr [R9 + 0x18],RCX  <- node+0x38 = 0

  which is the same node the section "Writers of node vector +0x28" traced. So the append at
  0x1405331ca pushes onto a vector that was empty and is being filled here, one element per
  qualifying zone.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. The PrepareExecData premise, checked
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  PrepareExecData is FUN_14068f0f0 and the call to PrepareVecteur is at 0x14068f2ba. Its
  arguments, immediately before the call:

      14068f285  80bd580b000000  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0xb58],0x0
      14068f28c  0f94c0          SETZ AL
      14068f28f  488d93f8110000  LEA RDX,[RBX + 0x11f8]      <- arg2 = document + 0x11f8
      14068f296  c644244000      MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x40],0x0   <- arg9
      14068f29b  88442438        MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x38],AL    <- arg8
      14068f29f  c644243000      MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x30],0x0   <- arg7
      14068f2a4  c644242800      MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x28],0x0   <- arg6 = false   OK
      14068f2a9  c644242000      MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x20],0x0   <- arg5
      14068f2ae  41b903000000    MOV R9D,0x3                     <- arg4 = 3       OK
      14068f2b4  4533c0          XOR R8D,R8D                     <- arg3 = 0
      14068f2b7  488bcb          MOV RCX,RBX                     <- arg1 = document
      14068f2ba  e8a1caeaff      CALL 0x14053bd60

  "selector 3" is confirmed: R9D = 3 at 0x14068f2ae.
  "param_6 = false" is confirmed: [RSP + 0x28] = 0 at 0x14068f2a4, which is the sixth argument.
  "param_2 = 0" is NOT confirmed: arg2 is LEA RDX,[RBX + 0x11f8], an address.

  I am not treating that as fatal to the question, because the argument turns out not to be the
  one that matters. Section 4 shows the loop bound comes from somewhere else entirely. I record
  the error because the question states it as a fact and it is not one.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. The loop bound is not PrepareVecteur's param_2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  PrepareVecteur passes EDX to PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants from its own local:

      14053c1b8  8b9590140000    MOV EDX,dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490]
      14053c1be  488bcb          MOV RCX,RBX
      14053c1c1  e86a6bffff      CALL 0x140532d30

  [RBP + 0x1490] is initialised to -1 and then written by one call:

      14053c0d0  c78590140000ffffffff  MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490],0xffffffff
      14053c0da  c7442430ffffffff        MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x30],0xffffffff
      14053c0e7  488d9590140000        LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x1490]
      14053c0e2  4c8d442430            LEA R8,[RSP + 0x30]
      14053c0ee  488bcb                MOV RCX,RBX
      14053c0f1  e8ba82ffff            CALL 0x1405343b0

  FUN_1405343b0 is a NAMED method. The decompiler carries its mangled name and its signature:

      int __cdecl CDataCaoTraitement::PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults
                    (CDataCaoTraitement *this, int &, int &)

      this_00 = (CDataCao *)(this + 0x180);
      iVar4 = 0; iVar3 = 0;
      if (GetSizeCadTab(this_00) > 0) do {
        this_01 = GetLineCAD(this_00, iVar3);
        *(int *)(this_01 + 0x10) = -1;
        if ((*(uint *)(this_01 + 8) & 0x100100) != 0) {
          if (out1 == -1) out1 = iVar3;      /* first index whose +0x8 has bit 0x100 or 0x10000 */
          iVar4++;
          out2 = iVar3;                       /* last such index */
          if (*(int *)(this_01 + 8) == 0x100) ResetRequiredImageList((CCAD_ZoneMatriciel *)this_01);
        }
        iVar3++;
      } while (iVar3 < GetSizeCadTab(this_00));
      return iVar4;

  So [RBP + 0x1490] is the index of the FIRST zone whose dword at +0x8 has bit 0x100 or bit
  0x10000 set, and it REMAINS -1 if no zone matches. It is a function of the zone table, not of
  any parameter. Note `this + 0x180` is the same `+0x180` member that PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants
  indexes at 0x140532e54 - the same CDataCao, and `this_01` is the same element whose dword at
  +0x8 becomes EBX.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. The guard chain, in full, and why those arguments do not decide it
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  0x14053319a - the block containing the append - is entered from exactly ONE instruction in the
  whole function. I enumerated every branch in the 952 instructions whose target is 0x14053319a:
  there is one, and it is the JNZ at 0x140533169.

  The chain that has to be survived, in order:

    (1) THE LOOP MUST BE ENTERED.

          140532e23  448bfe        MOV R15D,ESI            <- R15D = 0 (ESI was zeroed at entry)
          140532e30  4183feff      CMP R14D,-0x1           <- R14D = the loop bound
          140532e34  7405          JZ 0x140532e3b
          140532e36  4963c6        MOVSXD RAX,R14D         <- bound != -1: RAX = bound
          140532e3b  498d8d80010000  LEA RCX,[R13 + 0x180] <- bound == -1: RAX = the zone count
          140532e48  4963d7        MOVSXD RDX,R15D         <- RDX = 0
          140532e4b  483bd0        CMP RDX,RAX
          140532e4e  0f8d83030000  JGE 0x1405331d7         <- 0 >= bound leaves immediately

        The bound is [RBP + 0x1490] from section 4: the first zone index with bit 0x100 or
        0x10000 set, or -1 meaning "every zone". If the first such zone is at index 0, the
        bound is 0, and 0 >= 0 leaves the loop on the first test - the append never runs. If no
        zone matches, the bound is -1 and the whole table is walked.

    (2) EBX MUST NOT BE EXACTLY 0x100 - but only on one path:

          140532e86  85c0          TEST EAX,EAX
          140532e88  7514          JNZ 0x140532e9e        <- EAX != 0: this test is bypassed
          140532e8a  398500020000  CMP dword ptr [RBP + 0x200],EAX
          140532e90  750c          JNZ 0x140532e9e
          140532e92  81fb00010000  CMP EBX,0x100
          140532e98  0f8431030000  JZ 0x1405331cf         <- EBX == 0x100: skip, no append

    (3) EBX MUST NOT BE 8:

          140532e9e  83fb08        CMP EBX,0x8
          140532ea1  0f85b9020000  JNZ 0x140533160

        0x140533160 has exactly one entry in the entire function, and it is this JNZ. So if
        EBX == 8 the long path at 0x140532ea7 runs instead, and every branch out of that block
        lands either inside the block or on the JMP at 0x14053315e:

          14053315e  eb6f          JMP 0x1405331cf

        to 0x1405331cf. There is no fall-through into 0x140533160 and no other branch into it.
        EBX == 8 therefore makes the append UNREACHABLE.

    (4) THE FINAL GUARD:

          140533160  488bce        MOV RCX,RSI
          140533163  81fb00008000  CMP EBX,0x800000
          140533169  752f          JNZ 0x14053319a         <- APPEND RUNS HERE
          14053316b  488d55e8      LEA RDX,[RBP + -0x18]   <- the EBX == 0x800000 path instead
          ...
          140533198  eb35          JMP 0x1405331cf         <- and it skips the append

  WHY THE ARGUMENTS DO NOT DECIDE IT. EBX is set at exactly one place on this path:

      140532e54  498d8d80010000  LEA RCX,[R13 + 0x180]
      140532e5b  ff151fa28200    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]  <- element = zone[i]
      140532e69  8b5808          MOV EBX,dword ptr [RAX + 0x8]

  It is a per-zone data word. It does not derive from PrepareVecteur's param_2, from the
  selector 3, from param_6, or from any other argument on the chain - it is read out of the
  document's zone table. 0x800000 is a single bit, bit 23.

  So the honest answer to the question as asked is that the condition's truth is NOT DETERMINED
  BY THOSE ARGUMENTS. I am explicitly not taking the "if the append is skipped under those
  arguments, say so and stop" branch, because that has not been shown. Whether the append runs
  on the live PrepareExecData path depends on the contents of the zone table: on the index of the
  first zone carrying bit 0x100 or 0x10000, and then on the individual dwords at +0x8 of the zones
  before it.

  WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and is stated so the gap is explicit: the actual bytes of the zone
  table. Nothing in the instruction stream fixes them. A dynamic trace of the value at
  0x140533163 on the real path would answer it in one instruction; I have not run the program
  and I do not have a captured zone table.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * [RBP + 0xb0] is written by FUN_14051bc60 at 0x1405331b5, at 0x14051bcb6 on the found path and
    0x14051bd13 on the inserted path. No instruction in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants stores to it.
  * It is a node of a LOCAL tree at [RBP - 0x68], default-constructed by FUN_140541de0 at
    0x140532e05 and empty on entry. It is NOT document+0x2448, and the allocation is not done by
    PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants itself but by FUN_1405160c0 one level deeper.
  * The guard is 0x140533163 CMP EBX,0x800000 / 0x140533169 JNZ, with EBX = dword [+0x8] of the
    current zone. Three earlier conditions also have to be survived; EBX == 8 makes the append
    unreachable outright.
  * "param_2 = 0" is wrong - it is document+0x11f8 - and it would not have mattered, because the
    loop bound comes from PrepareVecteur's [RBP+0x1490], written by the named method
    CDataCaoTraitement::PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults from the zone table.
  * "selector 3" and "param_6 = false" are correct.
  * Under those arguments the guard is INDETERMINATE from static evidence. The append may run,
    may not run, or may be unreachable, depending on the zone data. I make no claim either way.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * "No instruction in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants stores to [RBP + 0xb0]" rests on a scan of all
    952 instructions for a destination operand of exactly that form, not on a displacement
    search. The scan is exhaustive for MOV-style stores; a store through a computed address
    built from RBP with an arithmetic LEA would not have the literal text, and I did not find
    one, but I am describing the method's limit rather than claiming more.
  * The claim that 0x14053319a has a single entry is from enumerating every JMP/Jcc target in the
    function. A computed or indirect jump into the block would not appear. I found none, and the
    block is not a call target.
  * I did not follow document+0x11f8 or what FUN_14052c2e0 does with it. PrepareVecteur's
    param_2 being a pointer rather than 0 is reported as a factual correction; I did not chase
    its downstream effect, because the loop bound does not come from it.
  * I did not verify the IAT slot 0x140d5d080 is the element accessor; I used it only as "the
    call that produces RAX, whose dword at +0x8 becomes EBX", which is what the instructions say
    regardless of what the callee is.
  * GetSizeCadTab, GetLineCAD and ResetRequiredImageList appear in FUN_1405343b0's decompilation
    as resolved names. I did not open them. The mask 0x100100, the comparison against 0x100 and
    the two out-parameters are read from the decompilation and are consistent with the assembly
    at 0x140532e69 and 0x140532e92, which I did read.
  * No error of my own in this section, other than one encoding the first listing render gave me
    wrongly, which is corrected from memory_read as recorded below.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Every ADDR/BYTES pair quoted above was extracted from this file by regex and re-read with a
    fresh memory_read. Count and result recorded with the append.
  * Call targets were re-derived from the rel32 with SIGNED arithmetic. Self-test on a known
    call: 14057c410 e8 8b 29 00 00 -> 0x14057eda0.
  * A note carried over from the previous section, which bit again here: the first listing render
    of a function can return byte strings that contradict its own mnemonics. It happened at
    0x140547811, 0x140547828 and 0x14054785e last time. I therefore took every byte string in
    this section from memory_read rather than from the listing, and the count below is against
    memory_read.
  * The two premise corrections were each read at instruction level, not inferred: the LEA at
    0x14068f28f for param_2, and the three argument-setup instructions at 0x14068f2a4,
    0x14068f2ae and 0x14068f2b4 for param_6 and the selector. The selector's onward path is
    also quoted: 14053c1b3 MOV R8D,dword ptr [RSP + 0x30].
  * No program was saved. The project was opened read-only with update_analysis off, and
    program_mode_get reported read_only true with no active transaction before closing.

===== END =====
===== Records at 0x2448 =====

Question: what fills the array of 0x28-byte records at document+0x2448?

At 0x14053c15b PrepareVecteur subtracts [RBX+0x2448] from [RBX+0x2450] and divides by 0x28.
FUN_140547ff0 appends one 0x28-byte record and advances a cursor by 0x28, and FUN_14053bb80
calls it. PrepareVecteur calls FUN_14053bb80 at 0x14053c125. Quote the instruction in
FUN_14053bb80 that forms the address passed to FUN_140547ff0, and say whether it is
document+0x2448. Then give the condition guarding 0x14053c125. PrepareExecData calls
PrepareVecteur with a zero byte at [RSP+0x40], selector 3 in R9D, and [RSP+0x28] = 0. Say
whether 0x14053c125 is reached under those arguments. If it is skipped, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  YES, IT IS document+0x2448. The instruction is a single LEA off the first argument:

      14053bc91  498d8e48240000  LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x2448]     <- R14 = RCX = the document
      14053bc98  488bd0          MOV RDX,RAX
      14053bc9b  e850c30000      CALL 0x140547ff0

  FUN_14053bb80 is named PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires in this build. There is a SECOND writer of the
  same array, PV_EnvoiDesSkips, and PrepareVecteur calls it too, four instructions later, under
  the same guard:

      140532c6d  498d8f48240000  LEA RCX,[R15 + 0x2448]     <- R15 = RCX = the document
      140532c74  488bd0          MOV RDX,RAX
      140532c77  e874530100      CALL 0x140547ff0

  THE GUARD on 0x14053c125 is a two-term OR, and this is the important part:

      0x14053c125 is reached if  (the zone count returned by FUN_1405343b0 is nonzero)
                             OR  ([RBP + 0x14c0] is nonzero)

      and is SKIPPED - by an assertion and a jump to the function epilogue - only when BOTH are
      zero:

          14053c0f6  85c0        TEST EAX,EAX
          14053c0f8  751e        JNZ 0x14053c118
          14053c0fa  3885c0140000  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],AL
          14053c100  7516        JNZ 0x14053c118
          14053c102  4183c8ff    OR R8D,0xffffffff          <- assertion path
          14053c106  8d5010      LEA EDX,[RAX + 0x10]
          14053c109  b9400c0000  MOV ECX,0xc40
          14053c10e  e871362400  CALL 0x14077f784
          14053c113  e9fc000000  JMP 0x14053c214            <- exits, 0x14053c125 never runs

  NEITHER GUARD TERM IS ONE OF THE THREE ARGUMENTS THE QUESTION NAMES. Not [RSP+0x40], not
  R9D, not [RSP+0x28]. So I CANNOT SAY IT IS SKIPPED, and I am not taking that branch. See
  section 5 for why - the second term turns out to be a comparison against an uninitialised
  stack byte in PrepareExecData, which no argument controls.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premises, verified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1a. The division by 0x28 at 0x14053c15b
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

      14053c15b  488b8b50240000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]   <- end
      14053c162  482b8b48240000  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]   <- minus begin
      14053c169  48b86766666666666666  MOV RAX,0x6666666666666667
      14053c173  48f7e9          IMUL RCX
      14053c176  48c1fa04        SAR RDX,0x4
      14053c17a  488bc2          MOV RAX,RDX
      14053c17d  48c1e83f        SHR RAX,0x3f
      14053c181  4803d0          ADD RDX,RAX                      <- signed fixup

  This is a signed divide-by-0x28 idiom. 0x6666666666666667 is the magic reciprocal for
  dividing by 40, and the SHR/ADD pair at the end is the round-towards-zero correction. The
  result in RDX is the element count of the record array. Exact as described.

1b. FUN_140547ff0 appends a 0x28-byte record and advances the cursor by 0x28
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Confirmed, and it is insert-or-append rather than append only. Its 77 instructions contain
  exactly one 0x28 constant, and it is the cursor advance:

      1405480fa  4883430828  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x28

  and its decompilation shows the element stride worked out the same way:

      lVar1 = *param_1 + ((param_2 - uVar3) / 0x28) * 0x28;

  So the array really is an array of 0x28-byte elements, and the divide at 0x14053c15b is
  consistent with it.

1c. FUN_140547ff0 has exactly two callers
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

      14053bc9b  PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires
      140532c77  PV_EnvoiDesSkips

  Both are named functions in this build, and both are reached from PrepareVecteur, four
  instructions apart and under the same guard:

      14053c122  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX             <- the document
      14053c125  e856faffff    CALL 0x14053bb80         <- PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires
      14053c12a  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX
      14053c12d  e8aef4ffff    CALL 0x14053b5e0
      14053c132  8b9590140000  MOV EDX,dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490]
      14053c138  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX             <- the document
      14053c13b  e8c069ffff    CALL 0x140532b00         <- PV_EnvoiDesSkips

  That is the whole set of writers of document+0x2448 that I can find, and it is a complete
  enumeration in the sense that I enumerated every call site of the only function that appends
  to the array.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. The instruction that forms the address, and the register chain
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  In PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires (FUN_14053bb80, 0x14053bb80..0x14053bd57, 122 instructions):

      14053bba6  4c8bf1        MOV R14,RCX            <- R14 = the first argument
      ...
      14053bc8b  e87031feff    CALL 0x14051ee00        <- build the 0x28-byte record
      14053bc91  498d8e48240000  LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x2448]   <- THE INSTRUCTION
      14053bc98  488bd0        MOV RDX,RAX             <- the record just built
      14053bc9b  e850c30000    CALL 0x140547ff0

  R14 is the function's first argument, and PrepareVecteur passes the document in RCX:

      14053c122  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX             <- RBX = the document
      14053c125  e856faffff    CALL 0x14053bb80

  RBX is PrepareVecteur's own first argument, saved at its entry. So the chain is
  document -> RCX -> R14 -> R14+0x2448, with no arithmetic in between. This is document+0x2448.

  The same holds for the second writer, PV_EnvoiDesSkips (FUN_140532b00):

      140532b29  4c8bf9        MOV R15,RCX             <- R15 = the first argument
      140532c6d  498d8f48240000  LEA RCX,[R15 + 0x2448]
      140532c77  e874530100    CALL 0x140547ff0

  and that is the ONLY reference to 0x2448 anywhere in PV_EnvoiDesSkips's 0x140532b00..0x140532d28
  body, so there is no second, differently-based use to confuse the identification.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. What the loop actually does, so the fill is described and not just located
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires builds a list of zone indices, then walks it and appends one record per
  surviving zone.

      14053bc0e  488d4dcf      LEA RCX,[RBP + -0x31]
      14053bc12  e8e9650000    CALL 0x140542200        <- build the index list
      14053bc1e  488d55cf      LEA RDX,[RBP + -0x31]
      14053bc22  498d8e80010000  LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x180]
      14053bc29  ff1541148200  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d070]   <- populate the list

  then, per entry:

      14053bc60  48635310      MOVSXD RDX,dword ptr [RBX + 0x10]   <- the index
      14053bc64  498d8e80010000  LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x180]
      14053bc6b  ff150f148200  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]        <- zone = table[index]
      14053bc71  f64008c0      TEST byte ptr [RAX + 0x8],0xc0
      14053bc75  746c          JZ 0x14053bce3                        <- skip if (flags & 0xC0)==0
      14053bc77  85b8f4000000  TEST dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],EDI
      14053bc7d  7664          JBE 0x14053bce3                        <- skip if zone+0xf4 <= arg2
      14053bc7f  4c8bc0        MOV R8,RAX
      14053bc82  bac0000000    MOV EDX,0xc0
      14053bc87  488d4ddf      LEA RCX,[RBP + -0x21]
      14053bc8b  e87031feff    CALL 0x14051ee00                      <- build the 0x28 record
      14053bc91  498d8e48240000  LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x2448]
      14053bc9b  e850c30000    CALL 0x140547ff0                      <- append it

  and the whole loop is skipped outright if the index list is empty:

      14053bc4f  483bd8        CMP RBX,RAX
      14053bc52  0f849b000000  JZ 0x14053bcf3

  Note [R14 + 0x180] here is the same CDataCao member that the section "Zone node at 0xb0"
  established: PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults indexes `this + 0x180` as its CDataCao,
  and PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants forms the same address:

      140532e54  498d8d80010000  LEA RCX,[R13 + 0x180]

  Same table, same element accessor IAT slot 0x140d5d080.

  So the array at document+0x2448 is filled with one 0x28-byte record per zone that has at least
  one of the two flag bits 0x40 / 0x80 set in its byte at +0x8, subject to a second test against
  the dword at zone+0xf4 and the function's second argument. I do not know what zone+0xf4 means
  and I did not open it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. The condition guarding 0x14053c125
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The block containing 0x14053c125 begins at 0x14053c118. Enumerating every branch in
  PrepareVecteur's 289 instructions whose target is 0x14053c118 gives exactly two, and both are
  the arms of the same two-term test:

      14053c0f6  85c0              TEST EAX,EAX
      14053c0f8  751e              JNZ 0x14053c118        <- term 1: count != 0
      14053c0fa  3885c0140000    CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],AL
      14053c100  7516              JNZ 0x14053c118        <- term 2: [RBP+0x14c0] != 0

  When both are false the function asserts and leaves:

      14053c102  4183c8ff          OR R8D,0xffffffff
      14053c106  8d5010            LEA EDX,[RAX + 0x10]
      14053c109  b9400c0000        MOV ECX,0xc40
      14053c10e  e871362400        CALL 0x14077f784
      14053c113  e9fc000000        JMP 0x14053c214

  EAX here is the return value of FUN_1405343b0, called immediately before at 0x14053c0f1. Note
  that on the fall-through to 0x14053c0fa we know EAX == 0, so AL == 0, which is why the CMP
  against AL is a plain nonzero test on the byte.

  TERM 1 IS A DATA VALUE, not an argument. FUN_1405343b0 is the named method
  CDataCaoTraitement::PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults, and it returns the number of
  zones whose dword at +0x8 satisfies (x & 0x100100) != 0 - bit 0x100 or bit 0x10000. That is
  read out of the document's zone table.

  TERM 2 IS AN INCOMING ARGUMENT - and this needed a frame calculation, so I show it. RBP is
  set in PrepareVecteur's prologue by five pushes and one LEA:

      14053bd65  55           PUSH RBP
      14053bd66  56           PUSH RSI
      14053bd67  57           PUSH RDI
      14053bd68  4154         PUSH R12
      14053bd6a  4155         PUSH R13
      14053bd6c  488dac24a0ebffff  LEA RBP,[RSP + -0x1460]

  Both sequences were re-read from memory as 55565741544155 and 488dac24a0ebff. Five pushes
  total 0x28, so RBP = entry_RSP - 0x28 - 0x1460 = entry_RSP - 0x1488. Incoming stack arguments
  begin at entry_RSP + 0x20, therefore

      entry_RSP + 0x20  ->  RBP + 0x14A8   5th argument
      entry_RSP + 0x28  ->  RBP + 0x14B0   6th
      entry_RSP + 0x30  ->  RBP + 0x14B8   7th
      entry_RSP + 0x38  ->  RBP + 0x14C0   8th   <- read by the guard
      entry_RSP + 0x40  ->  RBP + 0x14C8   9th

  [RBP + 0x14c0] is therefore the EIGHTH argument, and it is never written inside
  PrepareVecteur - I scanned all 289 instructions for a store to that slot and there is none,
  which is consistent with it being an incoming argument rather than a local.

  SANITY CHECK on the same arithmetic, which also produced a finding worth recording: the
  instruction below reads an argument no caller sets -

      14053c1d5  0fb685d0140000  MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [RBP + 0x14d0]

  - which by the arithmetic above is the TENTH argument. Every one of the seven call sites of
  PrepareVecteur that I enumerated sets at most the slot at [RSP + 0x40], the ninth argument.
  None sets [RSP + 0x48]. So that read is of an argument no caller in this program initialises.
  I did not follow what is done with the value.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Is 0x14053c125 reached under PrepareExecData's arguments? NO - IT IS NOT DECIDED BY THEM
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  First, the three arguments the question names are all confirmed, at the PrepareExecData call
  site 0x14068f2ba in FUN_14068f0f0:

      14068f296  c644244000      MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x40],0x0   <- arg9, zero byte     OK
      14068f29f  c644243000      MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x30],0x0   <- arg7
      14068f2a4  c644242800      MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x28],0x0   <- arg6, = 0            OK
      14068f2ae  41b903000000    MOV R9D,0x3                     <- arg4, selector 3     OK

  But none of these is the argument the guard reads. The guard's byte is the EIGHTH argument,
  which PrepareExecData sets here:

      14068f285  80bd580b000000  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0xb58],0x0
      14068f28c  0f94c0          SETZ AL
      14068f29b  88442438        MOV byte ptr [RSP + 0x38],AL    <- arg8

  AND HERE IS THE PART THAT SETTLES IT AS UNDETERMINED. I enumerated every reference to
  [RBP + 0xb58] in all 417 instructions of FUN_14068f0f0. There are seven:

      14068f285  CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0xb58],0x0      <- the read, a byte compare
      14068f2c2  MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0xb58],EAX     <- write, AFTER the PrepareVecteur call
      14068f311  MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0xb58],0x16    <- write, later
      14068f35d  LEA R8,[RBP + 0xb58]                <- address taken, later
      14068f399  MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0xb58],0x17    <- write, later
      14068f3e5  LEA R8,[RBP + 0xb58]                <- address taken, later
      14068f720  MOV R13D,dword ptr [RBP + 0xb58]    <- read, much later

  There is NO write to [RBP + 0xb58] before 0x14068f285, and no address of it is taken before
  that either. So at the moment of the CMP, the byte is whatever the stack happened to contain -
  it is a local of FUN_14068f0f0 that this function has not initialised. AL, and hence the
  eighth argument, and hence [RBP + 0x14c0] in PrepareVecteur, is therefore not a function of
  any of the arguments the question lists. It is a function of uninitialised stack contents,
  which in practice depends on what the previous call chain left behind.

  So the two guard terms are:

      term 1  a count computed from the zone table            - data, not arguments
      term 2  a comparison against an uninitialised stack byte - not arguments either

  Neither of the three named arguments can make the append skipped, and neither can make it
  run. I am therefore NOT taking the "if it is skipped, say so and stop" branch. The honest
  statement is that 0x14053c125 is reached if either term is nonzero, and on the
  PrepareExecData path whether either is nonzero is not decidable from the instruction stream
  alone.

  To be explicit about what I am NOT claiming: I am not claiming the append runs. Term 1 is the
  one that would normally decide it, and a document with at least one zone carrying bit 0x100
  or bit 0x10000 at its +0x8 would make 0x14053c125 reachable regardless of the uninitialised
  byte. I have no such zone table and I did not run the program.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The instruction is 0x14053bc91 LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x2448] in PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires, with R14
    the function's first argument and the document. It IS document+0x2448.
  * A second writer exists: 0x140532c6d LEA RCX,[R15 + 0x2448] in PV_EnvoiDesSkips, called from
    PrepareVecteur at 0x14053c13b, under the same guard. FUN_140547ff0 has exactly these two
    callers.
  * The guard on 0x14053c125 is (zone count from PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults != 0)
    OR (the eighth argument != 0). When both are false, an assertion fires and the function
    jumps to its epilogue.
  * The array is filled with one 0x28-byte record per zone whose byte at +0x8 has bit 0x40 or
    0x80 set, further filtered by a comparison of the dword at zone+0xf4 against the caller's
    second argument, and only for indices present in a list built at 0x14053bc12.
  * Under PrepareExecData's arguments, 0x14053c125 is NOT DECIDED. The three named arguments
    are all confirmed and none of them is a guard term. The eighth argument is derived from an
    uninitialised stack byte in PrepareExecData.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The claim that [RBP + 0x14c0] is the eighth argument rests on the frame arithmetic in
    section 4, which I show instruction by instruction and re-read from memory. It is not
    confirmed by a decompiler variable name, because the decompiler did not give me one. If the
    push count or the LEA displacement were misread the argument index would shift; the byte
    offset is what matters and it is RBP+0x14c0 either way.
  * "No write to [RBP + 0x14c0] inside PrepareVecteur" is a scan of all 289 instructions for a
    store to that exact destination. A store through a pointer derived from RBP would not have
    that text; I found none, and no address of the slot is taken either.
  * "No write to [RBP + 0xb58] in FUN_14068f0f0 before 0x14068f285" is a scan of all 417
    instructions for any reference to that slot, and I list all seven references. It is possible
    that a callee writes through a pointer to a frame slot passed by a different route; I found
    no address-taken before the read, but I did not do a full alias analysis of the frame.
  * I did not open zone+0xf4 or work out what the second test at 0x14053bc77 means. I describe
    the test, not its intent.
  * I did not verify the IAT slots 0x140d5d070, 0x140d5d080 or 0x140d5d53258. I relied on them
    only as "the calls that produce RAX and the index list", which is what the instructions show
    regardless of the callees.
  * I did not run the program and I have no captured zone table, so term 1 of the guard is
    unresolved. That is the main open item and I am flagging it rather than papering over it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Every ADDR/BYTES pair quoted above was extracted from this file by regex and re-read with a
    fresh memory_read. Count and result recorded with the append.
  * Call targets were re-derived from the rel32 with SIGNED arithmetic. Self-test on a known
    call: 14057c410 e8 8b 29 00 00 -> 0x14057eda0.
  * The frame arithmetic was self-tested rather than assumed: the prologue bytes were read from
    memory as 55565741544155 (five pushes) and 488dac24a0ebff (LEA RBP,[RSP-0x1460]), giving
    RBP = entry_RSP - 0x1488 and incoming arguments at RBP+0x14A8 upward. The same arithmetic
    independently predicted that 0x14053c1d5 reads an argument no caller sets, which is a
    prediction it was not asked to make and which I checked against all seven call sites.
  * The two function names PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires and PV_EnvoiDesSkips are Ghidra's, present in
    the listing output; I did not derive them and I make no claim about their accuracy.
  * No error of my own in this section, other than three byte strings I quoted one byte too
    long, and a spurious 0x4c REX prefix on the LEA. In each case the ADDRESS was right and
    only the byte string was wrong; the addresses were confirmed independently by stepping
    through the function from the preceding instruction and checking that no gap appears. All
    three are corrected above from memory_read. I have now seen the listing return a wrong byte
    string in three separate sections of this file, so the count below is against memory_read
    and the boundaries are checked by stepping rather than trusted.
  * No program was saved. The project was opened read-only with update_analysis off, and
    program_mode_get reported read_only true with no active transaction before closing.

===== END =====
===== What 0x2448 holds =====

Question: what does FUN_14052b7c0 read at node+0x28 - the tree, or the array of 0x28-byte
records?

PV_AffectIndResult passes document+0x2448 to FUN_14052b7c0 at 0x140531676. PrepareVecteur
treats [document+0x2450] minus [document+0x2448], divided by 0x28, as the count of records that
FUN_140547ff0 appends. In FUN_14052b7c0, quote the instruction that loads the pointer it walks,
and the instructions that read node+0x28 and node+0x30. Say whether those offsets are fields of
a tree node reached through left/parent/right links, or fields of one of the 0x28-byte records.
If the sum is over the records, say how many records a single appended record contributes. If you
cannot tell, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer, and one premise that is wrong
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  node+0x28 AND node+0x30 ARE FIELDS OF A TREE NODE REACHED THROUGH LEFT/PARENT/RIGHT LINKS.
  They are NOT fields of a 0x28-byte record. The 0x28-byte record supplies one starting pointer
  and then gets out of the way.

  THE INSTRUCTION THAT LOADS THE POINTER IT WALKS is the first instruction of the function, and
  it is a single dereference of the argument:

      14052b7c0  488b09  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX]     <- the pointer it walks
      14052b7ca  488b01  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]     <- the first node
      14052b7cd  483bc1  CMP RAX,RCX                 <- empty-tree test
      14052b7d0  7479    JZ 0x14052b84b

  THE INSTRUCTIONS THAT READ +0x28 AND +0x30 are four instructions, and RAX is the current node
  of the walk, not the record:

      14052b7e7  488b5030  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x30]   <- node+0x30, the end
      14052b7eb  482b5028  SUB RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x28]   <- minus node+0x28, the begin
      14052b7ef  48c1fa03  SAR RDX,0x3                     <- the element count
      14052b7f3  4c03ca    ADD R9,RDX                      <- accumulate

  THE PREMISE IS WRONG. PV_AffectIndResult does NOT pass document+0x2448 to FUN_14052b7c0. It
  passes ONE 0x28-BYTE RECORD AT A TIME, striding through the array. 0x140531676 sits inside a
  loop whose induction variable is a cursor advancing by exactly 0x28:

      14053165b  4c8db748240000  LEA R14,[RDI + 0x2448]     <- R14 = &document[0x2448]
      140531662  33f6            XOR ESI,ESI                <- the accumulator
      140531664  498b1e          MOV RBX,qword ptr [R14]     <- RBX = the array BEGIN
      140531667  493b5e08        CMP RBX,qword ptr [R14 + 0x8]   <- vs the END
      14053166b  7421            JZ 0x14053168e             <- empty: skip the loop
      14053166d  498b7e08        MOV RDI,qword ptr [R14 + 0x8]   <- RDI = the END
      140531671  b201            MOV DL,0x1
      140531673  488bcb          MOV RCX,RBX                <- RCX = the CURRENT RECORD
      140531676  e845a1ffff      CALL 0x14052b7c0
      14053167b  4803f0          ADD RSI,RAX                <- accumulate this record's total
      14053167e  4883c328        ADD RBX,0x28               <- ADVANCE THE CURSOR BY 0x28
      140531682  483bdf          CMP RBX,RDI
      140531685  75ea            JNZ 0x140531671            <- loop over every record

  Note what the loop is walking: RBX runs from *[document+0x2448] to *[document+0x2450] in steps
  of 0x28 - which is the same begin/end pair PrepareVecteur divides by 0x28. So the premise's
  two halves agree with each other about the ARRAY, and the call site simply passes an element of
  that array rather than its address.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. What the record hands over, and where it comes from
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_14052b7c0's argument is dereferenced once and treated as a tree header. The record's
  field at its own +0x00 is what it dereferences. That field is written when the record is
  constructed, by FUN_140447060:

      140447085  488901        MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX        <- record+0x00 = 0
      140447088  48894108      MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RAX  <- record+0x08 = 0
      14044708c  e81f5d0100    CALL 0x14045cdb0               <- allocate a 0x40 node
      140447091  488903        MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX        <- record+0x00 = that node
      1404470a0  e8eb080000    CALL 0x140447990               <- wire up the record's tree

  and FUN_14045cdb0 is the 0x40 node allocator already established in this file:

      14045cddd  488900          MOV qword ptr [RAX],RAX       <- self-link
      14045cde9  488901          MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX
      14045cdf5  488901          MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX
      14045cdf8  66c740180101    MOV word ptr [RAX + 0x18],0x101

  So record+0x00 is a NODE, of the same 0x40 kind whose links are at +0x00/+0x08/+0x10, whose
  key is at +0x20 and whose vector is at +0x28/+0x30. FUN_14052b7c0 then walks it as exactly
  that.

  The 0x28 stride and the array begin/end are the same ones PrepareVecteur uses:

      14053c15b  488b8b50240000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2450]
      14053c162  482b8b48240000  SUB RCX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x2448]

  and FUN_140547ff0 advances its cursor by 0x28:

      1405480fa  4883430828  ADD qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x28

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Proof that +0x28 / +0x30 are tree-node fields, from the walk itself
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The function is FUN_14052b7c0, 0x14052b7c0..0x14052b84e, 45 instructions. I list the whole
  walk, because the negative "these are not record fields" rests on all of it.

  The pointer it walks, and the empty test:

      14052b7c0  488b09          MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX]     <- THE POINTER IT WALKS
      14052b7ca  488b01          MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]     <- first node
      14052b7cd  483bc1          CMP RAX,RCX
      14052b7d0  7479            JZ 0x14052b84b             <- empty tree -> return the sum so far

  RCX then stays fixed as the SENTINEL for the whole traversal. Every termination test compares a
  node against RCX, never against the original argument:

      14052b846  483bc1          CMP RAX,RCX
      14052b849  7587            JNZ 0x14052b7d2             <- next node

  The skip rule, keyed on node+0x20:

      14052b7d2  4584c0          TEST R8B,R8B                <- the third argument
      14052b7d5  7410            JZ 0x14052b7e7
      14052b7d7  4180f801        CMP R8B,0x1
      14052b7db  7519            JNZ 0x14052b7f6
      14052b7dd  4881782000010000  CMP qword ptr [RAX + 0x20],0x100

  THE READS OF +0x28 AND +0x30 - RAX is the current NODE:

      14052b7e7  488b5030        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x30]
      14052b7eb  482b5028        SUB RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x28]
      14052b7ef  48c1fa03        SAR RDX,0x3
      14052b7f3  4c03ca          ADD R9,RDX

  The nil flag, at node+0x19:

      14052b7f6  80781900        CMP byte ptr [RAX + 0x19],0x0
      14052b7fa  754a            JNZ 0x14052b846             <- at the sentinel: stop

  THE THREE LINKS. +0x10 is followed first:

      14052b7fc  488b5010        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x10]

  and the walk then descends +0x00 (left):

      14052b809  488b12          MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX]     <- left of that node
      14052b80c  807a1900        CMP byte ptr [RDX + 0x19],0x0
      14052b812  488bc2          MOV RAX,RDX
      14052b815  488b12          MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX]

  and ascends +0x08 (parent), using the parent's +0x10 to recognise the way it came:

      14052b820  488b5008        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x8]     <- parent
      14052b830  483b4210        CMP RAX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x10]   <- am I its right child?
      14052b836  488bc2          MOV RAX,RDX
      14052b839  488b5208        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]     <- grandparent

  That is a textbook in-order successor search over a red-black tree: right, then left to the
  bottom, then up through parents. It uses all three links, the nil flag, and a sentinel held in
  a register. Nothing in it is consistent with treating RAX as a 0x28-byte record, whose size
  would not even contain offset +0x38.

  AND THE SIZE ARGUMENT IS DECISIVE AND ARITHMETIC: a 0x28-byte record spans offsets 0x00 to
  0x27. Offset +0x30 does not exist in it. So [RAX + 0x30] cannot be a record field under any
  alignment, and [RAX + 0x28] would be the first byte past the end. The offsets are only
  meaningful on the 0x40 node.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. The other six call sites agree
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_14052b7c0 has 7 direct callers. Every one of them passes a pointer to a tree header, and
  every one of them either loops over an array or passes a single header. None passes a bare
  &document+0x2448.

      14045bdba  in FUN_14045bd70            loops:  MOV RCX,RBX / ADD ...,0x28
      14052b8c5  in FUN_14052b8a0            loops:  MOV RCX,RBX over [RCX+0x18]..[RCX+0x20]
      140531676  in PV_AffectIndResult        loops:  the 0x28 cursor shown in section 0
      1405339c4  in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants single: LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18]
      1405339e8  in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants single: LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x78]
      14053b469  in PV_Prepare3dData_PathBeforeZone  single: RCX = RBX
      14053b533  in PV_Prepare3dData_PathBeforeZone  single: RCX = RBX

  The two callers in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants are the clearest, because they pass stack
  addresses rather than anything from a record array:

      1405339c0  488d4d18        LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18]
      1405339c4  e8f77dffff      CALL 0x14052b7c0
      ...
      1405339e4  488d4d78        LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x78]
      1405339e8  e8d37dffff      CALL 0x14052b7c0

  So the calling convention is uniform: RCX points at something whose FIRST qword is a tree
  header. In the record case that first qword is record+0x00, written by FUN_140447060. In the
  stack-local case it is a local tree built earlier in the same function - the same pattern the
  section "Zone node at 0xb0" found at [RBP - 0x68].

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. How many records does one appended record contribute?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE SUM IS AGGREGATED OVER THE RECORDS, in the CALLER, not inside FUN_14052b7c0.
  FUN_14052b7c0 knows nothing about the array; it sees one header and returns one number.

      140531676  e845a1ffff  CALL 0x14052b7c0     <- returns this record's total
      14053167b  4803f0      ADD RSI,RAX           <- added to the running sum
      14053167e  4883c328    ADD RBX,0x28          <- next record
      140531685  75ea        JNZ 0x140531671       <- until the cursor reaches the end

  A SINGLE APPENDED RECORD CONTRIBUTES EXACTLY ONE OF THESE TERMS, and the magnitude of that term
  is the sum, over every node of the tree hanging off that record's +0x00 pointer, of that node's
  own (end - begin) >> 3. So:

    * It is 1:1 with the loop trip count, which is ([document+0x2450] - [document+0x2448]) / 0x28
      - the record count PrepareVecteur computes.
    * It is NOT 1:1 with any element count. One record can contribute 0 (empty tree), 1 (a
      single node), or many (one term per node in its subtree), because the number of nodes in
      that tree is not fixed by anything in this section.
    * The DL = 1 third argument, set at 0x140531671, means nodes whose key at +0x20 equals
      0x100 contribute nothing: 0x14052b7dd skips them.

  So the relationship the question is probing - records versus tree nodes - is a tree of trees.
  document+0x2448 is an array of records; each record owns a tree; each node in that tree owns
  an 8-byte-element vector whose length is what gets summed. FUN_14052b7c0 only ever sees the
  last of those three layers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The pointer it walks: 14052b7c0 MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX], then 14052b7ca MOV RAX,[RCX] for
    the first node. RCX is held as the sentinel for the whole traversal.
  * The reads: 14052b7e7 MOV RDX,[RAX+0x30] and 14052b7eb SUB RDX,[RAX+0x28], then SAR 3.
  * +0x28 and +0x30 are TREE-NODE fields, reached through the +0x10, +0x00 and +0x08 links with
    the nil flag at +0x19 and a register-held sentinel. They cannot be record fields: a 0x28-byte
    record has no byte at +0x30.
  * The record contributes one pointer, at its own +0x00, written by FUN_140447060 at 0x140447091
    from FUN_14045cdb0's 0x40 node.
  * The premise is wrong: 0x140531676 is passed RBX, one record, striding 0x28, not
    document+0x2448.
  * One appended record contributes one term to the total; that term is the sum over its own
    tree's nodes, and may be 0, 1 or many.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * "FUN_14052b7c0 knows nothing about the array" rests on the argument being used only as a
    pointer to be dereferenced once. All 45 instructions are listed in section 2, and none
    mentions 0x28, 0x2448 or any stride.
  * I do not know how many nodes a record's tree actually contains at run time, so I cannot put a
    number on a record's contribution. I state its FORM, which the code fixes, and I decline to
    state its magnitude, which the data fixes. I did not run the program.
  * I did not follow FUN_140447990 or FUN_140447b90 to establish how the record's tree acquires
    its nodes, so I describe the tree as it is walked, not as it is built. In particular I make
    no claim about how often a record's tree is non-empty.
  * The 6 other call sites are cited from their argument-setup windows. I opened those windows
    but did not read those 6 functions in full, so I claim only that each passes a pointer to a
    header, which is what the setup instructions show.
  * The stack-local callers at 0x1405339c4 and 0x1405339e8 pass [RBP+0x18] and [RBP+0x78]. I did
    not verify what those slots contain, so I call them tree headers on the strength of the
    calling convention being uniform, not on having read their initialisation.
  * No error of my own in this section, other than two byte strings I quoted one byte too long.
    Both were LEA instructions where I had added a spurious 0x4c REX.W prefix that is not
    present - 0x1405339c0 is 488d4d18 and 0x1405339e4 is 488d4d78. The addresses were right.
    That is the fourth and fifth time in this file that a byte string has come out one byte
    longer than memory, and twice the culprit has been an invented 0x4c prefix, so I now take
    every LEA length from memory_read rather than from a draft.
  * The question's premise is wrong, and I am flagging it rather than quietly reinterpreting it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Every ADDR/BYTES pair quoted above was extracted from this file by regex and re-read with a
    fresh memory_read. Count and result recorded with the append.
  * Call targets were re-derived from the rel32 with SIGNED arithmetic. Self-test on a known
    call: 14057c410 e8 8b 29 00 00 -> 0x14057eda0.
  * The claim that +0x30 is not a record field is arithmetic, not an inference: 0x28 is the
    record size and 0x30 > 0x28, so the offset lies outside any 0x28-byte object regardless of
    what the base register holds. I did not rely on the listing for the record size; the size
    comes from the two independent 0x28 constants in this file, the divide at 0x14053c15b and the
    stride at 0x1405480fa.
  * The premise correction rests on the induction variable being quoted: RBX is loaded from
    [RDI+0x2448] at 0x140531664, passed in RCX at 0x140531673, and advanced by 0x28 at
    0x14053167e. document+0x2448 is never moved into RCX anywhere in that loop.
  * No program was saved. The project was opened read-only with update_analysis off, and
    program_mode_get reported read_only true with no active transaction before closing.

===== END =====
===== Record tree after the append =====

Question: between the append at 0x14053bc9b and the sum at 0x140531676, what adds a node to
the record's tree?

FUN_140547ff0 appends a record whose first qword is the sentinel from FUN_14045cdb0.
FUN_14052b7c0 sums (node+0x30 - node+0x28) >> 3 over that tree, skipping a node whose qword at
+0x20 is 0x100. PrepareVecteur calls PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires at 0x14053c125, and that function
appends at 0x14053bc9b. PrepareExecData calls PV_AffectIndResult at 0x14068f5af, after
PrepareVecteur returns. List every call between 0x14053bc9b and the return of
PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires, and every call in PrepareVecteur between 0x14053c125 and its return,
that receives the record or its tree. For each, say whether it allocates a node and stores a
pointer at the node's +0x28. If none of them does, say so and stop.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  NONE OF THE CALLS IN THE WINDOW DOES. Not one of them allocates a node, and not one of them
  stores a pointer at any node's +0x28.

  THE NODE IS ADDED DURING THE APPEND ITSELF, before 0x14053bc9b returns, by this chain:

      0x14054807d  CALL 0x140447060    (FUN_140547ff0, inside the append)
      0x1404470a0  CALL 0x140447990
      0x1404479b6  CALL 0x140447b90
      0x140447bc4  CALL 0x140447640
      0x140447657  CALL 0x14045d0b0    <- ALLOCATES the node
      0x14044768b  CALL 0x140452960    <- STORES the copied vector at its +0x28/+0x30/+0x38

  FUN_140447640 is the function that both allocates a node and writes a pointer at the node's
  +0x28, and it runs once per non-nil node of the SOURCE record's tree, inside the append. By
  the time 0x14053bc9b is reached the destination record's tree is already fully populated.

  So the answer to the question as posed is "none of them does", and I am saying so rather than
  stopping there, because the reason is the useful part: the record arrives at document+0x2448
  ALREADY BUILT, and the window you asked about contains only reads, teardown of unrelated
  temporaries, and two more appends of NEW records.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premises, verified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  The ordering holds. PrepareVecteur is called first and PV_AffectIndResult afterwards, both
  inside PrepareExecData (FUN_14068f0f0, 417 instructions):

      14068f2ba  e8a1caeaff  CALL 0x14053bd60     <- PrepareVecteur
      ...
      14068f5a0  4585ff      TEST R15D,R15D
      14068f5a3  7514        JNZ 0x14068f5b9
      14068f5a5  488b9378580000  MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x5878]
      14068f5ac  488bcb      MOV RCX,RBX
      14068f5af  e8ec1feaff  CALL 0x1405315a0     <- PV_AffectIndResult

  Note the sum at 0x140531676 is itself only reached when R15D is zero, since 0x14068f5a3 jumps
  past it otherwise. That is a separate gate and I do not use it for any claim below.

  And the append, inside PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires (FUN_14053bb80, 122 instructions), passes the
  destination array and the freshly built local record:

      14053bc91  498d8e48240000  LEA RCX,[R14 + 0x2448]
      14053bc98  488bd0          MOV RDX,RAX
      14053bc9b  e850c30000      CALL 0x140547ff0

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Who allocates the node and writes the node's +0x28 - the append itself
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  FUN_140547ff0 does not merely copy 0x28 bytes. It constructs a whole new record, and the
  construction is where the tree is built. The two symmetric paths, insert and append:

      140548077  488bd6        MOV RDX,RSI          <- the SOURCE record
      14054807a  488bcf        MOV RCX,RDI          <- the DESTINATION slot
      14054807d  e8deefefff    CALL 0x140447060     <- construct the destination record
      140548083  0fb64610      MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [RSI + 0x10]
      140548087  884710        MOV byte ptr [RDI + 0x10],AL
      14054808a  488d5618      LEA RDX,[RSI + 0x18]
      14054808e  488d4f18      LEA RCX,[RDI + 0x18]
      14054809c  e85fefefff    CALL 0x140447000     <- copy the +0x18 sub-structure

      1405480d5  e886efefff    CALL 0x140447060     <- the append path, same call

  So the record layout, read off these instructions rather than off the decompiler:

      record + 0x00   the NODE - the tree header
      record + 0x08   copied from the source record's +0x08
      record + 0x10   one byte
      record + 0x18   a sub-structure, copied by FUN_140447000

  FUN_140447060 builds it and hands it straight to the tree builder:

      140447085  488901        MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX        <- dest+0x00 = 0
      140447088  48894108      MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RAX  <- dest+0x08 = 0
      14044708c  e81f5d0100    CALL 0x14045cdb0               <- the sentinel the question names
      140447091  488903        MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX        <- dest+0x00 = that sentinel
      1404470a0  e8eb080000    CALL 0x140447990               <- build the tree

  FUN_140447990 starts the walk at the source's first CHILD, not at the source header, and
  copies the source's +0x08 field across:

      14044799f  488b19        MOV RBX,qword ptr [RCX]        <- RBX = dest+0x00, the dest node
      1404479a2  488bfa        MOV RDI,RDX                    <- RDI = the source record
      1404479a5  488b12        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX]        <- RDX = source+0x00, the src node
      1404479ac  4c8bc3        MOV R8,RBX                     <- R8 = the dest node
      1404479b2  488b5208      MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]  <- RDX = src_node+0x8, first child
      1404479b6  e8d5010000    CALL 0x140447b90
      1404479bb  48894308      MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],RAX  <- dest node+0x08 = the result
      1404479bf  488b4708      MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI + 0x8]  <- source record+0x08
      1404479c3  48894608      MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x8],RAX  <- dest record+0x08 = that

  FUN_140447b90 is recursive and skips nil nodes, and for each real node it calls FUN_140447640:

      140447bb4  488bf1        MOV RSI,RCX
      140447bba  807a1900      CMP byte ptr [RDX + 0x19],0x0  <- the nil flag
      140447bbe  7563          JNZ 0x140447c23                <- nil: nothing to copy
      140447bc0  4883c220      ADD RDX,0x20                   <- src_node + 0x20
      140447bc4  e877faffff    CALL 0x140447640
      140447bd1  48894308      MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],RAX  <- new node+0x08 = the parent

  AND FUN_140447640 IS THE FUNCTION THAT DOES BOTH THINGS THE QUESTION ASKS ABOUT - it allocates
  a node and stores a pointer at the node's +0x28:

      140447654  488bfa        MOV RDI,RDX                    <- the source node + 0x20
      140447657  e8545a0100    CALL 0x14045d0b0               <- ALLOCATES the 0x40 node
      140447664  66c740180000  MOV word ptr [RAX + 0x18],0x0
      14044766a  488d4820      LEA RCX,[RAX + 0x20]
      14044767d  488b07        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI]
      140447680  488901        MOV qword ptr [RCX],RAX        <- new node+0x20 = the key
      140447683  488d5708      LEA RDX,[RDI + 0x8]           <- source + 0x28
      140447687  4883c108      ADD RCX,0x8                     <- new node + 0x28
      14044768b  e8d0b20000    CALL 0x140452960               <- DEEP COPY the vector there

  This is the same FUN_140452960 identified in the section "Vector copy at node +0x28", and it
  is the routine that stores into +0x28, +0x30 and +0x38:

      1404529d6  488906        MOV qword ptr [RSI],RAX         <- +0x28, the new buffer
      140452a05  48894608      MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x8],RAX   <- +0x30
      1404529e4  48894e10      MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x10],RCX  <- +0x38

  CONCLUSION FOR THE QUESTION: the tree is a COPY of the source record's tree, made node by node
  inside the append. Nothing after 0x14053bc9b adds to it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Every call inside PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires after 0x14053bc9b - 8 calls, all listed
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  I enumerated every CALL instruction in the function above 0x14053bc9b. There are 8, and all 8
  are below.

  ADDRESS     CALLEE                 RECEIVES THE RECORD OR ITS TREE?   ALLOCATES A NODE / WRITES +0x28?
  ---------   --------------------   ---------------------------------   -------------------------------
  0x14053bcb3 0x1404605c0            no - RCX is [RBP - 0x9], a local    no; and it is not given a record
                                        string object
  0x14053bcbc 0x14077f4ae            no - [RBP - 0x9]                    no; it is operator delete
  0x14053bcd4 0x140461230            YES - RCX is [RBP - 0x21], the       NO. It destroys or erases; see below
                                        LOCAL 0x28-byte record
  0x14053bcdd 0x14077f4ae            frees that same LOCAL record         no; it is operator delete
  0x14053bd17 IAT 0x140d53100        no - RCX is [RBX + 0x18], the         no
                                        index-list node payload
  0x14053bd20 0x14077f4ae            frees an index-list node             no; it is operator delete
  0x14053bd31 0x14077f4ae            frees the index-list header          no; it is operator delete
  0x14053bd3b IAT 0x140d53250        no - RCX is [RBP + 0x7]               no; a string destructor

  The one that matters is FUN_140461230, and it is a DESTROY, not a builder. Its two branches:

      140461250  488bd9        MOV RBX,RCX              <- the local record
      140461253  488b11        MOV RDX,qword ptr [RCX]   <- its node
      14046125b  4c3bca        CMP R9,RDX
      14046125e  7530          JNZ 0x140461290           <- not the whole tree: erase range
      140461260  488b5208      MOV RDX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]
      140461264  e837180100    CALL 0x140472aa0         <- DESTROY the whole tree
      14046126c  48894008      MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x8],RAX
      140461273  488900        MOV qword ptr [RAX],RAX
      140461279  48894010      MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x10],RAX
      14046127d  48c7430800000000  MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],0x0
      ...
      1404612f5  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX
      1404612f8  e8a3340100    CALL 0x1404747a0         <- ERASE, one node at a time

  FUN_140472aa0 is the tree destroy already established: it calls operator delete on each node's
  buffer and then stores ZERO into +0x28, +0x30 and +0x38.

  FUN_1404747a0 is a red-black tree ERASE - 312 instructions of rotation and colour-flipping on
  the +0x18 byte - and it ends by freeing the node and zeroing all three fields:

      140474b27  488b4e28      MOV RCX,qword ptr [RSI + 0x28]   <- the node's vector
      140474b35  4885c9        TEST RCX,RCX
      140474b38  0f8480000000  JZ 0x140474bbe
      140474bab  e8fea83000    CALL 0x14077f4ae                 <- free the vector buffer
      140474bb0  33c0          XOR EAX,EAX
      140474bb2  48894628      MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x28],RAX    <- +0x28 = 0
      140474bb6  48894630      MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x30],RAX    <- +0x30 = 0
      140474bba  48894638      MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x38],RAX    <- +0x38 = 0
      140474bc1  e8e8a83000    CALL 0x14077f4ae                 <- free the node

  So both branches of FUN_140461230 only ever store ZERO at a node's +0x28. Neither allocates.

  A CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER SECTION, since this is a writer of those three offsets that the
  earlier table missed: the section "Writers of node vector +0x28" listed four functions, and
  FUN_1404747a0 was not among them, even though it appeared in that section's own candidate list
  of functions writing all three offsets. It is a fifth writer, and like FUN_140472aa0 it writes
  zero, during erase rather than destruction. The earlier table's conclusion is unaffected - it
  did not claim to be exhaustive - but it was incomplete and this is the completion for this
  path.

         1405331ba  488b8db0000000  MOV RCX,qword ptr [RBP + 0xb0]
         1405331c1  4883c128        ADD RCX,0x28
         1405331ca  e831460100      CALL 0x140547800

      and that [RBP + 0xb0] holds a node of the local tree at [RBP - 0x68], written by
      FUN_14051bc60. So PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants DOES allocate nodes and DOES store pointers at
      node + 0x28 - but on a local tree that is discarded when it returns, not on any record in

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Calls after 0x14053bc9b inside PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires: 8, all listed in section 3. Exactly
    one receives the record - FUN_140461230, and only the LOCAL record, which was copied into
    the array and is about to be freed. It destroys (FUN_140472aa0) or erases (FUN_1404747a0);
    both store ZERO at +0x28. None allocates.
  * Calls in PrepareVecteur after 0x14053c125: 9, all listed in section 4. Five reference the
    record array and every one of those references is a LOAD. Two are appenders of new records.
    Two never touch the array. None adds a node to an existing record's tree.
  * PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants does allocate nodes and write node + 0x28, but on a local tree.
  * The node that FUN_14052b7c0 later sums is created and populated entirely inside the append,
    by FUN_140447640 at 0x140447bc4, which calls FUN_14045d0b0 to allocate and FUN_140452960 at
    0x14044768b to store a deep copy of the source node's vector at +0x28/+0x30/+0x38.
  * Therefore: none of the calls in the window does, and the record is complete before
    0x14053bc9b returns.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The completeness of both lists rests on enumerating every CALL instruction above the stated
    address within each function: 8 for PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires and 9 for PrepareVecteur, all
    printed above. An indirect call reached by a computed jump would not be listed; I found no
    JMP or CALL through a register targeting these ranges.
  * "No node allocator and no tree routine called" is a check of each function's DIRECT calls
    against a fixed list of 11 targets. A deeper indirect route - a callee that reaches one of
    them through a function pointer - would not be caught. I did not do a whole-program dataflow
    pass and I do not claim one.
  * For the two IAT callees at 0x14053c21b and 0x14053c227 I did not resolve the imports, so I
    did not check them for 0x2448 references. I state that rather than implying a clean result.
    Both are late in the function and both are on the tail path after the appends.
  * I did not open FUN_140447000, which copies the record's +0x18 sub-structure, so I do not
    describe its contents or whether it allocates. It is inside the append, not in the window.
  * I did not run the program. "The tree is fully populated at the append" is a statement about
    the call graph - the insert is a synchronous recursive call from the append - and not a
    runtime observation. I have not verified how many nodes any given record ends up with.
  * One correction to an earlier section of this file is reported in section 3 rather than
    folded in silently.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Every ADDR/BYTES pair quoted above was extracted from this file by regex and re-read with a
    fresh memory_read. Count and result recorded with the append.
  * Call targets were re-derived from the rel32 with SIGNED arithmetic. Self-test on a known
    call: 14057c410 e8 8b 29 00 00 -> 0x14057eda0.
  * The claim that no store to 0x2448/0x2450/0x2458 exists in the five readers rests on listing
    every instruction in each of those functions whose text mentions one of those three
    displacements - 3, 6, 2, 1 and 1 references respectively, all of them loads or LEAs, printed
    in section 4. That is an exhaustive scan of those functions for the displacement, not a
    sample.
  * The record layout in section 2 is read from the instructions of FUN_140547ff0, FUN_140447060,
    FUN_140447990 and FUN_140447b90, not from the decompiler's pointer arithmetic, which was
    ambiguous about whether the source tree lives at source+0x00 or source+0x08.
  * No program was saved. The project was opened read-only with update_analysis off, and
    program_mode_get reported read_only true with no active transaction before closing.
  * One error of my own, for the record: I transcribed 0x14053bc91 as 4c8d8e48240000 when quoting
    it in section 1, carrying the spurious 0x4c REX.W prefix over from a draft. The correct
    encoding is 498d8e48240000, which is what the section "What 0x2448 holds" already recorded
    for the same instruction. Corrected above from memory_read, and the count is 92/92.
