--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. The four virtual calls - what I tried, and why I stopped
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  These are the reason I cannot give a clean "none does". All four dispatch through a vtable, so
  the target is only knowable from the object's vtable pointer at run time, or from RTTI.

      140682230  488b01        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]        <- RAX = the vtable
      140682243  ff9090010000  CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x190]
      ...
      14068226a  488b03        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX]        <- RAX = the document's vtable
      140682270  ff9030020000  CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x230]
      140682276  4c8b08        MOV RCX... [R9 = [RAX]]
      140682281  41ff5120      CALL qword ptr [R9 + 0x20]

  WHAT I DID. I took the document class to be CProductionDoc, whose TypeDescriptor I have on
  record at 0x1410df988, and went to derive its vftable the way earlier sections in this file
  did: COL -> pVft -> vftable, then read the slot.

  WHERE I WENT WRONG, twice, and I am recording it because both would have produced a confident
  wrong answer:

    1. I read the COL RVA at 0x1410df988 + 0x0C. That is the exact error this file has recorded
       before - the TypeDescriptor's pTypeDescriptor field is at o + 0x0C where o = -8, not at
       +0x0C. It returned a plausible-looking non-zero and I discarded the result.
    2. Corrected to td - 8, it produced an RVA that pointed outside the address space, and the
       memory read failed outright. I then checked whether 0x1410df988 was the TypeDescriptor or
       its name string, and found the name ".?AVCProductionDoc@@" at 0x1410df998 - ten bytes
       higher, which means 0x1410df988 IS the TypeDescriptor after all, and what I had decoded
       as a string was the TypeDescriptor's 16-byte binary header.

  So I fell back to scanning for the TD RVA itself, and that is where the second error was. I
  scanned 92 blocks of 0x140e00000-0x1410e0000 for the little-endian TD RVA 0x0010df988 and got
  three hits, all of which I had to discard: the TypeDescriptor RVA also appears inside
  ClassHierarchyDescriptor and BaseClassDescriptor records, and my signature==1 filter did not
  exclude them. The vftable values I derived from those hits were self-inconsistent - the pSelf I
  read came back equal to the COL address itself - which is the signature of reading the wrong
  structure, and I did not want to build a conclusion on it.

  I stopped there rather than keep iterating. The remaining work is a bounded and mechanical
  RTTI job - validate each hit as a real _RTTI_COMPLETE_OBJECT_LOCATOR by checking that
  pClassDescriptor points at a plausible ClassHierarchyDescriptor, then compute
  vftable = pSelf - pVft and read slots 0x190 and 0x230 - and guessing at it would be worse than
  reporting it open. I would rather hand over four named call sites than a slot value I cannot
  stand behind.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. What this does and does not tell you about the flag
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  THE POSITIVE HALF, which is solid: between CheckTstWithMachineLimits returning and
  PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires testing the flag, the twelve calls I could examine do not clear it. The
  one in-image function with any real body, IsProgramCompatibleWithThisHead, never even mentions
  the offset. The other nine are string and logging helpers that are handed CStringT objects.

  THE OPEN HALF: four virtual calls sit in that window, and one of them - 0x140682270, dispatched
  on the DOCUMENT's own vtable at slot 0x230 - is exactly the shape of call that could reach back
  into the zone table and clear a flag. I have not ruled it out and I am not ruling it out.

  SO THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS PUT IS: NOT ESTABLISHED, in the direction of "no". There is no
  evidence of a clear in the twelve calls I could examine, and four unexamined calls remain in
  which one could occur. I am explicitly not treating the 0xf4 stores in
  VerifyAndSetFiducialSections as evidence either way - those target a different register
  derivation, as the previous section set out, and the limit I recorded there still stands: I
  could not prove that a CMire's +0x8 field never points at a CAD row.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * "19 calls in FUN_140682130" and "2 calls in ReloadDoc" are complete lists for those ranges,
    produced by enumerating every CALL mnemonic rather than by reading. FUN_140682130's last
    instruction is a RET, so nothing escapes the range.
  * The four unresolved virtual calls are the whole of the gap. I have not examined a single
    instruction of any of their bodies, and I do not characterise what they do beyond the argument
    registers.
  * "NONE of the nine imports is given a zone row" is an argument about the arguments at the call
    sites, which I read, not a property of the imported code, which I did not read. An import
    could in principle write anywhere it is pointed.
  * The two IAT slots I named by decoding a hint/name RVA were verified by that arithmetic. The
    five I named from the listing's labels were not - their slot contents are not name RVAs, so I
    am relying on Ghidra's naming there.
  * My RTTI derivation failed twice before I stopped, for the reasons in section 4. The failure
    mode worth noting is that the intermediate values looked plausible - a non-zero "COL RVA", a
    plausible-looking hit count - and would have produced a wrong slot read rather than an error,
    had the memory access happened to land inside the image.
  * I did not run the program, so which of these calls executes on any given pass is a static
    reachability statement, not an observation.
  * No error of my own in the twelve resolved cases. The two errors were in the abandoned RTTI
    route, and both are reported above rather than dropped.

  * Every ADDR/BYTES pair quoted above was extracted from this file by regex and re-read with a

  * The 0xf4 negative for IsProgramCompatibleWithThisHead came from a scan for any instruction

===== Controller slot 0x20 =====

Question: what does CALL qword ptr [R9+0x20] at 0x140682281 call, and does that function store
displacement 0xf4?

The nonzero return from FUN_140682130 reaches it like this. Document slot +0x230 is 0x14045c520,
which returns [document+0x19e8]. The next instructions are MOV R9, [RAX] / LEA RDX, [RSP+0x50] /
MOV RCX, RAX / CALL [R9+0x20]. RCX is that object. RDX is the stack CString destroyed at
0x140682338. SetProductionVMC stores an IVMachineController there. The two CALL [RAX+0x190] sites
return zero and do not reach this call.

If slot +0x20 of that object is a function in Vision3D.exe, say whether its body stores
displacement 0xf4. If it is only a jump into another module, name the module and stop. Do not open
that module.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  IT IS A FUNCTION IN Vision3D.exe, NOT A JUMP INTO ANOTHER MODULE. It is at 0x1405217f0, it is 24
  instructions long, and the token 0xf4 DOES NOT APPEAR IN IT AT ALL.

      vptr of the controller      0x140e4d620
      [R9 + 0x20] reads at        0x140e4d640
      value there                 0x1405217f0        <- the target
      0xf4 occurrences in body    ZERO

  So I do not take the "name the module and stop" branch. There is no module to name for the slot
  itself.

  BUT THE ANSWER IS NOT AS CLEAN AS IT LOOKS, AND I WILL NOT LET IT BE MISREAD. The target is the
  SCALAR DELETING DESTRUCTOR for CCAD_ZoneMatriciel. It calls the real destructor through an IAT
  slot - 0x140d5d0d8, which resolves to ??1CCAD_ZoneMatriciel@@UEAA@XZ - and that body is NOT in
  this image. I did not open it, per your instruction. The in-image 24 instructions clear nothing,
  but they do not run the base destructor either; they call out to it. Whether THAT clears a +0xf4
  is outside what I examined and I am flagging it rather than letting the zero stand as a blanket
  answer.

  AND THE CALL DESTROYS THE OBJECT. RCX is the controller at document+0x19e8, and the routine
  reached is a destructor followed by operator delete. So 0x140682281 is not a method call on the
  controller - it is the controller being torn down and freed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise, verified
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Document slot +0x230 returns [document+0x19e8], exactly as stated. The function is named GetVMC
  and is two instructions:

      14045c520  488b81e8190000  MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX + 0x19e8]
      14045c527  c3              RET

  The call sequence at the question's address, with the argument setup:

      14068226a  488b03        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RBX]        <- the document's vtable
      14068226d  488bcb        MOV RCX,RBX
      140682270  ff9030020000  CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x230]  <- GetVMC -> RAX = the controller
      140682276  4c8b08        MOV R9,qword ptr [RAX]        <- R9 = the controller's vtable
      140682279  488d542450    LEA RDX,[RSP + 0x50]          <- the stack CStringT
      14068227e  488bc8        MOV RCX,RAX                    <- RCX = the controller
      140682281  41ff5120      CALL qword ptr [R9 + 0x20]    <- THE CALL

  And RDX is the same CStringT destroyed at 0x140682338, confirming the question's reading of it:

      140682331  b301            MOV BL,0x1
      140682333  488d4c2450      LEA RCX,[RSP + 0x50]
      140682338  ff15bacd6d00    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]   <- CStringT::~CStringT

  A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, which I had written as the CDataCaoTraitement constructor
  "putting a controller in that slot". It does not - it NULLS the slot. The two instructions are

      14051e3ba  33db              XOR EBX,EBX
      14051e3bc  48899ee8190000    MOV qword ptr [RSI + 0x19e8],RBX

  so 0x19e8 starts null and is filled later by SetVMC. The member is still confirmed as a real,
  lifecycle-managed field of CDataCaoTraitement rather than a coincidence of offsets, and its
  destructor reads it back - but the correct statement is that the constructor clears it, not that
  it initialises a controller.

  and SetVMC is the setter named in the question:

      140540e58  488991e8190000  MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x19e8],RDX

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Identifying the controller's vtable - three independent confirmations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  This is the step that failed in the previous section, so I am showing all three anchors rather
  than one.

  (a) THE CLASS. The TypeDescriptor name in the RTTI blob is

        .?AVCZone3DExecInfo@ViVMachineController@@      at 0x1410d79c8

      so the most-derived class is CZone3DExecInfo over the ViVMachineController interface. I
      found the name by scanning .data for the byte pattern of "MachineController", which returned
      three hits, and then reading a window around the first to recover the full string.

  (b) THE COL. The TypeDescriptor sits at name - 0x10 = 0x1410d79b8, RVA 0x10d79b8. I scanned 92
      blocks of 0x140e00000-0x1410e0000 for that RVA in little-endian and got 2 raw hits - the
      previous section got 3 bogus hits from the same kind of scan, because the TypeDescriptor RVA
      also occurs inside ClassHierarchyDescriptor and BaseClassDescriptor records. The filter that
      fixes it is a self-consistency test on the COL itself:

        signature at +0x00 == 1, pTypeDescriptor at +0x0C == 0x10d79b8, and
        pSelf at +0x14 == the COL's OWN RVA.

      Exactly one hit passes:

        COL     0x140f04c60
        pSelf   0x140f04c60   (self-consistent)

  (c) THE VFTABLE, located the direct way rather than by formula. In the x64 scheme the vftable
      offset is NOT stored in the COL - I confirmed that against a known-good pair from an earlier
      section, CDataCaoTraitement with vftable 0x140e4d8a0 and COL 0x140f04cd8, whose COL fields
      give pSelf = 0xf04cd8 at +0x14 and a data pointer at +0x10, while the true vftable offset
      0xb7438 appears nowhere in the 24-byte COL. What does hold is vftable[-1] = a pointer to the
      COL. So I scanned .rdata for the qword 0x140f04c60 and got exactly one hit, at 0x140e4d618,
      making the vftable 0x140e4d620 - with the caveat, caught below, that the first entry I read
      at that address was garbage.

      CONTROL: I ran the same vftable[-1] test on the known CDataCaoTraitement pair first, and
      0x140e4d8a0 - 8 holds 0x140f04cd8, exactly its COL. The test works.

  (d) THE CORRECTION, and it matters. Reading entries from 0x140e4d620 gave a garbage first entry
      (0x203a74616877) and the COL pointer in the SECOND slot. So the COL pointer is at
      0x140e4d618 and the first real vtable entry is at 0x140e4d620, making

        vftable = 0x140e4d620,  and  vftable[-1] = 0x140f04c60 = the COL.  Verified.

  (e) THE DECISIVE CONFIRMATION, from code rather than data. A vtable is referenced from exactly
      one place, its own constructor. A search of all of .text for the address 0x140e4d620 returns
      exactly one instruction:

        14051ce2b  488d05ee079300  LEA RAX,[0x140e4d620]
        14051ce32  488903          MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX

      The constructor loads 0x140e4d620 into an object's first qword. That is the vptr store, so
      the vptr IS 0x140e4d620, and [R9 + 0x20] reads 8 bytes at 0x140e4d640.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. The target, and its body
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

      [0x140e4d640] = 0x1405217f0

  which is inside .text (0x140001000-0x140d509ff). It is NOT a thunk and NOT a jump into another
  module - it is 24 instructions of real code that then calls onward. Its complete body:

      1405217f0  48895c2408        MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RBX
      1405217f5  57                PUSH RDI
      1405217f6  4883ec20          SUB RSP,0x20
      1405217fa  8bfa              MOV EDI,EDX
      1405217fc  488bd9            MOV RBX,RCX
      1405217ff  ff15d3b88300      CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d0d8]   <- the real destructor
      140521805  40f6c701          TEST DIL,0x1
      140521809  7426              JZ 0x140521831
      14052180b  488bcb            MOV RCX,RBX
      14052180e  40f6c704          TEST DIL,0x4
      140521812  7513              JNZ 0x140521827
      140521814  e895dc2500        CALL 0x14077f4ae                 <- operator delete
      140521819  488bc3            MOV RAX,RBX
      14052181c  488b5c2430        MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x30]
      140521821  4883c420          ADD RSP,0x20
      140521825  5f                POP RDI
      140521826  c3                RET
      140521827  ba48040000        MOV EDX,0x448
      14052182c  e88f3ef3ff        CALL 0x1404556c0                 <- a sized free
      140521831  488bc3            MOV RAX,RBX
      140521834  488b5c2430        MOV RBX,qword ptr [RSP + 0x30]
      140521839  4883c420          ADD RSP,0x20
      14052183d  5f                POP RDI
      14052183e  c3                RET

  THE 0xf4 RESULT: I scanned all 24 instructions for the token 0xf4 in any form - not only for
  stores, but for any mention whatsoever - and the result is an EMPTY list. The offset does not
  appear in this function.

  WHAT IT IS. The decompiler types the first argument CCAD_ZoneMatriciel*, and the IAT slot it
  calls resolves to

        0x140d5d0d8  ->  ??1CCAD_ZoneMatriciel@@UEAA@XZ

  so this is the SCALAR DELETING DESTRUCTOR for CCAD_ZoneMatriciel: run the destructor, and then
  either operator_delete (0x14077f4ae) or, if bit 2 of the flags is set, the sized free at
  0x1404556c0 with size 0x448. CZone3DExecInfo derives from CCAD_ZoneMatriciel, which is
  consistent with the vtable belonging to CZone3DExecInfo while its deleting destructor is the
  inherited base one.

  AN ARGUMENT OBSERVATION, since it looks odd and someone will ask. RDX at the call site is
  [RSP+0x50], a CStringT, but this function treats its second argument as a bit field and reads
  only bits 0 and 2 of it. So the low two bits of a CStringT's first qword decide whether the
  object is freed here or left for a later sized free. I am describing what the instructions do
  with the register; I am not asserting the call is well-typed, and I did not check what
  [RSP+0x50] holds at that moment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. What this settles, and what it deliberately does not
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  SETTLED. The target of CALL [R9+0x20] is 0x1405217f0, a function in Vision3D.exe, and its own 24
  instructions contain no occurrence of displacement 0xf4. There is no other module to name for
  the slot, so the "stop" branch does not apply.

  NOT SETTLED, and I am putting it in bold because the zero above is easy to over-read. The
  in-image function is a DELEGATING DESTRUCTOR. Its very first action is

      1405217ff  ff15d3b88300  CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d0d8]

  which is CCAD_ZoneMatriciel::~CCAD_ZoneMatriciel, reached through the import table. That
  function's body is not in this image, I did not open it, and you told me not to. A destructor is
  precisely the kind of routine that clears a flag field, and a CAD row's +0xf4 is exactly such a
  field. So the correct statement is: THIS FUNCTION does not store 0xf4; the destructor it calls
  may.

  ALSO WORTH RECORDING, because it changes what the call site is doing. RCX is the controller at
  document+0x19e8, and the routine reached tears that object down and frees it. So 0x140682281 is
  not a query or an update of the machine controller - it is its destruction. If a later
  instruction in FUN_140682130 uses the controller again, that would be a use-after-free; I have
  not looked, and I am not claiming there is or is not one.

  AND THE RELATION TO THE PREVIOUS SECTION. This closes one of the four virtual calls left open
  there. The remaining three are the two CALL [RAX+0x190] sites - which you state return zero, so
  they do not reach this one - and CALL [RAX+0x230], which is GetVMC, a two-instruction accessor
  that also contains no 0xf4. So the window now has one genuinely open item rather than four.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. Summary
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * CALL qword ptr [R9 + 0x20] at 0x140682281 calls 0x1405217f0, a function in Vision3D.exe.
    There is no module to name and no reason to stop.
  * Its body is 24 instructions and contains ZERO occurrences of displacement 0xf4 - not merely no
    store, no occurrence at all.
  * It is the scalar deleting destructor for CCAD_ZoneMatriciel, reached through the vtable of
    CZone3DExecInfo (vftable 0x140e4d620, vptr confirmed by the constructor's LEA/MOV pair at
    0x14051ce2b and 0x14051ce32).
  * It calls CCAD_ZoneMatriciel::~CCAD_ZoneMatriciel through IAT slot 0x140d5d0d8, whose body is
    outside this image and which I did not open, as instructed. A clear of +0xf4 there is not
    ruled out.
  * The call destroys and frees the controller held at document+0x19e8.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Limits, stated honestly
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * The vftable identification rests on three things that agree: a self-consistent COL, a
    vftable[-1] pointing at that COL, and a constructor that stores that exact address into an
    object. The third is the strongest and is a direct instruction, so I regard the vptr as settled.
  * "Zero occurrences of 0xf4" is a scan of the function's own 24 instructions for the token in any
    form. It is not a statement about the IAT destructor it calls, and I keep those separate
    deliberately.
  * The vtable's first two entries are irregular - the slot at +0x08 is zero and the one at +0x10
    is a data address, not code. That is consistent with a multiple-inheritance layout where the
    primary sub-table begins later, but I did not analyse the class hierarchy, so I am not
    describing the interface layout beyond the one slot the question asked about. It does not
    affect the answer, because the vptr is fixed by the constructor store and [R9 + 0x20] is a
    fixed offset from it.
  * I did not verify what [RSP+0x50] contains at the call, so my remark about the CStringT's low
    bits steering the free path is a description of the register use, not a claim about the
    runtime value.
  * I did not check whether FUN_140682130 touches the controller after 0x140682281, so I make no
    claim about a use-after-free.
  * No error of my own in the final identification. Two in the drafting, both reported: I wrote
    that the CDataCaoTraitement constructor installs a controller at +0x19e8 when it in fact
    zeroes that slot, corrected in section 1; and the vftable work went wrong twice - the same two
    RTTI mistakes as the previous section, since I re-used the route - where the correction that
    worked was the pSelf self-consistency test plus the vftable[-1] search, neither of which I had
    applied last time. I record that because it is the reusable lesson: on this binary, find the
    COL by validating pSelf, and find the vftable by searching for the COL pointer at
    vftable[-1], never by a formula involving a field in the COL.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Verification record
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Every ADDR/BYTES pair quoted above was extracted from this file by regex and re-read with a
    fresh memory_read. Count and result recorded with the append.
  * The vftable[-1] technique was self-tested on a known-good pair before being applied to the new
    class: for CZoneJokerDlg-style known data, 0x140e4d8a0 - 8 holds 0x140f04cd8, its own COL.
  * The 0xf4 negative came from a scan for the token in any form across the whole function body,
    which is a stronger statement than a store-pattern match.
  * The IAT name for 0x140d5d0d8 was derived by reading the slot as a hint/name RVA and decoding
    the string at imagebase + rva + 2, using the same le32 helper and self-test
    (14057c410 e8 8b 29 00 00 -> 0x14057eda0) as the rest of this file.
  * The misaligned first entry at 0x140e4d620 was caught by reading the slot's neighbours rather
    than accepting the first value, and the correction was confirmed by the single code reference
    to the address.
  * No program was saved. The project was opened read-only with update_analysis off, and
    program_mode_get reported read_only true with no active transaction before closing.

===== END =====
===== CAD row type =====

Question: what writes the type dword at CCAD_Base+8 before CheckTstWithMachineLimits tests it?

  Find a store to displacement 8 on a pointer returned by GetLineCAD, or an import whose name sets
  that type. Quote the instruction and name the function. If every writer is an import with no body
  in this image, name the import and stop. Do not open another module.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. Short answer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  EVERY WRITER OF +0x8 THAT CAN SET THE BITS THE TEST LOOKS AT IS AN IMPORT WITH NO BODY IN THIS
  IMAGE. I take the stop branch and name it:

      VITDATACAD.DLL::CDataCao::Serialize(CArchive &)      IAT slot 0x140d5d050
      called at 0x14053e98f, with RCX = document+0x180

  That is the same CDataCao whose rows CheckTstWithMachineLimits reads through GetLineCAD. Its body
  is not in this image. I did not open VITDATACAD.DLL, and I did not reopen the IVMachineController
  module.

  I DID NOT FIND the first form you asked for. There is no store to displacement 8 on a pointer
  returned by GetLineCAD, and there is no in-image store to +0x8 of a CAD row that can set bit 0x40
  or bit 0x80 of byte +0x8. Below is the whole search, with the positive controls that make the
  negative trustworthy.

  THERE IS NO IMPORT NAMED "SetType". I enumerated every constructor and every method name in the
  CAD import block, 0x140d5c400 through 0x140d5d950: 20 CAD-row constructor slots and 397 CAD
  method names. Not one of them sets a type by name. The closest is a constructor whose only
  parameter is a type enum, and it is called with 0 - see section 5.

  TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS FIRST, because both affect how the rest reads:

    (a) +0x8 IS NOT A DWORD. Both consumers test it as a BYTE.

          140526ad1  f64008c0          TEST byte ptr [RAX + 0x8],0xc0
          14072455a  f6470801          TEST byte ptr [RDI + 0x8],0x1

        The second one is in a different function and tests a different bit, which is what
        convinces me byte granularity is right and not just one odd instruction.

    (b) THE +0xf4 STORE IS A DWORD, NOT A BYTE FLAG.

          140526adb  c780f4000000010000  MOV dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],0x1

        Ten bytes, immediate 1, 32-bit destination. Sections 53, 54 and 55 of this file describe
        +0xf4 as a byte flag that gets set and cleared. The store is 32-bit wide. This does not
        change any control-flow conclusion in those sections - the store is still the only one and
        the branch structure is unaffected - but the field description was wrong and is corrected
        in section 6.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. The premise, verified at instruction level
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  GetLineCAD is an import whose name I decoded from the slot:

      IAT 0x140d5d080  ->  ?GetLineCAD@CDataCao@@QEAAPEAVCCAD_Base@@_J@Z

  It returns CCAD_Base*. 187 call sites of that slot exist in .text.

  The test, with every byte re-read from memory rather than from the listing render, at 0x140526ac6:

      140526a9c  4c8db780010000  LEA R14,[RDI + 0x180]            <- this = document+0x180
      140526aa3  498bce          MOV RCX,R14
      140526aa6  ff15b4628300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cd60]    <- CDataCao::GetSizeCadTab
      140526aac  4885c0          TEST RAX,RAX
      140526aaf  0f8e3a010000    JLE 0x140526bef
      140526ac0  488bd7          MOV RDX,RDI                     <- the loop index
      140526ac3  498bce          MOV RCX,R14
      140526ac6  ff15b4658300    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]    <- GetLineCAD(this, i)
      140526acc  4885c0          TEST RAX,RAX                    <- row
      140526acf  7423            JZ 0x140526af4
      140526ad1  f64008c0        TEST byte ptr [RAX + 0x8],0xc0   <- THE TEST
      140526ad5  0f8414010000    JZ 0x140526bef
      140526adb  c780f4000000010000  MOV dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],0x1  <- the +0xf4 store

  Concatenated bytes read from memory at 0x140526ac6, 30 bytes:

      ff15b4658300 4885c0 7423 f64008c0 0f8414010000 c780f4000000010000

  I stepped these by hand against the disassembly so that every instruction boundary is anchored to
  bytes I actually read, not to the renderer.

  The second, independent byte test, at 0x14072455a in FUN_140724140, four bytes read from memory:

      f6470801   ->   TEST byte ptr [RDI + 0x8],0x1

  RDI is the GetLineCAD result there: at 0x14072450c MOV RDI,RAX comes straight out of the call at
  0x140724506, and nothing overwrites RDI before 0x14072455a. So a row's +0x8 is read at byte
  granularity by two functions in two different parts of the program.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Detector A - every immediate store to displacement 8 in .text
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Search: search_instructions for the literal substring "+ 0x8]," over
          0x140001000 - 0x140d509f8.

  The search tool matches rendered operand text literally, not as a regular expression. I proved
  that first: "^MOV dword ptr [" returned zero while "0x140d5d080" and "0x8],0x2000000" each
  returned hits, so the tool does substring matching and a leading ^ is not an anchor.

      raw hits                                      9831
      mnemonic is a store AND the memory operand is the DESTINATION operand
      AND the displacement is exactly 0x8             9047
      of those, the source is an immediate              530
      of those, (value & 0xff) & 0xc0 != 0               9

  POSITIVE CONTROL, so the negative is not a broken detector: two of the 530 are the real writers
  named in section 4, and both are in the 530 set.

      0x1405fb559  MOV dword ptr [RSI + 0x8],0x2000000
      0x1405fb63a  MOV dword ptr [R13 + 0x8],0x4000000

  The full value census of the 530, which is what makes the negative concrete:

      byte  0x1     294        qword 0x40      1      dword 0x2        1
      byte  0x0     137        qword 0xf      5      dword 0x1       53
      dword 0x0      30        qword 0x8      1      dword 0x0       30
      dword 0x1      53        qword 0x7      1      dword 0x2000000  1
      dword 0xe       1        qword 0x200000 1      dword 0x4000000  1
      dword 0x8       1        qword 0x1      1      dword 0x201      1

  Not one value in that table has 0x40 or 0x80 in its low byte. The only low-byte match in the whole
  image is "qword 0x40", one instruction, and it is a frame slot - see section 3.

  A NOTE ON MY OWN FIRST PASS AT THIS FILTER. My first version produced nine "hits" and I expected
  them to be gone. They were not, and I nearly wrote the negative on that basis. The bug was in my
  reasoning, not the code: the eight values -1 and -2 do have 0xc0 bits in their low byte (0xff
  and 0xfe) and correctly stayed in. That is right. What I had to check separately is whether they
  are row stores, which is section 3. I am flagging it because a reader skimming the census above
  would otherwise ask why 0xff and 0xfe are missing from the value table.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Detector B - the exact form you asked for: stores to +0x8 in GetLineCAD callers
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  This is the literal question, so I ran it first and on its own.

      call sites of CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]      187
      distinct containing functions                     104
      instructions disassembled                     37457
      instructions with a [reg + 0x8] memory operand  215

  Filtering the 215 to real stores, by destination-operand position rather than by matching the
  displacement anywhere in the text, leaves three dword stores. All three are ruled out, each for a
  different reason.

  (a) 0x1405ebc07  MOV dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],EBP   in FUN_1405ebbd0
      RAX is the entry stack pointer. Verified by reading 60 bytes from 0x1405ebbd0 and stepping:

          1405ebbd0  488bc4            MOV RAX,RSP
          1405ebbd3  57                PUSH RDI
          1405ebbd4  4154              PUSH R12
          1405ebbd6  4155              PUSH R13
          1405ebbd8  4156              PUSH R14
          1405ebbda  4157              PUSH R15
          1405ebbdc  4881ec60070000    SUB RSP,0x760
          1405ebbe3  48c7442420feffffff  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x20],-0x2
          1405ebbec  48895810          MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x10],RBX
          1405ebbf0  48896818          MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x18],RBP
          1405ebbf4  48897020          MOV qword ptr [RAX + 0x20],RSI
          1405ebbf8  450fb6e8          MOVZX R13D,R8B
          1405ebbfc  448be2            MOV R12D,EDX
          1405ebbff  4c8bf1            MOV R14,RCX
          1405ebc02  33ed              XOR EBP,EBP
          1405ebc04  448bfd            MOV R15D,EBP
          1405ebc07  896808            MOV dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],EBP

      The neighbouring MOVs at +0x10, +0x18 and +0x20 spill the register arguments into the caller's
      shadow-space home area. [RAX + 0x8] is the home slot for RDX, initialised to 0. It is a stack
      slot, not a CAD row.

  (b) 0x140724b4c and 0x140724b9c  MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0x8],EAX   in FUN_140724140
      These copy a dword field inside an array whose stride is 0x28. The stride is not guessed, it
      is computed in the same loop:

          LEA RAX,[R14 + R14*0x4]        ->  R14*5
          LEA R14,[R8 + RAX*0x8]         ->  R8 + R14*40        =  stride 0x28
          and the matching index is  RCX/40  via  MOV RAX,0x6666666666666667 / IMUL RCX

      A 0x28-byte element cannot be a CCAD_Base. The deleting destructor path frees
      CCAD_ZoneMatriciel with size 0x448, so a zone row is 0x448 bytes, not 0x28. This is the same
      0x28 record shape recorded in section 50 of this file, whose +0x08 field is a copied value.
      So these are record copies, not type writes.

      I ALSO GOT THE CALLEE WRONG ON THE WAY TO THIS CONCLUSION AND AM CORRECTING IT HERE. While
      reading this window I assumed the call at 0x140724b41 was CCAD_Base::operator= and named the
      IAT slot 0x140d5f108 for it. It is not. That slot holds 0x8000000000000000, not a name RVA,
      so it cannot be decoded that way at all. CCAD_Base::operator= is at 0x140d5d100. The ruling-out
      of 0x140724b4c does not depend on the callee identity - it rests on the stride and on the 0x448
      allocation size - so the conclusion is unaffected, but the wrong identification was doing real
      work in my draft and would have been wrong to print.

  (c) The third dword store is at the same offset in the same two-instruction pattern as 0x140724b4c
      and is disposed of by the same stride-and-size argument.

  Also in the 215 are loads, not stores, which the destination-position rule excludes: for example
  0x140526ad1 TEST byte ptr [RAX + 0x8],0xc0 and 0x1405320ec TEST dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],0x202009.
  TEST and CMP put the memory operand first, so a naive "left of the comma" test would have counted
  them. That is exactly why the filter is by mnemonic as well as position.

  The one "qword 0x40" from section 2 also lands here. 0x140001989, in FUN_140001920:

      140001984  e8c1487a00        CALL 0x1407a624a
      140001989  48c7450840000000  MOV qword ptr [RBP + 0x8],0x40
      140001991  48c7451820000000  MOV qword ptr [RBP + 0x18],0x20
      140001999  410fb64500        MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [R13]
      1400019b0  6bf621            IMUL ESI,ESI,0x21

  Frame slots being built for something else, in a function that never calls GetLineCAD and never
  touches a CAD row. Not a type write.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Detector C - every function that CONSTRUCTS a CAD row
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Rows are created in one place and read through GetLineCAD in another, so the writer cannot live
  in a GetLineCAD caller. I therefore enumerated the construction side instead.

  I decoded the whole CAD constructor block out of the IAT first, taking each slot's contents as a
  name RVA and decoding the string at imagebase + rva + 2, with the le32 helper self-tested on
  e83aade1ff -> 0xffe1da3a at every call.

      CAD-row constructor slots found, 0x140d5c548 - 0x140d5d0d0

        0x140d5c548  ??0CCAD_ZoneMatriciel@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5c560  ??0CComposant@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5c5c0  ??0CCAD_OCV_Reader@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5c7e8  ??0CAD_Region@@QEAA@AEBW4eCadRegionType@@@Z
        0x140d5cab0  ??0CDataMatrixInt@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5cab8  ??0CMire@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5cad0  ??0CCAD_OCV_Reader@@QEAA@CStringT/CDPoint/CDSize/H
        0x140d5cae8  ??0CSkip_bloc@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5caf0  ??0CCAD_Trace@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5cb00  ??0CAD_Region@@QEAA@CStringT/CPolygone/NAEBH/eCadRegionType
        0x140d5cb70  ??0CPad@@QEAA@AEBV0@@Z
        0x140d5cc88  ??0CMacro@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5cdb0  ??0CCAD_Base@@QEAA@XZ
        0x140d5cdc0  ??0CComposant@@QEAA@CDPoint/NNNN/HHHH/CStringT/NNNNN
        0x140d5ce08  ??0CPad@@QEAA@CStringT/CViUnitPoint/CViUnitSize/NAEBHAEBI

  THE WRITER ON THE LOAD PATH.

      VITDATACAD.DLL::CDataCao::Serialize(CArchive &)     IAT 0x140d5d050

  already resident in document+0x180. I am NOT claiming to have proven which of those six call

6. Correction to the previous sections
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  CORRECTION 1 - +0xf4 IS A DWORD, NOT A BYTE FLAG.

      140526adb  c780f4000000010000  MOV dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],0x1

  Thirty-two-bit destination. Sections 53, 54 and 55 of this file call +0xf4 a byte flag, section 53
  says "flag 0xf4 set", and section 55 says the fiducial routine "only clears RBX+0xf4". The store
  being 32-bit wide does not move any branch and does not change which routine is the only writer,
  so those sections' conclusions stand as conclusions. The field description does not, and it is
  corrected here. I re-read the ten bytes from memory rather than trusting the section.

  CORRECTION 2 - MY OWN MISIDENTIFIED CALLEE, from section 3(b).

  IAT slot 0x140d5f108 does not decode to a name; it holds 0x8000000000000000, one of the slots in
  the 0x140d5f0xx / 0x140d5f1xx group that carry that sentinel rather than name RVAs. I had called
  it CCAD_Base::operator=; that name belongs to slot 0x140d5d100. The conclusion about 0x140724b4c
  rests on the 0x28 stride and the 0x448 allocation size and is unaffected.

  CORRECTION 3 - "+0x8 IS A TYPE DWORD" IS WRONG IN THE QUESTION AS ASKED, and I have answered the
  byte question instead, because that is what the program does.

  Both consumers test one byte. A dword store to +0x8 would also write that byte, so a dword writer
  is still in scope, and detector A covers dword, qword and byte stores alike. But nothing anywhere
  reads +0x8 as a 32-bit quantity, so calling it a type dword overstates what is observed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Limits of this negative, stated rather than buried
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  1. Detector A matches the rendered operand substring "+ 0x8],". It finds [reg + 0x8]. It does NOT
     find a store written as [reg + reg*8 + 0x8] or any other indexed spelling, and it does not see
     a store performed by a callee through a computed vtable index of the form CALL [reg + rcx*8].
     No search over computed displacements was done. This is the same gap recorded against the
     fixed-displacement detectors earlier in this file.

  2. A bulk copy would move +0x8 without any +0x8 store existing. I did not enumerate rep movs /
     memcpy paths that copy a whole 0x100, 0x188 or 0x448 CAD object. The obvious such routes -
     CCAD_Base::operator= at 0x140d5d100, CCAD_ZoneMatriciel::operator= at 0x140d5d118,
     CCAD_BaseContainer::Duplique at 0x140d5d140 and CCAD_ZoneMatriciel::Duplique at 0x140d5d148,
     all four with single call sites at 0x14076df9a, 0x14076dfac, 0x14076dfca and 0x14076dfd0 - are
     imports with no body here, so they could not have been examined even if I had tried.

  3. I did not open the CMire or CCAD_Base layouts, so I cannot prove by construction that a mire's
     +0x8 is a different field from a CAD row's +0x8. What I did do is narrow the question to
     objects that are provably CAD rows: allocated by operator new immediately before an imported
     CCAD_* / CAD_* constructor, with the store's base register holding that pointer. Both surviving
     writers satisfy that test. A mire reached through GetLineMire at 0x140d5d098 is a different
     accessor and I did not treat the two as interchangeable.

  4. I did not prove the ordering of Serialize at 0x14053e8f0 relative to
     CheckTstWithMachineLimits. Naming Serialize is a statement about which import can write the
     field, and about it being the only reachable candidate on the path that already has rows in
     document+0x180. It is not a proof that a given load call site runs first.

  5. GetLineCAD is a stable-key thunk. There is also GetLineCAD_const at 0x140d5cda8 in the same
     import block. I used the non-const slot because that is the one the question named and the one
     the 187 call sites call; I did not run detector A against the const thunk's callers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Session hygiene
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  * Opened once, read-only, update_analysis off, against the copy project v3d_files_uncomp_copy /
    V3D_SKIP. program_mode_get reported read_only true and active_transaction null before the work.
    One session for the whole question; program_close at the end with sessions_still_open checked
    at zero.
  * No program was saved.
  * No other module was opened. VITDATACAD.DLL, which owns CCAD_Base, CDataCao and all the CAD-row
    classes, was not opened. The IVMachineController module was not reopened.
  * Every instruction quoted above was re-read from memory. Instruction lengths were taken from the
    bytes I read and boundaries were stepped through by hand, because the listing render has
    previously returned byte strings one byte too long.
  * Every IAT name in this section was derived from the slot contents as a name RVA, decoding at
    imagebase + rva + 2, with the le32 helper self-tested on e83aade1ff -> 0xffe1da3a on every call.
    Slots holding 0x8000000000000000 are reported as undecodable rather than guessed.
  * maps/rev2a-entry-gates.md was not touched.

===== END =====
===== Serialize before CheckTst =====

Question: on the production path that reaches ReloadDoc, does 0x14053e8f0 run before
CheckTstWithMachineLimits? Which of the five direct callers sits on the path from
HandlerProduction or OnOpenDocument into ReloadDoc?

SHORT ANSWER

  None of the five. Zero of five, including the CProductionDoc::Serialize override that
  contains one of the five (0x140695b3d). The user's list of direct call sites does not
  contain the Serialize that actually runs on the production path.

  Serialize does still run before CheckTstWithMachineLimits. It runs by VIRTUAL dispatch,
  from inside ReloadDoc itself, 0xA6 = 166 bytes before the call into the check:

      0x140692ff8   CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x10]   ; RCX = RSI = this
                  -> CProductionDoc primary vftable slot +0x10 = 0x140695ac0
                  -> 0x140695ac0 = CProductionDoc::Serialize
                  -> 0x140695b3d CALL 0x14053e8f0

  That Serialize is a DESERIALIZE (load) of the "TST file". ReloadDoc opens the TST file
  for read, deserializes it, closes it, logs "[3.3] New TST file loaded '%s'.\n", and only
  then calls FUN_140682130, whose first act is CheckTstWithMachineLimits. So the check
  runs on data that was just loaded.

  Two premises need correcting; both are given in full in section 6.
    (1) OnOpenDocument does not reach ReloadDoc in this image at all.
    (2) HandlerProduction is not a symbol in this image. It exists only as a log string.

3. None of the five callers is on that path
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Three negatives, each taken from a full enumeration rather than from a text grep, and each
  checked against a positive control from the same enumeration.

  3.1  HandlerProduction, FUN_1406a20d0 (0x1406a20d0-0x1406a4946), 454 CALL instructions.
       None is 0x14053e8f0, because reference_to 0x14053e8f0 lists exactly 6 code call sites
       and none of the 6 lies inside 0x1406a20d0-0x1406a4946. Positive control: all 6 sites
       ARE enumerated by the same reference_to call.

  3.2  FUN_14069e2d0 (0x14069e2d0-0x14069e720). Full disassembly: 264 instructions,
       61 CALL instructions, and ZERO indirect vtable calls, i.e. no CALL qword ptr [R..]
       anywhere in the function. Exactly one of its 61 calls touches this chain:

          14069e5f6   e8f544ffff         CALL 0x140692af0

       No call to 0x14053e8f0, 0x140695ac0, 0x1405e9cd0, 0x1407482a0, 0x140748db0 or
       0x14069653c. Positive control: all 61 calls enumerated, the ReloadDoc call included.

  3.3  ReloadDoc, 0x140692af0 (0x140692af0-0x140694180). Full disassembly: 1143
       instructions, 217 CALL instructions. Filtering that list for 0x14053e8f0, 0x140695ac0,
       0x1405e9cd0, 0x1407482a0, 0x140748db0 and 0x14069653c returns ZERO hits. Positive
       control: the same 217-call enumeration does yield the 10 indirect vtable calls listed
       in section 4.

  3.4  FUN_140682130 also contains no Serialize-related call. Its 6 calls are
       0x140682187 -> 0x140526970, CALL [RAX+0x190] at 0x140682243 and 0x14068230d,
       CALL [RAX+0x230], CALL [R9+0x20] -> 0x1405217f0, and CALL 0x14052ddc0.

  So: 0 of 5. Stating it and stopping on that sub-question.

  For completeness, where the five actually live:

    FUN_1407482a0   zero code callers AND zero vtable entries. Its only two references are a
                    .pdata RUNTIME_FUNCTION_ENTRY and an IPToStateMapEntry. Unreachable in
                    this image.

                    slot (0x140e76088 - 0x140e76078) / 8 = 2.
    FUN_140695ac0   one code caller, which is its own thunk at 0x140696543 (JMP 0x140695ac0).

        0x140ea3868   0x0000000001406892a0    <- slot 0
        0x140ea3870   0x0000000001406807e0    <- slot +0x08
        0x140ea3878   0x000000000140695ac0    <- slot +0x10   *** Serialize ***

     memory_read 0x140f12e78, 32 bytes:

        01000000 00000000 00000000 88f90d01 a02ef100 782ef100

     decoded as _RTTICompleteObjectLocator: signature 1, offset 0, cdOffset 0,
     pTypeDescriptor RVA 0x010df988, pClassHierarchyDescriptor RVA 0x00f12ea0,
     pSelf RVA 0x00f12e78. pSelf equals the COL's own RVA, so the COL validates.

     TypeDescriptor at 0x1410df988, name at +0x10 = 0x1410df998:

        .?AVCProductionDoc@@

     offset 0 means 0x140ea3868 is a PRIMARY vftable. So slot +0x10 of CProductionDoc's
     own vftable holds 0x140695ac0.

4.3  FUN_140695ac0 is CProductionDoc::Serialize, and it names itself:

        140695af2   4c8d15f7f28000     LEA RDX,[0x140ea4df0]

     0x140ea4df0 = "CProductionDoc::Serialize". reference_to 0x140ea4df0 returns exactly ONE
     reference, 0x140695af2, inside FUN_140695ac0. Nothing else in the image claims that name.

     Its argument forwarding, byte-exact, which is why 0x140695b3d exists at all:

        140695aec   4c8bfa             MOV R15,RDX        ; the CArchive
        140695aef   488bf1             MOV RSI,RCX        ; this
        ...
        140695b37   498bd7             MOV RDX,R15
        140695b3a   488bce             MOV RCX,RSI
        140695b3d   e8ae8deaff         CALL 0x14053e8f0

     So FUN_140695ac0 forwards (this, CArchive&) unchanged to 0x14053e8f0. That is the whole
     reason one of the user's five call sites sits one instruction away from the production
     path while not being on it as a call site.

4.4  The this-adjusting thunk corroborates the slot number, both ways:

        14069653c   4881e980010000     SUB RCX,0x180
        140696543   e978f5ffff         JMP 0x140695ac0

     This thunk occupies slot +0x08 of the CDataCao sub-vftable at 0x140ea3b08. Its COL at
     0x140ea3b00 is 0x140f12f48, and memory_read 0x140f12f48, 32 bytes, gives

        01000000 80010000 00000000 88f90d01 a02ef100 482ff100

     signature 1, offset 0x180, cdOffset 0, pTypeDescriptor CProductionDoc, pSelf == own RVA.

     And slot +0x08 of CDataCao's vftable in CDataCaoTraitement, at 0x140e4db40, holds
     0x14053f1cc = SUB RCX,0x180 / JMP 0x14053e8f0. Its COL at 0x140e4db38 is 0x140f04de8,
     which decodes as

        01000000 80010000 00000000 f8790d01 004df000 e84df000

     offset 0x180, pTypeDescriptor 0x1410d79f8, name at 0x1410d7a08 = ".?AVCDataCaoTraitement@@".
     This is the explanation of the user's own observation that slot +8 of the vftable at
     0x140e4db40 is the thunk: the COL offset is 0x180 and the thunk subtracts exactly 0x180.

     The two CDataCao sub-vftables agree from slot +0x10 onward (0x14076dfb2, 0x14076dfc4,
     0x14076dfbe), so CProductionDoc::Serialize is the +0x08 override of CDataCao's Serialize,
     and it is also what lands at +0x10 of the primary vftable.

4.5  It is a LOAD, not a save. The whole site, byte-exact:

5. Correction to the previous section
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The previous section is "CAD row type" (Q58). Its conclusions are not overturned: the six
direct callers of 0x14053e8f0 and the single VITDATACAD.DLL import call at 0x14053e98f both
stand. What Q58 lacked, and what this section adds:

  (a) 0x140695ac0 is not an unnamed neighbour of Serialize. It is CProductionDoc::Serialize,
      named by its own body at 0x140695af2 -> 0x140ea4df0. One of the six direct callers,
      0x140695b3d, is therefore the CProductionDoc override delegating to the document
      Serialize. Q58 reported it only as FUN_140695ac0.

  (b) Serialize is virtual and reachable from the document at two different slot numbers:
      +0x08 of CDataCao's vftable (thunk 0x14053f1cc) and +0x10 of CProductionDoc's primary
      vftable (FUN_140695ac0, unadjusted). Q58 treated Serialize as reachable only by direct
      call, and it enumerated call sites only. On the production path it is reached by
      neither. The site that matters is 0x140692ff8.

  (c) The vtable premise supplied with this question is confirmed and now explained rather
      than merely checked. Slot +8 of the vftable at 0x140e4db40 does hold 0x14053f1cc, and
      the reason is that the COL at 0x140f04de8 carries offset 0x180, so CDataCao sits at
      CDataCaoTraitement+0x180 and the thunk subtracts exactly 0x180.

  (d) Q58's framing of the six direct callers as "the call sites" of Serialize is
      insufficient. Counter-example now on record: 0x140692ff8.

6. Correction to the question's premises
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1  "the path from HandlerProduction or OnOpenDocument into ReloadDoc"

     OnOpenDocument does not reach ReloadDoc in this image. CDataCaoTraitement::OnOpenDocument
     is 0x14052f840, body 0x14052f840-0x14052f935, 57 instructions, signature
     "int __thiscall OnOpenDocument(CDataCaoTraitement * this, char * param_1)". It has
     exactly 9 CALL instructions:

        14052f869   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f100]
        14052f87f   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f100]
        14052f8a4   CALL qword ptr [0x140d532b8]
        14052f8b3   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]
        14052f8c2   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]
        14052f8ce   CALL 0x14077fe1a
        14052f8e9   CALL qword ptr [0x140d53258]
        14052f90c   CALL qword ptr [0x140d53258]
        14052f91e   CALL qword ptr [0x140d53250]

     No call to ReloadDoc, to FUN_14069e2d0, to HandlerProduction, or to any of the five
     Serialize callers. 0x14077fe1a is a one-instruction thunk, JMP qword ptr [0x140d5f608],
     which Ghidra also names OnOpenDocument, i.e. the MFC base CDocument::OnOpenDocument.
     That base is outside this image and I did not open MFC140.DLL, so no route from it into
     ReloadDoc is visible here, and I am not claiming there is none.

     The premise is therefore wrong for OnOpenDocument and right for HandlerProduction.

6.2  "HandlerProduction"

     There is no symbol with that name in this image. The function exists and is identified
     here by the string it logs: CProductionThread::HandlerProduction = FUN_1406a20d0.
     Accepting that identification of the string is the only step between the premise and
     the code.

6.3  ReloadDoc has a second caller that I did not classify:

        0x1404be407   CALL 0x140692af0

     inside FUN_1404be260 (body 0x1404be260-0x1404be5b7), whose own callers are FUN_1404accf0
     via 0x1404ae309 and FUN_1404becc0 via 0x1404bf68e. I did not determine whether that route
     is production or wizard/simulation, and I did not check it for Serialize. It is outside
     the production path established in section 2, but it is not shown to be absent from
     production. ReloadDoc's two other references, 0x1412cf730 and 0x140fd10c0, are a .pdata
     RUNTIME_FUNCTION_ENTRY and an IPToStateMapEntry, not call sites and not vtable slots.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Limits of these results
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1  The one thing I could not prove statically is that ReloadDoc's `this` at runtime is
     exactly a CProductionDoc whose vptr is 0x140ea3868. Supporting evidence: ReloadDoc's own
     log string is "CProductionDoc::ReloadDoc"; the COL in front of 0x140ea3868 validates by
     pSelf and names CProductionDoc with offset 0. What is missing is that I did not
     enumerate every primary vftable in the image to show that no class derives from
     CProductionDoc. A derived class would need its own primary vftable with its own COL
     naming the derived type. I found no such COL for CDataCao either, since the CDataCao
     sub-vftable COL at 0x140f12f48 names CProductionDoc, which is consistent with
     CProductionDoc being most-derived, but that absence was not verified exhaustively.

     If that assumption holds, Serialize runs before the check. If a deeper document class
     overrides slot +0x10 with something else, it would not.

7.2  IAT slot 0x140d5f128, called at 0x140692f4e with RCX = R14 to produce the path handed to
     CFile::Open, is an ordinal import. The slot holds 0x8000000000000667 and Ghidra labels it
     PTR_operator_char_const*___ptr64_140d5f128. Ordinal 667 cannot be named from this image,
     so the code that builds the TST filename is not identified. It is called twice, at
     0x140692f4e and 0x140692f84.

7.3  0x14077f8a4, 0x14077f8aa, 0x14077f8bc, 0x14077f904, 0x14077f940, 0x14077f94c,
     0x14077f946, 0x14077fdd8 and 0x14077fdc0 are all one-instruction thunks. Their names are
     Ghidra's, taken from the IAT slots: CFile, Open, Close, Copy, CArchive, Close, ~CArchive,
     ~CUIntArray, ~CDWordArray, jumping through 0x140d5f320, 0x140d5f318, 0x140d5f2a0,
     0x140d5fe10, 0x140d5fd78, 0x140d5fd68, 0x140d5fd70, 0x140d5f660, 0x140d5f680.
     Note that 0x14077f94c and 0x14077f8bc are both rendered "Close"; they are distinguishable
     only by their IAT slots, 0x140d5fd68 and 0x140d5f2a0.

7.4  Not opened, per instruction: VITDATACAD.DLL. CDataCao::Serialize's body is still
     unavailable, so nothing here says what it reads from the archive or what it writes into
     document+0x180, and therefore nothing here explains how the 0xf4 flag or the +0x8 type
     field of the CAD rows get their values from this load. MFC140.DLL was not opened either.

7.5  Ordering is proven for a single pass only. The Serialize at 0x140692ff8 sits on the
     success branch of CFile::Open: "140692f6a 85c0 TEST EAX,EAX" then
     "140692f6c 7534 JNZ 0x140692fa2" jumps to the "[3.2] Deserializing" log when Open
     succeeded, while the fall-through at 0x140692f71 logs "Failed to open TST file" and
     "140692f9d e92c020000 JMP 0x1406931ce" leaves. So Serialize runs before CheckTst on the
     pass that opens the TST file successfully; on a pass where the open fails, Serialize does
     not run on this path at all. Whether FUN_14069e2d0, and hence ReloadDoc, is re-entered on
     a later pass is a control-flow question I did not answer: FUN_1406a20d0 is a state machine
     invoked repeatedly from FUN_1406a1c80.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Own errors and broken detectors in this pass
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1  I misread a virtual-call address and briefly reported it as a phantom instruction. My
     first extraction of ReloadDoc's indirect calls printed "140692975 CALL qword ptr
     [RAX + 0x10]", and from memory_read(0x140692973) = ff157fc76c00, from
     listing_disassemble_range(0x140692975) returning 0 items, and from
     function_at(0x140692973) = FUN_1406928d0, I concluded the entry was fabricated. That
     conclusion was wrong. The real instruction is at 0x140693975, inside ReloadDoc, and it is
     genuine, bytes ff5010.

     My own detector was at fault, not the tool. I had built a second extraction testing
     x.address === "140692975", which returned false because the true address is
     0x140693975, and I read that false as "the instruction is absent" instead of "I tested
     the wrong address". Ground truth, from the address-sorted listing of all 1143 ReloadDoc
     instructions, which has no ordering break at all:

        14069395d   e8debf0e00         CALL 0x14077f940
        140693975   ff5010             CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x10]
        140693980   e8c7bf0e00         CALL 0x14077f94c

     No tool misbehaved. The corrected finding is used in sections 4 and 4.7.

8.2  The zero-item result at 0x140692975 is correct but says nothing about ReloadDoc. That
     address lies inside FUN_1406928d0 (body 0x1406928d0-0x140692ac5), a separate function
     that ends before ReloadDoc begins at 0x140692af0. Its instruction there is
     "ff157fc76c00 CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]". I initially over-read this result.

8.3  Two regex mistakes in my own filters, recorded so they are not repeated. Filtering on
     /^qword ptr \[R/ against the text field returned zero hits, because the text field
     already begins with the mnemonic, so a value looks like "CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x10]".
     And I once compared an address field against a literal that had been transcribed from a
     neighbouring entry rather than captured from the field, which is the error in 8.1.

8.4  Not an error, but recorded because it nearly became one: I initially assumed
     FUN_1406a15d0 was a GetDocument accessor. Its body, 0x1406a15d0-0x1406a162f, ends in
     JMP qword ptr [RAX + 0xe0] after a CALL 0x1407a6238 lookup, so it is a dispatcher. Nothing
     above asserts the accessor reading; section 2 carries the caveat instead.

8.5  Earlier, in the section before this one, I recorded that the two CALL [RAX+0x190] sites in
     FUN_140682130 at 0x140682243 and 0x14068230d had unexamined bodies and that the RTTI
     route needed to be applied. It has now been applied and is what resolved 4.2 through 4.4.
     Those two sites are still unexamined; they are not on the Serialize path.

8.6  Session hygiene: one session, opened read-only with update_analysis false against the
     copy project v3d_files_uncomp_copy / V3D_SKIP, program /Vision3D.exe. program_mode_get
     confirmed read_only true and active_transaction null before any query was run.
     program_close at the end, and program_list_open then reported count 0. Nothing was saved.
     Every instruction quoted above was re-read from memory, instruction lengths were taken
     from the bytes I read, and boundaries were stepped through rather than taken from the
     rendering. COL fields were decoded by hand and each was accepted only after its pSelf
     matched its own RVA. maps/rev2a-entry-gates.md was not touched.

===== END =====
===== After document Serialize =====

Question: after CProductionDoc::Serialize calls 0x14053e8f0 at 0x140695b3d, does the rest of
that function write the CAD row type? List every store after 0x140695b3d whose displacement is
8 and whose base is a CAD row, and every call to GetLineCAD (IAT 0x140d5d080). If there are
none, say so and stop.

SHORT ANSWER

  There are none. Zero stores with displacement 8 after 0x140695b3d, and zero calls to
  GetLineCAD anywhere in 0x140695ac0..0x140696539. The rest of the function does not write the
  CAD row type. Per the scope stop, this is stated and the search ends here.

  The type byte is set inside 0x14053e8f0 (the callee), not by this function. This section
  only establishes that this function's tail is not a second writer.

FUNCTION BOUNDS CONFIRMED

  listing_disassemble_function on 0x140695ac0 returned body_start 140695ac0, body_end
  140696539, 586 instructions, first 140695ac0, last 140696539. The user's stated range
  0x140695ac0 through 0x140696539 matches the tool's own body exactly. The instruction at
  the call site:

      0x140695b3d   e8ae8deaff   CALL 0x14053e8f0

  5 bytes, taken from the bytes, not from the rendering. rel32 = 0xFFEA8DAE, signed
  0x140695b3d + 5 + 0xFFEA8DAE = 0x14053E8F0. Target confirmed as 0x14053e8f0.

  Forwarding is unchanged from the previous section and was re-checked at the call site:
  0x140695aec MOV R15,RDX / 0x140695aef MOV RSI,RCX, so RDX (the CArchive) and RCX (this)
  arrive intact.

PREMISE CHECKED: THE 0xf4 NEGATIVE IS CORRECT

  The user stated that a store of displacement 0xf4 does not appear in this function.
  Confirmed and stronger than asked: zero instructions in the entire function body contain
  the substring 0xf4 at all, store or otherwise. The premise is right.

THE ONLY DISPLACEMENT-8 STORE IN THE FUNCTION IS BEFORE THE CALL

  Scanning every instruction of the body for a memory operand whose displacement is exactly
  8, using /[+\-] 0x8\]/, gives 5 instructions in the whole function:

      0x140695adc   48c74508feffffff   MOV qword ptr [RBP + 0x8],-0x2
      0x140695c65   488b4808           MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x8]
      0x1406961e7   488b4808           MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x8]
      0x14069636d   488b4808           MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x8]
      0x1406963ef   488b4808           MOV RCX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x8]

  Classified by destination operand position (memory operand LEFT of the comma):
  4 are LOADS (destination is RCX, a register), 1 is a STORE.

  The single store is 0x140695adc, which is BEFORE 0x140695b3d. Its base is not a CAD row.
  RBP is a stack frame pointer, set by the prologue:

      0x140695ac0   4055              PUSH RBP
      ... 8 pushes total, RBP .. R15
      0x140695acd   488dac2478fbffff  LEA RBP,[RSP + -0x488]
      0x140695ad5   4881ec88050000    SUB RSP,0x588
      0x140695adc   48c74508feffffff  MOV qword ptr [RBP + 0x8],-0x2

  [RBP + 0x8] with RBP = RSP - 0x488 is a stack local, not heap and not a CAD row. -0x2 is
  a small sentinel, not a CAD type tag.

  Absolute-form [0x8] also checked: 0 occurrences.

  The 4 loads are not writes. Their base RAX is the return value of the immediately preceding
  CALL 0x14077f7f6, e.g. at 0x140695c4a, and the sequence is
  MOV RCX,[RAX + 0x8] / CALL 0x1407a6238. The loaded value is passed as RCX onward. No
  value is stored back to any +8.

GETLINECAD: ZERO CALLS IN THIS FUNCTION

  search_instructions for the literal 0x140d5d080 over the whole program returns count 187,
  187 items, all with mnemonic CALL, 0 non-CALL mentions, first 0x140526ac6, last
  0x140764d01. This matches the 187 GetLineCAD call sites recorded in the CAD row type
  section, so the query is live and its image-wide total is unchanged.

  Inside FUN_140695ac0: 0 instructions mention 0x140d5d080 or GetLineCAD at all. Not one.

  The one instruction at 0x140526ac6 in that image-wide list, 0x140526ac6 CALL qword ptr
  [0x140d5d080], is the known CheckTstWithMachineLimits site. It is not in this function.

POSITIVE CONTROLS, BOTH DETECTORS PROVEN LIVE

  A negative is only worth reporting if the detector that produced it can also produce a
  positive. Both were run against values already established in this file.

  Control 1, the displacement-8 store classifier. Run unchanged over FUN_1405fb3e0, the
  function holding the two real +8 writers identified in the CAD row type section, it
  returns 3 stores at displacement 8, including both known writers:

      0x1405fb3e0   48894c2408          MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RCX
      0x1405fb559   c7460800000002      MOV dword ptr [RSI + 0x8],0x2000000
      0x1405fb63a   41c7450800000004    MOV dword ptr [R13 + 0x8],0x4000000

  0x1405fb559 = 0x2000000 and 0x1405fb63a = 0x4000000 are the values already recorded for
  the CAD row type field. The classifier is live and is the same code path that returned
  the 0 hits in FUN_140695ac0.

  Control 2, the GetLineCAD call query. Returned 187 CALL sites image-wide, listed above.
  Live.

WHAT THE TAIL OF THE FUNCTION ACTUALLY DOES

  Not required for the answer, recorded so the negative is not mistaken for "the tail is
  empty". There are 124 CALLs after 0x140695b3d across 66 distinct targets. Memory
  destinations in the tail fall into three groups, none of them a CAD row +8:

    Stack locals      0x20, 0x28, 0x30, 0x40, 0x48, 0x4c, 0x4d0, 0x4d1, 0x4d8, 0x4e0,
                      0x4e8, 0x60, 0x70, 0x78, 0x140, 0x150
    this-relative      0x61f0, 0x6074, 0x3980, 0x2408, 0x240c
    IAT thunk slots    0x140d5f0f8 (13x), 0x140d532f8 (7x), 0x140d52e90 (5x), and others

  The only instruction adjacent to the call that touches the CAD area is the immediate
  successor pair:

      0x140695b42   4c8d05c7f28000   LEA R8,[0x140ea4e10]
      0x140695b49   ba02000000       MOV EDX,0x2
      0x140695b4e   488d4dd8         LEA RCX,[RBP + -0x28]
      0x140695b52   ff15a0d76b00     CALL qword ptr [0x140d532f8]
      0x140695b58   488d8e88010000   LEA RCX,[RSI + 0x188]
      0x140695b5f   ff1593736c00     CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cef8]

  0x140695b58 builds document + 0x188, not document + 0x8. 0x140d5cef8 is not a
  GetLineCAD-family slot and its callee body is an import, so the name is not asserted here.
  This is the closest thing to a CAD-area write in the tail and it is at 0x188.

  Four LEA RCX,[RSI + 0x180] instructions also appear in the tail, at 0x140695bf4,
  0x140695bde, 0x140695c26 and 0x1406964b5. RSI + 0x180 is the CDataCao subobject. All four
  pass it as RCX to a callee. None stores into it.

SCOPE STOP

  Stopped as instructed. VitDataCAD.dll was not opened, and no other module was opened.
  The analysis is confined to /Vision3D.exe in project copy v3d_files_uncomp_copy /
  V3D_SKIP, program /Vision3D.exe, read_only true, update_analysis false. Not saved. The
  locked GUI project v3d_files_uncomp / V3D_SKIP was not opened.

  What was NOT opened, and therefore not claimed: the body of 0x14053e8f0, which is where
  the +8 write actually happens and which is the subject of the next question; the body
  behind IAT 0x140d5cef8 called with document + 0x188; any RTTI or vftable for the classes
  used in the 124 tail calls.

LIMITS OF THIS NEGATIVE

  A store to a CAD row +8 written with a displacement other than 8, for example through a
  register already holding row + 8, or through a scaled index, would not be caught by a
  displacement test. For this function that hole is closed as far as the listing allows:
  the only two indexed memory operands in the whole body are

      0x140695f47   CMP byte ptr [RAX + RCX*0x1],0x0     ; a compare, reads
      0x140695f9c   LEA RDX,[RDI + RSI*0x1]             ; an address computation, not a store

  neither is a displacement-8 store, so no scaled form is hiding one. A store through a
  pointer already advanced to row + 8 (displacement 0, bare [RAX]) cannot be excluded from
  the listing alone and is not excluded here.

OWN-ERRORS THIS SECTION

  9.1  I mis-derived the address of the name string behind IAT slot 0x140d5d080. I added
       the RVA 0x010abee6 (slot contents e6eb0a01 00000000, little-endian) to 0x140001000,
       the start of .text, instead of to the image base 0x140000000, and read 0x1400febe8.
       That returned code bytes, not a name. Correct address is imagebase + rva + 2 =
       0x1410ABE8.
  9.2  The corrected read at 0x1410abe8 then failed twice: memory_read returned
       MemoryAccessException, and listing_data_at returned an empty data_hex. So the
       *name* of slot 0x140d5d080 is NOT re-derived this round. The identification of that
       slot as GetLineCAD is carried over from the CAD row type section, where it was
       decoded successfully. The 187-call-site count is independently reproduced here and is
       consistent, but the name itself is taken on that earlier reading, not on a fresh one.
  9.3  No tool misbehaved in the store and call detectors. Both returned correct data and
       both passed their positive controls. The two failures above are my own address
       arithmetic and a genuine unreadable block.
