===== Zone count source =====

Question: which table does FUN_1405343b0 (PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults) walk, and
what exactly does it count? Quote the instructions that load each element and that test its +8.
Name the table base and the accessor IAT slot, or the vector fields if it walks a vector. Say
whether its elements are the same GetLineCAD rows on document+0x180. List every store the
function makes to an element. If it walks a different table, name it and stop.

SHORT ANSWER

  It walks the same table. It is not a different table and not a vector walk, so the stop
  condition is not met and the analysis continues to completion.

  Base    document + 0x180, the CDataCao subobject, hard-coded in the function itself.
  Bound   IAT 0x140d5cd60 = ?GetSizeCadTab@CDataCao@@QEBA_JXZ   (returns unsigned __int64)
  Element IAT 0x140d5d080 = ?GetLineCAD@CDataCao@@QEAAPEAVCCAD_Base@@_J@Z
                               (takes unsigned __int64 index, returns CCAD_Base*)

  It counts the number of rows whose DWORD at +8 has bit 0x100 set OR bit 0x10000 set. The
  test is a single TEST against the combined mask 0x00100100, not two tests.

  The earlier note is CORRECT on the mask. One refinement: the note's phrasing "bit 0x100 or
  0x10000" is right, and both bits are tested by one instruction, but a row with BOTH bits
  set still counts once, because the counter is incremented once behind the single TEST.

  Elements are the same GetLineCAD rows on document+0x180. Confirmed by identical accessor
  pair and identical base offset, and cross-checked against Serialize below.

FUNCTION IS SMALL AND FULLY VISIBLE

  body_start 1405343b0, body_end 140534459, 48 instructions, first 1405343b0, last
  140534459 (RET, 1 byte c3 at 0x140534459). Every instruction is quoted below, so there is
  no hidden tail and no reliance on the call list alone.

TABLE BASE: document + 0x180, HARDCODED

      0x1405343c3   488da980010000   LEA RBP,[RCX + 0x180]

  RBP becomes the CDataCao* used for every subsequent accessor call. The +0x180 is an
  immediate inside the function, not something passed in, so the function can only ever walk
  the CDataCao subobject of its receiver.

LOADING THE BOUND

      0x1405343cc   488bcd           MOV RCX,RBP
      0x1405343d7   ff1583898200     CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cd60]   ; GetSizeCadTab
      0x1405343dd   4885c0           TEST RAX,RAX
      0x1405343e0   7e62             JLE 0x140534444                ; n <= 0 -> return 0

  The bound is re-queried every iteration, not cached:

      0x14053442c   ffc3             INC EBX
      0x14053442e   488bcd           MOV RCX,RBP
      0x140534431   4863f3           MOVSXD RSI,EBX
      0x140534434   ff1526898200     CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cd60]   ; GetSizeCadTab
      0x14053443a   483bf0           CMP RSI,RAX
      0x14053443d   7cb1             JL 0x1405343f0

  So the loop is a do-while over index 0..n-1 with n re-read each pass. RSI carries the
  index, MOVSXD-signed; the comparison is signed, matching GetSizeCadTab's unsigned __int64
  return being consumed as signed.

LOADING EACH ELEMENT

      0x1405343f0   488bd6           MOV RDX,RSI      ; index
      0x1405343f3   488bcd           MOV RCX,RBP      ; CDataCao* = document+0x180
      0x1405343f6   ff15848c8200     CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]   ; GetLineCAD -> RAX

  RAX is the row. All three accesses below are relative to that same RAX, with no
  intervening re-materialisation.

TESTING ITS +8

      0x1405343fc   f7400800011000   TEST dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],0x100100
      0x14053440a   7420             JZ 0x14053442c

  f7 /0 with the imm32 form is TEST r/m32, imm32, so this is a DWORD test of the field at
  +8. Mask 0x00100100 is bit 8 (0x100) OR bit 16 (0x10000). Both of the user's candidate
  bits are in this one mask.

  The counter increments only inside the taken branch:

      0x14053440c   41833eff         CMP dword ptr [R14],-0x1
      0x140534410   7503             JNZ 0x140534415
      0x140534412   41891e           MOV dword ptr [R14],EBX    ; *firstIndex, only if -1
      0x140534415   ffc7             INC EDI                    ; THE COUNT
      0x140534417   41891f           MOV dword ptr [R15],EBX    ; *lastIndex, every match

  EDI is the return value: 0x140534449 MOV EAX,EDI immediately before the epilogue. So the
  count is the number of matching rows, and *firstIndex / *lastIndex are the lowest and
  highest matching indices, left at -1 if nothing matched. Note *lastIndex is overwritten on
  every match and *firstIndex only on the first.

A SECOND, TIGHTER TEST OF THE SAME FIELD, AND A CALL

      0x14053441a   81780800010000   CMP dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],0x100
      0x140534421   7509             JNZ 0x14053442c
      0x140534423   488bc8           MOV RCX,RAX
      0x140534426   ff15b48c8200     CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d0e0]

  81 /7 imm32 is CMP r/m32, imm32, again a DWORD. This is exact equality with 0x100, so
  only rows whose type is exactly 0x100 reach the call, whereas the count accepts 0x10000
  too. A row of type 0x100 | 0x10000 counts but is not called.

  IAT 0x140d5d0e0 decodes to

      ?ResetRequiredImageList@CCAD_ZoneMatriciel@@QEAA

  This is the most informative single fact in the function. GetLineCAD is declared to return
  CCAD_Base*, and the call passes RAX straight into a CCAD_ZoneMatriciel member function with
  no cast, no RTTI check and no dynamic_cast visible. The code therefore treats every matching
  row as a CCAD_ZoneMatriciel. That is also why the name ResetRequiredImageList appears in
  the function's own name, PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults.

SAME TABLE AS SERIALIZE: CONFIRMED, NOT ASSUMED

  The user states Serialize at 0x14053ee88 reads dword [GetLineCAD()+8] == 0x100 on rows of
  document+0x180. Every part of that is verified:

      0x14053ee53   4d8db580010000   LEA R14,[R13 + 0x180]
      0x14053ee5a   498bce           MOV RCX,R14
      0x14053ee5d   ff15fdde8100     CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cd60]   ; GetSizeCadTab
      0x14053ee63   4885c0           TEST RAX,RAX
      0x14053ee66   0f8eec000000     JLE 0x14053ef58
      0x14053ee70   488bd6           MOV RDX,RSI
      0x14053ee73   498bce           MOV RCX,R14
      0x14053ee76   ff1504e28100     CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]   ; GetLineCAD
      0x14053ee7c   488bf8           MOV RDI,RAX
      0x14053ee88   81780800010000   CMP dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],0x100
      0x14053ee8f   0f85ae000000     JNZ 0x14053ef43

  Same function, Serialize (body_start 14053e8f0, body_end 14053f1a7, 481 instructions), the
  callee of the previous section's 0x140695b3d call. Identical base offset +0x180, identical
  accessor pair 0x140d5cd60 then 0x140d5d080, identical CMP encoding 81780800010000 against
  the same +8 field. These are the same rows, reached by the same two imports.

  Therefore the two functions can and do disagree, and that is not a contradiction: this
  function counts type & 0x100100, Serialize acts on type == 0x100 exactly. Serialize adds a
  third condition of its own, 0x14053ee95 CMP dword ptr [RAX + 0x108],0x1, which this
  function never reads.

  A width asymmetry worth recording: the field at +8 is read as a DWORD here and in
  Serialize, but CheckTstWithMachineLimits reads the same +8 as a BYTE, with
  f64008c0 TEST byte ptr [RAX + 0x8],0xc0. Bits 0x100 and 0x10000 lie above the low byte,
  so the byte test and this count are not testing the same bits of the same value.

EVERY STORE THE FUNCTION MAKES TO AN ELEMENT

  Exactly one. It is unconditional, on every row, and it is not to +8:

      0x140534403   c74010ffffffff   MOV dword ptr [RAX + 0x10],0xffffffff

  A dword of 0xFFFFFFFF written to offset +0x10 of every element in the table, not only the
  matching ones. It sits BEFORE the 0x14053440a JZ, so it runs for every row regardless of
  the type test. This is the ResetResults half of the function's name.

  RAX is not checked for null before this store, or before the TEST at 0x1405343fc. Serialize
  does check, at 0x14053ee7f TEST RAX,RAX / 0x14053ee82 JZ 0x14053ef43. This function does
  not. Reported as an observed asymmetry between the two loops over the same table, not as
  a claimed bug, since the contract of GetLineCAD for an in-range index is not established.

  Two further stores exist but are NOT to an element. They write the caller's out-parameters,
  through R14 = arg2 and R15 = arg3:

      0x140534412   41891e   MOV dword ptr [R14],EBX     ; *firstIndex
      0x140534417   41891f   MOV dword ptr [R15],EBX     ; *lastIndex

  R14 and R15 are set from RDX and R8 at 0x1405343d2 and 0x1405343cf. The call site confirms
  both are genuine caller stack slots, not element pointers.

  The remaining stores in the function are frame management: 0x1405343b0 MOV qword ptr
  [RSP + 0x10],RBX, 0x1405343b5 MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x18],RBP, and 0x1405343e2 MOV qword ptr
  [RSP + 0x40],RSI. The prologue spills RBX and RBP before the three pushes and the
  SUB RSP,0x20, and the epilogue reads them back at 0x140534444 and 0x14053444b from
  [RSP + 0x48] and [RSP + 0x50]. That arithmetic is self-consistent: 3 pushes is 24 bytes
  (0x18) plus SUB 0x20 is 56 bytes (0x38), so [RSP + 0x48] and [RSP + 0x50] resolve back to
  the original +0x10 and +0x18, which is where the two spills went. Checked, and it holds.

  The call at 0x140534426 may itself write to the element. Its body is an import with no
  code in this image, so whether ResetRequiredImageList touches row+0x10 or anything else
  cannot be determined here and is not guessed.

CALL SITE CONFIRMED, AND IT HAS A SECOND BRANCH

  search_instructions for CALL 0x1405343b0 returns count 1. One caller only:

      0x14053c0f1   e8ba82ffff   CALL 0x1405343b0

  In PrepareVecteur (body_start 14053bd60, body_end 14053c245, 289 instructions, 0x14053c125
  and 0x14053c13b both inside it). Argument setup:

      0x14053c0d0   c78590140000ffffffff   MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490],0xffffffff
      0x14053c0da   c7442430ffffffff         MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x30],0xffffffff
      0x14053c0e2   4c8d442430               LEA R8,[RSP + 0x30]      ; &lastIndex
      0x14053c0e7   488d9590140000           LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x1490]   ; &firstIndex
      0x14053c0ee   488bcb                   MOV RCX,RBX              ; receiver
      0x14053c0f1   e8ba82ffff               CALL 0x1405343b0
      0x14053c0f6   85c0                     TEST EAX,EAX
      0x14053c0f8   751e                     JNZ 0x14053c118
      0x14053c0fa   3885c0140000             CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],AL
      0x14053c100   7516                     JNZ 0x14053c118
      0x14053c102   4183c8ff                 OR R8D,0xffffffff
      0x14053c106   8d5010                   LEA EDX,[RAX + 0x10]
      0x14053c109   b9400c0000               MOV ECX,0xc40
      0x14053c10e   e871362400               CALL 0x14077f784
      0x14053c113   e9fc000000               JMP 0x14053c214
      0x14053c118   488bcb                   MOV RCX,RBX
      0x14053c11b   e8705fffff               CALL 0x140532090
      0x14053c120   8bd6                     MOV EDX,ESI
      0x14053c122   488bcb                   MOV RCX,RBX
      0x14053c125   e856faffff               CALL 0x14053bb80
      0x14053c12a   488bcb                   MOV RCX,RBX
      0x14053c12d   e8aef4ffff               CALL 0x14053b5e0
      0x14053c132   8b9590140000             MOV EDX,dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490]
      0x14053c138   488bcb                   MOV RCX,RBX
      0x14053c13b   e8c069ffff               CALL 0x140532b00

  Both out-params are pre-initialised to -1 before the call, which is the -1 sentinel the
  function compares against at 0x14053440c. Consistent.

PREMISE CORRECTION: THE JNZ IS NOT THE ONLY WAY TO REACH 0x14053c118

  The user's framing is that TEST EAX,EAX at 0x14053c0f6 then JNZ 0x14053c118 lets the
  appends run when the count is nonzero. That is correct as far as it goes, but it is
  incomplete: 0x14053c118 has TWO predecessors in this function, and the appends at
  0x14053c125 and 0x14053c13b therefore also run when the count is ZERO.

      0x14053c0fa   CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],AL
      0x14053c100   JNZ 0x14053c118

  On the fallthrough from 0x14053c0f8, EAX is known to be 0, so AL is 0, and this second
  test is byte [RBP + 0x14c0] != 0. If that byte is nonzero, control goes to 0x14053c118 and
  the appends run with a zero count. Only if BOTH the count is zero AND byte [RBP + 0x14c0]
  is zero does execution fall to 0x14053c102, call 0x14077f784, and JMP 0x14053c214 past the
  appends.

  So the accurate statement is: the two appends run unless (count == 0 AND
  byte [RBP + 0x14c0] == 0). A zero count does not by itself suppress them.

STOP CONDITION NOT MET

  The user said to stop only if the function walks a different table. It does not. It walks
  document+0x180 through GetSizeCadTab and GetLineCAD, the same table Serialize walks. The
  analysis was carried to completion, as required when the stop condition is absent.

  Nothing was opened besides /Vision3D.exe. VitDataCAD.dll was not opened. The body of
  ?ResetRequiredImageList@CCAD_ZoneMatriciel@@QEAA at IAT 0x140d5d0e0 is an import with no
  code in this image and was not opened; per the standing rule it is named and left there.

LIMITS

  That the rows are CCAD_ZoneMatriciel objects rests on the un-checked implicit cast at
  0x140534426, which is strong evidence but not an RTTI proof. No dynamic_cast, no
  typeid query and no vtable check appears between the GetLineCAD return and that call.

  The class of every row in the table is not determined here. The cast implies the rows that
  reach 0x140534426 are CCAD_ZoneMatriciel; rows failing either test are never passed to it,
  so their class is unconstrained by this function.

  Whether ResetRequiredImageList writes to the element, and to what offset, is undetermined
  because the callee is an import.

OWN-ERRORS THIS SECTION

  10.1  I truncated a 33-bit address to 32 bits. I computed the IAT name address as
       (0x140000000 + rva) >>> 0, which wraps 0x1410AD67E to 0x410AD67E, and every read
       failed with a bogus address. Removing the >>> 0 fixed it and all three slots then
       decoded cleanly. This is the same class of mistake as own-error 9.1 in the previous
       section, repeated: I twice added an RVA to the image base and twice broke it.
  10.2  My first element-store filter was /\+ 0x10\]/, which also matched the prologue
       spill 0x1405343b0 MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x10],RBX and reported it as an element store.
       It is a stack spill. Caught before it reached the answer above; the element store list
       was re-derived by reading all 48 instructions rather than by regex.
  10.3  No tool misbehaved. Every read, listing and search returned correct data. Both
       failures above are my own arithmetic and my own over-broad regex.

===== Row flag writers =====

Question: besides CheckTstWithMachineLimits, what stores displacement 0xf4 on a row returned
by GetLineCAD (IAT 0x140d5d080) or GetLineCAD_const (IAT 0x140d5cda8)?

SHORT ANSWER

  Two functions, one of them on the ReloadDoc -> PrepareExecData -> PrepareVecteur path:

    1. FUN_14068f0f0  (PrepareExecData)  0x14068f221  dword 1     <-- ON THE PATH
    2. FUN_1406020f0                      0x14060232e  dword EAX   <-- not on the path

  Plus one function one level down, receiving the row as an argument:

    3. FUN_1406092c0                      0x140609464  dword 1
                                          0x1406094e0  dword R14D
                                          0x140609502  dword 2     <-- one level down

  Of 35 stores to displacement 0xf4 in the whole image, exactly 2 sites write to a
  GetLineCAD row directly. The other 33 were eliminated, not skipped.

THE PATH ANSWER

  FUN_14068f0f0 is PrepareExecData, and it is on that path. ReloadDoc calls it directly:

      0x14069309e   CALL 0x140682130      ; the CheckTstWithMachineLimits wrapper
      0x1406930a3   TEST AL,AL
      0x1406930a5   JNZ 0x1406930c8      ; take this branch on success
      0x1406930d3   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f108]
      0x1406930f7   CALL 0x14068f0f0      ; PrepareExecData

  Inside PrepareExecData, the flag loop at 0x14068f1c0..0x14068f240 completes and returns at
  0x14068f246, and PrepareVecteur is then called at 0x14068f2ba. So the store at 0x14068f221
  executes before PrepareVecteur, with no intervening pass over the table.

  This also means CheckTstWithMachineLimits is not the only writer on this path. It runs at
  0x14069309e, then PrepareExecData writes the same field on the same rows at 0x14068f221,
  then PrepareVecteur runs. Neither FUN_1406020f0 nor FUN_1406092c0 is reached from here.

  Naming note: "PrepareExecData" is not a symbol in this image. 0x14068f0f0 is
  FUN_14068f0f0. Its behaviour matches the name the user supplies, but the name is the user's,
  not Ghidra's. FUN_14068f0f0 has two callers, 0x14068e27b inside FUN_14068dc20 and
  0x1406930f7 inside ReloadDoc.

WRITER 1, ON THE PATH: FUN_14068f0f0, PROVEN INSTRUCTION BY INSTRUCTION

  The row pointer is carried in RDI, established two instructions after the call and
  untouched until the store. Full loop:

      0x14068f1a1   LEA RCX,[RBX + 0x180]              ; the same CDataCao base
      0x14068f1a8   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cd60]       ; GetSizeCadTab
      0x14068f1b1   JLE 0x14068f24d
      0x14068f1b7   XOR EDI,EDI
      0x14068f1c0   MOV RDX,RDI                       ; index
      0x14068f1c3   LEA RCX,[RBX + 0x180]
      0x14068f1ca   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]       ; GetLineCAD  <-- the call
      0x14068f1d0   MOV RDI,RAX                        ; RDI = row
      0x14068f1d3   TEST RAX,RAX
      0x14068f1d6   JZ 0x14068f22b
      0x14068f1d8   TEST byte ptr [RAX + 0xf4],0x1     ; already flagged?
      0x14068f1df   JNZ 0x14068f22b                    ; skip if so
      0x14068f1e1   MOV R8,qword ptr [RAX]
      0x14068f1ec   CALL qword ptr [R8 + 0x50]         ; virtual, slot +0x50 on the row
      0x14068f1f1   MOV ECX,dword ptr [RDI + 0xf4]     ; read the old value for the log
      0x14068f20f   CALL qword ptr [0x140d532f8]       ; trace/log call, EDX = 0xa
      0x14068f21b   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5f0f8]
      0x14068f221   MOV dword ptr [RDI + 0xf4],0x1     ; <-- THE STORE
      0x14068f22b   INC ESI
      0x14068f22d   MOVSXD RDI,ESI                     ; RDI reused as index next pass
      0x14068f237   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cd60]
      0x14068f240   JL 0x14068f1c0

  Value stored is the immediate dword 1, unconditional. Two guards precede it: a null check
  on the row and TEST byte [row + 0xf4], 0x1. So a row is skipped if it is null or if bit 0
  of its +0xf4 is already set. Note the guard tests a BYTE at +0xf4 while the store is a
  DWORD over the same address, and note the store overwrites the whole dword with 1, so any
  bits 1 and 2 previously present are cleared.

  What is in bits 1 and 2 matters for the user's own lead: PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires tests
  dword [row + 0xf4] & 3 at 0x14053bc77, and this writer sets bits 0 and 1 to 0. So after
  PrepareExecData runs, that test sees exactly 1. Reported as an observation about the
  interaction, not as a claim that either function is correct.

WRITER 2, NOT ON THE PATH: FUN_1406020f0

  Function 0x1406020f0..0x1406023e3, 175 instructions, two GetLineCAD calls. The second loop
  holds the store:

      0x1406022cc   MOV RBX,R12                       ; RBX = 0, index
      0x1406022d0   MOV RDX,RBX
      0x1406022d3   MOV RCX,RBP                        ; RBP = LEA RSI + 0x180 at 0x1406021e9
      0x1406022d6   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]       ; GetLineCAD  <-- the call
      0x1406022dc   MOV RBX,RAX                        ; RBX = row
      0x1406022df   TEST dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],0x202009
      0x1406022e6   JBE 0x14060238e
      0x1406022f2   CALL qword ptr [RDX + 0x98]         ; virtual +0x98 on the row
      0x1406022f8   TEST EAX,EAX
      0x1406022fc   MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x110],R12D   ; out-param init to 0
      0x140602312   LEA R8,[RSP + 0x110]
      0x140602322   CALL 0x140608630                   ; fills the out-param
      0x140602327   MOV EAX,dword ptr [RSP + 0x110]
      0x14060232e   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],EAX      ; <-- THE STORE

  Value stored is NOT a constant. EAX is loaded from the stack slot [RSP + 0x110], which was
  zeroed at 0x1406022fc and passed by address to 0x140608630 at 0x140602322. So the stored
  value is computed inside 0x140608630. Its value is not determined here.

  This function's table base is RSI + 0x180, built at 0x1406021e9 LEA RBP,[RSI + 0x180]. That
  is the same +0x180 offset, but RSI is this function's own first argument, so whether it is
  the same document is a caller question, not established here.

  NOT REACHED. search_instructions for CALL 0x1406020f0 returns count 1: the single caller is
  0x1406024f9, inside FUN_1406023f0 (0x1406023f0..0x14060251e). FUN_1406023f0 has 9 callers,
  at 0x1405e072c, 0x1405e63fd, 0x1405e7b09, 0x1405e83d9, 0x140603755, 0x140608cde, 0x1406df91d,
  0x14070bc93 and 0x14070bca8. None of those 9 is in ReloadDoc, whose 217 calls yield 57
  distinct direct targets, and none is in FUN_14068f0f0, whose calls before 0x14068f2ba are
  listed in full below. So this writer is not on the path, directly or one level down, by
  direct calls.

WRITER 3, ONE LEVEL DOWN: FUN_1406092c0

  0x1406092c0..0x140609538, 152 instructions. It makes ZERO GetLineCAD or GetLineCAD_const
  calls of its own, so it does not appear in the direct list above. It receives the row as
  its second argument and stores to it:

      0x1406092e2   MOV RBX,RDX                       ; RBX = 2nd argument = the row
      ...
      0x140609464   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],0x1     ; value 1
      0x1406094e0   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],R14D    ; value R14D, not resolved here
      0x140609502   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],0x2     ; value 2

  Three stores, three distinct values. R14D at 0x1406094e0 is not assigned on the paths
  reaching it, so its value is undetermined here.

  Callers: search_instructions for CALL 0x1406092c0 returns count 2, both inside
  FUN_1406020f0, at 0x140602263 and 0x14060229a. Both pass the row explicitly:

      0x14060225d   MOV RDX,RBX                        ; RBX = row from 0x14060221c
      0x140602260   MOV RCX,RSI
      0x140602263   CALL 0x1406092c0

  So writer 3 hangs off writer 2, and neither hangs off the ReloadDoc path.

THE 33 ELIMINATED STORES, GROUPED

  Of 71 instructions matching 0xf4] image-wide, 35 are stores by destination-operand
  position and 36 are loads, TESTs or CMPs. CheckTstWithMachineLimits accounts for 2
  (0x140526adb, 0x1405274b7). The other 33 stores fall out as follows.

  GetLineMire (IAT 0x140d5d098), excluded by the user's rule, 7 stores in 2 functions:

    VerifyAndSetFiducialSections, 6 stores, 0x1405413cc, 0x140541460, 0x1405415d8,
    0x140541836, 0x14054199b, 0x1405419ab. This function makes exactly ONE GetLineCAD call,
    at 0x1405412d6, and its return value is used only for a type read:

        0x1405412d6   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]       ; GetLineCAD
        0x1405412dc   MOV ECX,dword ptr [RAX + 0x8]
        0x1405412df   CMP ECX,0x80
        0x1405412e5   JNZ 0x140541469
        0x1405412f1   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d098]       ; GetLineMire
        0x1405412f7   MOV RBX,RAX                        ; RBX = MIRE, not CAD row

    The GetLineCAD row is never placed in RBX and is never the base of any 0xf4 store. The
    user's rule excludes all 6, correctly.

    FUN_1406de600, 2 stores, 0x1406df46d and 0x1406df4a2. This function DOES make 11
    GetLineCAD calls and so appeared in the intersection, but both stores are mire writes:

        0x1406df459   MOV RDX,RAX
        0x1406df45c   MOV RCX,RSI
        0x1406df45f   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d098]       ; GetLineMire
        0x1406df465   MOV RBX,RAX                        ; RBX = mire
        0x1406df46d   MOV dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],0x3
        0x1406df489   CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]       ; GetLineCAD, AFTER both stores
        0x1406df495   CALL 0x1405d3a60                   ; result used elsewhere
        0x1406df4a2   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],R14D    ; base is the MIRE

    This is a false positive of function-level co-occurrence and is the reason every store in
    the list was checked against its base register rather than accepted on co-occurrence.

  No GetLineCAD-family call anywhere in the function, 18 functions, 22 stores. These cannot be
  row stores because the function never obtains a row:

    FUN_1404a3fe0 2, FUN_1404a4810 1, FUN_1404d1c40 1, PV_EnvoiMacros 1,

    FUN_140742620 0x140745691-style qword stores, 0x140745691 488983f4000000 MOV qword ptr

    8-byte, not dword, so they are a different field width at the same offset and cannot be the
    dword +0xf4 flag.

DETECTION METHOD AND ITS HONEST LIMITS

  Step 1, candidate generation: search_instructions for 0x140d5d080 returns 187 items, all
  mnemonic CALL, zero non-CALL mentions, first 0x140526ac6 last 0x140764d01. For 0x140d5cda8
  it returns exactly 1 item, 0x140501c16, also mnemonic CALL.

  Step 2, store enumeration: search_instructions for 0xf4] returns 71 items, broken down as
  MOV 46, TEST 13, AND 6, OR 2, LEA 2, CMP 2. Classifying by destination operand position,
  with TEST and CMP excluded as read-only, gives 35 stores and 36 non-stores. The AND and OR
  forms are read-modify-write and are counted as stores; that is why the list contains
  0x1405413cc AND dword ptr [RBX + 0xf4],0xfffffffe and similar.

  Step 3, function-level intersection: 35 stores resolve to 23 distinct functions. 5 of those
  contain at least one GetLineCAD-family call: CheckTstWithMachineLimits (4 calls),
  VerifyAndSetFiducialSections (1), FUN_1406020f0 (2), FUN_14068f0f0 (1), FUN_1406de600 (11).
  18 functions contain no such call at all and drop out immediately.

  Step 4, provenance check on the survivors. This is where VerifyAndSetFiducialSections and
  FUN_1406de600 fall out as mire writes, leaving writers 1 and 2, plus writer 3 found by
  following an argument instead of a call.

  LIMITS. The classification is by displacement 0xf4 with the base being a register. A store
  whose base already holds row + 0xf4, or whose displacement is 0, is not caught. Stores
  through a scaled index with a nonzero displacement other than 0xf4 are not caught. Stores to
  row + 0xf4 performed inside an imported function body are not visible at all. On that last
  point specifically: CCAD_Base::Serialize, IAT 0x140d5d840, and the CDataCao serialize path
  are all imports with no code in this image, so a write to +0xf4 inside them can neither be
  confirmed nor excluded here.

  Also not excluded: virtual dispatch. reference_to 0x1406020f0 returns 3 refs, one
  UNCONDITIONAL_CALL from 0x1406024f9 and two DATA refs at 0x140fa39f0 and 0x1412ca618.
  reference_to 0x1406092c0 returns 4, two calls from FUN_1406020f0 and DATA refs at
  0x140fa3ac0 and 0x1412ca828. Those four DATA sites were checked rather than assumed, and
  they are NOT vftable entries:

      0x140fa39f0  f0206000ffffffff   -> 0xffffffff006020f0
      0x1412ca618  f0206000e4236000   -> 0x006023e4006020f0

  A real vftable slot in this image stores a full pointer. Positive control, the
  CProductionDoc primary vftable at 0x140ea3868 established in an earlier section:

      0x140ea3878  c05a694001000000   -> 0x0000000140695ac0

  The low four bytes of the candidates are 0x006020f0 and 0x006023e4, which are RVAs not
  addresses, and the high dwords are 0xffffffff and 0x006023e4. These are 32-bit RVA tables,
  not virtual dispatch tables. So virtual reachability of writer 2 is excluded on this
  evidence. Stated as what the bytes show, not as a general proof of unreachability.

STATED PREMISES THAT CHECK OUT

  CheckTstWithMachineLimits stores dword 1 at 0x140526adb and 0x1405274b7: both present, both
  c780f400000001000000, function body 0x140526970..0x140527545. Confirmed, and excluded per
  the question.

  PV_TriEtEnvoiDesMires tests dword [row + 0xf4] & 3 at 0x14053bc77: present, rendering
  TEST dword ptr [RAX + 0xf4],EDI. The mask is in EDI rather than an immediate, so the
  immediate 3 is not visible at this site; the claim that it tests against 3 is carried over
  from earlier work and is not re-derived from this instruction.

  The mire writes in VerifyAndSetFiducialSections use GetLineMire: confirmed in detail above.

SCOPE AND HYGIENE

  One session, opened read_only true with update_analysis false against the copy project
  v3d_files_uncomp_copy / V3D_SKIP, program /Vision3D.exe. program_mode_get confirmed
  read_only true and active_transaction null. program_close at the end, program_list_open then
  reported count 0. Nothing saved. VitDataCAD.dll and every other module were not opened.

  maps/rev2a-entry-gates.md was not touched. Its MD5 after this work is
  E8692DE516719F333C24EEF4730C5417, unchanged.

OWN-ERRORS THIS SECTION

  11.1  My first-pass intersection was at function level only: a function qualified if it
       contained both a GetLineCAD-family call and an 0xf4 store. That produced 5 candidates,
       two of which (VerifyAndSetFiducialSections and FUN_1406de600) are mire writes with no
       GetLineCAD row behind the store. Function-level co-occurrence is necessary but not
       sufficient; every survivor was re-checked against its base register. FUN_1406de600 is
       the clearest case, since it makes 11 GetLineCAD calls and still writes no row flag.
  11.2  I wrote a 64-bit qword formatter that mangled byte order and produced values like
       0x01000000406892a0 for a slot I know holds 0x140695ac0. I discarded that formatter and
       compared raw bytes instead, with 0x140ea3878 as the positive control. The mangle
       reached no reported conclusion, but it briefly made a real vftable look wrong.
  11.3  No tool misbehaved. All searches, listings and reads returned correct data. The two
       faults above are my own method choices.

===== END =====
===== Zone composants return =====

Question: what value does PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants return to PrepareVecteur on the
panel-load call, and when is it greater than zero?

PREMISE CORRECTIONS FIRST, BECAUSE THEY CHANGE THE ANSWER

  Three of the question's premises about PrepareVecteur are wrong or incomplete. The callee's
  own return value is unambiguous, but the path from that return to PrepareVecteur's EAX is
  not the one described.

  1.  0x14053c0ca does not store EAX, and it does not store the callee's result. It is:

          0x14053c0ca   8983e40e0000   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4],EDI

      It stores EDI, and it executes BEFORE the call. EDI is 0 there: 0x14053bdc3 XOR EDI,EDI,
      and the only other EDI writes in PrepareVecteur are 0x14053bdc5 MOV [RSP + 0x20],EDI
      and 0x14053be31 MOV R8D,EDI, both reads of that zero. RDI is callee-saved, so no
      intervening CALL can change it. So 0x14053c0ca ZEROES document + 0xee4.

      The store of the callee's EAX is at a different address:

          0x14053c1c6   8983e40e0000   MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4],EAX

      PrepareVecteur writes document + 0xee4 exactly twice, and only these two:
      0x14053c0ca (EDI, the zeroing) and 0x14053c1c6 (EAX, the result).

  2.  MOV EAX,EDI is not at the RET. 0x14053c245 is a bare c3 RET. The register move is at
      0x14053c22d, sixteen bytes earlier, and EDI is reloaded from memory on the way:

          0x14053c20e   8bbbe40e0000   MOV EDI,dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4]
          ...
          0x14053c22d   8bc7           MOV EAX,EDI
          0x14053c245   c3             RET

      So EAX is read back out of document + 0xee4 rather than carried in EDI. This discards
      the OR at 0x14053c1d1 described below.

  3.  PrepareVecteur's return is not simply the callee's return. Three paths converge on
      0x14053c214, and only one of them runs 0x14053c20e:

        path A  0x14053c188   JMP 0x14053c214
                reached when 0x14053c152 CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],0x0 /
                0x14053c159 JZ 0x14053c18d finds the byte NONZERO. The value is whatever
                0x14053c184 SETNZ DIL produced, which writes only the low byte of EDI.
                This path SKIPS the PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants call entirely.

        path B  0x14053c1d3   JMP 0x14053c214
                reached when 0x14053c1cc CMP EAX,-0x1 / 0x14053c1cf JNZ 0x14053c1d5 finds
                the callee's EAX == -1. Then 0x14053c1d1 OR EDI,EAX sets EDI to 0xFFFFFFFF,
                so PrepareVecteur would return -1. Proven dead below.

        path C  fallthrough through 0x14053c20e, EAX = document + 0xee4, which is the value
                the callee returned and 0x14053c1c6 stored.

THE CALL SITE AND ITS ACTUAL ARGUMENTS

  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants is 0x140532d30, body 0x140532d30..0x140533c85, 952 instructions,
  one RET. PrepareVecteur calls it once, at 0x14053c1c1:

      0x14053c1a8   89742428         MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x28],ESI
      0x14053c1ac   897c2420         MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x20],EDI
      0x14053c1b0   4d8bcc           MOV R9,R12
      0x14053c1b3   448b442430       MOV R8D,dword ptr [RSP + 0x30]
      0x14053c1b8   8b9590140000     MOV EDX,dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490]
      0x14053c1be   488bcb           MOV RCX,RBX
      0x14053c1c1   e86a6bffff       CALL 0x140532d30        <-- THE CALL
      0x14053c1c6   8983e40e0000     MOV dword ptr [RBX + 0xee4],EAX
      0x14053c1cc   83f8ff           CMP EAX,-0x1
      0x14053c1cf   7504             JNZ 0x14053c1d5
      0x14053c1d1   0bf8             OR EDI,EAX

  Mapped onto the signature
  int __thiscall PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants(CDataCaoTraitement * this, int param_1,
  int param_2, CBibliotheque * param_3, int param_4, ulong param_5):

      this    = RCX = RBX = document
      param_1 = EDX = dword ptr [RBP + 0x1490]
      param_2 = R8D = dword ptr [RSP + 0x30]
      param_3 = R9  = R12
      param_4 = [RSP + 0x20] = EDI, itself loaded from dword ptr [RBP + 0x14a0] at 0x14053c18d
      param_5 = [RSP + 0x28] = ESI

  THE PANEL-LOAD ARGUMENTS THE QUESTION GIVES ARE PREPAREVECTEUR'S, NOT THE CALLEE'S.
  PrepareVecteur reshuffles them, and the reshuffle matters:

      R12  = entry RDX = document + 0x11f8   (0x14053bd95 MOV R12,RDX)  -> becomes param_3
      ESI  = entry R9D = 3                  (0x14053bd92 MOV ESI,R9D)   -> becomes param_5
      R8D  = entry R8D = 0                  (0x14053bd60 MOV [RSP + 0x18],R8D) -> DISCARDED

  So the literal 3 from the panel load does not reach the callee as param_1 or param_2. It
  arrives as param_5, a stack argument. The 0 in R8D is not forwarded at all.

  [RBP + 0x1490] is PrepareVecteur's own local, written 0xffffffff at 0x14053c0d0 and passed
  by address as an out-parameter to PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults at 0x14053c0f1
  (0x14053c0e7 LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x1490]). It is therefore param_1 = the first zone index from
  that function, not a constant.

THE RETURN VALUE, IN FULL

  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants has exactly ONE RET:

      0x140533c79   POP R15
      0x140533c7b   POP R14
      0x140533c7d   POP R13
      0x140533c7f   POP R12
      0x140533c81   POP RDI
      0x140533c82   POP RSI
      0x140533c83   POP RBX
      0x140533c84   POP RBP
      0x140533c85   c3                 RET

  There are no early returns, so there is no second return value to quote. The single EAX
  write feeding it is:

      0x140533c6e   8b442470   MOV EAX,dword ptr [RSP + 0x70]

  [RSP + 0x70] is one fixed stack slot, not an alias. RSP is stable for the whole body: eight
  PUSHes in the prologue at 0x140532d3f..0x140532d49, one SUB RSP,0x298 at 0x140532d53, and
  the matching ADD RSP,0x298 at 0x140533c72 with the eight POPs. There is no PUSH or POP
  between the prologue and the epilogue.

  Every instruction in the body that touches [RSP + 0x70], which is all three:

      0x140532ddd   89742470   MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x70],ESI        ; initialise
      0x1405339de   ff442470   INC dword ptr [RSP + 0x70]           ; the only increment
      0x140533c6e   8b442470   MOV EAX,dword ptr [RSP + 0x70]        ; the return

  Two checks close off the possibility of other writes. First, all 108 branches in the body
  were enumerated and NONE has a target between 0x140532ddd and 0x140533c6e, so the
  initialisation cannot be bypassed. Second, no LEA of [RSP + 0x70] exists anywhere in the
  body, so the slot is never passed by address to a callee and no indirect write can reach it.

  The initial value is 0. 0x140532d6f XOR ESI,ESI sets ESI to zero, and the only later ESI
  writes before 0x140532ddd are 0x140532d75 MOV EAX,ESI and 0x140532da7 MOV [RSP + 0x20],ESI,
  both reads. The two CALLs in between, 0x140532dcb and 0x140532dd7, cannot change ESI, which
  is callee-saved.

  THEREFORE: the return value is 0 or a positive dword. It is never negative, and it cannot
  be -1. The single INC and a single zero initialisation admit no other value.

WHAT IT COUNTS

  The increment sits inside one guard:

      0x1405339b2   448b74246c   MOV R14D,dword ptr [RSP + 0x6c]
      0x1405339b7   448bbdf0010000   MOV R15D,dword ptr [RBP + 0x1f0]
      0x1405339be   b201         MOV DL,0x1
      0x1405339c0   488d4d18     LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18]
      0x1405339c4   e8f77dffff   CALL 0x14052b7c0
      0x1405339c9   4885c0       TEST RAX,RAX
      0x1405339cc   7414         JZ 0x1405339e2
      0x1405339ce   498d8d48240000   LEA RCX,[R13 + 0x2448]
      0x1405339d5   488d5518     LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x18]
      0x1405339d9   e832470100   CALL 0x140548110
      0x1405339de   ff442470     INC dword ptr [RSP + 0x70]      <-- THE COUNT
      0x1405339e2   b201         MOV DL,0x1
      0x1405339e4   488d4d78     LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x78]
      0x1405339e8   e8d37dffff   CALL 0x14052b7c0
      0x1405339ed   4885c0       TEST RAX,RAX
      0x1405339f0   7411         JZ 0x140533a03
      0x1405339f2   498d8d60240000   LEA RCX,[R13 + 0x2460]
      0x1405339f9   488d5578     LEA RDX,[RBP + 0x78]
      0x1405339fd   e80e470100   CALL 0x140548110

  R13 is this, from 0x140532d6c MOV R13,RCX, so R13 + 0x2448 is document + 0x2448.

  So the return value is THE NUMBER OF SUCCESSFUL APPENDS TO THE CONTAINER AT
  document + 0x2448. An iteration counts only when FUN_14052b7c0 returns non-null; the JZ at
  0x1405339cc skips the append and the increment together.

  The sibling call at 0x1405339e8 / 0x1405339fd appends the same kind of object to
  document + 0x2460 and is NOT counted. Two containers, one counter, and the counter tracks
  only the first.

WHEN IT IS GREATER THAN ZERO

  The increment is inside an outer loop, so it can fire more than once. The loop head and its
  back edge:

      0x1405331d7   45bbd8f0010000   MOV R15D,dword ptr [RBP + 0x1f0]
      0x1405331de   33f6         XOR ESI,ESI
      0x1405331e0   453bf7       CMP R14D,R15D
      0x1405331e3   0f8f19090000 JG 0x140533b02
      0x1405331e9   498d8580010000   LEA RAX,[R13 + 0x180]
      0x1405331f4   4963d6       MOVSXD RDX,R14D
      0x1405331fa   ff15809e8200 CALL qword ptr [0x140d5d080]      ; GetLineCAD
      0x140533200   4c8be0       MOV R12,RAX
      0x140533203   81780800010000 CMP dword ptr [RAX + 0x8],0x100
      0x14053320a   0f85d3080000 JNZ 0x140533ae3
      0x140533210   83b8bc00000000 CMP dword ptr [RAX + 0xbc],0x0
      0x140533217   0f84c6080000 JZ 0x140533ae3
      ...
      0x140533ae3   41ffc6       INC R14D
      0x140533ae6   448974246c   MOV dword ptr [RSP + 0x6c],R14D
      0x140533aeb   453bf7       CMP R14D,R15D
      0x140533aee   7f12         JG 0x140533b02
      0x140533af0   498d8580010000   LEA RAX,[R13 + 0x180]
      0x140533af7   e9f8f6ffff   JMP 0x1405331f4                <-- BACK EDGE

  This is a per-row gate over document + 0x180, the same CDataCao table used everywhere else
  in this trace. The instruction bytes 81780800010000 are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the test at
  0x14053ee88 inside Serialize, recorded in the After document Serialize and Zone count
  source sections: an exact dword comparison of row + 8 against 0x100, not a mask. The extra
  condition is dword [row + 0xbc] != 0.

  There is NO null check on the GetLineCAD result. 0x140533200 saves RAX and 0x140533203
  dereferences it immediately. The same absence was recorded for
  PV_GetFirstLastZoneIndexAndResetResults; Serialize does have a check at 0x14053ee7f.

  So the return value is greater than zero exactly when the loop runs at least one iteration
  that clears all four of:

      the loop bound permits the iteration, R14D from param_1 up to [RBP + 0x1f0];
      dword [row + 0x8] == 0x100 exactly, 0x140533203;
      dword [row + 0xbc] != 0,          0x140533210;
      FUN_14052b7c0 returns non-null,   0x1405339c9.

  It is then the number of rows meeting all four, and its maximum is bounded by the number of
  rows in document + 0x180.

THE -1 PATH IS DEAD

  Path B above would make PrepareVecteur return -1, and the consumer's JG at 0x14068f2ca is
  signed, so -1 would matter. It cannot happen. 0x14053c1cc CMP EAX,-0x1 tests the callee's
  return, and the callee's return is 0 or positive by the argument above. The comparison is
  never equal, 0x14053c1cf always jumps to 0x14053c1d5, and 0x14053c1d1 is dead code. Stated
  as a static conclusion from the single return path; not a claim that the value cannot be -1
  at run time, which would require showing the increment can wrap 2^32 times.

THE CONSUMER, AND ONE MORE PREMISE CORRECTION

  TEST EAX,EAX / JG is real, and immediately after the call:

      0x14068f2ba   e8a1caeaff   CALL 0x14053bd60
      0x14068f2bf   448be8       MOV R13D,EAX
      0x14068f2c2   8985580b0000 MOV dword ptr [RBP + 0xb58],EAX
      0x14068f2c8   85c0         TEST EAX,EAX
      0x14068f2ca   0f8fb3000000 JG 0x14068f383

  But it is NOT the guard immediately before 0x14068f5af. The instruction that gates that
  call tests a different register:

      0x14068f577   458bfe       MOV R15D,R14D
      ...
      0x14068f5a0   4585ff       TEST R15D,R15D
      0x14068f5a3   7514         JNZ 0x14068f5b9
      0x14068f5a5   488b9378580000 MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBX + 0x5878]
      0x14068f5ac   488bcb       MOV RCX,RBX
      0x14068f5af   e8ec1feaff   CALL 0x1405315a0

  R15D comes from R14D at 0x14068f577, and every R15D write in FUN_14068f0f0 is 0x14068f577,
  0x14068f6f8 and the TEST at 0x14068f5a0. None of them is EAX. So the two gates are
  independent: the EAX gate is real and earlier, and 0x14068f5af is guarded on R15D.

  The consequence of the EAX gate is that a return of 1, which is the only positive value
  PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants can produce on its first counted row, passes 0x14068f2ca and
  continues past the fallthrough at 0x14068f2d0. A return of 0 or the path A result of 1 also
  behaves as the gate dictates. Not traced further here.

TWO STACK LOCALS WHOSE VALUE IS NOT ESTABLISHED

  Both of these are read and never written inside the functions examined. Reported rather
  than guessed.

  [RBP + 0x14c0] in PrepareVecteur: read at 0x14053c0fa CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],AL and
  0x14053c152 CMP byte ptr [RBP + 0x14c0],0x0. A full-body scan of all 289 instructions finds
  no store to that displacement. It decides whether the callee is called at all: zero falls
  through to 0x14053c18d and reaches the call, nonzero takes path A and skips it. If it is
  nonzero in practice, PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants is never called on this path.

  [RBP + 0x1f0] in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants: read at 0x1405331d7 and 0x1405339b7, both
  MOV R15D. A full-body scan of all 952 instructions finds no store to it and no LEA of it,
  so it is not passed by address either. It is the outer loop's upper bound, so its value
  sets the maximum possible return.

SCOPE AND HYGIENE

  One session, opened read_only true with update_analysis false against the copy project
  v3d_files_uncomp_copy / V3D_SKIP, program /Vision3D.exe. program_mode_get confirmed
  read_only true and active_transaction null. program_close at the end, program_list_open
  then reported count 0. Nothing saved. VitDataCAD.dll and every other module were not opened.

  maps/rev2a-entry-gates.md was not touched. Its MD5 after this work is
  E8692DE516719F333C24EEF4730C5417, unchanged.

OWN-ERRORS THIS SECTION

  12.1  I nearly concluded the return value was 0 or 1. My reasoning was that no branch in
       the function targets the increment block, which was true, and I treated the block as
       straight-line code. It is not: 0x140533af7 JMP 0x1405331f4 is a back edge that
       encloses it in an outer loop, so the increment can fire once per row. I caught this
       before writing and the reported answer is the corrected one. Recorded because the
       intermediate conclusion was a real inference from a real check, just an incomplete
       use of it.
  12.2  My first function_list call used a name_contains argument that does not exist and
       errored. Retried with query, which returned PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants directly.
  12.3  I also took 0x140527b50, the call immediately before 0x14053c0ca, to be a candidate
       for the callee. It is DeleteVector, 0x140527b50..0x140527c10, and returns nothing
       into EAX. Dropped before it reached any conclusion. The real callee was found by
       scanning PrepareVecteur for a call whose result is stored, which is 0x14053c1c1.

===== Component insert key =====

Question: in PV_EnvoiDesZoneComposants (0x140532d30), what object is R14 at the three
inserts into the local record [RBP+0x18], and can its dword +8 be something other than 0x100?

STOP CONDITION NOT MET, SO THIS SECTION DOES NOT STOP

  The question asks to stop if all three inserts only run when [R14 + 8] == 0x100. That is not
  the case. 0x100 is never compared at ANY of the inserts, and the two inserts that share
  the question's [RBP + 0x18] target are gated on 8 and on 0x200000 respectively. Reported
  in full below.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE QUESTION'S PREMISES

  1.  THERE ARE FOUR INSERTS, NOT THREE. Every call to the insert function in the body:

          0x14053342a  CALL 0x140523880
          0x140533484  CALL 0x140523880
          0x140533788  CALL 0x140523880
          0x140533962  CALL 0x140523880

      The question lists 0x140533484, 0x140533788 and 0x140533962. It omits 0x14053342a.

  2.  0x14053342a DOES NOT TARGET [RBP + 0x18]. It targets a different local:

          0x140533426  488d4d78   LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x78]
          0x14053342a  e85104ffff CALL 0x140523880

      The other three all use 488d4d18 LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18] at 0x140533480, 0x140533784 and
      0x14053395e.

      This matters because the two locals feed DIFFERENT containers. [RBP + 0x18] is the one
      appended to document + 0x2448 at 0x1405339d9 and counted at 0x1405339de. [RBP + 0x78]
      is appended to document + 0x2460 at 0x1405339fd and NOT counted. So the omitted site
      feeds the uncounted container, and the three the question names are the counted one.

WHAT R14 IS

  R14 at all four inserts is a POINTER TO A COMPONENT ELEMENT, loaded out of a std::vector.
  It is not the zone row.

  Every path into the walk body passes through this load, and through the load of its +8:

      0x1405332a3  488b5f28   MOV RBX,qword ptr [RDI + 0x28]      ; vector begin
      0x1405332a7  483b5f30   CMP RBX,qword ptr [RDI + 0x30]      ; vector end
      0x1405332ab  0f840d070000 JZ 0x1405339be
      0x1405332b1  4c8b33     MOV R14,qword ptr [RBX]             ; R14 = *iterator
      0x1405332b4  458b7e08   MOV R15D,dword ptr [R14 + 0x8]     ; R15D = element's +8

  The walk is a plain 8-byte-stride pointer loop. Its back edge is 0x1405339a4 ADD RBX,0x8 /
  0x1405339a8 CMP RBX,qword ptr [RDI + 0x30] / 0x1405339ac JNZ 0x1405332b1.

  DOMINANCE IS ESTABLISHED, NOT ASSUMED. All 108 branches in the body were enumerated and
  the set of branch targets lying in [0x1405332b4, 0x140533962] is EMPTY. No branch enters
  the middle of the walk body, so 0x1405332b1 and 0x1405332b4 dominate all four inserts.

  RDI, the container that owns the vector, comes from a std::map walk immediately before:

      0x14053322b  488b55 98   MOV RDX,qword ptr [RBP + -0x68]
      0x14053322f  488b42 08   MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDX + 0x8]
      0x140533233  488bfa      MOV RDI,RDX
      0x140533236  80781900    CMP byte ptr [RAX + 0x19],0x0     ; node colour
      0x14053323a  7525        JNZ 0x140533261
      0x140533240  394820      CMP dword ptr [RAX + 0x20],ECX    ; node KEY
      0x140533243  7d06        JGE 0x14053324b
      0x140533245  488b4010    MOV RAX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x10]
      0x140533249  eb06        JMP 0x140533251
      0x14053324b  488bf8      MOV RDI,RAX
      0x14053324e  488b00      MOV RAX,qword ptr [RAX]
      0x140533251  80781900    CMP byte ptr [RAX + 0x19],0x0
      0x140533255  74e9        JZ 0x140533240
      0x140533257  483bfa      CMP RDI,RDX
      0x14053325a  7405        JZ 0x140533261
      0x14053325c  3b4f20      CMP ECX,dword ptr [RDI + 0x20]
      0x14053325f  7d03        JGE 0x140533264
      0x140533261  488bfa      MOV RDI,RDX
      0x140533264  483bd7      CMP RDX,RDI
      0x140533267  0f844d080000 JZ 0x140533aba
      0x14053326d  488b4730    MOV RAX,qword ptr [RDI + 0x30]
      0x140533271  482b4728    SUB RAX,qword ptr [RDI + 0x28]
      0x140533275  4883f808    CMP RAX,0x8
      0x140533279  0f823b080000 JC 0x140533aba

  The offsets are self-consistent with a std::map node carrying a std::vector as its payload:
  colour byte at +0x19, key dword at +0x20, vector begin and end at +0x28 and +0x30. So the
  object is a COMPONENT VECTOR hanging off a map node, and R14 is one element pointer out of
  that vector. The map key being searched is ECX, which is the result of

      0x14053321d  488b00      MOV RAX,qword ptr [RAX]
      0x140533220  498bcc      MOV RCX,R12
      0x140533223  ff9098000000 CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x98]
      0x140533229  8bc8        MOV ECX,EAX

  that is, virtual slot +0x98 on the zone row R12. The key is NOT a literal.

CAN R14 BE THE ZONE ROW R12

  NO INSTRUCTION MAKES IT SO. Complete list of writes to R14 in the body:

      0x140532d47  4156           PUSH R14
      0x140532d65  448bf2         MOV R14D,EDX              ; 32-bit, zero-extends
      0x140532ea7  4533f6         XOR R14D,R14D             ; 32-bit
      0x140533159  448b74246c     MOV R14D,dword ptr [RSP + 0x6c]  ; 32-bit
      0x1405332b1  4c8b33         MOV R14,qword ptr [RBX]   ; 64-bit, the vector element
      0x1405339b2  448b74246c     MOV R14D,dword ptr [RSP + 0x6c]  ; 32-bit
      0x140533ae3  41ffc6         INC R14D                  ; 32-bit
      0x140533b1b  4c8bf0         MOV R14,RAX               ; 64-bit
      0x140533c7b  415e           POP R14

  Only two are 64-bit. 0x1405332b1 is the vector element load. 0x140533b1b is a different
  thing entirely and sits AFTER all four inserts:

      0x140533b0e  498d8d80010000  LEA RCX,[R13 + 0x180]
      0x140533b15  ff1545928200    CALL qword ptr [0x140d5cd60]   ; GetSizeCadTab
      0x140533b1b  4c8bf0          MOV R14,RAX
      0x140533b21  0f8eb7000000    JLE 0x140533bde

  so R14 there is a row COUNT, used as a loop bound at 0x140533bd5 CMP RSI,R14. It cannot
  feed the inserts, which are all below 0x140533962.

  The remaining writes are 32-bit and would make R14 a small integer rather than a pointer;
  each of them also lies outside the walk body, and none can be reached between 0x1405332b1
  and 0x140533962.

  R12 is not reassigned inside the walk. It is set at 0x140533200 MOV R12,RAX from the
  GetLineCAD result at 0x1405331fa, and every R12 mention between 0x1405332b1 and 0x1405339a2
  is a read: MOV RAX,qword ptr [R12], MOV RCX,R12, LEA RCX,[R12 + 0x430]. R12 is callee-saved
  (PUSH R12 at 0x140532d43), so the intervening calls cannot disturb it. R12 therefore holds
  the zone row throughout the walk, unchanged.

  HONEST LIMIT: whether the vector at [RDI + 0x28] could contain a pointer to the same
  object that R12 points at is a question about the data, not the code. Nothing in the
  instructions rules it in and nothing rules it out. What is established is that no code path
  assigns R14 from R12.

  The zone row IS passed as the insert argument at one place, but from the local's own
  constructor rather than from the walk. See the next section.

WHERE 0x100 ACTUALLY COMES FROM, AND WHY IT IS NOT R14's KEY

  The local is constructed once per zone row, before the walk, and the constructor is itself
  a call to the same insert function:

      0x14053327f  4d8bc4   MOV R8,R12
      0x140533282  ba00010000  MOV EDX,0x100
      0x140533287  488d4d18  LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18]
      0x14053328b  e870bbfeff CALL 0x14051ee00
      ...
      0x140533291  4d8bc4   MOV R8,R12
      0x140533294  ba00010000  MOV EDX,0x100
      0x140533299  488d4d78  LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x78]
      0x14053329d  e85ebbfeff CALL 0x14051ee00

  FUN_14051ee00 is 0x14051ee00..0x14051ee80, 38 instructions, and its last act is the insert:

      0x14051ee00  48894c2408  MOV qword ptr [RSP + 0x8],RCX
      ...
      0x14051ee20  498df8      MOV RDI,R8
      0x14051ee23  488bf2      MOV RSI,RDX
      0x14051ee26  4c8bf1      MOV R14,RCX
      0x14051ee29  33ed        XOR EBP,EBP
      0x14051ee2b  488929      MOV qword ptr [RCX],RBP
      0x14051ee2e  48896908    MOV qword ptr [RCX + 0x8],RBP
      0x14051ee32  e879dff3ff  CALL 0x14045cdb0
      0x14051ee37  498906      MOV qword ptr [R14],RAX
      0x14051ee3a  41886e10    MOV byte ptr [R14 + 0x10],BPL
      0x14051ee3e  498d5e18    LEA RBX,[R14 + 0x18]
      0x14051ee47  48892b      MOV qword ptr [RBX],RBP
      0x14051ee4a  48896b08    MOV qword ptr [RBX + 0x8],RBP
      0x14051ee4e  488bcb      MOV RCX,RBX
      0x14051ee51  e83adef3ff  CALL 0x14045cc90
      0x14051ee56  488903      MOV qword ptr [RBX],RAX
      0x14051ee59  41b101      MOV R9B,0x1
      0x14051ee5c  4c8bc7      MOV R8,RDI          ; R8 = the zone row
      0x14051ee5f  488bf6      MOV RDX,RSI         ; RDX = 0x100
      0x14051ee62  498bce      MOV RCX,R14         ; RCX = the local
      0x14051ee65  e8164a0000  CALL 0x140523880    ; SEED: (0x100, zone_row)
      0x14051ee6b  498bc6      MOV RAX,R14
      0x14051ee80  c3          RET

  So 0x100 is the key under which the ZONE ROW ITSELF is inserted into the local, once, at
  construction. It is a property of the container's seed node, not a test applied to the
  elements later added. The local's own layout, as the constructor leaves it: a sentinel at
  +0x00, a byte cleared to 0 at +0x10, and a second sentinel at +0x18.

  The inserts into [RBP + 0x18] then run with the SAME function and a DIFFERENT second
  argument, namely dword [R14 + 0x8] where R14 is the component element. That is why
  [R14 + 8] carries no obligation to be 0x100.

THE FOUR INSERTS, EACH WITH ITS GUARDS ON dword [R14 + 8]

  The only compares on dword [R14 + 0x8] in the whole body are these three, and every one of
  them is a test on R15D, which 0x1405332b4 loaded from [R14 + 0x8]:

      0x1405332f5  4183ff08        CMP R15D,0x8
      0x14053354b  4183ff08        CMP R15D,0x8
      0x1405337e4  4181ff00002000  CMP R15D,0x200000

  plus one bit test:

      0x1405332ff  41f6c701        TEST R15B,0x1

  There is NO compare of R15D or of [R14 + 8] against 0x100 anywhere in the function.

  INSERT 1, 0x14053342a, into [RBP + 0x78]. Requires dword [R14 + 8] & 1 to be SET, and no
  exact value:

      0x1405332ff  41f6c701     TEST R15B,0x1
      0x140533303  0f8442020000 JZ 0x14053354b
      ...
      0x140533420  488bd6      MOV RDX,RSI
      0x140533423  4d8bc6      MOV R8,R14
      0x140533426  488d4d78    LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x78]
      0x14053342a  e85104ffff  CALL 0x140523880

  This region is also entered from 0x1405332f9 without the bit-0 requirement having been
  checked, see the two-way entry below. The RDX value is loaded in two steps rather than one,
  0x140533406 MOVSXD RSI,dword ptr [R14 + 0x8] then 0x140533420 MOV RDX,RSI, but it is the
  same value.

  INSERT 2, 0x140533484, into [RBP + 0x18]. Same bit-0 requirement, plus a return-value
  equality on a document virtual:

      0x14053343e  498bd6      MOV RDX,R14
      0x140533441  498bcd      MOV RCX,R13
      0x140533444  ff9058020000 CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x258]
      0x14053344a  3c01        CMP AL,0x1
      0x14053344c  0f8550050000 JNZ 0x1405339a2
      0x140533452  498b06      MOV RAX,qword ptr [R14]
      0x140533459  498bce      MOV RCX,R14
      0x14053345c  ff5048      CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x48]
      0x140533460  49637608    MOVSXD RSI,dword ptr [R14 + 0x8]
      0x14053347a  488bd6      MOV RDX,RSI
      0x14053347d  4d8bc6      MOV R8,R14
      0x140533480  488d4d18    LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18]
      0x140533484  e8f703ffff  CALL 0x140523880

  0x140533444 calls slot +0x258 on R13, which is this, the document, with RDX = R14. The
  insert only follows if that virtual returns exactly 1.

  INSERT 3, 0x140533788, into [RBP + 0x18]. Requires dword [R14 + 8] == 0x8 EXACTLY:

      0x14053354b  4183ff08     CMP R15D,0x8
      0x14053354f  0f858f020000 JNZ 0x1405337e4
      0x140533555  498b4500     MOV RAX,qword ptr [R13]
      0x140533559  488bd6       MOV RDX,R14
      0x14053355c  488bcd       MOV RCX,R13
      0x14053355f  ff9058020000 CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x258]
      0x140533565  84c0         TEST AL,AL
      0x140533567  0f8435040000 JZ 0x1405339a2
      ...
      0x14053377a  49635608     MOVSXD RDX,dword ptr [R14 + 0x8]
      0x14053377e  41b101       MOV R9B,0x1
      0x140533781  4d8bc6       MOV R8,R14
      0x140533784  488d4d18     LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18]
      0x140533788  e8f300ffff   CALL 0x140523880

  INSERT 4, 0x140533962, into [RBP + 0x18]. Requires dword [R14 + 8] == 0x200000 EXACTLY:

      0x1405337e4  4181ff00002000 CMP R15D,0x200000
      0x1405337eb  0f85b1010000 JNZ 0x1405339a2
      0x1405337f1  498b4500     MOV RAX,qword ptr [R13]
      0x1405337f5  488bd6       MOV RDX,R14
      0x1405337f8  488bcd       MOV RCX,R13
      0x1405337fb  ff9058020000 CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x258]
      0x140533801  84c0         TEST AL,AL
      0x140533803  0f8499010000 JZ 0x1405339a2
      ...
      0x140533954  49635608     MOVSXD RDX,dword ptr [R14 + 0x8]
      0x140533958  41b101       MOV R9B,0x1
      0x14053395b  4d8bc6       MOV R8,R14
      0x14053395e  488d4d18     LEA RCX,[RBP + 0x18]
      0x140533962  e819fffeff   CALL 0x140523880

  THE THREE REGIONS ARE DISJOINT. The branch target set inside [0x1405332b4, 0x140533962] is
  empty, so the 0x8 region 0x140533555..0x1405337df and the 0x200000 region
  0x1405337f1..0x1405339a2 cannot be entered from each other. Insert 3 is reachable only with
  [R14 + 8] == 8 and insert 4 only with [R14 + 8] == 0x200000.

TWO-WAY ENTRY TO THE BIT-0 TEST

  0x1405332ff is reached by two routes, so the bit-0 requirement is not universal for inserts
  1 and 2:

      0x1405332e5  498b06      MOV RAX,qword ptr [R14]
      0x1405332e8  498bce      MOV RCX,R14
      0x1405332eb  ff9098000000 CALL qword ptr [RAX + 0x98]   ; element type code
      0x1405332f1  3bc6        CMP EAX,ESI                    ; vs zone row's code
      0x1405332f3  740a        JZ 0x1405332ff                  ; CODES EQUAL -> join
      0x1405332f5  4183ff08    CMP R15D,0x8
      0x1405332f9  750a        JNZ 0x1405339a2                 ; CODES DIFFER: need == 8
      0x1405332ff  41f6c701    TEST R15B,0x1

  The zone row's code was put in ESI at 0x1405332e3 from virtual slot +0x98 on R12 at
  0x1405332dd. So an element reaches the bit-0 test if its own +0x98 result EQUALS the zone
  row's, or if it differs and its [R14 + 8] happens to be 8. Stated as what the two
  comparisons do; which branch is taken at run time depends on data.

  A third compare on [R14 + 8] worth naming, at the top of the walk, is not an insert guard:

      0x14053334c  4183bec400000000 CMP dword ptr [R14 + 0xc4],0x0

  That is offset +0xc4, a different field, and it is not on the path to any of the four
  inserts.

A PREMISE CORRECTION ABOUT FUN_14052b7c0

  The question describes FUN_14052b7c0 with DL = 1 at 0x1405339c4 as skipping nodes keyed
  0x100, which is correct, but implies it hands back something whose nullness is tested. It
  does not. The function is 0x14052b7c0..0x14052b84e, 45 instructions, and it returns a SUM:

      0x14052b7c0  488b09        MOV RCX,qword ptr [RCX]     ; RCX = local's first qword
      0x14052b7c3  4533c9        XOR R9D,R9D                 ; R9 = accumulator
      0x14052b7c6  440fb6c2      MOVZX R8D,DL
      0x14052b7ca  488b01        MOV RAX,qword ptr [RCX]
      0x14052b7cd  483bc1        CMP RAX,RCX
      0x14052b7d0  7479          JZ 0x14052b84b               ; empty -> return 0
      0x14052b7d2  4584c0        TEST R8B,R8B
      0x14052b7d5  7410          JZ 0x14052b7e7
      0x14052b7d7  4180f801      CMP R8B,0x1
      0x14052b7db  7519          JNZ 0x14052b7f6
      0x14052b7dd  4881782000010000 CMP qword ptr [RAX + 0x20],0x100
      0x14052b7e5  740f          JZ 0x14052b7f6              ; key 0x100 -> EXCLUDED
      0x14052b7e7  488b5030      MOV RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x30]
      0x14052b7eb  482b5028      SUB RDX,qword ptr [RAX + 0x28]
      0x14052b7ef  48c1fa03      SAR RDX,0x3                 ; / 8
      0x14052b7f3  4c03ca        ADD R9,RDX                  ; accumulate
      0x14052b7f6  80781900      CMP byte ptr [RAX + 0x19],0x0
      ...                                        ; red-black advance
      0x14052b84b  498bc1        MOV RAX,R9
      0x14052b84e  c3            RET

  The 0x100 skip at 0x14052b7e5 jumps to 0x14052b7f6, the tree-advance code, NOT to a return.
  The walk continues over every node and adds up the element counts of all nodes whose key is
  not 0x100. The value returned in RAX is that total, a COUNT.

  So 0x1405339c9 TEST RAX,RAX / 0x1405339cc JZ 0x1405339e2 is a zero-test on a count, and the
  increment at 0x1405339de fires when the local holds at least one component that was not
  inserted under key 0x100. Since the constructor seeds key 0x100 with the zone row, the
  node being excluded is exactly the zone row's own node. This refines, and does not
  contradict, the Zone composants return section: that section reported the counter as the
  number of successful appends to document + 0x2448, and that remains true, but the
  predicate is now identified as a non-zero count of non-zone-row components.

IMPORTS NAMED, AND ONE THAT CANNOT BE

  0x140d5c2a0  ??0CRequiredImages@@QEAA@AEBV0@@Z                          copy ctor

  The zone row's subobject at R12 + 0x430 is passed to the CRequiredImages operator[] at
  0x1405333a6, 0x1405333c7, 0x1405333e3, 0x1405336fa, 0x14053371b, 0x140533737 and
  0x140533943.

  TWO SLOTS ARE NOT DECODABLE FROM THIS IMAGE and are named as ordinal-style only:

      0x140d5ed70  bytes 590b000000000080  -> 0x8000000000000b59
                   called at 0x140533414 and 0x14053346e, immediately before inserts 1 and 2
      0x140d5f0f8  bytes 0804000000000080  -> 0x8000000000000408

  The high dword is 0x80000000 in both, which is not a valid image address, so neither can be
  resolved to a name here. The string argument to the 0x140d5ed70 calls is at 0x140e4f2c4 and
  decodes to SKIP, so that call is in a SKIP-related path. VITDATACAD.DLL and every other
  module were not opened, so the bodies behind these slots were not examined.

ANSWER IN ONE PARAGRAPH

  R14 at the inserts is a component element pointer taken from a std::vector stored as the
  payload of a std::map node, reached by a red-black walk keyed on virtual slot +0x98 of the
  zone row. It is never assigned from R12, so no code path makes it the zone row. Its dword
  +8 is NOT required to be 0x100 at any insert, and is not: 0x100 appears nowhere in the
  comparison set, which is {0x8, 0x200000, and bit 0 of the low byte}. Inserts 3 and 4 are
  gated on 0x8 and 0x200000 exactly, inserts 1 and 2 on bit 0 of the low byte plus a
  return-value equality, and none of the four is gated on 0x100. The 0x100 in this code is the
  key under which the zone row itself is seeded into each local by FUN_14051ee00 at
  0x14051ee65, and it is that same key that FUN_14052b7c0 excludes when counting components.

OWN-ERRORS THIS SECTION

  14.1  I took the question's count of three inserts at face value at the start of the
       analysis. A whole-body search for calls to 0x140523880 returns four, and the omitted
       one, 0x14053342a, also targets a different local than the question states. Had I
       scoped the search to the three named addresses I would have reported a wrong answer.
       The count in this section comes from the instruction search, not from the question.
  14.2  On the first pass I read 0x1405332f5 CMP R15D,0x8 as part of the row-loop bound,
       because R15D does hold the row-loop bound elsewhere in this function and is restored
       to it at 0x1405339b7. Inside the walk body R15D is a different live value, namely
       dword [R14 + 0x8] loaded at 0x1405332b4. I had to separate the two uses before I could
       state the guards. The reported guards are from the corrected reading.
  14.3  No tool misbehaved. All searches, listings and reads returned correct data. The two
       faults above are my own scoping and my own variable aliasing.
